張元舉
同考試官教諭林批詞暢理順善學聖賢而有得者
同考試官教諭蕭批聖賢氣象讀此宛然可見
===
考試官教諭林批言志處親切有味佳士也
考試官教授詹批能發聖賢之蘊宜魁多士錄之
聖賢問答各言其志而小大可見也夫志於人
大矣觀於聖賢之志而其小大之異有不可見
哉昔顏淵季路侍於聖門夫子啓之曰士固有
志人每異趨二子之志何不各言之蓋示以辨
志之教也子路乃言曰人惟病于自私是故不
能以所有者公於人由則願己之有是車馬輕
裘焉通於朋友初無所吝也至於敝壞亦不為
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

顏淵季路侍，子曰：「盍各言爾志？」子路曰：「願車馬衣輕裘，與朋友共，敝之而無憾。」顏淵曰：「願無伐善，無施勞。」子路曰：「願聞子之志。」子曰：「老者安之，朋友信之，少者懷之。」

張元舉

同考試官教諭林批：「詞暢理順，善學聖賢而有得者。」

同考試官教諭蕭批：「聖賢氣象，讀此宛然可見。」

考試官教諭林批：「言志處親切有味，佳士也。」

考試官教授詹批：「能發聖賢之蘊，宜魁多士，錄之。」

聖賢問答，各言其志，而小大可見也。夫志於人大矣，觀於聖賢之志，而其小大之異有不可見哉？昔顏淵季路侍於聖門，夫子啓之曰：「士固有志，人每異趨，二子之志何不各言之？」蓋示以辨志之教也。子路乃言曰：「人惟病于自私，是故不能以所有者公於人。由則願己之有是車馬輕裘焉，通於朋友，初無所吝也。至於敝壞，亦不為
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Yan Yuan and Jilu were attending the Master. The Master said, “Why not each speak of your aspirations?” Zilu said, “I wish to share my carriages, horses, and light fur robes with my friends, with no regret even if they wear them out.” Yan Yuan said, “I wish neither to boast of my merits nor to proclaim my exertions.” Zilu said, “We would like to hear your aspirations, Master.” The Master said, “To bring peace to the aged, to be trustworthy to friends, and to cherish the young.”

Zhang Yuanju

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The language flows freely and the reasoning proceeds smoothly. Here is someone who has learned well from the sages and worthies and gained insight.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “In reading this, one can clearly perceive the bearing of the sages and worthies.”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The passages expressing aspirations are intimate and full of savor. An excellent scholar.”

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: “He can reveal the profound meanings of the sages and worthies. He deserves to head the assembled scholars. Select this essay.”

As the sage and worthies exchanged questions and answers, each expressed his aspirations, and their relative scope became apparent. Aspirations are indeed of great consequence to a person. When we consider the aspirations of the sage and worthies, how could the differences in their scope remain unseen?

Formerly, Yan Yuan and Jilu were attending the sage. The Master prompted them, saying, “Scholars certainly have aspirations, yet people often pursue different ends. Why do you two not each express your aspirations?” In this way he offered instruction in discerning aspirations.

Zilu then said, “People are afflicted by selfishness, and for this reason cannot share what they possess with others. As for me, You, I wish to share whatever carriages, horses, and light fur robes I possess with my friends, without the slightest reluctance from the outset. Even when these become worn out or damaged, I would not…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
矣然他日四子言志獨與曾點而此不與回由
豈弗如點哉或與或告無非至教告之者乃所
以深與之故聖人之教猶天地之化不可以淺
近窺也
上天之載無聲無臭至矣
鍾來秀
考試官教諭林批不顯篤恭之妙惟天道足以擬之
義理精深作者往往難於措辭此篇善形容善發明非有心得者不
能宜錄之
===
考試官教授詹批無聲無臭不過見天道之微妙必
循字求義則失之粗矣此作獨爲得之至矣處講尤透徹蓋其力學
深造故言之親切而有味也魁選允宜
中庸引言天道之至妙足以狀君子之至德也
夫德而不顯德之至者也非卽天道其何以擬
之子思子由下學立心之始而推以及此若曰
言道君子盡之矣言德不顯盡之矣然所謂不
顯之德者可以易言哉彼皇矣烝民之詩猶有
迹也是未足以盡其妙也不若文王之詩有曰
punctuated:
矣。然他日四子言志，獨與曾點，而此不與回、由，豈弗如點哉？或與或告，無非至教。告之者，乃所以深與之。故聖人之教，猶天地之化，不可以淺近窺也。

「上天之載，無聲無臭。」至矣！
鍾來秀

考試官教諭林批：不顯篤恭之妙，惟天道足以擬之。義理精深，作者往往難於措辭。此篇善形容，善發明，非有心得者不能，宜錄之。

考試官教授詹批：無聲無臭，不過見天道之微妙，必循字求義，則失之粗矣。此作獨爲得之。「至矣」處講尤透徹，蓋其力學深造，故言之親切而有味也。魁選允宜。

《中庸》引言天道之至妙，足以狀君子之至德也。

夫德而不顯，德之至者也。非卽天道，其何以擬之？子思子由下學立心之始，而推以及此，若曰：言道，君子盡之矣；言德，不顯盡之矣。然所謂不顯之德者，可以易言哉？彼《皇矣》《烝民》之詩，猶有迹也，是未足以盡其妙也。不若《文王》之詩有曰：
translation_en:
…Yet on another occasion, when the four disciples spoke of their aspirations, he approved only of Zeng Dian. Does his not approving of Hui and You here mean that they were inferior to Dian? Whether he offered approval or instruction, it was always teaching of the highest order. His instructing them was precisely his way of expressing profound approval. Thus the sage’s teaching resembles the transforming activity of Heaven and Earth: it cannot be fathomed through a shallow understanding.

“The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” This is the utmost!
Zhong Laixiu

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The subtlety of unmanifest virtue and earnest reverence can be likened only to the Way of Heaven. The principles involved are profound, and writers often find them difficult to express. This essay excels in description and elucidation; without personal insight, its author could not have achieved this. It merits inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: “Neither sound nor smell” simply reveals the subtlety of the Way of Heaven. To insist on seeking the meaning by following the individual words would make one’s understanding crude. This composition alone grasps it. Its treatment of “This is the utmost” is particularly penetrating. This surely results from the author’s diligent study and profound attainment; hence his words are immediate and full of meaning. His selection for first place is entirely fitting.

The Doctrine of the Mean quotes words describing the supreme subtlety of the Way of Heaven, sufficient to portray the consummate virtue of the noble man.

Virtue that does not display itself is virtue at its utmost. What could serve as its likeness except the Way of Heaven itself? Master Zisi proceeds from the beginnings of establishing one’s purpose through elementary learning and extends his reasoning to this point, as if to say: When speaking of the Way, the noble man embodies it fully; when speaking of virtue, its being unmanifest expresses it fully. Yet can this so-called unmanifest virtue be spoken of lightly? The odes “August Indeed” (Huang yi) and “The Multitudes of the People” (Zheng min) still contain perceptible traces and thus cannot fully express its subtlety. They do not equal the ode “King Wen” (Wen wang), which says: …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
上天之載無聲無臭夫聲臭有氣無形固極天
下之微妙者矣然猶曰無聲猶曰無臭則是動
靜不可求其端也陰陽不可求其始也以是而
擬不顯之德吾知微乎至微同一見聞所不及
妙乎至妙均非方體所能窺於穆之命即君子
之退藏於密理固徹上而徹下者也可謂上下
異致乎無極之眞即君子之神明其德善言人
而徵諸天者也可以天人殊觀乎乾知始而妙
萬物者精矣性性以存神者亦非粗也於稽其
===
類足以極形容之妙蓋得意而不可得名焉天
不言而成變化者深矣物物以過化者亦非淺
也即彼喻此足以盡擬議之微蓋至極而無復
餘蘊焉吁不顯之德擬諸天道君子之所以不
可及也德至于此謂之天德學至于此謂之聖
學過此以往其未之或知者乎抑觀子思子之
作中庸始以天命之性終以上天之載者其義
何居始之以天言自天賦人也終之以天言以
人合天也天人合一終篇之義淵乎深矣而其
punctuated: 「上天之載，無聲無臭。」夫聲臭有氣無形，固極天下之微妙者矣。然猶曰無聲，猶曰無臭，則是動靜不可求其端也，陰陽不可求其始也。以是而擬不顯之德，吾知微乎至微，同一見聞所不及；妙乎至妙，均非方體所能窺。於穆之命，即君子之退藏於密，理固徹上而徹下者也，可謂上下異致乎？無極之眞，即君子之神明其德，善言人而徵諸天者也，可以天人殊觀乎？乾知始而妙萬物者，精矣；性性以存神者，亦非粗也。於稽其類，足以極形容之妙，蓋得意而不可得名焉。天不言而成變化者，深矣；物物以過化者，亦非淺也。即彼喻此，足以盡擬議之微，蓋至極而無復餘蘊焉。吁！不顯之德擬諸天道，君子之所以不可及也。德至于此，謂之天德；學至于此，謂之聖學。過此以往，其未之或知者乎？抑觀子思子之作《中庸》，始以天命之性，終以上天之載者，其義何居？始之以天，言自天賦人也；終之以天，言以人合天也。天人合一，終篇之義淵乎深矣，而其
translation_en:
…“The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” Sound and smell possess vital energy but no visible form; surely they are among the subtlest and most wondrous things under Heaven. Yet the poem still says “without sound” and “without smell.” Thus no first point can be sought in its movement or stillness, nor any beginning in its yin or yang. If we use this to describe virtue that does not display itself, we know that both are subtle to the utmost degree, equally beyond the reach of sight and hearing; both are wondrous to the utmost degree, equally beyond what spatial location or bodily form can reveal. Heaven’s profound and august mandate is precisely the gentleman’s withdrawal into hiddenness. Principle indeed penetrates both above and below: can their ultimate purport be said to differ? The reality of the Ultimate of Nonbeing is precisely the gentleman’s making his virtue numinous and luminous. This is to speak well of the human and verify it by reference to Heaven: can Heaven and humanity be viewed separately? Qian, the Creative, governs beginnings and wondrously brings forth the myriad things: this is refined. To fulfill one’s nature as nature and thereby preserve the spirit is likewise no coarse undertaking. Examining their affinities allows the utmost subtlety of description: their meaning can be apprehended, but no name can adequately capture it. Heaven accomplishes its transformations without speaking: this is profound. To treat each thing according to its nature and transform whatever one passes among is likewise no shallow undertaking. Using the former to elucidate the latter exhausts the subtleties of comparison and deliberation: the utmost point has been reached, with no further depths left unexplored. Ah! That his undisplayed virtue can be compared to the Way of Heaven is what makes the gentleman beyond others’ reach. Virtue that reaches this point is called heavenly virtue; learning that reaches this point is called sagely learning. Beyond this, perhaps no one has any knowledge!

Now consider Master Zisi’s composition of the Doctrine of the Mean: it begins with the nature conferred by Heaven’s mandate and ends with the workings of Heaven above. What is the meaning of this? Beginning with Heaven speaks of what Heaven endows in human beings; ending with Heaven speaks of human beings uniting with Heaven. Heaven and humanity united as one: how profound is the meaning with which the work concludes! And its…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
具是理也心所同得者也懿德之好非秉彞之
性乎及其旣感之後用顯而義行是義也心所
同有者也時出之宜非可欲之善乎至虛者必
至靈良心眞切之地以已而度人一也有物者
必有則良知良能之天以一心而觀萬心同也
夫理義爲心所同然如此不觀諸聖人乎語聰
明之盡若弗可及矣然不過清明在躬先知乎
此理之在我者察之由之無思而無不通焉耳
語道德之極若出乎類矣然不過陽明常勝先
===
覺乎此義之在我者性焉安焉不勉而無不中
焉耳理所同也而盡性踐形以至於順理之裕
者聖人亦率是性豈能於性分之外而有所增
益者乎義所同也而觀物察則以極於精義之
妙者聖人亦與人同豈能外人性之常而更有
所事者乎吁此可見理義不假外求聖人可學
而至也人性之善豈不信哉抑是理也卽吾心
之全體喜怒哀樂未發之中仁義禮智之性也
是義也卽吾心之大用發而皆中節之和惻隱
punctuated:
具是理也，心所同得者也。懿德之好，非秉彞之性乎？及其旣感之後，用顯而義行。是義也，心所同有者也。時出之宜，非可欲之善乎？至虛者必至靈，良心眞切之地，以已而度人，一也；有物者必有則，良知良能之天，以一心而觀萬心，同也。夫理義爲心所同然如此，不觀諸聖人乎？語聰明之盡，若弗可及矣，然不過清明在躬，先知乎此理之在我者，察之由之，無思而無不通焉耳。語道德之極，若出乎類矣，然不過陽明常勝，先覺乎此義之在我者，性焉安焉，不勉而無不中焉耳。理所同也，而盡性踐形，以至於順理之裕者，聖人亦率是性，豈能於性分之外而有所增益者乎？義所同也，而觀物察則，以極於精義之妙者，聖人亦與人同，豈能外人性之常而更有所事者乎？吁！此可見理義不假外求，聖人可學而至也。人性之善，豈不信哉？

抑是理也，卽吾心之全體，喜怒哀樂未發之中，仁義禮智之性也。是義也，卽吾心之大用，發而皆中節之和，惻隱
translation_en:
…possess this principle: it is what all hearts alike receive. Is fondness for admirable virtue not part of the nature endowed with constant moral norms? Once the heart has been moved, its functioning becomes manifest and righteousness is put into practice. This righteousness is what all hearts alike possess. Is the fitting response brought forth as circumstances require not the goodness that is worthy of desire? What is utterly empty must be utterly responsive. At the point where the innate good heart is genuine and sincere, judging others by oneself reveals that we are one. Wherever there is a thing, there must be a norm. In the Heaven-endowed capacity to know and act without learning, examining the myriad hearts through a single heart reveals their commonality. Since principle and righteousness are thus what all hearts alike affirm, should we not look to the sages? Speaking of their consummate perceptiveness, it seems beyond our reach. Yet it amounts only to clarity embodied in their persons: they are first to know this principle within themselves, discerning and following it, comprehending everything without deliberation. Speaking of their utmost moral attainment, they seem to surpass their kind. Yet it amounts only to the constant ascendancy of luminous yang: they are first to awaken to this righteousness within themselves, making it their nature and resting securely in it, hitting the mark in everything without effort. Principle is shared by all; those who fully realize their nature and fulfill their bodily endowment, attaining an ample ease in following principle, are sages who likewise follow this nature. How could they add anything beyond their allotted nature? Righteousness is shared by all; those who observe things and discern their norms, reaching the subtle perfection of finely discerning righteousness, are sages who likewise share in what others possess. How could they undertake anything further outside the constant constitution of human nature? Ah! From this we can see that principle and righteousness need not be sought outside ourselves, and that sagehood can be attained through learning. Is the goodness of human nature not indeed trustworthy?

Furthermore, this principle is the complete substance of our heart: the equilibrium before pleasure, anger, sorrow, and joy arise, and the nature constituted by benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom. This righteousness is the full functioning of our heart: the harmony in which these feelings, once aroused, all attain their proper measure, and the feeling of compassion…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
羞惡辭讓是非之情也孺子入井而怵惕形焉
爾汝之受而慚忿生焉此則悅理義之眞也學
而至於能悅火然泉達理義不可勝用矣然則
悅之時義大矣哉
易
彖曰大畜剛健篤實輝光日新其德
張元舉
同考試官敎諭林批充養立意甚是切當詞亦純雅可取
同考試官敎諭蕭批畜德全功盡於此矣錄以為式
===
考試官敎諭林批畜義詳明易道精矣
考試官敎授詹批以內外言畜是知易者
彖傳發大畜之義必本其德之所由畜焉夫德
必內外交修而後日新之盛可幾也卦德具有
是善名卦之義有在矣彖傳之意若謂君子之
學不有所畜固无以要其成畜之不大亦无以
致其極伏羲所以名卦爲大畜者蓋言學裕諸
中而涵養足以資无窮之用道充于已而蘊畜
有以妙不匱之源固有大畜之義矣而果何所
punctuated:
羞惡、辭讓、是非之情也。孺子入井而怵惕形焉，爾汝之受而慚忿生焉，此則悅理義之眞也。學而至於能悅，火然泉達，理義不可勝用矣。然則悅之時義大矣哉！

易
彖曰：「大畜，剛健篤實輝光，日新其德。」
張元舉
同考試官敎諭林批：「充養立意甚是切當，詞亦純雅可取。」
同考試官敎諭蕭批：「畜德全功盡於此矣，錄以為式。」
考試官敎諭林批：「畜義詳明，易道精矣。」
考試官敎授詹批：「以內外言畜，是知易者。」

彖傳發大畜之義，必本其德之所由畜焉。夫德必內外交修，而後日新之盛可幾也。卦德具有是善，名卦之義有在矣。彖傳之意若謂君子之學，不有所畜，固无以要其成；畜之不大，亦无以致其極。伏羲所以名卦爲大畜者，蓋言學裕諸中，而涵養足以資无窮之用；道充于已，而蘊畜有以妙不匱之源，固有大畜之義矣。而果何所
translation_en:
…the feelings of shame and aversion, deference and yielding, and approval and disapproval. When a young child falls into a well, alarm appears; when one is addressed disrespectfully as “you,” shame and indignation arise. These are genuine manifestations of delight in principle and righteousness. When learning reaches the point of being able to take such delight, it is like fire catching or a spring breaking through: principle and righteousness become inexhaustible in their application. Great indeed are the significance and timeliness of such delight!

Book of Changes
The Commentary on the Judgments states: “Great Accumulation: firm and vigorous, substantial and steadfast, radiant and luminous; daily renewing one's virtue.”
Zhang Yuanju
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The conception of nourishing and developing virtue is most apt. The language, too, is pure and elegant, worthy of selection.”
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: “The complete work of accumulating virtue is fully expressed here. Recorded as a model.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of accumulation is explained thoroughly and clearly; the Way of the Changes is treated with precision.”
Examiner Zhan, Professor, comments: “He discusses accumulation in terms of the inner and outer: here is someone who understands the Changes.”

In elucidating the meaning of Great Accumulation, the Commentary on the Judgments necessarily takes as its basis the means by which virtue is accumulated. Virtue must be cultivated both inwardly and outwardly before the flourishing of daily renewal can be attained. The virtues of the hexagram possess all these excellences; herein lies the reason for its name. The Commentary on the Judgments seems to mean that, in the learning of the gentleman, without accumulation there is certainly no way to secure accomplishment; and unless that accumulation is great, there is likewise no way to reach its utmost extent. Fuxi named the hexagram Great Accumulation presumably to signify that learning becomes abundant within, and its nurturing suffices to support inexhaustible application; the Way fills oneself [?], and its stored abundance brings forth the subtle workings of an unfailing source. This certainly conveys the meaning of Great Accumulation. But on what, precisely, is it based…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
取乎蓋大畜之爲卦也內體乾也其德爲剛健
外體艮也其德爲篤實輝光惟其內之剛健則
天德之良不奪於攻取之私而毅然者不失吾
常強立之德常伸於萬物之上而浩然者適得
吾體天理爲主人欲退聽矣惟其外之篤實輝
光則庸行之謹允廸乎道義之正而敦復足以
自考君子之光日著於踐履之餘而昭明足以
有融闇然而章誠不可揜矣夫然則敬以直內
而義方於外者有本利用安身而致養於內者
===
有資學不病于一偏而德自修于罔覺有長裕
不設之機矣功已極於交致而道自積於厥躬
有時乃日新之益矣蓋至是則由美而大而窮
神知化之地可馴至焉謂之大畜信其然乎大
抵天下之德必畜之大而後可以會其全畜德
之功必循其序而後可以造其極否則凌節不
遜者失之驟矣惡足以言畜德哉故夫子之行
不踰矩必自志學始而孟子之自得亦于深造
以道得之也後之君子欲從事于畜德之功者
punctuated: 取乎？蓋大畜之爲卦也，內體乾也，其德爲剛健；外體艮也，其德爲篤實輝光。惟其內之剛健，則天德之良不奪於攻取之私，而毅然者不失吾常；強立之德常伸於萬物之上，而浩然者適得吾體。天理爲主，人欲退聽矣。惟其外之篤實輝光，則庸行之謹允廸乎道義之正，而敦復足以自考；君子之光日著於踐履之餘，而昭明足以有融。闇然而章，誠不可揜矣。夫然則敬以直內，而義方於外者有本；利用安身，而致養於內者有資。學不病于一偏，而德自修于罔覺，有長裕不設之機矣；功已極於交致，而道自積於厥躬，有時乃日新之益矣。蓋至是則由美而大，而窮神知化之地可馴至焉。謂之大畜，信其然乎！大抵天下之德，必畜之大而後可以會其全；畜德之功，必循其序而後可以造其極。否則凌節不遜者失之驟矣，惡足以言畜德哉？故夫子之行不踰矩，必自志學始；而孟子之自得，亦于深造以道得之也。後之君子欲從事于畜德之功者，
translation_en:
…from what does it derive this meaning? In the hexagram Great Accumulation (Daxu), the inner trigram is Qian, whose virtue is strength and vigor; the outer trigram is Gen, whose virtue is solidity, sincerity, and radiance. Through its inward strength and vigor, the goodness of Heaven’s virtue is not wrested away by selfish desires to contend and acquire, and steadfast resolve preserves my constant nature. The virtue of standing firm continually rises above the myriad things, and its vastness accords precisely with my essential being. Heavenly principle presides, and human desires withdraw in submission. Through its outward solidity, sincerity, and radiance, care in everyday conduct truly follows the rectitude of the Way and righteousness, and wholehearted return to goodness suffices for self-examination. The gentleman’s radiance becomes daily more apparent through his conduct, and his luminous clarity suffices to shine forth. Unassuming yet manifest, his sincerity cannot be concealed.

Thus, reverence that straightens the inner self provides a foundation for righteousness that squares outward conduct; beneficial action that brings security to one’s person provides resources for inward nourishment. Learning does not suffer from one-sidedness, and virtue cultivates itself imperceptibly: herein lies the impetus for growth and abundance without contrivance. Effort reaches its fullest extent through the joint attainment of inward and outward cultivation, and the Way accumulates within one’s person: herein lies the benefit of daily renewal. At this point, one advances from beauty to greatness and may gradually reach the realm of fathoming the spiritual and understanding transformation. How truly apt it is to call this Great Accumulation!

In general, virtue must be accumulated abundantly before its entirety can be comprehended; the work of accumulating virtue must follow its proper sequence before its utmost height can be reached. Otherwise, those who skip stages and disregard the proper order err through haste. How could this count as accumulating virtue? Thus, the Master’s conduct that never overstepped the bounds necessarily began with setting his heart on learning. Likewise, Mengzi’s personal attainment came through advancing deeply by the proper Way. Gentlemen of later generations who wish to undertake the work of accumulating virtue…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
可不致審于内外交修之學哉
易與天地準故能彌綸天地之道
李際時
同考試官教諭林批易道之大子能真知而善言者可録
同考試官教諭蕭批易書盡天地之道是作能發易書之蘊
考試官教諭林批理順語新彌綸處尤見善講
考試官教授詹批論易與天地之道皆自胸中流出
大傳言易書之大而有以妙乎造化之道也夫
道莫大于天地而皆具于易書此易道之大所
===
以侔乎天地而聖人用之也與嘗謂易書未作
道在天地易書旣作道具易書是易者聖人載
道之器也吾嘗仰而觀之天以道而運于上故
言大者必歸焉而易之于天初无彼此之別也
吾嘗俯而察之地以道而奠于下故言大者必
歸焉而易之于地實有合一之妙也超乎形器
之外與上下而同其神運于陰陽之表兼俯仰
而一其類信乎惟天地爲大惟易書準之矣故
凡道之散見于兩間者若是乎不一也易則渾
punctuated:
可不致審于内外交修之學哉？

易與天地準，故能彌綸天地之道。
李際時

同考試官教諭林批：易道之大，子能真知而善言者，可録。
同考試官教諭蕭批：易書盡天地之道，是作能發易書之蘊。
考試官教諭林批：理順語新，彌綸處尤見善講。
考試官教授詹批：論易與天地之道，皆自胸中流出。

大傳言易書之大，而有以妙乎造化之道也。夫道莫大于天地，而皆具于易書，此易道之大所以侔乎天地，而聖人用之也與！嘗謂易書未作，道在天地；易書旣作，道具易書。是易者，聖人載道之器也。吾嘗仰而觀之，天以道而運于上，故言大者必歸焉，而易之于天，初无彼此之別也。吾嘗俯而察之，地以道而奠于下，故言大者必歸焉，而易之于地，實有合一之妙也。超乎形器之外，與上下而同其神；運于陰陽之表，兼俯仰而一其類。信乎惟天地爲大，惟易書準之矣。故凡道之散見于兩間者，若是乎不一也，易則渾
translation_en:
…can they fail to examine carefully the learning through which inward and outward cultivation advance together?

“The Changes accords with Heaven and Earth; hence it can encompass and give order to the Way of Heaven and Earth.”
By Li Jishi.

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “You truly understand the greatness of the Way of the Changes and express it well. This merits selection.”
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: “The Book of Changes fully comprehends the Way of Heaven and Earth. This composition brings out the profundities of the Book of Changes.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning flows smoothly and the language is fresh. The treatment of ‘encompass and give order’ particularly demonstrates skill in exposition.”
Examiner Zhan, Professor, comments: “The discussion of the Changes and the Way of Heaven and Earth flows entirely from the writer’s own understanding.”

The Great Commentary speaks of the greatness of the Book of Changes and its capacity to fathom the wondrous workings of the Way of creation and transformation. Now, nowhere is the Way greater than in Heaven and Earth, yet it is wholly contained in the Book of Changes. Is this not why the greatness of the Way of the Changes matches Heaven and Earth, and why the sages employ it? It has been said that before the Book of Changes was composed, the Way resided in Heaven and Earth; once the Book of Changes was composed, the Way was fully contained within it. Thus the Changes is the vessel in which the sages embodied the Way.

I have looked upward and observed: Heaven moves above through the Way. Thus those who speak of greatness must turn to it; yet between the Changes and Heaven there has never been any distinction of this and that. I have looked downward and examined: Earth is established below through the Way. Thus those who speak of greatness must turn to it; yet between the Changes and Earth there is indeed a wondrous unity. Transcending physical forms and concrete things, it shares the spiritual efficacy of what is above and below; operating beyond yin and yang, it embraces what is seen looking down and looking up, uniting them in one kind. Truly, Heaven and Earth alone are great, and the Book of Changes alone accords with them. Thus the manifestations of the Way scattered throughout the space between Heaven and Earth are so manifold, while the Changes gathers them into a whole…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曰俞咨伯汝作秩宗夙夜惟寅直哉惟清
伯拜稽首讓于夔龍帝曰俞往欽哉
陶曾
同考試官教諭馬批虞廷慎重典禮之意發明殆盡作
為程式之文錄之
考試官教諭林批寅直意講得透徹取之
考試官教授詹批此作詞既清雅氣亦充暢深得帝
舜命官典禮之意宜為多士式
聖君求禮官得人而命之因讓而申飭之也夫
===
典禮貴得人也觀聖君所以命夷者不亦慎且
專耶昔舜重禮官之選而咨于四岳謂夫人
之道莫急於禮而禮莫重於祭是故三禮也者
所以備郊社之義而修孝享之誠也惟賢者達
其情亦惟賢者能其事汝諸臣有能典朕三禮
者乎于是僉協廷論之公而以伯夷對蓋諒其
足以膺帝之命也此固素履之孚者故帝然其
舉而咨伯曰汝作秩宗而以禮神為職其知交
神之道乎夫交神之道格之以心而已汝其致
punctuated:
曰：「俞！咨，伯，汝作秩宗，夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。」伯拜稽首，讓于夔、龍。帝曰：「俞！往，欽哉！」
陶曾
同考試官教諭馬批：「虞廷慎重典禮之意，發明殆盡。作為程式之文，錄之。」
考試官教諭林批：「寅直意講得透徹，取之。」
考試官教授詹批：「此作詞既清雅，氣亦充暢，深得帝舜命官典禮之意，宜為多士式。」
聖君求禮官，得人而命之，因讓而申飭之也。夫典禮貴得人也，觀聖君所以命夷者，不亦慎且專耶？昔舜重禮官之選，而咨于四岳，謂夫人之道莫急於禮，而禮莫重於祭。是故三禮也者，所以備郊社之義，而修孝享之誠也。惟賢者達其情，亦惟賢者能其事。「汝諸臣有能典朕三禮者乎？」于是僉協廷論之公，而以伯夷對，蓋諒其足以膺帝之命也。此固素履之孚者，故帝然其舉，而咨伯曰：「汝作秩宗，而以禮神為職，其知交神之道乎？夫交神之道，格之以心而已。汝其致
translation_en:
…said: “Yes! Ah, Bo, you shall serve as Director of the Ancestral Temple. Morning and night be reverent; be upright and pure.” Bo bowed and knocked his head to the ground, declining in favor of Kui and Long. The emperor said: “Yes! Go, and be reverent!”
Tao Zeng
Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: “The intention of the court of Shun to treat ritual administration with the utmost care is elucidated almost exhaustively. This is writing that can serve as a model; include it in the record.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of reverence and uprightness is explained thoroughly. Accept it.”
Examiner Zhan, Professor, comments: “The diction of this composition is pure and elegant, and its vital force is full and fluent. It profoundly grasps Emperor Shun’s intention in appointing an official to administer the rites. It should serve as a model for the many scholars.”
The sage ruler sought an official for the rites; having found the right man, he appointed him, and when that man declined, he reiterated his admonition. In administering the rites, obtaining the right man is paramount. If we consider how the sage ruler appointed Yi, was he not both circumspect and single-minded? In former times, Shun attached great importance to choosing an official for the rites and consulted the Four Mountains. He held that, in the human Way, nothing was more pressing than ritual, and that within ritual nothing was weightier than sacrifice. Thus the three rites fulfill the obligations of the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and cultivate the sincerity of filial offerings to the ancestors. Only a worthy man comprehends their underlying sentiments, and only a worthy man can carry out their duties. “Among you, my ministers, is there anyone capable of administering my three rites?” Thereupon, all concurred in the impartial judgment of the court and named Bo Yi in reply, trusting that he was fully capable of receiving the emperor’s charge. This confidence rested upon his established conduct. The emperor therefore approved their recommendation and addressed Bo: “You shall serve as Director of the Ancestral Temple, taking the ritual service of the spirits as your duty. Do you understand the way to commune with the spirits? The way to commune with the spirits consists simply in reaching them through the heart. You should bring to bear…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
嚴於夙夜而亹亹乎善事吾心務祗肅之匪懈
操存於念慮而惺惺乎敬以直內使私曲之弗
萌則其心無物欲之汚自有得乎靜虚之體而
精明之德已豫孚於對越之先矣寧不可以事
神乎哉既而夷致拜稽之敬而讓於夔龍蓋慮
己不足以堪帝之命也然夔龍匪優於夷者故
帝雖然之而復飭之曰秩宗之命朕方嚴於汝
而汝可遜諸人乎況廷論有歸勿之廢焉爾矣
汝其往涖厥職而寅直之語奉之以周旋慎乃
===
攸司而主敬之心勿忘於夙夜庶百神爲之受
職三禮不爲虚文而民心以同治道於是乎出
矣其無替朕命也哉噫帝之委重乎夷亦至矣
抑于是見任選之嚴焉見荐揚之公焉見推讓
之和焉見簡畀之專焉夫咨四岳嚴也舉伯夷
公也讓夔龍和也不聽其讓專也一事而衆美
咸備此禮官所以得其人也厥后伯夷降典並
禹稷而成殷民之功有以哉
文王惟克厥宅心乃克立兹常事司牧人
punctuated:
嚴於夙夜，而亹亹乎善事吾心，務祗肅之匪懈；操存於念慮，而惺惺乎敬以直內，使私曲之弗萌。則其心無物欲之汚，自有得乎靜虚之體，而精明之德已豫孚於對越之先矣，寧不可以事神乎哉？既而夷致拜稽之敬，而讓於夔龍，蓋慮己不足以堪帝之命也。然夔龍匪優於夷者，故帝雖然之，而復飭之曰：「秩宗之命，朕方嚴於汝，而汝可遜諸人乎？況廷論有歸，勿之廢焉爾矣。汝其往涖厥職，而寅直之語，奉之以周旋；慎乃攸司，而主敬之心，勿忘於夙夜。庶百神爲之受職，三禮不爲虚文，而民心以同，治道於是乎出矣。其無替朕命也哉！」噫！帝之委重乎夷，亦至矣。抑于是見任選之嚴焉，見荐揚之公焉，見推讓之和焉，見簡畀之專焉。夫咨四岳，嚴也；舉伯夷，公也；讓夔龍，和也；不聽其讓，專也。一事而衆美咸備，此禮官所以得其人也。厥后伯夷降典，並禹稷而成殷民之功，有以哉！

文王惟克厥宅心，乃克立兹常事司牧人。
translation_en:
…be earnest day and night, tirelessly tending your own heart and striving never to slacken in reverent solemnity. Preserve it amid your thoughts, remaining alert and using reverence to make the inner self upright, so that selfishness and perversity do not arise. Then your heart will be free from the pollution of material desires, naturally attaining the substance of stillness and emptiness; its lucid virtue will already have established communion with the spirits before you stand before them. Could you then fail to serve the spirits?

Thereupon, Yi respectfully bowed and knocked his head to the ground, yielding the appointment to Kui and Long, presumably fearing that he himself was unequal to the Emperor’s charge. Yet Kui and Long were not superior to Yi. Thus, although the Emperor approved his gesture, he admonished him once more: “I am solemnly entrusting you with the appointment of Minister of Rites; how can you yield it to others? Moreover, the court’s deliberations have reached agreement: simply do not set their decision aside. Go and assume your office, taking the words ‘reverence and uprightness’ as your guide in all your conduct. Attend carefully to your responsibilities, and never, day or night, forget to make reverence the master of your heart. Then may the hundred spirits each receive their appointed functions, the three rites cease to be empty forms, and the people’s hearts be united. From this the way of good government will emerge. Do not neglect my command!”

Ah! The Emperor went to the utmost in entrusting weighty responsibility to Yi. Here we see rigor in selection for office, impartiality in recommendation, harmony in yielding to others, and singleness of purpose in choosing and appointing. Consulting the Four Mountains showed rigor; recommending Bo Yi showed impartiality; yielding to Kui and Long showed harmony; refusing to accept his yielding showed singleness of purpose. Every excellence was present in this one affair: this is how the right man was obtained for the ritual office. There was good reason why Bo Yi later promulgated the statutes and, alongside Yu and Ji, accomplished the work of enriching the people!

It was only because King Wen could settle his heart that he could appoint these regular officers to shepherd the people…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以克俊有德
周希正
同考試官教諭馬批善發文王知人得人之旨結復歸
重純心尤爲有見
考試官教諭林批周公告成王法祖用人意子能言之
考試官教授詹批知至信篤意發明無遺且文理瑩
粹子亦宅俊之賢者允宜高薦
聖君於三宅惟其知而信之故能用得其人也
蓋知之至信之篤則用無弗當者矣此聖君所
===
以爲知恤歟周公告成王若曰建官爲治之要
也三宅百官之表也苟得其人則用使皆吉人
矣文王於三宅何如哉蓋寧卽其行事觀其用
心而於精神心術之微真有以洞察而無眩相
知以心相得以道而於聚精會神之日直與之
孚契而弗疑不徒謀諸面也而究極其底蘊之
精是能獨觀其深而明哲之用有真知也不徒
信以迹也而起信於中孚之吉是能深諒其德
而忱恂之及皆至誠也所謂惟克厥宅心如此
punctuated:
以克俊有德。
周希正。
同考試官教諭馬批：善發文王知人得人之旨，結復歸重純心，尤爲有見。
考試官教諭林批：周公告成王法祖用人意，子能言之。
考試官教授詹批：知至信篤意，發明無遺，且文理瑩粹，子亦宅俊之賢者，允宜高薦。
聖君於三宅，惟其知而信之，故能用得其人也。蓋知之至，信之篤，則用無弗當者矣。此聖君所以爲知恤歟？周公告成王若曰：「建官，爲治之要也；三宅，百官之表也。苟得其人，則用使皆吉人矣。文王於三宅何如哉？蓋寧卽其行事觀其用心，而於精神心術之微，真有以洞察而無眩；相知以心，相得以道，而於聚精會神之日，直與之孚契而弗疑。不徒謀諸面也，而究極其底蘊之精，是能獨觀其深，而明哲之用有真知也；不徒信以迹也，而起信於中孚之吉，是能深諒其德，而忱恂之及皆至誠也。所謂惟克厥宅心如此，
translation_en:
…so as to select outstanding men possessed of virtue.

Zhou Xizheng.

Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor: You ably elucidate how King Wen understood men and obtained the right men for office. Your conclusion returns the emphasis to purity of heart, showing particular insight.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: You have expressed the Duke of Zhou’s intention in advising King Cheng to follow his ancestor’s example in employing men.

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: You fully elucidate the meaning of complete understanding and steadfast trust, leaving nothing unexplained. Moreover, the reasoning and composition are lucid and refined. You too are a worthy man fit for appointment among the outstanding; you certainly deserve a high recommendation.

In making the three appointments, the sage ruler understood and trusted the men concerned, and thus secured the right men for service. For when understanding is complete and trust steadfast, no appointment will be inappropriate. Is this what enabled the sage ruler to understand where his concern should lie? The Duke of Zhou’s advice to King Cheng was as if to say: “Establishing offices is essential to government; the three appointments provide models for all officials. If the right men are obtained, those employed in service will all be good men. How did King Wen approach the three appointments? Rather, by considering their conduct, he observed the workings of their hearts; he truly penetrated the subtleties of their spirit and inner dispositions without being misled. They understood one another through their hearts and found accord through the Way. When their concentrated spirits met, he was in direct, trusting accord with them, free of doubt. He did not merely judge them by their outward appearance, but explored the very essence of their innermost qualities. Thus he alone could perceive their depths, and his exercise of discerning wisdom rested on true knowledge. He did not merely trust them on the evidence of outward deeds, but grounded his trust in the auspiciousness of inner sincerity. Thus he could deeply appreciate their virtue, and the confidence he extended to them was entirely sincere. Such was the meaning of ‘he was able to settle their hearts’…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而用之有不得其人乎蓋惟其知之至也既足
爲選用之地而信之篤也又極其簡在之專故
能度德定位而立爲常事者用得乎一時之俊
彦而卓乎爲有德之人以德詔爵而用爲常伯
者克致乎俊乂之在官而藹乎爲常德之士天
事之理天民之托凡所以相修和之治者非三
德之宣則六德之嚴也夫孰非德稱其位者乎
以之任事以之牧民凡所以弼咸和之化者非
純德之望則秉德之良也又焉有位浮其德者
===
乎是皆用得其人而準人可類見矣我文王知
恤而興夫豈偶哉抑文之知恤亦以純心爲之
地耳詩人頌文王曰緝熈敬止又曰文王之德
之純言純心也夫純則一一則公公則明明且
公而知人善任固其所矣易𤾉之言曰純心要
矣用賢急焉文王蓋兼有之
詩
昭兹來許繩其祖武於萬斯年受天之祜
受天之祜四方來賀於萬斯年不遐有佐
punctuated:
而用之有不得其人乎？蓋惟其知之至也，既足爲選用之地；而信之篤也，又極其簡在之專。故能度德定位，而立爲常事者，用得乎一時之俊彦，而卓乎爲有德之人；以德詔爵，而用爲常伯者，克致乎俊乂之在官，而藹乎爲常德之士。天事之理，天民之托，凡所以相修和之治者，非三德之宣，則六德之嚴也。夫孰非德稱其位者乎？以之任事，以之牧民，凡所以弼咸和之化者，非純德之望，則秉德之良也。又焉有位浮其德者乎？是皆用得其人，而準人可類見矣。我文王知恤而興，夫豈偶哉？抑文之知恤，亦以純心爲之地耳。詩人頌文王曰：「緝熈敬止。」又曰：「文王之德之純。」言純心也。夫純則一，一則公，公則明。明且公，而知人善任，固其所矣。易𤾉之言曰：「純心要矣，用賢急焉。」文王蓋兼有之。

詩
昭兹來許，繩其祖武。於萬斯年，受天之祜。受天之祜，四方來賀。於萬斯年，不遐有佐？
translation_en:
…and in employing them, could he fail to obtain the right men? His understanding of them was so complete that it provided a sufficient basis for selecting and appointing them; his trust was so firm that his choice of them was wholly assured. Thus, when he assessed virtue, assigned positions, and appointed regular administrators, he employed the outstanding talents of his age, men distinguished by their virtue. When he conferred rank according to virtue and appointed chief officers, he brought accomplished and capable men into office, an abundant company of men of constant virtue. In managing Heaven’s affairs and caring for Heaven’s people entrusted to them, all who assisted in establishing harmonious government either manifested the three virtues or held rigorously to the six virtues. Whose virtue did not match his position? Whether entrusted with affairs or charged with governing the people, all who assisted in bringing about universal harmony were either esteemed for pure virtue or worthy men who upheld virtue. How could any hold a position exceeding his virtue? In all these appointments he obtained the right men; from these examples one can also infer the character of those who served as standards for others. Our King Wen understood what should concern him and thereby rose to greatness: could this have been accidental?

Yet King Wen’s understanding of what should concern him likewise rested upon purity of heart. The poet praised King Wen, saying, “Continuously bright, he abided in reverence,” and again, “The purity of King Wen’s virtue.” These words speak of purity of heart. Purity brings singleness of purpose; singleness brings impartiality; impartiality brings discernment. Being discerning and impartial, he naturally understood men and employed them well. Yi [?] said, “Purity of heart is essential; employing worthy men is urgent.” King Wen possessed both.

Book of Odes

Illustrious are these successors,
Following the footsteps of their ancestors.
For ten thousand years,
May they receive Heaven’s blessing.
Receiving Heaven’s blessing,
They are congratulated by all four quarters.
For ten thousand years,
Will they not have helpers?

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
趙恂
同考試官教諭聞批脩詞純整說理詳明盖有志於光
裕之孝者
同考試官教諭江批此作能得詩人本意說天人處尤
明暢善學詩者矣
考試官教諭林批此篇簡而備純而切誦之而有餘
味錄之可傳
考試官教授詹批措辭清簡不失經旨是善言創守
者可取
===
詩人賛聖孝之著而因推其垂裕之遠焉甚矣
聖人之孝通于天下也繼其道而天人交與不
亦垂裕之遠哉是詩美武王作也至此若曰德
之未至者固不足以成可大之業則亦不足以
垂可久之休惟我武王孝思之至孚于萬邦順
德之應光于四海其道之昭明也有如此吾知
創守一道前之所詒後之所承也誠使為之來
世者率乃攸行而繼序之不忘監于成憲而率
履之不越世德之所在夫固天命之所歸而祿
punctuated:
趙恂

同考試官教諭聞批：脩詞純整，說理詳明，盖有志於光裕之孝者。
同考試官教諭江批：此作能得詩人本意，說天人處尤明暢，善學詩者矣。
考試官教諭林批：此篇簡而備，純而切，誦之而有餘味，錄之可傳。
考試官教授詹批：措辭清簡，不失經旨，是善言創守者，可取。

詩人賛聖孝之著，而因推其垂裕之遠焉。甚矣，聖人之孝通于天下也！繼其道而天人交與，不亦垂裕之遠哉？是詩，美武王作也。至此若曰：德之未至者，固不足以成可大之業，則亦不足以垂可久之休。惟我武王，孝思之至，孚于萬邦；順德之應，光于四海。其道之昭明也有如此。吾知創守一道，前之所詒，後之所承也。誠使為之來世者，率乃攸行而繼序之不忘，監于成憲而率履之不越，世德之所在，夫固天命之所歸，而祿
translation_en:
Zhao Xun 趙恂

Associate Examiner Wen, an Instructor, comments: “The diction is pure and well ordered, and the exposition of principle detailed and clear. The author evidently aspires to the filial piety that brings glory to his forebears and leaves abundance to his descendants.”
Associate Examiner Jiang, an Instructor, comments: “This composition grasps the poet’s original intent. Its discussion of Heaven and humanity is especially clear and fluent. Here is someone skilled in studying the Poetry.”
Examiner Lin, an Instructor, comments: “This essay is concise yet comprehensive, pure yet pertinent. Reciting it leaves a lingering savor; it merits recording and transmission.”
Examiner Zhan, a Professor, comments: “The phrasing is lucid and concise and remains faithful to the meaning of the Classic. It discusses well the founding and preservation of a royal enterprise and merits acceptance.”

The poet praises the manifest filial piety of the sage and proceeds to infer how far into the future his legacy of abundance will extend. How profound is the sage’s filial piety, which reaches throughout the realm! When his way is continued, Heaven and humanity alike give their support: does this not show how far that legacy extends? This poem was composed in praise of King Wu. At this point it seems to say: One whose virtue has not reached perfection is certainly incapable of accomplishing an enterprise that can become great, and is likewise incapable of bequeathing blessings that can long endure. Our King Wu alone, through the utmost sincerity of his filial devotion, won the trust of the myriad states; the response to his compliant virtue shone throughout the Four Seas. Such was the radiant clarity of his way. I know that founding and preserving an enterprise follow a single way: what predecessors bequeath is what successors inherit. If those of later generations truly follow the course he pursued, never forgetting to continue the succession, and take the established statutes as their model, never transgressing them in their conduct, then where hereditary virtue resides is assuredly where Heaven’s Mandate devolves, and emoluments…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
位名壽集之於大來之慶也豐亨豫泰引之於
優游之休也君德之無窮則天命亦無窮於萬
斯年殆不改夫于京之舊受天之祜寧有窮乎
夫旣受天之祜則天人一機天之所與人之所
歸也將見爲之諸侯者切朝宗之心冠裳於是
乎咸萃虔入覲之禮玉帛於此乎攸同人心之
所趨夫固多助之所至而疏附先後罔不輸沃
心之益也奔走禦侮咸願盡篤棐之忠也君德
之無窮則人心亦無窮於萬斯年殆不異夫媚
===
茲之日得人之助又可旣乎是何也武王之道
天命人心之本也不惟可法於天下而且可傳
於後世盛德大業亦至矣周之子孫惡得而不
繹思之抑觀中庸論武王周公之達孝曰善繼
人之志善述人之事至此詩所稱則又言武王
之孝光裕先後而道爲可傳焉是蓋能繼人之
志者故其志爲可繼能述人之事者故其事爲
可述也厥後明文昭定武烈成鳧鷖旣醉之太
平者論者以爲有所本信矣是故頌武王而稱
punctuated:
位名壽集之於大來之慶也，豐亨豫泰引之於優游之休也。君德之無窮，則天命亦無窮，於萬斯年，殆不改夫于京之舊，受天之祜，寧有窮乎？夫旣受天之祜，則天人一機，天之所與，人之所歸也。將見爲之諸侯者切朝宗之心，冠裳於是乎咸萃；虔入覲之禮，玉帛於此乎攸同。人心之所趨，夫固多助之所至，而疏附先後，罔不輸沃心之益也；奔走禦侮，咸願盡篤棐之忠也。君德之無窮，則人心亦無窮，於萬斯年，殆不異夫媚茲之日，得人之助，又可旣乎？是何也？武王之道，天命人心之本也，不惟可法於天下，而且可傳於後世，盛德大業亦至矣。周之子孫，惡得而不繹思之？
抑觀《中庸》論武王、周公之達孝曰：「善繼人之志，善述人之事。」至此詩所稱，則又言武王之孝光裕先後，而道爲可傳焉。是蓋能繼人之志者，故其志爲可繼；能述人之事者，故其事爲可述也。厥後明文昭，定武烈，成《鳧鷖》《旣醉》之太平者，論者以爲有所本，信矣。是故頌武王而稱
translation_en:
…rank, renown, and longevity gather in the auspicious advent of greatness; abundance, success, ease, and peace extend into the blessings of untroubled repose. If the ruler’s virtue is inexhaustible, Heaven’s mandate is likewise inexhaustible. For ten thousand years, things will surely remain as they were of old in the capital. Could the blessings received from Heaven ever end? When one receives Heaven’s blessings, Heaven and humanity act through a single impulse: those whom Heaven favors are those to whom the people turn. We shall see the feudal lords earnestly desiring to attend court, gathering there in their ceremonial caps and robes; reverently observing the rites of audience, they assemble there with jade and silk. Where the people’s hearts turn, abundant assistance naturally follows. Those who draw others close, those who attach themselves, those who lead, and those who follow all contribute counsel that enriches the ruler’s mind. Those who hasten to serve and those who ward off aggression all wish to devote their loyalty to steadfast support. If the ruler’s virtue is inexhaustible, the people’s allegiance is likewise inexhaustible. For ten thousand years, it will surely remain as it was in the days when he was beloved here. Could the assistance received from others ever cease? Why is this so? King Wu’s Way is the foundation of Heaven’s mandate and the people’s allegiance. It can serve as a model throughout the world and can also be transmitted to later generations. His abundant virtue and great achievements reached their utmost perfection. How could the descendants of Zhou fail to ponder them continually?
Furthermore, consider how the Doctrine of the Mean describes the universally acknowledged filial piety of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou: “They were skilled in carrying on others’ intentions and in continuing others’ undertakings.” What this poem celebrates goes further: King Wu’s filial piety brought glory and abundance to those before and after him, and his Way could be handed down. Precisely because he could carry on others’ intentions, his own intentions could be carried on; because he could continue others’ undertakings, his own undertakings could be continued. Later, his successors made manifest King Wen’s brilliance, secured King Wu’s achievements, and brought about the great peace depicted in “Wild Ducks and Gulls” (Fu yi) and “Already Drunk” (Ji zui). Those who discuss this hold that it had a foundation; truly this is so. Thus, in extolling King Wu and praising …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
成康之德不衰有以哉
四海來假來假祈祈景員維河殷受命咸
宜百祿是何
張翀
同考試官教諭聞批此題因見成湯世澤之遠亦重後
王能以武德繼湯故受命咸宜此為得之
同考試官教諭江批商家以世德相承故得人心土地
之盛而命祿因之此作發揮明備用錄以式
考試官教諭林批講以德字立意詞亦整明商家一
===
統之盛讀此可見矣
考試官教授詹批此篇說成湯遺後之德意極詳盡
真佳士也
商人祀先必言時王一統之盛而表其得天之
隆也夫人心萃而國勢尊王者大一統之盛也
則其受命之宜獲福之多不亦從可見乎此商
人所以播之於宗廟登歌也其意蓋謂一代王
業有開必先有承必後而世德世業夫固有相
因者矣我商今日之天下何如哉是故王者饗
punctuated:
成康之德不衰，有以哉！

四海來假，來假祈祈。景員維河，殷受命咸宜，百祿是何。

張翀

同考試官教諭聞批：此題因見成湯世澤之遠，亦重後王能以武德繼湯，故受命咸宜，此為得之。

同考試官教諭江批：商家以世德相承，故得人心土地之盛，而命祿因之。此作發揮明備，用錄以式。

考試官教諭林批：講以德字立意，詞亦整明。商家一統之盛，讀此可見矣。

考試官教授詹批：此篇說成湯遺後之德，意極詳盡，真佳士也。

商人祀先，必言時王一統之盛，而表其得天之隆也。夫人心萃而國勢尊，王者大一統之盛也，則其受命之宜、獲福之多，不亦從可見乎？此商人所以播之於宗廟登歌也。其意蓋謂一代王業，有開必先，有承必後，而世德世業，夫固有相因者矣。我商今日之天下何如哉？是故王者饗
translation_en:
…that the virtue of Cheng and Kang did not decline—there was good reason for this!

“From the Four Seas they come; they come in great multitudes. The vast domain extends to the Yellow River [?]. Yin received the Mandate in full fitness, bearing its hundred blessings.”

Zhang Chong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: This topic reveals the far-reaching beneficence that Cheng Tang transmitted through the generations. It also stresses that later kings could succeed Tang through martial virtue, and thus were fully fit to receive the Mandate. This essay grasps that meaning.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: The house of Shang transmitted its virtue from generation to generation. Thus it won the allegiance of the people and possessed extensive territory; the Mandate and blessings followed from these. This composition develops the theme clearly and fully. It is selected for inclusion as a model.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The exposition takes virtue as its central idea, and its language is orderly and clear. Reading this reveals the flourishing unity of the house of Shang.

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: This essay explains with great thoroughness the virtue Cheng Tang bequeathed to his descendants. Truly an excellent scholar!

When the people of Shang sacrificed to their ancestors, they invariably spoke of the flourishing unity achieved by the reigning king, thereby displaying the abundance of Heaven’s favor toward him. When the people’s hearts converge upon the ruler and the state stands exalted, this is the flourishing realization of a king’s great unity. Does this not also reveal his fitness to receive the Mandate and the abundance of the blessings he obtains? This is why the people of Shang proclaimed it in the songs sung in the hall of the ancestral temple. Their meaning was surely that, in the royal enterprise of a dynasty, those who inaugurate it must come first, and those who carry it forward must follow; virtue and achievement transmitted through the generations necessarily build upon one another. What, then, is the realm of our Shang like today? Thus, when the king offers a sacrificial feast…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
親而祀所以明有孝也而人心之萃渙恒於是
今焉龍旂之載有以奔走乎群工大禧之承有
以會同乎四海凡夫肅雝秉德以為有廟之假
者固已祈祈然其眾多矣夫王者宅中而治所以
明有尊也而國勢之盛衰恒於是今焉景山峙
於中有以會陰陽之交大河環於外有以據天
設之險則夫居重馭輕以為四方之極者固已
翼翼然其整飭矣夫以人心向往之同山河表
裏之固如此則受命不殆在殷之先后有以逢
===
其適世德重光在武丁孫子有以承其休曆數
膺而帝心簡在夫固履之不疚而質之不愧矣
其受命也不亦咸宜乎由是命之所集者畀之
福澤以厚其生天之所眷者錫之富有以大其
業百順聚而天休滋至夫固受之不匱而積之
不苑矣其荷百祿也不其信然乎是則即其統
治之盛見其得天之隆天人上下之間其機固
如此揆厥所由何莫非先后貽福之所及哉大
抵王者中天下而立有可傳之業必有可繼之
punctuated: 親而祀，所以明有孝也，而人心之萃渙恒於是。今焉龍旂之載，有以奔走乎群工；大禧之承，有以會同乎四海。凡夫肅雝秉德，以為有廟之假者，固已祈祈然其眾多矣。夫王者宅中而治，所以明有尊也，而國勢之盛衰恒於是。今焉景山峙於中，有以會陰陽之交；大河環於外，有以據天設之險。則夫居重馭輕，以為四方之極者，固已翼翼然其整飭矣。夫以人心向往之同、山河表裏之固如此，則受命不殆，在殷之先后有以逢其適；世德重光，在武丁孫子有以承其休。曆數膺而帝心簡在，夫固履之不疚而質之不愧矣。其受命也，不亦咸宜乎？由是命之所集者，畀之福澤以厚其生；天之所眷者，錫之富有以大其業。百順聚而天休滋至，夫固受之不匱而積之不苑矣。其荷百祿也，不其信然乎？是則即其統治之盛，見其得天之隆。天人上下之間，其機固如此。揆厥所由，何莫非先后貽福之所及哉？大抵王者中天下而立，有可傳之業，必有可繼之
translation_en:
…his ancestors and offers sacrifices, thereby manifesting his filial piety; the gathering or dispersal of the people’s allegiance always hinges upon this. Now the dragon banners are raised, bringing all the officers hastening to their duties; great blessings are received, bringing all within the Four Seas together. Those who approach the ancestral temple, reverent, harmonious, and holding fast to virtue, already form a vast multitude moving with solemn composure. The king resides at the center and governs, thereby manifesting his exalted position; the strength or weakness of the state always hinges upon this. Now Mount Jing rises in the center, where yin and yang converge; the great Yellow River encircles the outer territory, providing natural defenses established by Heaven. Thus the seat of central authority, controlling the subordinate regions and serving as the pole toward which the four quarters turn, is already solemnly ordered.

With the people so united in their allegiance, and mountains and rivers providing such security within and without, the mandate was received without peril: the former kings of Yin encountered the fitting moment. The virtue of successive generations shone anew: the descendants of Wu Ding inherited its blessings. Receiving the allotted succession to rule and being chosen in the heart of the Lord on High, they could indeed act without fault and submit themselves to examination without shame. Was it not entirely fitting that they received the mandate? Thus those upon whom the mandate rests are granted blessings to enrich their lives; those whom Heaven favors are bestowed wealth to enlarge their undertaking. Every favorable circumstance gathers, and Heaven’s blessings arrive in increasing abundance. Indeed, they receive them without exhaustion and accumulate them without decay [?]. Is it not truly so that they bear a hundred blessings?

Thus, in the flourishing of their unified rule, one sees the greatness of Heaven’s favor toward them. Such indeed is the working of the relationship between Heaven above and humanity below. If we examine its source, what part of it does not derive from the blessings bequeathed by the former kings? In general, when a king takes his place at the center of all under Heaven, if he has an undertaking that can be handed down, he must have something that can be carried on…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
德德盛而可繼業之傳也不亦遠哉商之天下
歷數世而人心土宇如故固湯之武德遺之也
遺之而不忘所遺則又存乎爲後者所繼承何
如耳讀詩者固當知先德之所遺又當知所以
不忘所遺者然後可
春秋
秦人伐晋〔文公三年〕晋侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
鍾徠秀
考試官教諭林批〔此題作者類多以王事常情分說〕
===
子獨歸善秦穆深得傳意可以爲式
考試官教授詹批〔讀此終篇不惟知秦穆之賢亦可〕
見聖人責備賢者與人改過之意宜錄之
春秋以王事望賢君因其貳過而責之備因其
改過而善之深蓋遷善補過王者之事觀秦晋
交伐而春秋之予奪秦穆者義可見矣秦抱取
汪彭衙之耻于是有伐晋之役胡以責秦君子
曰穆自殽函以來歸作誓言一念悔悟之明匪
曰自責如流者乎使其勇於改過不遠之復誰
punctuated:
德。德盛而可繼，業之傳也不亦遠哉？商之天下，歷數世而人心土宇如故，固湯之武德遺之也。遺之而不忘所遺，則又存乎爲後者所繼承何如耳。讀詩者，固當知先德之所遺，又當知所以不忘所遺者，然後可。
春秋
秦人伐晋〔文公三年〕，晋侯伐秦〔文公四年〕。
鍾徠秀
考試官教諭林批〔此題作者類多以王事常情分說〕子獨歸善秦穆，深得傳意，可以爲式。
考試官教授詹批〔讀此終篇不惟知秦穆之賢亦可〕見聖人責備賢者、與人改過之意，宜錄之。
春秋以王事望賢君，因其貳過而責之備，因其改過而善之深。蓋遷善補過，王者之事。觀秦晋交伐，而春秋之予奪秦穆者，義可見矣。秦抱取汪彭衙之耻，于是有伐晋之役。胡以責秦？君子曰：穆自殽函以來，歸作誓言，一念悔悟之明，匪曰自責如流者乎？使其勇於改過，不遠之復，誰
translation_en:
…virtue. When virtue is abundant and can be carried on, will not the inheritance of the enterprise endure far into the future? The Shang realm passed through several generations, yet the allegiance of the people and the extent of its territory remained as before. This was assuredly the legacy of Tang’s martial virtue. But whether those who receive a legacy remember what has been bequeathed depends upon how their successors carry it on. Readers of the Book of Odes must understand what the virtue of the forebears has bequeathed, and must also understand how that legacy is kept from being forgotten. Only then will their understanding suffice.
Spring and Autumn Annals
“The men of Qin attacked Jin.” 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕 “The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin.” 〔Fourth year of Duke Wen.〕
Zhong Laixiu
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔Most writers on this topic discuss separately the affairs of a true king and ordinary human feelings.〕 You alone accord praise to Duke Mu of Qin, profoundly grasping the commentary’s meaning. This may serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: 〔Reading this entire essay, one not only recognizes Duke Mu of Qin’s worthiness, but can also〕 perceive the Sage’s intention in demanding perfection of the worthy and approving people’s correction of their faults. It deserves to be recorded.
The Spring and Autumn Annals expects worthy rulers to conduct themselves as true kings. When they repeat their faults, it demands perfection of them; when they correct their faults, it praises them deeply. For turning toward goodness and making amends for faults are the affairs of a true king. By considering the reciprocal attacks of Qin and Jin, one can discern the principles behind the Spring and Autumn Annals’ praise and censure of Duke Mu of Qin. Qin harbored the humiliation of [an unclear reference: 取汪] and Pengya [?], and thus undertook its campaign against Jin. Why does it censure Qin? The gentleman says: After the events at Yao and Han, Duke Mu returned and composed his oath. In that flash of clear repentance, could he not be said to have reproached himself as freely as flowing water? Had he been courageous in correcting his faults and returned before straying far, who…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
能議之乃以為三戰三北吾辱矣濟河焚舟封
尸取邑必願比一洒然後快於心與忿不懲慾
不窒有如是者是其內訟之念不勝夫耻敗之
心前日之誓蓋靜言而庸則違矣曾是可以為
賢乎經於秦穆以人稱豈固微秦哉若曰文過
者庸人之事穆以賢者而亦為此其去庸人一
間耳於王事不已遠乎是故貶而稱人所以備
責之云晉懷取官及郊之憤于是有伐秦之師
胡以善秦君子曰穆自彭衙以來罔恤誓詞一
===
念逞忿之私匪曰責人無難者乎使其終於憚
改迷復之凶誰其與之乃以為構怨構兵吾過
矣攻我邠邑圍我新城固甘於直受不復尤而
效之也爭以息怨以遠有如是者是其令圖之
美足以蓋既往之愆前日之言始躬行而允蹈
之矣非賢而能若是乎經於晉襄以爵稱豈徒
恕晉哉若曰報怨者常人之情穆處無道而弗
報焉其視常人有間矣於王事不已近乎是故
不譏晉侯所以深善秦伯云明乎此則知聖人
punctuated:
能議之？乃以為：「三戰三北，吾辱矣。濟河焚舟，封尸取邑，必願比一洒，然後快於心與？」忿不懲，慾不窒，有如是者！是其內訟之念不勝夫耻敗之心，前日之誓，蓋靜言而庸則違矣。曾是可以為賢乎？經於秦穆以人稱，豈固微秦哉？若曰：「文過者，庸人之事。穆以賢者而亦為此，其去庸人一間耳，於王事不已遠乎？」是故貶而稱人，所以備責之云。
晉懷取官及郊之憤，于是有伐秦之師。胡以善秦？君子曰：「穆自彭衙以來，罔恤誓詞，一念逞忿之私，匪曰責人無難者乎？使其終於憚改，迷復之凶，誰其與之？乃以為：『構怨構兵，吾過矣。攻我邠邑，圍我新城，固甘於直受，不復尤而效之也。』爭以息，怨以遠，有如是者！是其令圖之美足以蓋既往之愆，前日之言，始躬行而允蹈之矣。非賢而能若是乎？經於晉襄以爵稱，豈徒恕晉哉？若曰：『報怨者，常人之情。穆處無道而弗報焉，其視常人有間矣，於王事不已近乎？』是故不譏晉侯，所以深善秦伯云。」明乎此，則知聖人
translation_en:
…who could have criticized him? Instead, he thought: “Three battles and three defeats: I have been humiliated. I shall cross the river and burn the boats, raise burial mounds over the dead, and seize towns. Must I not wash away this humiliation [?] before my heart can be satisfied?” Such was his failure to restrain anger and curb desire! His impulse to reproach himself could not overcome his shame at defeat. His earlier oath was thus something he spoke in repose but contradicted in practice. Could this possibly count as being worthy? When the Classic calls Lord Mu of Qin merely a “man,” is it simply belittling Qin? It is as though it says: “Concealing one’s faults is the business of an ordinary man. If Mu, though worthy, also does this, he stands only a little apart from an ordinary man. Is he not already far removed from the work of a true king?” Thus, demoting him by calling him a “man” serves to hold him fully accountable.
Jin harbored resentment over the capture of Guan [?] and the attack on its outskirts, and consequently sent an army against Qin. Why, then, is Qin praised? The gentleman says: “Since Pengya, Mu had disregarded the words of his oath, his thoughts bent selfishly on venting his anger. Was he not what is meant by one who finds it easy to blame others? Had he persisted in fearing to reform, bringing upon himself the misfortune of losing the way back, who would have approved of him? Instead, he thought: ‘Stirring up enmity and warfare was my fault. They attack our town of Bin and besiege our Xincheng; I willingly accept this outright and shall no longer blame them and imitate their actions.’ Such was his success in ending contention and putting enmity behind him! The excellence of his good resolve was sufficient to cover his past transgressions. Only now did he personally put his earlier words into practice and faithfully fulfill them. Could anyone but a worthy man act thus? When the Classic refers to Lord Xiang of Jin by his noble rank, is it merely excusing Jin? It is as though it says: ‘Repaying resentment is the natural feeling of ordinary men. Mu suffers unjust treatment yet does not retaliate. He stands apart from ordinary men. Is he not already close to the work of a true king?’ Thus, withholding censure from the Marquis of Jin serves to express profound approval of the Earl of Qin.” Understanding this, one recognizes that the Sage…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
所以待秦晉者大改過嘉釋怨樂與人爲善之
意深矣抑仲虺之誥唯曰改過吉甫之詩唯曰
補闕商湯周宣固由此其選乎秦誓之詞蓋庶
幾焉所以列于百篇之末也惜乎賤勇夫貴良
士惡娼疾思彥聖徒托空言而孟明子桑無能
將順此秦穆所以僅霸西戎君子不能無遺憾
焉
夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷齊人
來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔俱定公十年〕叔孫州仇
===
帥師墮郈季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費
〔俱定公十有二年〕
胡希旦
考試官教諭林批〔曲盡孔子神化之妙非邃於經學者不能及此〕
考試官教授詹批〔聖人以禮行于齊魯俄頃之化未易形容此能發明之而歸重於禮是善作者可以薦矣〕
春秋紀望國外服內順之事見聖化之大行也
夫聖人者存神而過化者也齊服而侵地歸三
punctuated:
所以待秦晉者，大改過，嘉釋怨，樂與人爲善之意深矣。抑《仲虺之誥》唯曰改過，吉甫之詩唯曰補闕，商湯、周宣固由此其選乎？《秦誓》之詞蓋庶幾焉，所以列于百篇之末也。惜乎賤勇夫、貴良士，惡娼疾、思彥聖，徒托空言，而孟明、子桑無能將順。此秦穆所以僅霸西戎，君子不能無遺憾焉。
夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔俱定公十年〕叔孫州仇帥師墮郈。季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。〔俱定公十有二年〕
胡希旦
考試官教諭林批〔曲盡孔子神化之妙，非邃於經學者不能及此。〕
考試官教授詹批〔聖人以禮行于齊魯，俄頃之化，未易形容。此能發明之，而歸重於禮，是善作者，可以薦矣。〕
《春秋》紀望國外服內順之事，見聖化之大行也。夫聖人者，存神而過化者也。齊服而侵地歸，三
translation_en:
…In his treatment of Qin and Jin, he greatly esteems the correction of faults and commends the relinquishment of resentment: profound indeed is his desire to help others do good. Moreover, the Announcement of Zhonghui speaks simply of correcting faults, and Jifu’s ode simply of remedying deficiencies. Surely it was through these that Tang of Shang and King Xuan of Zhou became outstanding? The language of the Oath of Qin comes close to this, which is why it is placed at the end of the hundred chapters of the Book of Documents. Regrettably, disparaging warriors and esteeming worthy men, abhorring “chang ji” [?] and longing for men of excellence and sagely wisdom remained mere empty words; neither Mengming nor Zisang could help him carry these intentions through. This is why Duke Mu of Qin achieved hegemony only over the Western Rong. The gentleman cannot but feel lingering regret.
“In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. The men of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” 〔All from the tenth year of Duke Ding.〕 “Shusun Zhouchou led an army to demolish Hou. Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army to demolish Fei.” 〔Both from the twelfth year of Duke Ding.〕
Hu Xidan
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔This fully captures the subtle marvel of Confucius’s spiritual transformation. No one without profound learning in the Classics could attain this.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: 〔The sage acted through ritual propriety in Qi and Lu. The transformation he brought about in an instant is not easy to describe. This essay elucidates it and assigns the chief importance to ritual propriety. Its author writes well and may be recommended.〕
The Spring and Autumn Annals records how a distinguished state secured submission abroad and obedience at home, revealing the far-reaching operation of the sage’s transforming influence. For the sage preserves spiritual efficacy within himself and transforms wherever he passes. Qi submitted and returned the lands it had seized; the three…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
家順而私邑毀其感化之機一何妙哉且魯本
周公之後世稱秉禮之邦定公嗣守日益弗競
以言乎敵國外患則有齊焉自楊州門廩丘攻
齊固甘心於魯者兩國之平未幾夾谷之會途
講時則犁彌以謀獻萊夷以兵逞乃齊人復以
享行震于其躬魯幾不測矣幸有孔子相君於
會歷階而升談笑而卻曰干盟偪好曰不祥愆
義其詞嚴而義則正者于是齊君愧於古道齊
臣引以謝過鄆讙龜陰之田章章然咸來歸焉
===
由以禮責齊而齊化也不然彼以覇國餘業華
車使從夫固脅持之術胡遽心服若此哉非所
謂一言而威重於三軍者乎故書會書來歸雖
疑於自序其績不以為嫌也以言乎越禮內叛
則有三家焉自世卿專郈費城三家固厲階於
魯者侯犯之叛未幾狃叛之謀益險時則費人
逞其奸家隸擬其後雖三卿亦不能制末大必
折魯幾不免矣幸而孔子為政於國明以禮制
諭以忠貞曰家藏甲兵曰邑固城池其名正而
punctuated:
家順而私邑毀，其感化之機一何妙哉！且魯本周公之後，世稱秉禮之邦。定公嗣守，日益弗競。以言乎敵國外患，則有齊焉。自楊州門廩丘攻，齊固甘心於魯者。兩國之平未幾，夾谷之會途講，時則犁彌以謀獻，萊夷以兵逞，乃齊人復以享行，震于其躬，魯幾不測矣！幸有孔子相君於會，歷階而升，談笑而卻，曰干盟偪好，曰不祥愆義。其詞嚴而義則正者，于是齊君愧於古道，齊臣引以謝過，鄆、讙、龜陰之田章章然咸來歸焉。由以禮責齊而齊化也。不然，彼以覇國餘業，華車使從，夫固脅持之術，胡遽心服若此哉？非所謂一言而威重於三軍者乎？故書會，書來歸，雖疑於自序其績，不以為嫌也。
以言乎越禮內叛，則有三家焉。自世卿專郈費城，三家固厲階於魯者。侯犯之叛未幾，狃叛之謀益險。時則費人逞其奸，家隸擬其後，雖三卿亦不能制。末大必折，魯幾不免矣！幸而孔子為政於國，明以禮制，諭以忠貞，曰家藏甲兵，曰邑固城池，其名正而
translation_en:
…the three houses submitted, and their private fortified towns were demolished. How wondrous was the working of his transforming influence! Lu was originally the domain of the Duke of Zhou’s descendants, renowned through the generations as a state that upheld ritual propriety. After Duke Ding succeeded to its rule, it grew weaker by the day. As for hostile states and external dangers, there was Qi. From the fighting at Yangzhou Gate and Linqiu [?], Qi had been intent on having its way with Lu. Not long after peace was established between the two states, the meeting at Jiagu was arranged [?]. Li Mi then offered his stratagem, and the Lai tribesmen brandished their weapons. The men of Qi further proposed holding a ceremonial feast, threatening the duke in person; Lu nearly suffered an unforeseen disaster. Fortunately, Confucius assisted his ruler at the meeting. He ascended the steps and, speaking with composure, repelled them. He declared that this violated their covenant and put coercion upon their friendly relations, that it was inauspicious and transgressed righteousness. His words were stern and his principles correct. Thus the ruler of Qi felt shame before the ancient Way, and Qi’s ministers acknowledged their fault and apologized. The lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin were all duly returned. This was because Confucius called Qi to account through ritual propriety, and Qi was transformed. Otherwise, with the surviving power of a hegemonic state and splendid carriages and accompanying attendants [?]—all instruments of coercion—why should Qi so suddenly have submitted wholeheartedly? Was this not what is meant by a single utterance carrying greater authority than the three armies? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals records the meeting and records the return of the lands. Although this might seem like Confucius recounting his own achievements, he did not regard that as grounds for avoiding it.
As for breaches of ritual propriety and internal rebellion, there were the three houses. With hereditary ministers monopolizing power and fortifying Hou and Fei, the three houses had become a source of calamity for Lu. Not long after Hou Fan’s rebellion, Niu’s plans for rebellion grew still more dangerous. The men of Fei pursued their treachery, while household retainers contemplated following their example. Even the three chief ministers could not control them. When the branches grow too large, the trunk must break: Lu nearly failed to escape disaster. Fortunately, Confucius held office in the state. He clarified the institutions of ritual propriety and instructed them in loyalty and steadfastness, speaking of armor and weapons stored in ministerial households and of towns secured with walls and moats. His formulation of the issues was correct, and…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
顏淵季路侍子曰盍各言爾志子路曰願
車馬衣輕裘與朋友共敝之而無憾顏
淵曰願無伐善無施勞子路曰願聞子
之志子曰老者安之朋友信之少者懷
之
上天之載無聲無臭至矣
至於心獨無所同然乎心之所同然者何
===
也謂理也義也聖人先得我心之所同
然耳
易
彖曰大畜剛健篤實輝光日新其德
受玆介福以中正也
易與天地準故能彌綸天地之道
復德之本也恒德之固也
書
帝曰咨四岳有能典朕三禮僉曰伯夷帝
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

顏淵、季路侍。子曰：「盍各言爾志？」子路曰：「願車馬衣輕裘，與朋友共，敝之而無憾。」顏淵曰：「願無伐善，無施勞。」子路曰：「願聞子之志。」子曰：「老者安之，朋友信之，少者懷之。」

上天之載，無聲無臭，至矣！

至於心，獨無所同然乎？心之所同然者何也？謂理也，義也。聖人先得我心之所同然耳。

易

彖曰：「大畜，剛健篤實，輝光日新其德。」

受玆介福，以中正也。

易與天地準，故能彌綸天地之道。

復，德之本也；恒，德之固也。

書

帝曰：「咨！四岳，有能典朕三禮？」僉曰：「伯夷。」帝
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Yan Yuan and Jilu were attending upon the Master. The Master said, “Why does each of you not state his aspirations?” Zilu said, “I wish to share my carriages, horses, and light fur robes with my friends, and to feel no regret even if they wear them out.” Yan Yuan said, “I wish neither to boast of my goodness nor to make a display of my services.” Zilu said, “We should like to hear your aspirations, Master.” The Master said, “To give the aged peace, to be trustworthy toward friends, and to cherish the young.”

“The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” This is perfection indeed!

As for the heart, is it alone without anything that all hearts acknowledge alike? What is it that all hearts acknowledge alike? It is principle and righteousness. The sage has merely apprehended before us what our hearts all acknowledge alike.

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Judgments says: “Great Accumulation: firm and vigorous, substantial and true, with radiance and brilliance, daily renewing its virtue.”

“He receives this great blessing” because he is central and correct.

The Changes accords with Heaven and Earth; thus it can encompass and give ordered expression to the Way of Heaven and Earth.

Return is the root of virtue; Constancy is the firmness of virtue.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬物得其理而後和又曰禮先樂後然則禮樂
之用爲急而推行之序又有所自始云
忠臣以事其君孝子以事其親其本一也
唐文迪
同考試官學正吳批忠孝本一意甚難發揮此作獨明
白順暢是學禮有得者也
考試官敎諭林批善道忠孝自盡之意
考試官敎授詹批即忠孝說出備義甚悉觀子之
文他日所樹立者可知矣勉之
===
觀賢者之敬於所事同於內盡其心也夫忠以
事君孝以事親臣子之道殊矣而內盡之心要
之無不同焉備之爲義端可識矣記祭統者意
謂賢者之能祭本於能備即其內盡外順而所
謂備者見矣是故賢者在國自事君言之有臣
道焉而忠其所先也今觀其事君也靖共爾位
利害休戚舉切于其心篤棐厥辟腹心手足若
爲之一體責難而弼唐虞之治恭之大也居安
而陳盛滿之戒慮之遠也是其所以忠于君者
punctuated:
萬物得其理而後和。又曰：「禮先樂後。」然則禮樂之用爲急，而推行之序又有所自始云。

忠臣以事其君，孝子以事其親，其本一也。
唐文迪
同考試官學正吳批：「忠孝本一意甚難發揮，此作獨明白順暢，是學禮有得者也。」
考試官敎諭林批：「善道忠孝自盡之意。」
考試官敎授詹批：「即忠孝說出備義甚悉。觀子之文，他日所樹立者可知矣。勉之！」

觀賢者之敬於所事，同於內盡其心也。夫忠以事君，孝以事親，臣子之道殊矣，而內盡之心，要之無不同焉。備之爲義，端可識矣。記祭統者意謂賢者之能祭，本於能備，即其內盡外順而所謂備者見矣。是故賢者在國，自事君言之，有臣道焉，而忠其所先也。今觀其事君也，靖共爾位，利害休戚舉切于其心；篤棐厥辟，腹心手足若爲之一體。責難而弼唐虞之治，恭之大也；居安而陳盛滿之戒，慮之遠也。是其所以忠于君者
translation_en:
…Only after all things attain their proper order is there harmony. It is also said: “Ritual comes first, music afterward.” Thus, putting ritual and music into practice is urgent, yet the sequence of their implementation has its own starting point.

“The loyal minister thereby serves his ruler, and the filial son thereby serves his parents: their foundation is one.”
Tang Wendi

Associate Examiner Wu, School Instructor, comments: “The idea that loyalty and filial piety share one foundation is very difficult to expound. This composition is exceptionally clear and fluent; its author has gained an understanding through studying ritual.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “He ably expresses the idea of giving oneself fully through loyalty and filial piety.”
Examiner Zhan, Professor, comments: “Through loyalty and filial piety, he explains the meaning of completeness in great detail. Reading your composition, one can discern what you will establish and accomplish in the future. Keep striving!”

When we observe the worthy person's reverence toward those he serves, we find that in each case he gives his heart fully within. Loyalty serves the ruler, and filial piety serves one's parents. The ways of minister and son differ, yet, fundamentally, the heart that gives itself fully within is the same in both. From this, the meaning of completeness can indeed be understood. The author of the Record of the Principles of Sacrifice meant that the worthy person's ability to offer sacrifice rests upon his ability to attain completeness. In giving himself fully within and acting in obedience without, this so-called completeness becomes manifest.

Thus, when the worthy person serves in the state, considered in terms of service to his ruler, he has the way of a minister to follow, and loyalty comes first. Observe how he serves his ruler: “Diligently and reverently attend to your office”—benefit and harm, good fortune and adversity all lie close to his heart. “Wholeheartedly assist your sovereign”—as belly and heart, hands and feet, he seems to form one body with him. By demanding difficult achievements of his ruler and assisting him toward the good government of Tang and Yu, he displays the utmost reverence. By presenting warnings against excessive prosperity even in times of security, he displays far-reaching concern. Such is the means by which he is loyal to his ruler…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
抑古人祭祀以感格爲重而幽明之交以忠信
爲先然必吾之備得于素定而後神之歆見于
陟降仁人享帝孝子享親端不外此書曰黍稷
非馨明德惟馨又曰鬼神無常享享于克誠夫
曰明德曰誠備之謂也至於能享則百神受職
百貨可極景福之介純嘏之錫無往不利矣然
則祭也者又休咎感召之機也可無愼乎
第貳場
論
===
君子脩之吉
張元舉
同考試官教諭林批通篇俱在圖內發明不事泛言是
有理學之士宜膺首選
同考試官教諭蕭批敬與吉意俱說有分曉蓋優於論者
考試官教諭林批以太極立意甚得周子之旨
考試官教授詹批此篇說太極之理洒然明白可錄
人心一太極也君子作聖之功主敬以全夫太
極而已矣太極之理隨物而賦隨在各足自聖
punctuated:
抑古人祭祀，以感格爲重，而幽明之交，以忠信爲先。然必吾之備得于素定，而後神之歆見于陟降。仁人享帝，孝子享親，端不外此。《書》曰：「黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。」又曰：「鬼神無常享，享于克誠。」夫曰明德，曰誠，備之謂也。至於能享，則百神受職，百貨可極，景福之介，純嘏之錫，無往不利矣。然則祭也者，又休咎感召之機也，可無愼乎？
第貳場
論
君子脩之吉
張元舉
同考試官教諭林批：「通篇俱在圖內發明，不事泛言，是有理學之士，宜膺首選。」
同考試官教諭蕭批：「敬與吉意俱說有分曉，蓋優於論者。」
考試官教諭林批：「以太極立意，甚得周子之旨。」
考試官教授詹批：「此篇說太極之理，洒然明白，可錄。」
人心一太極也。君子作聖之功，主敬以全夫太極而已矣。太極之理，隨物而賦，隨在各足，自聖
translation_en:
Moreover, the ancients regarded moving the spirits to come as the essential purpose of sacrifice, and held wholeheartedness and trustworthiness foremost in communication between the unseen and visible worlds. Yet our own completeness must first be firmly established in our habitual conduct; only then will the spirits manifest their acceptance as they descend and ascend. The benevolent person's offering to the Lord on High and the filial son's offering to his parents depend entirely upon this. The Book of Documents says: “It is not the millet that gives fragrance; luminous virtue alone gives fragrance.” It also says: “The spirits do not invariably accept offerings; they accept those of people capable of sincerity.” What it calls luminous virtue and sincerity is precisely this completeness. When offerings can indeed gain acceptance, the hundred spirits discharge their offices, all goods reach their fullest abundance, great blessings attend us, and unalloyed felicity is bestowed: nothing undertaken fails to prosper. Sacrifice, then, is also the crucial means by which good fortune or calamity is summoned in response. Can one fail to be cautious?
Second Session
Discourse
“The noble man cultivates it and obtains good fortune.”
Zhang Yuanju
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The entire essay elucidates the meaning within the Diagram, without indulging in generalities. This is a scholar versed in the Learning of Principle, who deserves first place.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “The meanings of reverent attentiveness and good fortune are both explained distinctly. He is surely an accomplished writer of discourses.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “He grounds his argument in the Supreme Ultimate and grasps Master Zhou's intention very well.”
Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: “This essay explains the principle of the Supreme Ultimate lucidly and clearly. It merits selection.”
The human mind is itself a Supreme Ultimate. The noble man's work of becoming a sage consists simply in making reverent attentiveness his guiding principle, thereby preserving the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety. title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
於動者如是也其行之也必求其中其處之也
必求其正其發之也必求其仁其裁之也必求
其義合動靜而一於敬者也一於敬則吾心常
惺惺矣常整齊嚴肅矣常虛常靈而夜氣清矣
陽明勝而德性用人欲淨而天理流行矣由是
而居之安資之深取之左右逢其原以靜則有
常以動則不括以之爲己則順而祥以之爲人
則愛而公以之爲天下國家則無所處而不當
所謂聰明睿智皆由是出者有也所謂守之貴
===
行之利廓之配天地者有也吾知天地之德也
日月之明也四時之序也鬼神之吉凶也一無
極而太極之理爲之也太極之理存乎我者旣
無闕欠則是踐形惟肖吾之德亦聖人之德矣
不愧屋漏吾之明亦聖人之明矣知化以善述
其事窮神以善繼其志吾心之照臨通乎晝夜
吾心之往來同乎屈伸一聖人之出入造化者
矣其合德合明合序合吉凶聖人之所能者吾
亦能之聖人固無欲而靜不假脩爲以立極吾
punctuated: 於動者如是也。其行之也，必求其中；其處之也，必求其正；其發之也，必求其仁；其裁之也，必求其義。合動靜而一於敬者也。一於敬，則吾心常惺惺矣，常整齊嚴肅矣，常虛常靈而夜氣清矣，陽明勝而德性用，人欲淨而天理流行矣。由是而居之安，資之深，取之左右逢其原。以靜則有常，以動則不括；以之爲己則順而祥，以之爲人則愛而公，以之爲天下國家則無所處而不當。所謂「聰明睿智皆由是出」者有也，所謂「守之貴，行之利，廓之配天地」者有也。吾知天地之德也，日月之明也，四時之序也，鬼神之吉凶也，一無極而太極之理爲之也。太極之理存乎我者旣無闕欠，則是踐形惟肖，吾之德亦聖人之德矣；不愧屋漏，吾之明亦聖人之明矣。知化以善述其事，窮神以善繼其志，吾心之照臨通乎晝夜，吾心之往來同乎屈伸，一聖人之出入造化者矣。其合德、合明、合序、合吉凶，聖人之所能者，吾亦能之。聖人固無欲而靜，不假脩爲以立極，吾
translation_en:
…with regard to activity, it is thus. In acting, one must seek the mean; in taking a position, one must seek correctness; in giving expression, one must seek benevolence; and in making judgments, one must seek righteousness. This is to unite activity and stillness in a single reverent attentiveness. With this unity in reverent attentiveness, my mind is always alert, always orderly and composed, always empty and responsive, and my vital energy at night is clear. Luminous yang predominates and my moral nature operates; human desires are purified away and Heaven’s principle flows freely. Through this, one dwells securely in it, draws deeply upon it, and finds its source wherever one turns. In stillness, there is constancy; in activity, there is no constraint. Applied to oneself, it brings accord and auspiciousness; applied to others, love and impartiality; applied to all under Heaven, the state, and the family, it makes every response appropriate. Here is what is meant by “Acuteness of hearing, clarity of sight, sagacity, and wisdom all issue from this,” and by “To preserve it is noble; to practice it is beneficial; to expand it is to match Heaven and Earth.”

I know that the virtue of Heaven and Earth, the brightness of the sun and moon, the sequence of the four seasons, and the good and ill fortune brought by ghosts and spirits are all the workings of the one principle of the Non-polar and yet the Supreme Polarity. Since the principle of the Supreme Polarity present within me lacks nothing, I fulfill my bodily form in true likeness to it, and my virtue is also the sage’s virtue. Having nothing to be ashamed of even in the secluded recesses of my room, my illumination is also the sage’s illumination. By understanding transformation, I fittingly carry forward its workings; by fathoming the spiritual, I fittingly continue its intent. The illumination of my mind extends through day and night; its coming and going accords with contraction and expansion. I am wholly like the sage moving within the processes of creation and transformation. In matching the virtue of Heaven and Earth, the brightness of the sun and moon, the sequence of the seasons, and the good and ill fortune of ghosts and spirits, what the sage can do, I too can do. The sage is indeed free of desire and still, and establishes the ultimate standard without relying on deliberate cultivation; I…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
亦敬以作所而人極於我乎立矣君子之吉孰
大於是然君子豈有心於獲吉而計其功哉亦
曰脩之自我者當如是其吉與否有不在我者
雖聖人不能必君子固將居易以俟之而已而
天之所助者順也人之所助者信也履信思乎
順是以自天祐之吉無不利也在易震之象曰
君子以恐懼脩省夫君子固動必以天者矣然
感洊雷之義則其恐懼脩省之心自有所不能
已也蹇之象曰君子以反身脩德夫君子之德
===
固無所闕矣然當處蹇之時則其反身脩德之
念自有所不容已也曰脩省曰脩德非所以全
夫太極之理哉非君子之脩之而求至於聖人
之立極者哉抑觀太極一圖周子嘗手授二程
矣二程有所得而廣之一則曰動亦定靜亦定
無將迎無內外固聖人主靜之說也一則曰涵
養須用敬固君子脩之之功也然於此圖則未
嘗輕以語人非以其微妙而難言者乎故曰先
生之精因圖以示先生之蘊因圖以發又曰自
punctuated:
亦敬以作所，而人極於我乎立矣。君子之吉，孰大於是？然君子豈有心於獲吉而計其功哉？亦曰脩之自我者當如是，其吉與否，有不在我者，雖聖人不能必。君子固將居易以俟之而已。而天之所助者順也，人之所助者信也。履信思乎順，是以自天祐之，吉無不利也。
在《易》，震之象曰：「君子以恐懼脩省。」夫君子固動必以天者矣，然感洊雷之義，則其恐懼脩省之心自有所不能已也。蹇之象曰：「君子以反身脩德。」夫君子之德固無所闕矣，然當處蹇之時，則其反身脩德之念自有所不容已也。曰脩省，曰脩德，非所以全夫太極之理哉？非君子之脩之而求至於聖人之立極者哉？
抑觀太極一圖，周子嘗手授二程矣。二程有所得而廣之，一則曰：「動亦定，靜亦定，無將迎，無內外。」固聖人主靜之說也。一則曰：「涵養須用敬。」固君子脩之之功也。然於此圖，則未嘗輕以語人，非以其微妙而難言者乎？故曰：「先生之精，因圖以示；先生之蘊，因圖以發。」又曰：「自
translation_en:
…I too make reverence my abiding place, and thus the ultimate standard for humanity is established within me. What good fortune for the gentleman could be greater than this? Yet would the gentleman deliberately seek good fortune and calculate the rewards of his efforts? He merely says that the cultivation which depends upon himself ought to be like this. Whether good fortune follows involves things beyond his control; even a sage cannot guarantee it. The gentleman will simply abide in what is easy and await what comes. What Heaven assists is compliance; what people assist is trustworthiness. Practicing trustworthiness and attending to compliance, he therefore receives Heaven’s aid: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.
In the Book of Changes, the Image commentary on Zhen (Thunder) says: “The gentleman, through fear and apprehension, cultivates and examines himself.” The gentleman assuredly accords with Heaven whenever he acts. Yet, moved by the significance of repeated thunder, he cannot suppress his impulse toward apprehensive self-cultivation and examination. The Image commentary on Jian (Obstruction) says: “The gentleman turns back upon himself and cultivates his virtue.” The gentleman’s virtue assuredly lacks nothing. Yet when he encounters obstruction, he cannot restrain his impulse to turn back upon himself and cultivate his virtue. Are this cultivation and examination, and this cultivation of virtue, not ways to preserve intact the principle of the Supreme Ultimate? Are they not the gentleman’s work of cultivation, through which he seeks to attain the sage’s establishment of the ultimate standard?
Consider, moreover, the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate: Master Zhou once personally transmitted it to the two Cheng brothers. The two Chengs grasped its meaning and elaborated upon it. One said: “In movement, there is stability; in stillness, there is stability. There is neither sending off nor welcoming, neither inner nor outer.” This is precisely the teaching that the sage takes stillness as his guiding principle. The other said: “Nurturing oneself requires reverence.” This is precisely the gentleman’s work of cultivation. Yet they never spoke lightly to others about this diagram. Was this not because its subtleties were difficult to express? title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天之命於穆不已誠也誠卽太極也聖人之同
天全乎動靜之德而已矣所以全動靜之德者
主靜而已矣卽誠也卽太極之所以立也天維
誠故陰陽錯焉五氣布焉四時行而萬物生焉
天之爲道盡于是矣聖人維誠故人極立焉中
正仁義出焉由是而與天地合其德日月合其
明四時合其序鬼神合其吉凶而聖人之爲聖
人盡于是矣夫天道若是乎其淵以妙也聖人
之道若是乎其高且美也語塗之人而曰天之
===
道備于而躬聖人者而可至也有不聞而駭畏
而阻者哉然不知天無心渾乎其誠也聖人有
心誠而已矣天之道唯聖人能全之而君子之
求道脩其爲聖人者而已矣蓋人之生也繼之
者善成之者性天之道在人也方其湛然虛明
萬理畢備何者非天聖人此心塗人亦此心也
然聖人所以異于人者不淆于欲而已君子之
脩之求所以無欲而已無欲則誠誠未可以遽
至持之以敬斯幾矣何以言之夫人之昏昧放
punctuated:
「天之命，於穆不已」，誠也。誠卽太極也。聖人之同天，全乎動靜之德而已矣。所以全動靜之德者，主靜而已矣，卽誠也，卽太極之所以立也。天維誠，故陰陽錯焉，五氣布焉，四時行而萬物生焉，天之爲道盡于是矣。聖人維誠，故人極立焉，中正仁義出焉。由是而與天地合其德，日月合其明，四時合其序，鬼神合其吉凶，而聖人之爲聖人盡于是矣。

夫天道若是乎其淵以妙也，聖人之道若是乎其高且美也。語塗之人而曰：「天之道備于而躬，聖人者而可至也。」有不聞而駭、畏而阻者哉？然不知天無心，渾乎其誠也；聖人有心，誠而已矣。天之道唯聖人能全之，而君子之求道，脩其爲聖人者而已矣。蓋人之生也，繼之者善，成之者性，天之道在人也。方其湛然虛明，萬理畢備，何者非天？聖人此心，塗人亦此心也。然聖人所以異于人者，不淆于欲而已。君子之脩之，求所以無欲而已。無欲則誠，誠未可以遽至，持之以敬，斯幾矣。何以言之？夫人之昏昧放
translation_en:
“Heaven’s mandate—how profound and unceasing!” This is sincerity. Sincerity is the Supreme Ultimate. The sage’s conformity with Heaven consists simply in fully realizing the virtues of activity and stillness. What enables him to realize these virtues fully is simply giving primacy to stillness: this is sincerity, and this is how the Supreme Ultimate is established. Heaven is sincere; thus yin and yang interweave, the five vital forces spread abroad, the four seasons proceed, and the myriad things come into being. In this the Way of Heaven is fully expressed. The sage is sincere; thus the supreme standard for humanity is established, and centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness emerge. Through this, his virtue accords with Heaven and Earth, his illumination with the sun and moon, his order with the four seasons, and his good and ill fortune with the spirits. In this, all that makes the sage a sage is fully expressed.

The Way of Heaven is so profound and subtle; the Way of the sage is so lofty and beautiful. If one were to tell a person on the road, “The Way of Heaven is fully present in your own person, and sagehood is something you can attain,” would anyone hear this without being startled, becoming fearful, and drawing back? Yet such people do not understand that Heaven has no deliberate mind and is wholly sincere; the sage has a mind, but is simply sincere. Only the sage can fully realize the Way of Heaven, while the gentleman’s pursuit of the Way consists simply in cultivating what enables him to become a sage. For in human beings’ coming into existence, what carries on the Way is goodness, and what completes it is their nature: this is the Way of Heaven within humanity. When the mind is limpid, empty, and luminous, with all principles fully present, what in it is not of Heaven? The sage has this mind, and the person on the road also has this mind. What distinguishes the sage from others is simply that he is not muddled by desires. The gentleman’s cultivation consists simply in seeking the means to be without desire. Without desire, one is sincere. If sincerity cannot yet be attained all at once, maintaining oneself through reverent attentiveness brings one close to it. Why do I say this? As for people’s benightedness and unrestrained…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
人與日月合其明吾而未能然當知當行可求
也從而脩之而日月之明幾矣聖人與四時合
其序鬼神合其吉凶吾而未能焉時止時行福
善禍淫可求也從而脩之而四時之序鬼神之
吉凶幾矣由是靜虛而明通動直而公溥以之
爲己則順而祥以之爲人則愛而公以之爲天
下國家則無所處而不當故曰吉是君子之所
履也非假于外也又由是將無所用于脩而聖
人之域忽不自知其優入而所謂天道者亦不
===
遠于我而得之矣於戲聖人以誠而合天君子
以敬而入聖道果遠乎哉學聖者不曰有階巳
哉然周子之望于人者深矣顧聞是圖手授程
子之外鮮有傳者程子得之不復聞有所授豈
默識言意之表固難其人邪朱子作解亦曰辯
詰紛然苦于應酬之不給則知而信之而果于
脩爲者亦希見矣抑周子豈徒望于當時巳也
百世而下神會心解有如周子承墜緒于孔孟
則倡鳴絶學者固不可病其寡和雖然以誠敬
punctuated:
人與日月合其明，吾而未能然，當知當行可求也。從而脩之，而日月之明幾矣。聖人與四時合其序，鬼神合其吉凶，吾而未能焉，時止時行，福善禍淫可求也。從而脩之，而四時之序、鬼神之吉凶幾矣。由是靜虛而明通，動直而公溥，以之爲己則順而祥，以之爲人則愛而公，以之爲天下國家則無所處而不當。故曰吉，是君子之所履也，非假于外也。又由是將無所用于脩，而聖人之域忽不自知其優入，而所謂天道者亦不遠于我而得之矣。
於戲！聖人以誠而合天，君子以敬而入聖，道果遠乎哉？學聖者不曰有階巳哉？然周子之望于人者深矣。顧聞是圖手授程子之外，鮮有傳者。程子得之，不復聞有所授，豈默識言意之表，固難其人邪？朱子作解，亦曰辯詰紛然，苦于應酬之不給，則知而信之而果于脩爲者亦希見矣。抑周子豈徒望于當時巳也？百世而下，神會心解，有如周子承墜緒于孔孟，則倡鳴絶學者固不可病其寡和。雖然，以誠敬
translation_en:
…[The sage] accords with the sun and moon in his brightness. If I cannot yet do so, I can seek what I ought to know and what I ought to practice. Cultivating myself accordingly, I shall approach the brightness of the sun and moon. The sage accords with the four seasons in their succession and with the spirits in their auspicious and inauspicious workings. If I cannot yet do so, I can seek the principles of stopping and acting at the proper times, and of blessing the good and bringing calamity upon the wicked. Cultivating myself accordingly, I shall approach the order of the four seasons and the auspicious and inauspicious workings of the spirits. Thus, in stillness one is empty, luminous, and perceptive; in activity, upright, impartial, and all-embracing. Applied to oneself, this brings harmony and auspiciousness; applied to others, it brings love and impartiality; applied to governing all under Heaven and the state, it leaves nothing improperly handled. Hence the word “auspicious”: this is what the gentleman practices, not something borrowed from outside. Proceeding further from this, one will eventually have no need to exert oneself in cultivation, and will suddenly find that one has entered the realm of the sage with ease, without knowing how. What is called the Way of Heaven will likewise be close to me, and I shall attain it.
Ah! Through sincerity the sage accords with Heaven; through reverence the gentleman enters sagehood. Is the Way truly distant? May not those who study to become sages say that they have steps by which to ascend? Yet Master Zhou’s hopes for others were profound. We hear, however, that apart from his personally handing this diagram to Master Cheng, it was seldom transmitted. After Master Cheng received it, we hear no further report of his passing it on. Could it be that someone capable of silently apprehending what lies beyond words and expressed meanings is indeed difficult to find? When Master Zhu wrote his explanation, he too said that disputes and challenges arose in such profusion that he struggled to respond to them all. Thus those who understand it, believe in it, and act resolutely in self-cultivation are seldom seen. Yet could Master Zhou’s hopes have been confined to his own age? A hundred generations later, someone may apprehend it in spirit and understand it in his heart, just as Master Zhou took up the broken thread of transmission from Confucius and Mencius. Those who proclaim and give voice to a learning whose transmission has been severed surely cannot be faulted because few respond. Nevertheless, taking sincerity and reverence…
