乾德四年正月某日，具官臣孔宜伏蒙聖恩，以臣宜爲曲阜主簿，奉臣祖孔丘祀，謹奉表稱謝者。伏以：運隆天造，恩徽穆被于宮墻；澤逮雲仍，
translation_en:
…as the gateway to learning, Master Cheng has surely already spoken of this.

Memorial
A model memorial of thanks, written as if under the Song, for the appointment of Kong Yi as Registrar of Qufu to conduct sacrifices to Confucius.
Qiande reign, fourth year [966].
By Zhao Xun.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: “Pure, elegant, and conforming to classical standards; it captures the style of Song memorials.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “Both the elaboration and the narration proceed in proper order. Worth selecting.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Memorials prize parallel phrasing and value precision and elegance still more. This composition merits acceptance.”
Comment by Examiner Zhan, Instructor: “It recounts the Former Sage without lapsing into exaggeration and speaks of the Five Dynasties without lapsing into resentment. It perfectly embodies the traditions of the Kong family and also achieves the proper form of respectful thanksgiving. An excellent memorial.”

On a certain day of the first month of the fourth year of Qiande, your servant Kong Yi, holding the specified office, has humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious favor in appointing your servant Yi as Registrar of Qufu to conduct sacrifices to my ancestor Kong Qiu. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks.

I humbly consider: as the fortunes of the age flourish through Your Majesty’s heaven-like creative power, gracious favor beautifully and harmoniously envelops the walls of the Sage’s temple; beneficence reaches his distant descendants…

text:
帝祉愉饗
天心
道統承千載之正傳
德業參兩間而成位
雅樂攸定協音律以宣八風
文德聿脩舞干羽以來五國
福昭景貺早傳沙塞之肅清
穰錫溥將永奠
瑶圖于鞏固臣無任瞻
===
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策〔五道〕
第一問
張元舉
punctuated:
帝祉愉饗天心。道統承千載之正傳，德業參兩間而成位。雅樂攸定，協音律以宣八風；文德聿脩，舞干羽以來五國。福昭景貺，早傳沙塞之肅清；穰錫溥將，永奠瑶圖于鞏固。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄場
策〔五道〕
第一問
張元舉
translation_en:
…Imperial blessings gladden and gratify Heaven’s heart [?]. The succession of the Way carries forward the orthodox transmission of a thousand years; your virtue and achievements stand alongside Heaven and Earth, establishing your rightful place. Elegant music is established, harmonizing the tones and pitches to spread the eight winds. Civil virtue is cultivated; dances with shields and pheasant plumes bring the five states into allegiance. Blessings manifest Heaven’s great gifts: already news arrives that the sandy frontier has been pacified. Abundant bounty is bestowed far and wide, forever securing the imperial realm on firm foundations. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, cannot contain his utmost fervor and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays〔Five questions〕
First Question
Zhang Yuanju 張元舉

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭林批我
聖祖曁我
皇上學術文章夐卓千古無能名狀此作頌揚有法錄之爲百世臣民佩服之助
同考試官敎諭蕭批鋪張不遺揄揚有則是必佳士
考試官敎諭林批我
聖祖
神孫授守一道此策備之猗歟盛哉
考試官敎授詹批敷對詳整必蘊藉之士錄之
知道統之承傳者可以論帝王之學術矣
===
知天地之易簡者可以論帝王之文章矣
夫道統之承傳非必其丁寧告語而後學
術之眞傳可得也卽其默契潜孚而妙若
合一者斯學術之至者也天地之易簡非
必其摹擬形似而後文章之眞訣可得也
卽其生成化育而妙出無心者斯文章之
至者也然根本盛大而後英華敷茂兼内
外而該本末其實一以貫之而已王天下
者員有君師之責故學術文章均之不可
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭林批：「我聖祖曁我皇上，學術文章夐卓千古，無能名狀。此作頌揚有法，錄之爲百世臣民佩服之助。」
同考試官敎諭蕭批：「鋪張不遺，揄揚有則，是必佳士。」
考試官敎諭林批：「我聖祖神孫，授守一道，此策備之。猗歟盛哉！」
考試官敎授詹批：「敷對詳整，必蘊藉之士，錄之。」
知道統之承傳者，可以論帝王之學術矣；知天地之易簡者，可以論帝王之文章矣。夫道統之承傳，非必其丁寧告語而後學術之眞傳可得也；卽其默契潜孚而妙若合一者，斯學術之至者也。天地之易簡，非必其摹擬形似而後文章之眞訣可得也；卽其生成化育而妙出無心者，斯文章之至者也。然根本盛大而後英華敷茂，兼内外而該本末，其實一以貫之而已。王天下者員有君師之責，故學術文章均之不可
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lin, School Instructor, comments: “The learning and literary accomplishments of our sagely founding ancestor and our present emperor stand far above those of all ages, beyond the power of words to describe. This composition offers praise with method; it is recorded to help subjects through a hundred generations revere and take them as their example.”
Associate Examiner Xiao, School Instructor, comments: “Its ample exposition omits nothing, and its praise observes proper standards. This must be an excellent scholar.”
Examiner Lin, School Instructor, comments: “Our sagely founding ancestor and his divine descendant transmit and preserve the same Way. This policy essay sets it forth fully. Ah, how splendid!”
Examiner Zhan, Instructor, comments: “The response is detailed and well ordered. Its author must be a scholar of cultivated depth. Record it.”
Those who understand the transmission of the succession of the Way may discuss the learning of emperors and kings; those who understand the ease and simplicity of Heaven and Earth may discuss the literary accomplishments of emperors and kings. The transmission of the succession of the Way does not necessarily require earnest verbal instruction before the true transmission of learning can be attained. Rather, silent accord and unspoken correspondence, so wondrous that they seem to merge into one, constitute the highest attainment of learning. Nor do the ease and simplicity of Heaven and Earth necessarily require imitation of outward forms before the true secret of literary accomplishment can be attained. Rather, bringing things into being and nurturing their transformation, with wonders arising without deliberate intent, constitute the highest attainment of literary accomplishment. Yet only when the roots are strong and ample can the blossoms unfold luxuriantly. Embracing both the internal and the external, encompassing both root and branch, these are in fact simply pervaded by a single principle. Those who rule all under Heaven bear [?] the responsibilities of both ruler and teacher; thus learning and literary accomplishment alike cannot …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
民之至仁諭將帥建學校而先北方罷詞
賦而顓經術削正山川之封號條定祭祀
之章程禁兄弟之婚均父母之服謹宮府
之政嚴內外之防大政大事未易縷數然
無一而非人倫之切近物理之精實皆所
以援拯生民之昏溺而覺之以斯道者也
是故學術之盛難乎其形容矣帝王有帝
王之文章非書生藻麗之云而已典謨其
至也□□□也乃其正詮平易敷暢發
===
揮事□□□□漢而下操其藝者或鑿矣
我
皇祖則駕千載而獨得之觀其
與學士詹同論文章曰古人爲文章明白易
知無深恠險僻之語近世文士不究道德之
本不達當世之務立詞雖艱深而意實淺近
卽使過於相如何裨實用斯言也非得于文
章之眞傳者而有是哉人見
皇祖之酬應萬幾諄切懇至洋洋乎如造化之
punctuated:
民之至仁，諭將帥，建學校而先北方，罷詞賦而顓經術，削正山川之封號，條定祭祀之章程，禁兄弟之婚，均父母之服，謹宮府之政，嚴內外之防。大政大事，未易縷數，然無一而非人倫之切近、物理之精實，皆所以援拯生民之昏溺而覺之以斯道者也。是故學術之盛，難乎其形容矣！
帝王有帝王之文章，非書生藻麗之云而已。典謨其至也，□□□也，乃其正詮平易，敷暢發揮，事□□□□漢而下，操其藝者或鑿矣。我皇祖則駕千載而獨得之。觀其與學士詹同論文章曰：「古人爲文章，明白易知，無深恠險僻之語。近世文士不究道德之本，不達當世之務，立詞雖艱深，而意實淺近。卽使過於相如，何裨實用？」斯言也，非得于文章之眞傳者而有是哉？人見皇祖之酬應萬幾，諄切懇至，洋洋乎如造化之
translation_en:
…the utmost benevolence toward the people. He instructed the commanders, established schools beginning with the northern regions, abolished verse and rhapsody in favor of classical learning, revised the honorific titles conferred on mountains and rivers, and systematically prescribed regulations for sacrifices. He prohibited marriages between brothers and sisters [?], equalized mourning observances for fathers and mothers, carefully regulated the administration of the palace and government offices, and strictly maintained the separation between the inner and outer spheres. His great policies and undertakings cannot readily be enumerated in detail. Yet every one concerned the immediate realities of human relationships and the essential truths of the principles of things. All served to rescue the people from their benighted confusion and awaken them through this Way. Thus the flourishing of learning is difficult indeed to describe!
Emperors and kings have their own kind of writing; it is more than the ornate elegance of scholars. The Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents represent its highest attainment. [Illegible passage.] Their correct exposition [?] is plain and accessible, expansively setting forth and elucidating their meaning; affairs [four illegible characters] … From the Han onward, some practitioners of this art became contrived. Our Imperial Ancestor, however, surpassed a thousand years and alone grasped its essence. Consider his discussion of writing with Academician Zhan Tong: “The ancients wrote clearly and intelligibly, without language that was obscure, strange, tortuous, or outlandish. Literary men of recent times neither investigate the foundations of the Way and virtue nor understand the affairs of their own age. Although their wording is difficult and abstruse, their meaning is actually shallow. Even if they surpassed Sima Xiangru, what contribution would they make to practical use?” Could anyone who had not received the true transmission of writing have spoken thus? People see how our Imperial Ancestor attended to the myriad affairs of government, earnest and deeply sincere, his abundant expression resembling that of the creative workings of Heaven and Earth …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曰周之仁厚可以爲法又
曰聖人統馭四海而宰制萬物仁以居之義
以行之故賢者樂有仁義而不肖者有所視
效於戲我
皇祖平時之言一則曰仁義二則曰仁義可以
仰窺
聖德精微
□□人理醇固此則所謂根本盛大與
□合一者然也當時臣下之
□□作爲文章舉筆立就莫不言近而
===
指遠至于
詔諭遐方明燭萬里若見肺肝又曰
帝爲文或不喜書命侍臣坐榻下操觚受詞終
食之頃滚滚千餘言
天光昭回赫著簡袠眞所謂天之文也於戲我
皇祖爲文之妙一則曰明燭二則曰昭回又可
以仰窺
punctuated:
曰：「周之仁厚可以爲法。」又曰：「聖人統馭四海而宰制萬物，仁以居之，義以行之，故賢者樂有仁義，而不肖者有所視效。」於戲！我皇祖平時之言，一則曰仁義，二則曰仁義，可以仰窺聖德精微，□□人理醇固。此則所謂根本盛大，與□合一者然也。
當時臣下之□□，作爲文章，舉筆立就，莫不言近而指遠。至于詔諭遐方，明燭萬里，若見肺肝。又曰：「帝爲文，或不喜書，命侍臣坐榻下，操觚受詞，終食之頃，滚滚千餘言。天光昭回，赫著簡袠，眞所謂天之文也。」於戲！我皇祖爲文之妙，一則曰明燭，二則曰昭回，又可以仰窺
translation_en:
… said: “The benevolence and generosity of the Zhou can serve as a model.” He also said: “The sage governs all within the Four Seas and orders the myriad things. He occupies his position through benevolence and acts through righteousness. Thus the worthy delight in possessing benevolence and righteousness, while the unworthy have something to observe and emulate.” Ah! In the ordinary words of our imperial ancestor, benevolence and righteousness were his first theme, and benevolence and righteousness his second. Through them we may reverently glimpse the subtle profundity of his sagely virtue, □□ [?], and the purity and firmness of human moral principles. This is what is meant by a foundation flourishing and great, united as one with □ [?].
At that time, his ministers’ □□ [?]—in composing literary works, the brush was raised and the piece immediately completed; without exception, the language was accessible yet its implications far-reaching. As for edicts addressed to distant regions, their illumination reached ten thousand li, as though laying bare the innermost thoughts. It is further said: “When the emperor composed, he sometimes preferred not to write himself. He ordered an attendant official to sit below his couch, take up a writing tablet, and receive his words. Within the time needed for a meal, more than a thousand words poured forth. Heavenly radiance shone all around, brilliantly manifest upon the written pages: truly, this was what is called the writing of Heaven.” Ah! The marvel of our imperial ancestor’s composition is described first as ‘illumination’ and second as ‘radiance shining all around.’ Through this, too, we may reverently glimpse …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖學啓口容聲莫非至德此則所謂英華敷茂
與天地化育同一妙出無心者然也若夫
漢高之不事詩書唐宗之閨門慚德宋藝
祖之質朴自然其得國致治與其學術文
章豈可以同日而語哉仰惟
皇上嗣承大統
聖神
□□
===
□□□□□□皿有
□□□不言
神授于默成者故學術無一而不孚契文章無
一而不脗合伏覩
明倫大典一書推明統嗣之不同詳論義情之
兼盡
尊尊
親親並行攸當名正言順禮備樂成
立人極而光
punctuated:
聖學，啓口容聲，莫非至德。此則所謂英華敷茂，與天地化育同一妙，出無心者然也。若夫漢高之不事詩書、唐宗之閨門慚德、宋藝祖之質朴自然，其得國致治與其學術文章，豈可以同日而語哉？仰惟皇上嗣承大統，聖神□□，□□□□□□皿有□□□不言，神授于默成者，故學術無一而不孚契，文章無一而不脗合。
伏覩《明倫大典》一書，推明統嗣之不同，詳論義情之兼盡，尊尊、親親，並行攸當，名正言順，禮備樂成，立人極而光
translation_en:
…His sagely learning: whenever he opened his mouth and gave voice, everything expressed consummate virtue. This is what is meant by splendid excellence flourishing luxuriantly, sharing the same wondrous workings as the transforming and nurturing powers of Heaven and Earth, and arising without conscious intent. As for Han Gaozu’s neglect of the Odes and Documents, the Tang emperor’s shameful failings in the inner household, and the Song founding emperor’s natural simplicity, how could their acquisition of the realm and achievement of orderly government, or their learning and literary compositions, be spoken of in the same breath as his? We reverently reflect that Your Majesty has succeeded to the great imperial line, sagely and divine [illegible passage containing 皿, “vessel,” and 不言, “without speaking”; connection uncertain [?]], receiving divine instruction through silent accomplishment. Thus, in learning there is nothing that does not accord, and in literary composition nothing that does not agree.
We humbly observe that the book Great Canon for Clarifying Human Relations (Minglun Dadian) elucidates the distinction between succession to the imperial line and succession as an heir, and discusses in detail how both moral duty and familial feeling are fully satisfied. Honoring the honored and cherishing one’s kin proceed together, each appropriately fulfilled. Names are correct and words accord; rites are complete and music perfected. It establishes the supreme standard for humanity and brings glory to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖孝所謂考三王而不謬建天地而不悖者也
是書也質諸
皇祖祖訓之篇
正本以睦親
齊家以及天下之義真同條而共貫矣至于
冊
天之文恭上
皇天上帝泰號義取人情道通神理蓋
===
重建極者也是文也質諸
皇祖初定郊
天之禮欽崇
昊天並隆
四祖三陽開泰敬率臣僚恭祀之文真異世而
同符矣嘗
御製敬一箴有曰匪一弗純匪敬弗聚即
皇祖之言曰兢兢業業不敢自逸曰誠一弗二
punctuated: 聖孝，所謂考三王而不謬，建天地而不悖者也。是書也，質諸皇祖祖訓之篇，正本以睦親，齊家以及天下之義，真同條而共貫矣。至于冊天之文，恭上皇天上帝泰號，義取人情，道通神理，蓋重建極者也。是文也，質諸皇祖初定郊天之禮，欽崇昊天，並隆四祖，三陽開泰，敬率臣僚恭祀之文，真異世而同符矣。嘗御製《敬一箴》，有曰：「匪一弗純，匪敬弗聚。」即皇祖之言曰：「兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」曰：「誠一弗二。」
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s sagely filial piety. This is what is meant by being tested against the Three Kings without error and established between Heaven and Earth without contradiction. If this book is measured against the Imperial Ancestor’s Ancestral Injunctions, its principles of rectifying the foundation to bring harmony among kin, and ordering the family to extend that order throughout the realm, truly belong to the same branch and run along a common thread.

As for the text conferring an investiture upon Heaven [?], it reverently bestows the exalted designation “August Heaven, Sovereign on High.” Its meaning draws upon human feelings, and its Way accords with divine principles: it renews the establishment of the supreme standard. Measure this text against the Imperial Ancestor’s text from when he first established the rites for sacrificing to Heaven in the suburbs: reverently exalting Vast Heaven, honoring the Four Ancestors together, and, when the three yang forces ushered in auspicious renewal, respectfully leading his officials in solemn sacrifice. Though belonging to different ages, the two truly tally.

His Majesty once composed the Admonition on Reverence and Unity, saying: “Without unity there can be no purity; without reverence there can be no concentration.” This accords with the Imperial Ancestor’s words: “Ever cautious and diligent, I dare not indulge in ease,” and “Sincere and single-minded, without divided purpose”…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
對越在天之義也心箴有註則揭要於克
正之一言四箴有註則歸重於辨賢否審
聽納善號令合道理之數語而皆究極於
此心卽
皇祖之言曰人心虛靈乘氣機出入操而存之
爲難之指也又如欽
天記頌之製答
□徵于於穆所以明祇受之誠也
□□□
===
□□□
□之求也其他
制禮作樂
宏綱大要浩博如天地流行如江河要皆學
術文章之昭著與
皇祖之學術文章同一煥乎炳蔚而爲太平有
道之長其在
今日則尤巍巍蕩蕩不可名言矣雖然文章
之美本於學術之正而學術文章又必本
punctuated:
對越在天之義也。心箴有註，則揭要於克正之一言；四箴有註，則歸重於辨賢否、審聽納、善號令、合道理之數語，而皆究極於此心。卽皇祖之言曰：「人心虛靈，乘氣機出入，操而存之爲難。」之指也。又如欽天記頌之製，答□徵于於穆，所以明祇受之誠也。□□□□□□□之求也。其他制禮作樂，宏綱大要，浩博如天地，流行如江河，要皆學術文章之昭著，與皇祖之學術文章同一煥乎炳蔚，而爲太平有道之長。其在今日，則尤巍巍蕩蕩，不可名言矣。

雖然，文章之美本於學術之正，而學術文章又必本
translation_en:
…this is the meaning of reverently attending to the one in Heaven. In the commentary on the Admonition on the Mind (Xin zhen), the essential point is brought out in the single expression “being able to rectify” [?]. In the commentary on the Four Admonitions (Si zhen), emphasis is placed on the phrases “distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy,” “carefully considering what one hears and accepts,” “making commands good,” and “conforming to moral principle”; all ultimately come down to this mind. This is precisely the purport of the Imperial Ancestor’s words: “The human mind is empty and numinous; it comes and goes with the workings of vital energy. Holding fast to it and preserving it is difficult.” Likewise, in the imperial compositions recording and praising reverence for Heaven, “responding to □ and finding confirmation in august profundity” [?] serves to make manifest the sincerity with which Heaven’s charge is reverently received. [Seven illegible characters] …the seeking of it [?]. His other works, establishing rites and making music, set forth grand guiding principles and essential points, vast as Heaven and Earth and flowing like rivers. All are manifestations of his learning and literary accomplishment. Together with the learning and literary accomplishment of the Imperial Ancestor, they shine with the same magnificent brilliance and stand foremost in an age of great peace governed by the Way. In the present day, they are especially lofty and expansive, beyond what words can express.

Nevertheless, the beauty of literary composition rests upon the correctness of learning, and learning and literary accomplishment must in turn be grounded…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
於道德我
皇祖曁我
皇上道德之隆與
天地並是以蘊之爲學術則道統相傳之緒
帝王之聖學也發之爲文章則日星山河之麗
天地之至文也敷之爲治道則兼五帝軼
三王雍熙泰和之至治也
皇明億萬載無疆之休端在是矣愚生莫罄揄
揚何
===
第二問
周希正
同考試官教諭馬批百家專門之學諸儒合一之見此
策備之可與論經矣
考試官教諭林批士以明經致用經疑一策折衷群議
盡覩子之蘊足占所用
考試官教授詹批經學疑義辯析無遺詎偏經曲學
之士可到是宜録出
punctuated:
於道德。我皇祖曁我皇上道德之隆，與天地並。是以蘊之爲學術，則道統相傳之緒，帝王之聖學也；發之爲文章，則日星山河之麗，天地之至文也；敷之爲治道，則兼五帝、軼三王，雍熙泰和之至治也。皇明億萬載無疆之休，端在是矣。愚生莫罄揄揚，何。

第二問
周希正

同考試官教諭馬批：百家專門之學，諸儒合一之見，此策備之，可與論經矣。

考試官教諭林批：士以明經致用，經疑一策，折衷群議，盡覩子之蘊，足占所用。

考試官教授詹批：經學疑義，辯析無遺，詎偏經曲學之士可到？是宜録出。
translation_en:
…upon moral virtue. The fullness of the moral virtue of our imperial ancestor and our reigning emperor equals Heaven and Earth. Thus, inwardly embodied as learning, it is the thread of the transmitted succession of the Way, the sagely learning of emperors and kings. Expressed as literary composition, it is the splendor of sun, stars, mountains, and rivers—the supreme patterned beauty of Heaven and Earth. Extended into the art of government, it combines the achievements of the Five Emperors and surpasses the Three Kings: consummate government marked by harmony, prosperity, and perfect peace. Here, indeed, lies the boundless felicity of the August Ming for countless millions of years. This humble student cannot exhaust his praise. How … [?]

Second Question
Zhou Xizheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor: “The specialized learning of the Hundred Schools and the views through which the various Confucian scholars bring these into unity are fully present in this policy essay. Its author is someone with whom one may discuss the Classics.”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “A scholar brings his understanding of the Classics to practical use. This policy essay on doubtful points in the Classics weighs and reconciles the various arguments. It fully reveals the learning you possess and suffices to foretell how you will put it to use.”

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: “Doubtful meanings in classical scholarship are distinguished and analyzed without omission. Could a scholar confined to a single Classic and narrow learning attain this? This essay should be selected for inclusion in the record.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖人之作經以明道也學者之窮經以會
道也道載於經經不作道幾乎息矣道不
會經不可傳矣訓詁者失之鑿擬經者失
之僭支離附會將以明之適以晦之將以
擬之適以叛之可乎知此則可以究經學
之微而辯諸儒之得失矣且夫六經之作
聖人所以洩天地之秘而教萬世無窮也
是經雖不同而其為明道則一而已蓋嘗
求之□□□□數以存理也數無定體故
===
夏商取□□以不變為占周取九六以變
為占取數於變者以其有變易之義也乃
若卦之別於上下經者則以卦可反觀而
無反者八上經反卦二十四止為十二而
不反者六固十八卦也下經反卦三十二
止為十六而不反者二亦十八卦也故曰
以反觀之皆十八卦聖人之㫖深哉書之
道紀帝王為治之迹也秦誓費誓並傳者
何費之誓師得甘誓牧誓之遺意秦之悔
punctuated:
聖人之作經，以明道也；學者之窮經，以會道也。道載於經，經不作，道幾乎息矣；道不會，經不可傳矣。訓詁者失之鑿，擬經者失之僭。支離附會，將以明之，適以晦之；將以擬之，適以叛之，可乎？知此，則可以究經學之微，而辯諸儒之得失矣。
且夫六經之作，聖人所以洩天地之秘，而教萬世無窮也。是經雖不同，而其為明道則一而已。蓋嘗求之，□□□□數以存理也。數無定體，故夏商取□□以不變為占，周取九六以變為占。取數於變者，以其有變易之義也。乃若卦之別於上下經者，則以卦可反觀，而無反者八。上經反卦二十四，止為十二，而不反者六，固十八卦也；下經反卦三十二，止為十六，而不反者二，亦十八卦也。故曰：「以反觀之，皆十八卦。」聖人之㫖深哉！
書之道，紀帝王為治之迹也。《秦誓》《費誓》並傳者，何？費之誓師，得《甘誓》《牧誓》之遺意；秦之悔
translation_en:
The sages composed the classics to illuminate the Way; scholars study the classics exhaustively to comprehend the Way. The Way is contained in the classics: had the classics not been composed, the Way would almost have ceased to exist; if the Way is not comprehended, the classics cannot be transmitted. Those who explicate words err through strained interpretations; those who imitate the classics err through presumption. With fragmented interpretations and forced connections, they intend to illuminate them but instead obscure them; they intend to emulate them but instead depart from them. Can this be acceptable? Understanding this, one can investigate the subtleties of classical learning and distinguish the successes and failings of the various scholars.
The composition of the Six Classics was the means by which the sages disclosed the secrets of Heaven and Earth and taught countless generations without end. Although these classics differ, they are one in illuminating the Way. I have sought to investigate this: [four illegible characters] numbers serve to preserve principle [?]. Numbers have no fixed form. Thus the Xia and Shang used [two illegible characters], taking the unchanging as the basis for divination, whereas the Zhou used nine and six, taking change as the basis for divination. They took their numbers from change because these embody the meaning of transformation. As for the division of the hexagrams between the upper and lower sections of the Classic of Changes, hexagrams can be viewed upside down, but eight have no distinct inverted counterpart. In the upper section, the twenty-four invertible hexagrams amount to just twelve pairs, while six remain unchanged when inverted, making eighteen in all. In the lower section, the thirty-two invertible hexagrams amount to just sixteen pairs, while two remain unchanged when inverted, likewise making eighteen in all. Hence the saying: “Viewed through inversion, both contain eighteen hexagrams.” How profound is the sages’ intent!
The purpose of the Book of Documents is to record the deeds of emperors and kings in governing. Why have both the “Oath of Qin” and the “Oath at Fei” been transmitted? The address to the troops at Fei preserves the intent handed down in the “Oath at Gan” and the “Oath at Mu”; Qin’s remorse …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
過有改過不吝之餘風亦可訓矣乃若古
今文之辨則自秦火旣烈孔壁所藏安國
所傳者二十五篇謂之古文卽蝌蚪書也
伏生所授鼂錯所傳者二十九篇謂之今
文卽漢隷書也然今文多艱澁古文反平
易學者可無辨與詩以志民風昭國政三
百篇而始關雎王化之本也漢儒四始之
說則以關雎之治家爲國風始鹿鳴之治
□□□□□文王之述先德爲大雅始淸
===
□□□□□□爲三頌始義各有攸當也若
春秋之作定褒貶示勸懲夫子假魯史以
寓王法也程子謂其大義數十炳如日星
非以尊君而卑臣貴王而賤霸內中國而
外夷狄之類乎至於微詞奧義各適乎時
措之宜者未易窺測故曰史外傳心要典
也禮記一書定於孔聖成於七十子之徒
示天下以恭儉莊敬之道也曲禮名義言
禮之委曲纖悉耳彼謂作於曲臺者其妄
punctuated:
過，有改過不吝之餘風，亦可訓矣。乃若古今文之辨，則自秦火旣烈，孔壁所藏、安國所傳者二十五篇，謂之古文，卽蝌蚪書也；伏生所授、鼂錯所傳者二十九篇，謂之今文，卽漢隷書也。然今文多艱澁，古文反平易，學者可無辨與？

詩以志民風，昭國政。三百篇而始關雎，王化之本也。漢儒四始之說，則以關雎之治家爲國風始，鹿鳴之治□□□□□，文王之述先德爲大雅始，淸□□□□□□爲三頌始，義各有攸當也。

若春秋之作，定褒貶，示勸懲，夫子假魯史以寓王法也。程子謂其大義數十，炳如日星，非以尊君而卑臣、貴王而賤霸、內中國而外夷狄之類乎？至於微詞奧義，各適乎時措之宜者，未易窺測。故曰史外傳心要典也。

禮記一書，定於孔聖，成於七十子之徒，示天下以恭儉莊敬之道也。曲禮名義，言禮之委曲纖悉耳。彼謂作於曲臺者，其妄
translation_en:
… remorse for errors preserves something of the spirit of correcting one’s faults without reluctance; it too can serve as instruction. As for the distinction between the Old Text and New Text versions of the Documents: after the devastating Qin book-burning, the twenty-five chapters concealed in the wall of Confucius’s residence and transmitted by Kong Anguo were called the Old Text, being written in tadpole script. The twenty-nine chapters taught by Fu Sheng and transmitted by Chao Cuo were called the New Text, being written in Han clerical script. Yet the New Text is often difficult and obscure, while the Old Text is, on the contrary, plain and accessible. Can students dispense with examining this distinction?

The Odes records the customs of the people and makes manifest the governance of the states. Its three hundred poems begin with “The Ospreys” (Guanju), the foundation of kingly transformation through moral instruction. According to the Han scholars’ explanation of the “four beginnings,” “The Ospreys,” concerning the ordering of the household, begins the Airs of the States; “The Deer Call” (Luming), concerning the ordering of [five illegible characters: ?]; “King Wen” (Wen Wang), recounting ancestral virtue, begins the Greater Elegantiae; and “Qing…” [six illegible characters: ?] begins the three collections of Hymns. Each interpretation has its appropriate application.

As for the composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals, it establishes praise and blame and sets forth encouragements and admonitions: the Master used the historical records of Lu to convey the laws of true kingship. Master Cheng said that its several dozen great principles shine like the sun and stars. Are these not such principles as exalting the ruler and subordinating ministers, esteeming true kings and disparaging hegemons, and treating the central states as the inner realm and the Yi and Di peoples as outside it? As for its subtle wording and profound meanings, each suited to what was appropriate to enact at a particular time, these are not easily fathomed. Thus it is called an essential canon that transmits the sage’s mind beyond the historical record.

The Record of Rites was settled by the sage Confucius and completed by the company of his seventy disciples. It shows all under Heaven the way of humility, frugality, solemnity, and reverence. The meaning of the title “Summary of Ritual” (Quli) refers simply to ritual’s intricate details. As for those who say it was composed at the Qu Terrace, their absurdity …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
誕不經之甚與緇衣之語意倣魯論而作
也然不免援引拘泥其漢儒附會之失與
吕不韋脩月令似也然紀時政而雜災異
嫌於巫史之流而王者四時異居服色悉
依方位則陰陽拘忌之說耳漢博士錄王
制似也然敘爵位而竊軻書不過因襲之
見而官制倣左氏之舊巡狩雜公穀之文
亦影響糟粕之粗耳惡足以知禮經者哉
□□□□□而紛紛究心經學而六經之
===
□□□□□□孟氏雜陰陽災異之說梁丘
本京房數學之流淺之乎言易矣若揚子
雲之太玄司馬光之潛虛則求之愈深而
失之愈遠優劣奚足較耶夏侯講明洪範
徒為希世取寵之資歐陽八世傳書未明
貨寶無總之義其言書可知矣若白居易
之湯征河内女子之泰誓則僭竊之甚而
繆妄之尤正否奚足言耶漢平帝立四家
詩固以申公轅固韓嬰毛公為宗也然申
punctuated: 誕不經之甚與！緇衣之語，意倣魯論而作也，然不免援引拘泥，其漢儒附會之失與！吕不韋脩月令，似也，然紀時政而雜災異，嫌於巫史之流；而王者四時異居，服色悉依方位，則陰陽拘忌之說耳。漢博士錄王制，似也，然敘爵位而竊軻書，不過因襲之見；而官制倣左氏之舊，巡狩雜公穀之文，亦影響糟粕之粗耳，惡足以知禮經者哉！□□□□□而紛紛究心經學，而六經之□□□□□□孟氏雜陰陽災異之說，梁丘本京房數學之流，淺之乎言易矣！若揚子雲之太玄、司馬光之潛虛，則求之愈深而失之愈遠，優劣奚足較耶？夏侯講明洪範，徒為希世取寵之資；歐陽八世傳書，未明貨寶無總之義，其言書可知矣。若白居易之湯征、河内女子之泰誓，則僭竊之甚而繆妄之尤，正否奚足言耶？漢平帝立四家詩，固以申公、轅固、韓嬰、毛公為宗也，然申
translation_en:
…fantastical and contrary to the classics in the extreme! The language of “Black Robes” (Ziyi) was apparently composed in imitation of the Lu version of the Analects. Yet its citations inevitably suffer from rigid literalism—is this not the fault of strained interpretation among Han scholars? That Lü Buwei compiled the “Monthly Ordinances” (Yueling) seems plausible. Yet it records seasonal governmental measures intermingled with accounts of calamities and anomalies, suggesting the work of shamans and scribes. Its prescriptions that the king occupy different quarters in each of the four seasons, and that the colors of his garments conform entirely to the cardinal directions, are merely theories of restrictive yin-yang taboos. That Han Erudites recorded the “Royal Regulations” (Wangzhi) also seems plausible. Yet its account of noble ranks borrows surreptitiously from Meng Ke’s book and amounts to no more than derivative views. Its official institutions imitate the old arrangements in Zuo’s Commentary, while its account of royal inspection tours mixes in passages from the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries. These too are merely crude echoes and dregs. How could they suffice for understanding the classic of ritual?

[Five illegible characters] and they busily devote themselves to classical learning, while the Six Classics’ [six illegible characters; connection uncertain]. Master Meng mixes in theories of yin and yang, calamities, and anomalies; Liangqiu follows the numerological school of Jing Fang [?]. How superficial their discussions of the Changes are! As for Yang Ziyun’s Supreme Mystery (Taixuan) and Sima Guang’s Hidden Void (Qianxu), the deeper their investigations, the farther they stray. What point is there in comparing their relative merits? Xiahou’s exposition of the “Great Plan” (Hongfan) merely provided him with a means of catering to contemporary tastes and winning favor. The Ouyang family transmitted the Documents for eight generations, yet failed to understand the meaning of “do not hoard goods and valuables.” The quality of their discussions of the Documents can thus be judged. As for Bai Juyi’s “Tang’s Campaign” (Tangzheng) and the “Great Declaration” (Taishi) of the woman from Henei, these are extreme instances of fraudulent appropriation and especially flagrant falsehood. What point is there in discussing whether they are correct? Emperor Ping of Han established the four schools of the Odes, taking Master Shen, Yuan Gu, Han Ying, and Master Mao as their respective authorities. Yet Shen…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
言乎適道則未也君子知此而求諸巳方
其無事之際涵養於內者必有不可易之
見以定其守及其事變之遇振作於外者
必有不可奪之氣以鼓其趨夫然後心與
道會道與天會行成而名立心安而德全
矣且夫蘇武之使匈奴猶洪皓之使金也
北海囓雪之苦無異於陰山瘴海之憂雖
其厚功薄賞與夫坐貶殊方均難以病其
忠要之□□□九年之久者其氣猶烈也
===
李密之陳□□歸養猶朱壽昌之棄官尋母
也形影之相弔無異於年久之不知一則
固終餘年之是慮一則不省所恃之爲憂
要皆不失其爲孝獨於少事僞朝之云不
無遺憾也金一也楊震畏四知而不受管
寧見攫金而不顧有所畏於心者終不若
不動於心者之爲優然關西孔子之語子
孫清白之遺而名動一時震亦未可厚非
焉惠一也晏嬰之待火千家范仲淹之給
punctuated:
言乎適道，則未也。君子知此而求諸巳，方其無事之際，涵養於內者，必有不可易之見以定其守；及其事變之遇，振作於外者，必有不可奪之氣以鼓其趨。夫然後心與道會，道與天會，行成而名立，心安而德全矣。
且夫蘇武之使匈奴，猶洪皓之使金也。北海囓雪之苦，無異於陰山瘴海之憂。雖其厚功薄賞，與夫坐貶殊方，均難以病其忠。要之，□□□九年之久者，其氣猶烈也。
李密之陳□□歸養，猶朱壽昌之棄官尋母也。形影之相弔，無異於年久之不知。一則固終餘年之是慮，一則不省所恃之爲憂，要皆不失其爲孝。獨於少事僞朝之云，不無遺憾也。
金一也，楊震畏四知而不受，管寧見攫金而不顧。有所畏於心者，終不若不動於心者之爲優。然關西孔子之語，子孫清白之遺，而名動一時，震亦未可厚非焉。
惠一也，晏嬰之待火千家，范仲淹之給
translation_en:
…As for attaining the Way, however, this falls short. The gentleman understands this and seeks within himself. In times free from affairs, his inward cultivation must rest on an unalterable conviction that steadies his resolve. When he encounters changing circumstances, his outward exertions must possess an indomitable spirit that spurs him forward. Only then does his mind accord with the Way, and the Way with Heaven; his conduct becomes accomplished and his reputation established, his mind at peace and his virtue complete.
Su Wu’s mission to the Xiongnu was like Hong Hao’s mission to the Jin. The hardship of gnawing snow beside the Northern Sea was no different from the suffering amid the Yin Mountains and pestilential seas. Whether great service received scant reward, or a man was punished with relegation to a distant region, neither could impair their loyalty. In sum, even after □□□ nine years [?], his spirit remained ardent.
Li Mi’s submission of □□ requesting to return home to care for his elder [?] was like Zhu Shouchang’s abandonment of office to search for his mother. Having only one’s body and shadow to console each other was no different from remaining ignorant for years of a mother’s whereabouts. The one was concerned to ensure care through the remaining years of his elder’s life; the other grieved at not knowing where his mother—the person on whom he depended—was. Both, in essence, remained filial. Only the statement about serving an illegitimate court in youth leaves some cause for regret.
The gold was the same: Yang Zhen refused it out of concern for the “four who know,” while Guan Ning saw gold being snatched up and paid no heed. Having something to fear in one’s heart is ultimately inferior to remaining inwardly unmoved. Yet Yang Zhen was called the “Confucius west of the passes,” and left his descendants a legacy of moral purity; his fame stirred his age. He should not be censured too severely.
The benevolence was the same: Yan Ying’s care for a thousand households affected by fire [?], and Fan Zhongyan’s provision of…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
此張栻所以惜其進之不能以正也張禹
之在漢庭望重師傅而災異之對陰黨王
氏槐里令朱雲所以欲請尚方之劔也禹
之邪佞可知或譏其不識剛正字者此爾
柳宗元之在柳州惠政流芳而王叔文母
死代𧠀陳情豈固甘心於王伾輩之外黨
耶宗元之悖謬可見或譏其不識節義字
者此爾之數子者人品不同行事亦異千
載而下公□□如是非得失固有不能遁
===
其情者矣□□粤西僻在嶺徼自有郡縣
以來風氣日開人文漸著如覃光佃之忠
言日進彈劾無避其爲臣忠矣而礬蠟召
兵卽募死士以入衛孤軍倍道敢抗金虜
而不辭李珙之忠又難於佃也丁蘭之刻
木祀母每事必稟其爲子孝矣而母喪廬
墓有甘露芝草之祥扁易亭名來蘇軾𧠀
章之美梁詔之孝無媿於蘭也論劉季述
輩而謝病以歸官終侍講者唐之趙觀文
punctuated:
此張栻所以惜其進之不能以正也。張禹之在漢庭，望重師傅，而災異之對，陰黨王氏，槐里令朱雲所以欲請尚方之劔也。禹之邪佞可知，或譏其不識剛正字者，此爾。柳宗元之在柳州，惠政流芳，而王叔文母死，代𧠀陳情，豈固甘心於王伾輩之外黨耶？宗元之悖謬可見，或譏其不識節義字者，此爾。之數子者，人品不同，行事亦異，千載而下，公□□如是非得失，固有不能遁其情者矣。
□□粤西僻在嶺徼，自有郡縣以來，風氣日開，人文漸著。如覃光佃之忠言日進，彈劾無避，其爲臣忠矣。而礬蠟召兵，卽募死士以入衛，孤軍倍道，敢抗金虜而不辭，李珙之忠又難於佃也。丁蘭之刻木祀母，每事必稟，其爲子孝矣。而母喪廬墓，有甘露芝草之祥，扁易亭名，來蘇軾𧠀章之美，梁詔之孝無媿於蘭也。論劉季述輩而謝病以歸，官終侍講者，唐之趙觀文
translation_en:
…This is why Zhang Shi regretted that his advancement had not been achieved through upright means. At the Han court, Zhang Yu enjoyed great prestige as an imperial tutor, yet in his response concerning calamities and anomalies he covertly sided with the Wang clan. This was why Zhu Yun, Magistrate of Huaili, wished to request the sword of the Imperial Manufactories. Zhang Yu’s wickedness and sycophancy are evident; this explains why some mocked him as not understanding the words “firmness and uprightness.” Liu Zongyuan left a lasting reputation for benevolent government in Liuzhou, yet when Wang Shuwen’s mother died, he drafted a memorial on Wang’s behalf setting forth his circumstances. Could he really have willingly become an outside partisan of Wang Pi and his associates? Liu Zongyuan’s perversity and error are apparent; this explains why some mocked him as not understanding the words “integrity and righteousness.” These men differed in character and conduct, yet a thousand years later, public judgment [?], concerning right and wrong, success and failure, still leaves them unable to conceal the truth of their actions.
[Two illegible characters] Guangxi lies remotely on the frontier beyond the mountain ranges. Since commanderies and counties were first established there, its customs have become increasingly enlightened and its cultural accomplishments gradually more conspicuous. Tan Guangdian, for example, offered loyal counsel daily and spared no one in his impeachments: he was indeed loyal as a minister. Yet when a summons for troops arrived by “alum and wax” [?], Li Gong immediately recruited men ready to die to enter and defend the court. With an isolated force, he marched at double speed, daring to resist the Jin invaders without demur. His loyalty was demonstrated under even greater difficulties than Guangdian’s. Ding Lan carved a wooden image of his mother to make offerings to her and reported every matter to it: he was indeed filial as a son. Yet Liang Zhao, upon his mother’s death, lived in a hut beside her grave, where auspicious sweet dew and numinous fungi appeared. A pavilion’s name was changed on its inscribed plaque [?], eliciting an elegant commemorative composition from Su Shi. Liang Zhao’s filial devotion was in no way inferior to Ding Lan’s. The man who denounced Liu Jishu and his associates, then pleaded illness and returned home, ending his official career as an Expositor-in-waiting, was Zhao Guanwen of the Tang…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也因李接攻城而奮兵與戰罵賊以斃者
宋之毛士毅也行不同而節同均之有可
取焉乞歸奉母不受錫賚而請蠲一郡丁
賦者後漢之梁嵩是已郡人立祠以報德
非其人情之感乎買妾憫父惻然遣還而
不索原受直金者有宋之馮商是已竟得
馮京以為嗣非其天道之報乎事不同而
義同均之為可嘉焉之數子者山川靈異
咸鍾其美□□高潔均適乎道忠孝節義
===
信其無愧於古人矣是皆廣右前哲而其
他光明俊偉作於前者殆未易悉舉唯論
世尚友者能自師法云爾極而論之則前
數子者皆一行一事之美適于道者或寡
矣必如周公之忠然後可以為忠之至所
謂赤舃几几德音不瑕者是已必如大舜
之孝然後可以為孝之至所謂為法於天
下可傳於後世者是已必如泰伯之節與
夫夷齊之義然後可以為節義之至所謂
punctuated:
也。因李接攻城而奮兵與戰，罵賊以斃者，宋之毛士毅也。行不同而節同，均之有可取焉。乞歸奉母，不受錫賚，而請蠲一郡丁賦者，後漢之梁嵩是已。郡人立祠以報德，非其人情之感乎？買妾憫父，惻然遣還，而不索原受直金者，有宋之馮商是已。竟得馮京以為嗣，非其天道之報乎？事不同而義同，均之為可嘉焉。之數子者，山川靈異，咸鍾其美，□□高潔，均適乎道。忠孝節義，信其無愧於古人矣。是皆廣右前哲，而其他光明俊偉作於前者，殆未易悉舉，唯論世尚友者能自師法云爾。
極而論之，則前數子者，皆一行一事之美，適于道者或寡矣。必如周公之忠，然後可以為忠之至，所謂「赤舃几几，德音不瑕」者是已。必如大舜之孝，然後可以為孝之至，所謂「為法於天下，可傳於後世」者是已。必如泰伯之節與夫夷齊之義，然後可以為節義之至，所謂
translation_en:
…was he. The man who, when Li Jie attacked the city, rallied his troops to fight him and died reviling the rebels was Mao Shiyi of the Song. Their deeds differed, but their integrity was the same; both had something worthy of emulation. The man who begged leave to return home to attend his mother, declined imperial gifts, and instead requested remission of the poll tax for an entire commandery was Liang Song of the Later Han. The people of the commandery erected a shrine to repay his kindness: was this not an expression of their heartfelt gratitude? The man who bought a concubine, took pity on her father, and compassionately sent her back without demanding repayment of the purchase money [?] was Feng Shang of the Song. He ultimately gained Feng Jing as his heir: was this not Heaven’s recompense? Their deeds differed, but their righteousness was the same; both were praiseworthy. In these men, the numinous powers of mountains and rivers concentrated all their excellence. [Two illegible characters] lofty and pure, they all accorded with the Way. In loyalty, filial piety, integrity, and righteousness, they were indeed worthy of the ancients. These were all worthy predecessors of Guangyou; the other illustrious and outstanding men who arose in earlier times can scarcely all be enumerated. Only those who consider the age in which the ancients lived and befriend them across time can take them as their own teachers and models.
Yet, considered in the fullest sense, the men mentioned above each possessed the excellence of a single practice or deed; the respects in which they accorded with the Way may have been few. Only loyalty such as that of the Duke of Zhou can be called loyalty in its highest form. This is what is meant by: “His red ceremonial shoes were dignified; his virtuous reputation was without blemish.” Only filial piety such as that of the great Shun can be called filial piety in its highest form. This is what is meant by: “He serves as a model for all under Heaven, fit to be handed down to later generations.” Only integrity such as that of Taibo and righteousness such as that of Boyi and Shuqi can be called integrity and righteousness in their highest forms. This is what is meant by…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
無得而稱求仁而得仁者是已是數聖賢
者道全而德備體立而用行遇君則爲忠
遇親則爲孝遇事變之來則爲節爲義不
思不勉從容中道蓋易地而皆然者也顧
士之所自擇者當何如亦曰取法乎上而
已矣雖然人秉天地之正氣與元氣相爲
流通三代以前道德隆盛泰和之氣渾厚
未鑿是故後先相望無非忠孝節義之士
粹乎其□□也三代以後道衰德薄人漸
===
澆漓故當□□忠孝節義者寥寥僅見可取
者少而可議者多亦其時勢然也於乎三
代以前之士吾不得而見得見如蘇武韓
愈范仲淹其人亦可矣蘇韓范三子吾不
得而見得見如丁蘭管寧楊震以下諸君
子亦可矣論人至此不能不重有所感云
第四問
鍾徠秀
考試官教諭林 批 條陳先正之賢補救今日之急識
punctuated:
無得而稱」、「求仁而得仁」者是已。是數聖賢者，道全而德備，體立而用行；遇君則爲忠，遇親則爲孝，遇事變之來則爲節、爲義，不思不勉，從容中道，蓋易地而皆然者也。顧士之所自擇者當何如？亦曰取法乎上而已矣。雖然，人秉天地之正氣，與元氣相爲流通。三代以前，道德隆盛，泰和之氣渾厚未鑿，是故後先相望，無非忠孝節義之士，粹乎其□□也。三代以後，道衰德薄，人漸澆漓，故當□□，忠孝節義者寥寥僅見，可取者少，而可議者多，亦其時勢然也。於乎！三代以前之士，吾不得而見，得見如蘇武、韓愈、范仲淹其人亦可矣。蘇、韓、范三子，吾不得而見，得見如丁蘭、管寧、楊震以下諸君子亦可矣。論人至此，不能不重有所感云。
第四問
鍾徠秀
考試官教諭林批：條陳先正之賢，補救今日之急，識
translation_en:
…“none could find words adequate to praise him” and “they sought benevolence and attained it”: these sayings describe them. These sages and worthies possessed the Way in its entirety and virtue in its fullness; their fundamental substance was established and its functions put into practice. In serving their rulers they showed loyalty; in serving their parents, filial devotion; when confronted with changing circumstances, integrity and righteousness. Without deliberation or effort, they naturally accorded with the Way. Had they exchanged places, each would have acted likewise. What, then, should a scholar choose for himself? Simply to take the highest as his model.
Nevertheless, human beings receive the upright vital energy of Heaven and Earth, which circulates in communion with primordial vital energy. Before the end of the Three Dynasties, the Way and virtue flourished, and the vital energy of supreme harmony remained abundant and unspoiled. Thus successive generations abounded in men of loyalty, filial devotion, integrity, and righteousness, pure in their □□ [?]. After the Three Dynasties, the Way declined, virtue weakened, and people gradually became shallow and insincere. Thus, amid □□ [?], men of loyalty, filial devotion, integrity, and righteousness were rarely seen. Few deserved approval, while many invited criticism: this, too, resulted from the circumstances of their times.
Alas! I cannot meet the scholars of the Three Dynasties and earlier; to meet men like Su Wu, Han Yu, and Fan Zhongyan would suffice. I cannot meet those three—Su, Han, and Fan; to meet worthy men such as Ding Lan, Guan Ning, Yang Zhen, and the others ranked below them would also suffice. Having discussed men to this point, I cannot help feeling deeply moved once again.
Fourth Policy Question
Zhong Laixiu
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: You systematically set forth the virtues of earlier worthies to remedy the urgent problems of today. Your discernment…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
如子言地方仰賴錄之
考試官教授詹批守令將帥在粵西尤急而貴於得
人子能較量不爽區畫周悉其識時務者乎
善爲治者能立天下之法而後天下之治
成善用法者能操天下之機而後天下之
法裕夫法立則可循機操則可久而古先
哲王所以長治久安凡有法以爲聯屬人
心之具而通變不窮與時偕行則又視法
之所趨□亟反而善調之非法則無所
===
依據將紛□而莫吾一非機以運之于中
吾見法敝而治亦隨之矣是可與語治哉
蓋嘗聞之書曰德惟善政政在養民言牧
民之良也詩曰文武吉甫萬邦爲憲言將
兵之善也是故三代而上治出于一州牧
侯伯皆惟其人無事則爲卿有事則爲將
此所以愛植甘棠績歌采芑召公之德方
叔之休至今猶爲美談自郡縣置而守令
設兵農分而將相不兼矣然亦未嘗借才
punctuated:
如子言，地方仰賴，錄之。

考試官教授詹批：守令將帥，在粵西尤急，而貴於得人。子能較量不爽，區畫周悉，其識時務者乎！

善爲治者，能立天下之法，而後天下之治成；善用法者，能操天下之機，而後天下之法裕。夫法立則可循，機操則可久，而古先哲王所以長治久安，凡有法以爲聯屬人心之具，而通變不窮，與時偕行，則又視法之所趨，□亟反而善調之。非法則無所依據，將紛□而莫吾一；非機以運之于中，吾見法敝而治亦隨之矣。是可與語治哉？

蓋嘗聞之，《書》曰：「德惟善政，政在養民。」言牧民之良也。《詩》曰：「文武吉甫，萬邦爲憲。」言將兵之善也。是故三代而上，治出于一，州牧侯伯，皆惟其人。無事則爲卿，有事則爲將。此所以愛植甘棠，績歌采芑，召公之德、方叔之休，至今猶爲美談。自郡縣置而守令設，兵農分而將相不兼矣。然亦未嘗借才
translation_en:
…If matters are as you say, the locality will benefit from them. Admit this essay to the record.

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Instructor: In western Guangxi, the appointment of prefects, magistrates, and military commanders is especially urgent; what matters is finding the right men. Your assessments are accurate, and your plans comprehensive. Surely you understand the needs of the times!

Those skilled in governing can establish laws for all under Heaven, and only then is orderly government achieved. Those skilled in applying laws can grasp the pivotal means of action throughout the realm, and only then do its laws allow ample scope. Once laws are established, they can be followed; once these pivotal means are grasped, government can endure. The wise kings of antiquity achieved lasting order and peace by using laws as instruments to bind people’s hearts together. Yet their inexhaustible adaptation to change and their ability to move with the times also depended on observing the direction in which the laws were tending, … swiftly reversing course and adjusting them effectively [?]. Without laws there would be nothing to rely upon: affairs would become confused [?], with nothing to bring them into unity. Without the pivotal means operating within them, I would see the laws deteriorate and government decline along with them. Could this be called an understanding of government?

I have heard it said in the Book of Documents: “Virtue consists in good government; government lies in nourishing the people.” This speaks of excellence in tending the people. The Book of Odes says: “Jifu, accomplished in civil and military affairs, is a model for the myriad states.” This speaks of excellence in commanding troops. Thus, in the Three Dynasties and earlier, government issued from a single source, and regional governors and the lords who led the domains were all chosen for their fitness. In peaceful times they served as ministers; when trouble arose they served as generals. Hence affection cherished the sweet pear tree, and achievements were sung in “Gathering Millet.” The virtue of the Duke of Shao and the excellence of Fang Shu remain celebrated to this day. Once commanderies and counties were established, prefects and magistrates were appointed; once soldiers and farmers were separated, military command and ministerial office were no longer held jointly. Yet there was never any need to borrow talent…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
於異代也以守令言之京師蒙福世祖所
以獎郭伋也願借一年河内所以留寇恂
也麥穗兩岐張堪所以守漁陽也化致三
異魯恭所以令中牟也宋均守九江虎爲
却走岑熈守魏郡犬不驚吠非有善政能
如是乎其視卓茂之力行敎化而民不忍
欺董宣之鋤擊豪強而人不敢犯賈敦實
之政尚清淨而民不見吏張允濟之治從
寛簡而路□拾遺治效淺深固較然矣以
===
將帥言之□□據函谷雄虎視於山東李
牧在鴈門絕胡騎於塞北三十餘年秦兵
不加廉頗之重趙也一人不戮江南自下
曹彬之取唐也非有勇略能如是乎其視
祭遵之取用儒術雅歌投壺羊祜之恩信
服人輕裘緩帶郭汾陽之威德素著單騎
見虜范文正之甲兵數萬西賊破膽事爲
優劣自可觀矣故嘗謂郭寇張堪宋岑能
吏也魯恭能而良者也卓董賈張其循良
punctuated:
於異代也。以守令言之，京師蒙福，世祖所以獎郭伋也；願借一年，河内所以留寇恂也；麥穗兩岐，張堪所以守漁陽也；化致三異，魯恭所以令中牟也。宋均守九江，虎爲却走；岑熈守魏郡，犬不驚吠。非有善政，能如是乎？其視卓茂之力行敎化而民不忍欺，董宣之鋤擊豪強而人不敢犯，賈敦實之政尚清淨而民不見吏，張允濟之治從寛簡而路□拾遺，治效淺深固較然矣。
以將帥言之，□□據函谷，雄虎視於山東；李牧在鴈門，絕胡騎於塞北。三十餘年秦兵不加，廉頗之重趙也；一人不戮，江南自下，曹彬之取唐也。非有勇略，能如是乎？其視祭遵之取用儒術，雅歌投壺；羊祜之恩信服人，輕裘緩帶；郭汾陽之威德素著，單騎見虜；范文正之甲兵數萬，西賊破膽，事爲優劣自可觀矣。
故嘗謂郭、寇、張堪、宋、岑，能吏也；魯恭，能而良者也；卓、董、賈、張，其循良
translation_en:
…from other ages, either. Speaking of prefects and magistrates: “The capital enjoys blessings”—this was how Emperor Shizu commended Guo Ji; “Let us borrow him for one more year”—this was how the people of Henei sought to retain Kou Xun. Wheat bore double ears under Zhang Kan’s administration of Yuyang, and moral transformation brought about three prodigies under Lu Gong’s administration of Zhongmou. When Song Jun governed Jiujiang, tigers withdrew; when Cen Xi governed Wei Commandery, dogs did not bark in alarm. Without good government, could such things have been achieved? Compare them with Zhuo Mao, who vigorously promoted moral instruction so that the people could not bear to deceive him; Dong Xuan, who rooted out and struck down powerful bullies so that people dared not transgress; Jia Dunshi, whose administration prized tranquility and freedom from interference, so that the people scarcely saw an official; and Zhang Yunji, whose government followed lenient and simple practices, so that lost articles on the road were not pocketed [?]. The relative depth of their achievements in government is surely clear.
Speaking of commanders: □□ [?] held Hangu Pass, gazing with tiger-like might over the lands east of the mountains; Li Mu, stationed at Yanmen, kept the Hu cavalry beyond the northern frontier. For more than thirty years Qin’s troops did not attack: such was the strength Lian Po gave Zhao. Not one person was executed, and Jiangnan submitted of its own accord: such was Cao Bin’s conquest of Southern Tang. Without courage and strategic skill, could such things have been achieved? Compare them with Ji Zun, who employed Confucian methods, sang refined songs, and played pitch-pot; Yang Hu, who won people’s submission through kindness and trustworthiness, wearing light furs and a loosely fastened sash; Guo, Prince of Fenyang, whose authority and virtue were long renowned, and who rode alone to meet the enemy; and Fan Wenzheng, whose tens of thousands of armored troops struck terror into the western foes. The relative merits of their deeds can be seen for themselves.
Thus I have often said: Guo Ji, Kou Xun, Zhang Kan, Song Jun, and Cen Xi were capable officials; Lu Gong was both capable and good; Zhuo Mao, Dong Xuan, Jia Dunshi, and Zhang Yunji, as exemplary and benevolent officials…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之儔匹與王李廉頗勇將也曹彬勇而仁
者也祭羊郭范其儒將之翹楚與我
國家以
神武定天下以
文德致太平憲
天立法酌古垂制布列郡縣者旣藹藹之吉人
守禦封疆者又赳赳之武士故百八十餘
年内安外謐文煕武恬眞匹休隆古三代
之盛而陋□□唐宋于下風者由此其選也
===
試舉其績□□嶺西者如章復之守桂林課
農興學百廢具舉暇日則行飮射讀法之
禮大旱則有每禱輒雨之應何源之守梧
州時値饑饉議欲請賑源恐待報之無及
乃亟捐俸以活民若張霖之宰馬平則有
愛民如子之心有感神捕虎之驗恩信孚
於峒賊衣冠化其強暴此三子者皆守令
之賢而章復則尤能以禮讓爲政敎有古
循良之風其與龔遂黃霸之治渤穎卓茂
punctuated:
之儔匹與？王李廉頗，勇將也；曹彬，勇而仁者也；祭羊郭范，其儒將之翹楚與？我國家以神武定天下，以文德致太平，憲天立法，酌古垂制。布列郡縣者，旣藹藹之吉人；守禦封疆者，又赳赳之武士。故百八十餘年，内安外謐，文煕武恬，眞匹休隆古三代之盛，而陋□□唐宋于下風者，由此其選也。

試舉其績□□嶺西者，如章復之守桂林，課農興學，百廢具舉；暇日則行飮射讀法之禮，大旱則有每禱輒雨之應。何源之守梧州，時値饑饉，議欲請賑，源恐待報之無及，乃亟捐俸以活民。若張霖之宰馬平，則有愛民如子之心，有感神捕虎之驗，恩信孚於峒賊，衣冠化其強暴。此三子者皆守令之賢，而章復則尤能以禮讓爲政敎，有古循良之風。其與龔遂黃霸之治渤穎、卓茂
translation_en:
…were they not their peers? Wang, Li, and Lian Po were courageous generals; Cao Bin was courageous and humane. Were Ji, Yang, Guo, and Fan not outstanding among Confucian generals? Our dynasty settled all under Heaven through divine martial prowess and brought about great peace through civil virtue. It modeled its laws on Heaven and weighed ancient precedents in establishing its institutions. Those stationed throughout the prefectures and counties have been a flourishing company of worthy men; those defending the frontiers have likewise been valiant warriors. Thus, for more than 180 years, there has been security within and tranquility without, flourishing civil government and peace in military affairs. Truly, this equals the splendid prosperity of the Three Dynasties of high antiquity, relegating [illegible] and the Tang and Song to an inferior position—all owing to such selections of men [?].

Let us cite some whose achievements [illegible] in Lingxi. As prefect of Guilin, Zhang Fu encouraged agriculture and promoted learning, restoring every neglected undertaking. In his leisure he conducted the ceremonies of communal drinking, archery, and reading the laws aloud. During severe droughts, his prayers were answered with rain every time. When He Yuan was prefect of Wuzhou, famine struck. There was discussion of requesting relief, but Yuan feared that waiting for a reply would make it too late, so he promptly contributed his salary to keep the people alive. As magistrate of Maping, Zhang Lin loved the people as his own children, and his sincerity moved the spirits, as demonstrated by the capture of a tiger. His kindness and trustworthiness won the confidence of the bandits of the mountain settlements, while his civilizing influence transformed their violent ways. These three were all worthy prefects and magistrates. Zhang Fu in particular made ritual propriety and deference the basis of government and instruction, possessing the spirit of the conscientious and benevolent officials of antiquity. Compared with Gong Sui and Huang Ba in their administration of Bohai and Yingchuan, and Zhuo Mao …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
魯恭之治密牟蓋相伯仲矣又如楊璟以
征南將軍攻克靜江戒張彬之屠戮下剽
掠之禁令卒致土官遣使齎印來降山雲
以總兵掛印出鎭廣西臨戰陳則身先士
卒持廉介則秋毫無犯卒致蠻夷懾服居
民安堵若江陰侯吳良之討兩江五谿懷
之以恩德招之以納款洞寨二百餘所悉
爲編戶興師不踰四月遂定古州此三子
者皆將帥之良而山雲則尤能以威信馭
===
土官有古□將之風其與馬援之在漢韓
世忠岳飛之在宋蓋相頡頏矣嗟乎宜於
古者或不宜於今遠有所慕者則近或有
所遺郭伋王剪之輩歷世遠矣姑舍是也
章復諸子非守令之法則乎山雲諸子非
將帥之軌範乎誠使今之爲守令者貪墨
是懲每先公而後私怠荒必戒不見利而
忘義勸相以時而賦稅以平優恤其財而
愛養其力常體乎節用愛人之意則居者
punctuated:
魯恭之治密牟，蓋相伯仲矣。又如楊璟以征南將軍攻克靜江，戒張彬之屠戮，下剽掠之禁令，卒致土官遣使齎印來降。山雲以總兵掛印出鎭廣西，臨戰陳則身先士卒，持廉介則秋毫無犯，卒致蠻夷懾服，居民安堵。若江陰侯吳良之討兩江五谿，懷之以恩德，招之以納款，洞寨二百餘所悉爲編戶，興師不踰四月，遂定古州。此三子者皆將帥之良，而山雲則尤能以威信馭土官，有古□將之風。其與馬援之在漢、韓世忠岳飛之在宋，蓋相頡頏矣。
嗟乎！宜於古者或不宜於今，遠有所慕者則近或有所遺。郭伋王剪之輩歷世遠矣，姑舍是也。章復諸子非守令之法則乎？山雲諸子非將帥之軌範乎？誠使今之爲守令者貪墨是懲，每先公而後私，怠荒必戒，不見利而忘義，勸相以時而賦稅以平，優恤其財而愛養其力，常體乎節用愛人之意，則居者
translation_en:
…and Lu Gong’s administration of Mi and Mou, they were surely on a par. Consider also Yang Jing, who, as General Who Subdues the South, captured Jingjiang, warned Zhang Bin against slaughter, and issued orders prohibiting plunder. In the end, the native officials sent envoys bearing their seals to surrender. Shan Yun, as Regional Commander, assumed his seal of command and went out to defend Guangxi. In battle formations he placed himself before his officers and soldiers; in maintaining integrity and uprightness, he would not encroach upon even a hair’s breadth of others’ property. In the end, the non-Han peoples submitted in awe, and the inhabitants lived securely. Likewise, when Wu Liang, Marquis of Jiangyin, campaigned against the Two Rivers and Five Streams, he won them over through kindness and virtue and summoned them to offer allegiance. More than two hundred cave settlements and stockaded villages were all incorporated into the household registers. Within four months of mobilizing his forces, he had pacified Guzhou. These three men were all excellent commanders, but Shan Yun was especially adept at governing native officials through authority and trustworthiness, displaying the spirit of the ancient [?] generals. He surely ranked alongside Ma Yuan of the Han and Han Shizhong and Yue Fei of the Song.
Alas! What was suitable in antiquity may not be suitable today; those who admire distant examples may overlook those close at hand. Men such as Guo Ji and Wang Jian lived many generations ago; let us set them aside for now. Are not Zhang Fu and the others models for prefects and magistrates? Are not Shan Yun and the others exemplars for military commanders? If only today’s prefects and magistrates would curb corruption, always put public interests before private ones, guard against negligence, and never forget righteousness at the sight of profit; if they would encourage and assist farming at the proper seasons, levy taxes equitably, take solicitous care of the people’s resources and conserve their strength, and constantly embody the principle of frugality in expenditure and love for the people, then those who remain in their homes…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有樂土之願逃者有復業之望又何戶口
流亡之足患哉爲將帥者公以奉法而衛
士不爲私門之役廉以蒞官而軍貲不爲
房闥之需督其屯種而斂納以時嚴其簡
敎而賞罰惟信常念乎士卒甘苦之同則
居常而結其歡心遇變而得其死力又何
盜賊充斥之足慮哉然此特論其槩耳若
夫粤西邊鄙民之生于其地者其害尤倍
于中州山□□而墾田寡也賊繁而角奪甚
===
也法廢而□横興也食衆而生產微也所
賴官于其地者爲之啓利而損害耳不然
中谷之歎興六月之師動邊民其終魚鱉
乎必于守令也超遷不拘于資格考覈靡
徇于愛憎如卓茂令密邑而以爲太傅張
平長全椒而以爲議郎可也不惑于卽墨
之毀言日至致察于膠東之戶口僞增可
也而又遴選近地沙汰老弱使風氣相宜
精神不倦庶得以安其位而行其志民患
punctuated:
有樂土之願，逃者有復業之望，又何戶口流亡之足患哉？爲將帥者，公以奉法，而衛士不爲私門之役；廉以蒞官，而軍貲不爲房闥之需；督其屯種，而斂納以時；嚴其簡敎，而賞罰惟信；常念乎士卒甘苦之同，則居常而結其歡心，遇變而得其死力，又何盜賊充斥之足慮哉？然此特論其槩耳。
若夫粤西邊鄙，民之生于其地者，其害尤倍于中州。山□□而墾田寡也，賊繁而角奪甚也，法廢而□横興也，食衆而生產微也。所賴官于其地者，爲之啓利而損害耳。不然，《中谷》之歎興，《六月》之師動，邊民其終魚鱉乎？必于守令也，超遷不拘于資格，考覈靡徇于愛憎。如卓茂令密邑而以爲太傅，張平長全椒而以爲議郎，可也；不惑于卽墨之毀言日至，致察于膠東之戶口僞增，可也。而又遴選近地，沙汰老弱，使風氣相宜，精神不倦，庶得以安其位而行其志，民患
translation_en:
…may hope to dwell in a happy land, while those who have fled may hope to resume their livelihoods. What cause, then, would there be to worry about households fleeing? Those serving as commanders should uphold the law impartially, so that guardsmen are not employed in service to private households; administer their offices incorruptibly, so that military funds do not supply the needs of their inner chambers; oversee military farming and collect its produce at the proper times; rigorously conduct troop selection and training, and ensure that rewards and punishments are reliable. If they constantly remember to share their soldiers’ hardships and comforts, they will win their affection in ordinary times and secure their willingness to fight to the death in emergencies. What cause, then, would there be to fear bandits overrunning the land? Yet these are only general observations.
As for the frontier districts of western Guangxi, the people born there suffer harms far greater than those in the central regions. The mountains are [two characters illegible], and cultivated fields are few; bandits are numerous, and competition and plunder are severe; the laws have fallen into disuse, and [illegible] lawlessness flourishes [?]; mouths to feed are many, and production is meager. Their sole reliance is on those holding office there to open up sources of benefit and reduce their hardships. Otherwise, the lament of “In the Valley” will arise and the armies of “The Sixth Month” will be mobilized: will the frontier people ultimately become fish and turtles? In the case of prefects and magistrates, exceptional promotion must not be constrained by formal qualifications, and performance evaluations must not yield to personal likes and dislikes. It would be fitting to follow the examples of Zhuo Mao, who was magistrate of Mi and was made Grand Mentor, and Zhang Ping, who headed Quanjiao and was made Court Gentleman for Consultation. It would likewise be fitting to remain undeceived by the slanders against the magistrate of Jimo that arrived daily, and to scrutinize the falsely inflated household and population figures of Jiaodong. Furthermore, officials should be selected from nearby areas, and the old and infirm weeded out, so that they are suited to the local climate and customs and remain vigorous in spirit. They may then be secure in their posts and carry out their intentions, and the people’s afflictions…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其有瘳乎于將帥也爵必視其功績任必
擇其智勇如范仲淹所謂搜羅班中試以
武藝歐陽脩所謂校其軍中拔爲大將可
也申武學之教不視爲虚文嚴臨陣之法
以驗其實用可也而又勿奪其權少繩以
法使鼓舞有方展布如意庶得以畢其技
而効其長民生其有賴乎是謂通其法于
不窮識其重而亟反之者也有復受直怠
事而不思□□以宣力布武者非夫也昔漢
===
文帝患匈奴難制而拊髀以思頗牧宣帝
稱良二千石欲與共圖治理故漢世良吏
爲盛而良將亦多享國長乆夷狄無患有
以也我
皇上明見萬里屢頒
綸音軫念遐陬凡所以
立天下之法
操天下之機以生以衛此粵西之民者無所
不至矣則夫厝斯民於袵席襁褓之安而
punctuated:
其有瘳乎？于將帥也，爵必視其功績，任必擇其智勇。如范仲淹所謂搜羅班中，試以武藝，歐陽脩所謂校其軍中，拔爲大將，可也。申武學之教，不視爲虚文；嚴臨陣之法，以驗其實用，可也。而又勿奪其權，少繩以法，使鼓舞有方，展布如意，庶得以畢其技而効其長，民生其有賴乎？是謂通其法于不窮，識其重而亟反之者也。有復受直怠事，而不思□□以宣力布武者，非夫也。
昔漢文帝患匈奴難制，而拊髀以思頗牧；宣帝稱良二千石，欲與共圖治理。故漢世良吏爲盛，而良將亦多，享國長乆，夷狄無患，有以也。我皇上明見萬里，屢頒綸音，軫念遐陬，凡所以立天下之法、操天下之機，以生以衛此粵西之民者，無所不至矣。則夫厝斯民於袵席襁褓之安而
translation_en:
…might these afflictions be cured? As for commanders, noble rank must depend on their achievements, and appointments must be made by selecting for wisdom and courage. One might follow Fan Zhongyan’s proposal to seek men out from among the ranks and test their martial skills, or Ouyang Xiu’s proposal to assess men within the army and promote them to high command. One might reinforce instruction in military studies, refusing to treat it as an empty formality, and enforce strict rules for facing the enemy, thereby testing their practical effectiveness. Furthermore, commanders should not be deprived of their authority, and legal restraints upon them should be kept few, so that they can inspire their men effectively and carry out their plans as intended. Thus they might fully exercise their skills and put their strengths to use. Would not the people’s livelihood then have something to depend upon? This is what it means to make institutions work without exhaustion, recognize what matters most, and promptly return to it. Anyone who still draws his pay while neglecting his duties, without giving thought to □□ [?] so as to exert himself in service and deploy military force, is no worthy man.
In former times, Emperor Wen of Han, troubled by the difficulty of controlling the Xiongnu, slapped his thigh and longed for men like Lian Po and Li Mu. Emperor Xuan praised good officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank and wished to work with them to achieve good government. Thus, under the Han, good civil officials flourished and good generals were also numerous. There was a reason why the dynasty endured so long and suffered no trouble from the non-Chinese peoples. Our sovereign sees clearly across ten thousand li, repeatedly issues imperial pronouncements, and shows compassionate concern for remote regions. In establishing laws for all under Heaven and controlling the crucial workings of government, he has left nothing undone to sustain and protect these people of Yuexi [Guangxi]. Thus, to settle these people in security like that of bedding and swaddling clothes, and …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
忠誠圖報以永紓
國家南顧之勤者守令事也將帥責也守令
得人則民安食足將帥可無事矣將帥得
人則兵強盜息守令可卧治矣而所以監
督守令將帥者尤不可不加之意焉昔人
有言太守吏民之本又曰禹稷伊尹之志
苟得一縣亦可小試孫子古之良將也其
言曰視卒如嬰兒可與赴深谿視卒如愛
子可與之俱死知此則知守令之可以行
===
吾志而將帥之可以成功矣竊嘗因是而
有感焉論治非難識體為難如有用我願
執此以往執事以為何如
第五問
唐文迪
同考試官學正吳批談要害如親歷論經畧如宿將非
徒以文事鳴者
考試官教諭林批有識見有區畫可與論兵矣斯粤
西休兵之助乎
punctuated:
忠誠圖報，以永紓國家南顧之勤者，守令事也，將帥責也。守令得人，則民安食足，將帥可無事矣；將帥得人，則兵強盜息，守令可卧治矣。而所以監督守令將帥者，尤不可不加之意焉。昔人有言：「太守，吏民之本。」又曰：「禹稷伊尹之志，苟得一縣，亦可小試。」孫子，古之良將也，其言曰：「視卒如嬰兒，可與赴深谿；視卒如愛子，可與之俱死。」知此，則知守令之可以行吾志，而將帥之可以成功矣。竊嘗因是而有感焉：論治非難，識體為難。如有用我，願執此以往。執事以為何如？

第五問
唐文迪

同考試官學正吳批：談要害如親歷，論經畧如宿將，非徒以文事鳴者。

考試官教諭林批：有識見，有區畫，可與論兵矣。斯粤西休兵之助乎？
translation_en:
…to seek loyally and sincerely to repay the state's favor, and thereby relieve it permanently of its anxious concern for the south: this is the task of prefects and county magistrates and the responsibility of military commanders. When prefects and magistrates are well chosen, the people are secure and provisions plentiful, and commanders can be free of trouble. When commanders are well chosen, the troops are strong and banditry ceases, and prefects and magistrates can govern at ease. Particular care must therefore be given to those charged with supervising prefects, magistrates, and commanders.

An ancient saying declares: “The prefect is the foundation of officials and people.” Another says: “With the aspirations of Yu, Ji, and Yi Yin, even someone entrusted with a single county can put them to the test on a small scale.” Master Sun was an excellent commander of antiquity. He said: “Regard your soldiers as infants, and you can go with them into deep ravines; regard your soldiers as beloved sons, and you can face death together with them.” Understanding this, one understands that serving as a prefect or magistrate offers a means to put one's aspirations into practice, and serving as a commander offers a means to accomplish great deeds. These considerations have prompted this reflection in me: discussing government is not difficult; discerning its essentials is difficult. If someone were to employ me, I would wish to proceed on these principles. What do you, honored examiners, think?

Fifth Policy Question
Tang Wendi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: He discusses strategic points as though he had visited them himself, and military planning like a veteran commander. He is not someone distinguished merely for literary accomplishments.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: He has discernment and practical plans; he is someone with whom one can discuss military affairs. Might this help bring an end to warfare in Guangxi?

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授詹批論兵策多出卓見非苟言者取之
蓋聞之才智之士有志于興世務豈徒然
哉明以照之隱微以疏解而通健以决之
礙塞以摧廓而裕是故天下無難處之事
無不可成之功惟夫見之弗審則疑疑則
阻廢墜之弊生矣行之弗勇則玩玩則弛
偏枯之患成矣易曰動而明雷電合而章
言威照之不可以已也經世務者亦于此
求之而已矣夫廣西亦飫壤也土田腴而
===
易耨山藪□而多產江四出而泉貨可通
民近質而繁訟罔作然而今日徵兵明日
理餉終歲文移強半居此此其故何哉無
亦諸夷爲之擾擾爾休兵偃武旣無其期
則治兵講武張皇而稽謀也者安可一日
忘
皇祖之訓哉且夷不可化而內邪然谷永恩信
烏滸冠帶國麒納土慶遠服屬是其樂生
之心與中國同也夷不可屏而外邪伏波
punctuated:
考試官敎授詹批：論兵策，多出卓見，非苟言者，取之。
蓋聞之，才智之士有志于興世務，豈徒然哉？明以照之，隱微以疏解而通；健以决之，礙塞以摧廓而裕。是故天下無難處之事，無不可成之功。惟夫見之弗審則疑，疑則阻，廢墜之弊生矣；行之弗勇則玩，玩則弛，偏枯之患成矣。《易》曰：「動而明，雷電合而章。」言威照之不可以已也。經世務者，亦于此求之而已矣。夫廣西亦飫壤也，土田腴而易耨，山藪□而多產，江四出而泉貨可通，民近質而繁訟罔作。然而今日徵兵，明日理餉，終歲文移，強半居此。此其故何哉？無亦諸夷爲之擾擾爾。休兵偃武旣無其期，則治兵講武、張皇而稽謀也者，安可一日忘皇祖之訓哉？且夷不可化而內邪？然谷永恩信，烏滸冠帶；國麒納土，慶遠服屬。是其樂生之心與中國同也。夷不可屏而外邪？伏波
translation_en:
Examiner Zhan, Instructor, comments: “This essay on military policy frequently offers outstanding insights. These are no idle remarks. Accept it.”
I have heard that when men of talent and wisdom aspire to advance the affairs of the age, their aspirations are surely not in vain. Illuminate matters with discernment, and what is hidden and obscure can be unravelled and made clear; resolve them with vigor, and obstructions can be broken down to leave ample room for action. Thus, under Heaven there are no affairs too difficult to manage and no achievements impossible to accomplish. Yet insufficiently careful judgment produces doubt; doubt produces obstruction, and the evils of neglect and failure arise. Insufficient courage in action produces carelessness; carelessness produces laxity, and the affliction of uneven development takes shape. The Book of Changes says: “Movement accompanied by clarity: thunder and lightning unite and shine forth.” This means that neither the exercise of authority nor discerning illumination may cease. Those who manage the affairs of the age need only seek their guidance here.
Guangxi, too, is a land of abundance [?]. Its fields are fertile and easy to weed; its mountains and marshes are [illegible] and yield plentiful products. Its rivers extend in all directions, allowing money and goods to circulate. Its people incline toward simplicity, and numerous lawsuits do not arise. Yet today troops are levied, tomorrow military provisions are arranged, and throughout the year more than half the official correspondence concerns these matters. Why is this? Is it not simply because the various non-Han peoples cause disturbances? Since there is no prospect of resting the troops and laying down arms, how could we, even for a single day, forget the Imperial Ancestor’s injunctions concerning the ordering of troops, the practice of military arts, the vigorous assertion of authority, and the deliberation of plans?
Moreover, can these peoples not be transformed and brought within the realm? Yet through Gu Yong’s benevolence and good faith, the Wuhu adopted caps and girdles; Guoqi surrendered his territory, and Qingyuan submitted to our rule. Thus their desire to live is the same as that of the people of the Central Kingdom. Can these peoples not be driven back and kept outside? The General Who Subdues the Waves…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
標銅柱遠人稽首武襄度崑崙智高喪魄
是其畏死之心與中國同也夫樂生畏死
彼旣與木石殊則所以制馭而羈縻之者
必有道矣執事謂三江之議紛紛未一此
非愚生所得聞也然耳目所及則有可言
者請得而終言之廣西之有三江是締絡
之大經而風氣之攸萃也然其地則廣矣
西極融洛南抵交阯北分湘源東帶蒼梧
其間郡縣之錯置堡寨之聯綿誠足以壯
===
雄偉之圖扼衝要之津矣然山麓險阻或
不足容方軌林木茂密或不勝施剪伐近
地犖确而不可田則屯戍弗便也峻嶺斗
析而不易達則樵牧弗便也是以盜賊窟
穴其間夷性無恒喜人怒獸未可常理格
而爲害滋蔓矣今舉左右兩江觀之自斷
藤平而左江之患十減其七何也山遠而
淵藪失憑江闊而踪跡易露舊日之峽爲
無人之境矣故謂左江一帶經畫已定不
punctuated: 標銅柱，遠人稽首；武襄度崑崙，智高喪魄。是其畏死之心與中國同也。夫樂生畏死，彼旣與木石殊，則所以制馭而羈縻之者，必有道矣。執事謂三江之議紛紛未一，此非愚生所得聞也。然耳目所及，則有可言者，請得而終言之。廣西之有三江，是締絡之大經，而風氣之攸萃也。然其地則廣矣：西極融洛，南抵交阯，北分湘源，東帶蒼梧。其間郡縣之錯置，堡寨之聯綿，誠足以壯雄偉之圖，扼衝要之津矣。然山麓險阻，或不足容方軌；林木茂密，或不勝施剪伐。近地犖确而不可田，則屯戍弗便也；峻嶺斗析而不易達，則樵牧弗便也。是以盜賊窟穴其間。夷性無恒，喜人怒獸，未可常理格，而爲害滋蔓矣。今舉左右兩江觀之，自斷藤平，而左江之患十減其七，何也？山遠而淵藪失憑，江闊而踪跡易露，舊日之峽爲無人之境矣。故謂左江一帶經畫已定，不
translation_en:
…erected bronze pillars, and the distant peoples bowed their heads; Wuxiang crossed Kunlun, and Zhigao lost heart. Thus their fear of death is the same as that of the people of the Central Realm. Since they cherish life and fear death, and thus differ from wood and stone, there must be a way to control them and keep them loosely bound in allegiance.

You say that the proposals concerning the Three Rivers are numerous and conflicting, with no agreement yet reached. This is not something that I, your humble student, have had the opportunity to hear about. Yet there are things within my own knowledge that I can discuss; allow me to finish setting them forth. Guangxi’s Three Rivers form the principal strands of its interconnected network and are where its vital influences converge. The territory, however, is extensive: westward it reaches Rong and Luo [?], southward Jiaozhi, northward it shares a boundary with Xiangyuan, and eastward it adjoins Cangwu. The prefectures and counties distributed throughout it, together with its continuous chains of forts and stockades, are indeed sufficient to strengthen this imposing territorial configuration and command its strategic crossings. Yet the mountain slopes are rugged, sometimes too narrow for carriages to pass abreast; the forests are dense, sometimes beyond the capacity of cutting and clearing. Where nearby ground is stony and cannot be cultivated, maintaining garrisons is difficult; where steep ridges are sharply cleft [?] and hard to reach, gathering firewood and pasturing livestock are difficult. Consequently, bandits make their lairs among them. The native peoples are inconstant by nature: when pleased they act as humans, when angry as beasts. They cannot yet be constrained by ordinary principles, and the harm they cause spreads and grows.

Consider now the Zuo and You Rivers. Since Duanteng was pacified, troubles along the Zuo River have diminished by seven-tenths. Why is this? The mountains are distant, so their lurking places no longer afford support; the river is broad, so their movements are easily exposed. The gorges of former days have become uninhabited territory. Thus the claim that arrangements for the Zuo River region have already been settled cannot…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
爲無見損之益之唯潯州分閫使得兼制
于都泥武宣之界以塞盜賊之門戶南太
二郡特假開府節鉞之副以爲粤駱之表
裏亦庶幾紀綱之密者乎自近歲五都之
役右江之威十伸其九何也強者觸目于
京觀弱者俯首于輸納沿江之隘已爲往
來之孔道矣故謂四三年間道路稀警不
爲無據益之損之唯象州永福之間移建
一縣邑則聲援有恃西融慶遠之間別假
===
一節鉞則振籲不虛亦庶幾經制之詳者
乎如此則明有所必照而夷情罔遁威有
所必伸而體勢其益尊矣雖然此二者若
不可已而可緩若在所當務而猶可待也
乃其最先莫如府江其最急莫如古田矣
夫府江何以言最先也是門庭之寇也平
樂而北三司控于會城龍江而南兩府扼
其總要而鳥鼠之穴顧盤亘其中悔禍無
日此可以不加之意邪間其沿江而盜往
punctuated:
爲無見。損之益之，唯潯州分閫，使得兼制于都泥、武宣之界，以塞盜賊之門戶；南太二郡，特假開府節鉞之副，以爲粤駱之表裏，亦庶幾紀綱之密者乎？自近歲五都之役，右江之威十伸其九，何也？強者觸目于京觀，弱者俯首于輸納，沿江之隘已爲往來之孔道矣。故謂四三年間道路稀警，不爲無據。益之損之，唯象州、永福之間移建一縣邑，則聲援有恃；西融、慶遠之間別假一節鉞，則振籲不虛，亦庶幾經制之詳者乎？如此，則明有所必照，而夷情罔遁；威有所必伸，而體勢其益尊矣。
雖然，此二者若不可已而可緩，若在所當務而猶可待也。乃其最先莫如府江，其最急莫如古田矣。夫府江何以言最先也？是門庭之寇也。平樂而北，三司控于會城；龍江而南，兩府扼其總要。而鳥鼠之穴顧盤亘其中，悔禍無日，此可以不加之意邪？間其沿江而盜往
translation_en:
…is not without insight. In adjusting and supplementing these arrangements, let the regional military command at Xunzhou exercise concurrent control over the borderlands of Duni and Wuxuan, thereby blocking the bandits’ gateways. For the two prefectures of Nan and Tai [Nanning and Taiping], specially appoint a deputy vested with the governor’s military authority, so that the outer and inner defenses of Yueluo support one another. Would this not bring us close to a tightly ordered system of control? Since the recent Wudu campaign, authority along the You River has been asserted to nine-tenths of its full extent. Why? The strong have been confronted with the sight of mounds of slain enemies; the weak have bowed their heads and made their payments. The river passes have already become thoroughfares for travel. Thus, the assertion that alarms along the roads have been rare during the past three or four years is not without foundation. In supplementing and adjusting these arrangements, relocate a county seat to a site between Xiangzhou and Yongfu, so that dependable support is available; separately confer military command upon an officer stationed between Xirong [?] and Qingyuan, so that calls for assistance do not go unanswered. Would this not bring us close to a fully elaborated administrative and military system? In this way, our discernment would surely illuminate its objects, leaving the circumstances of the non-Han peoples nowhere to escape notice; our authority would surely be asserted where needed, further enhancing the dignity of our position.
Nevertheless, although these two measures seem indispensable, they can be deferred; although they belong among the tasks we ought to undertake, they can still wait. Nothing takes precedence over the Fu River, and nothing is more urgent than Gutian. Why say that the Fu River takes precedence? These are bandits at our very gates. North of Pingle, the Three Provincial Commissions exercise control from the provincial capital; south of Longjiang, the two prefectures hold the principal strategic points. Yet these nests of birds and rats extend throughout the intervening country, with no day in sight when they will repent of their wrongdoing. Can we fail to give this our attention? As for [?] the stretch along the river, the bandits …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
往來自遠地東則富賀恭城西則永安脩
仁荔浦或百里而趨或數舍而至倏往忽
來皆無旬日之計驅而除之寧無法乎竊
嘗道聽適中之處爲昭平鎮城堡差壯野
亦寛衍說者謂于此地宜如北方之制設
一遊擊屯兵數千以十之三泝流駐于廣
運以十之三沿流駐于龍門三分其衆聯
以百艘畫地爲限截日爲役俾絡繹江洋
之中旌旗相望金鼓相聞上下呼應如左
===
右手彼爲盜者置足無所何時何地得肆
其掠舟之兇乎不唯不得肆而已彼失鹽
米之利既窘生理兼受巡邏之密復遭捕
縛吾見革面聽招且不暇矣又何盜之能
爲哉此一說也古田何以言最急也是腹
心之患也夫省城西北不踰一舍柳郡東
來纔接縣境而虎狼之毒顧根蔕其中輈
頑有年此可以不爲之所邪聞之縣之渠
魁往往刦挾良善阻其輸賦十年之前令
punctuated:
往來自遠地，東則富、賀、恭城，西則永安、脩仁、荔浦，或百里而趨，或數舍而至，倏往忽來，皆無旬日之計。驅而除之，寧無法乎？竊嘗道聽，適中之處爲昭平鎮，城堡差壯，野亦寛衍。說者謂，于此地宜如北方之制，設一遊擊，屯兵數千，以十之三泝流駐于廣運，以十之三沿流駐于龍門，三分其衆，聯以百艘，畫地爲限，截日爲役，俾絡繹江洋之中，旌旗相望，金鼓相聞，上下呼應，如左右手。彼爲盜者，置足無所，何時何地得肆其掠舟之兇乎？不唯不得肆而已，彼失鹽米之利，既窘生理，兼受巡邏之密，復遭捕縛，吾見革面聽招且不暇矣，又何盜之能爲哉？此一說也。
古田何以言最急也？是腹心之患也。夫省城西北不踰一舍，柳郡東來纔接縣境，而虎狼之毒顧根蔕其中，輈頑有年，此可以不爲之所邪？聞之，縣之渠魁往往刦挾良善，阻其輸賦。十年之前，令
translation_en:
…they come and go from distant places: Fu, He, and Gongcheng to the east, and Yong’an, Xiuren, and Lipu to the west. Some hasten a hundred li; others arrive after several stages of travel. They depart and appear suddenly, making no plans extending even ten days. Can there really be no way to drive them out and eliminate them? I have heard in passing that Zhaoping Garrison occupies a central position, with fairly strong fortifications and broad, open surrounding country. Some propose following northern practice here: appoint a mobile corps commander and station several thousand troops, sending three-tenths upstream to Guangyun and three-tenths downstream to Longmen. Divide the force into three contingents and connect them with a hundred vessels; assign territorial limits and fixed days of service. Have them ply the river continuously, their banners within sight of one another and their gongs and drums within earshot, the upstream and downstream forces responding to one another like the left and right hands. With nowhere to gain a foothold, when or where could the bandits indulge their violence against boats? Nor would it merely prevent their attacks. Deprived of the profits from salt and rice, their livelihood would become strained; closely pressed by patrols, they would also face arrest and confinement. I believe they would scarcely have time enough to assume an obedient demeanor and accept offers of submission. How could they continue as bandits? This is one proposal.
Why do I call Gutian the most urgent concern? It is an affliction at the very heart. It lies no more than one stage northwest of the provincial capital, while approaching eastward from Liu Prefecture brings one directly to its county boundary. Yet men as vicious as tigers and wolves have established deep roots there and remained stubbornly recalcitrant [?] for years. Can we fail to devise a remedy? I have heard that the county’s ringleaders frequently seize and coerce law-abiding people, preventing them from paying their taxes. Ten years ago, the magistrate …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
倐間至數歲以來徒事羈縻或叛或懷要
非一心之人從而攻之寧無成乎又嘗聞
麻陽之師連跨數省說者謂俟其收功移
而南向此不可失蓋靖州南指搗其腹心
武岡西出衝其肩腋而我全廣帥海南之
勝旅舉三州之勁卒數道並進彼區區一
隅腹背受敵顧此失彼將何以為謀乎第
見其進退維谷而已蓋武靖逼而南則退
失甌脫之地全廣張而北則進無獵獲之
===
塲吾知洗心乞命且不暇矣又何邑之敢
據哉此又一說也是在今之經世務者留
心焉爾然唐韓愈氏有言嶺外夷獠尋常
亦各營生急則屯聚相保德既不能綏懷
威又不能臨制以致攻劫侵暴在今日得
不有如其言者乎苟有之古田之叛拒固
當有別為之畫者矣宋紹興建議謂谿峒
綿亘非一州得專約束故遊民惡少之棄
本者商旅之避征稅者盜賊之亡命者往
punctuated:
倐間至數歲以來，徒事羈縻，或叛或懷，要非一心之人。從而攻之，寧無成乎？又嘗聞麻陽之師連跨數省，說者謂俟其收功，移而南向，此不可失。蓋靖州南指，搗其腹心；武岡西出，衝其肩腋；而我全廣帥海南之勝旅，舉三州之勁卒，數道並進。彼區區一隅，腹背受敵，顧此失彼，將何以為謀乎？第見其進退維谷而已。蓋武靖逼而南，則退失甌脫之地；全廣張而北，則進無獵獲之塲。吾知洗心乞命且不暇矣，又何邑之敢據哉？此又一說也。是在今之經世務者留心焉爾。
然唐韓愈氏有言：「嶺外夷獠，尋常亦各營生，急則屯聚相保。德既不能綏懷，威又不能臨制，以致攻劫侵暴。」在今日，得不有如其言者乎？苟有之，古田之叛拒，固當有別為之畫者矣。宋紹興建議，謂谿峒綿亘，非一州得專約束，故遊民惡少之棄本者、商旅之避征稅者、盜賊之亡命者，往
translation_en:
…[The opening phrase is unclear: 倐間至, ?] In recent years, they have merely pursued loose control, with the people sometimes rebelling and sometimes submitting; in any event, these are not people united in purpose. If we then attacked them, could we fail to succeed? I have also heard that the army campaigning at Mayang extends across several provinces. Some propose waiting until it has completed its task and then turning it southward. This opportunity must not be lost. Forces from Jingzhou could strike south into their heartland, while those from Wugang could advance west against their flank. Our forces in Quan and Guang [?] could lead the elite troops of Hainan and mobilize the picked soldiers of the three prefectures, advancing along several routes at once. Confined to that small corner, facing enemies in front and behind, and losing one position while attending to another, what strategy could they devise? They would simply find themselves trapped, unable either to advance or to retreat. With Wugang and Jingzhou pressing southward, they would lose their border refuge when retreating; with Quan and Guang [?] deploying northward, they would have no ground to plunder when advancing. I know they would scarcely have time to reform their hearts and beg for their lives. What town would they then dare occupy? This is another proposal. It remains for those who manage affairs of state today to give it their attention.
Yet Han Yu of the Tang said: “The Yi and Liao beyond the mountain passes ordinarily each pursue their livelihoods; when pressed, they gather together for mutual protection. When virtue cannot win their allegiance, and force cannot hold them in check, attacks, plunder, incursions, and violence result.” Can there be no circumstances today matching his words? If there are, then a different plan should certainly be devised for Gutian’s rebellion and resistance. A proposal made during the Shaoxing reign of the Song argued that the valleys and tribal settlements extended continuously over such distances that no single prefecture could exercise sole control over them. Consequently, wandering people and young troublemakers who abandoned their proper livelihoods, traveling merchants who evaded taxes, and robbers fleeing justice would often…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
往由入交相鼓煽深爲邊患在今日又不
有如其議者乎苟有之則府江之出沒固
當有別爲之防者矣雖然事之來也勢有
淹速君子之動也時有利鈍故惟剛明之
才審勢而應待時而行易曰出而有獲何
不利之有正謂此也此固經世道者之所
素定粵西之民方喁喁然羣切望焉狂瞽
及此不知忌諱惟執事大其爲容幸甚
punctuated: 往由入，交相鼓煽，深爲邊患。在今日，又不有如其議者乎？苟有之，則府江之出沒，固當有別爲之防者矣。雖然，事之來也，勢有淹速；君子之動也，時有利鈍。故惟剛明之才，審勢而應，待時而行。《易》曰：「出而有獲，何不利之有？」正謂此也。此固經世道者之所素定。粵西之民，方喁喁然羣切望焉。狂瞽及此，不知忌諱，惟執事大其爲容，幸甚。
translation_en:
…enter by this route [?], inciting one another and becoming a grave affliction on the frontier. Does the situation today not likewise match what that proposal described? If so, special measures should certainly be devised to guard against their incursions and retreats along the Fujiang River.

Nevertheless, as affairs arise, circumstances may develop slowly or swiftly; when a gentleman acts, the moment may favor or hinder him. Thus only someone resolute and discerning can assess circumstances and respond, awaiting the right moment to act. The Book of Changes says: “Going forth, one gains something. How could there be anything unfavorable?” This is precisely what it means. Those who bring order to the world have surely long since settled this in their minds. The people of western Guangxi are now all looking up in eager expectation.

In my rashness and blindness, I have ventured this far, heedless of what ought not to be said. I would count myself most fortunate if you, honored examiners, would generously indulge me.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
嘉靖己酉當天下大比之歲
高岡被聘校文粤西錄成有
序監臨御史王士翹授高岡
以末簡高岡何言哉夫振飭
科條以軌度其衆惴惴焉蚤
夜以𤾉仰成
===
聖天子求賢之
制此監臨者之心也百執事之
責也高岡何言哉高岡惟賓
興之典自周人三物之制不
行試言遂不可易後世之士
刼刼焉聲華是究而飭躬軌
道之意疎飾情而詭物深衷
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

嘉靖己酉，當天下大比之歲，高岡被聘校文粤西。錄成有序，監臨御史王士翹授高岡以末簡。高岡何言哉？夫振飭科條，以軌度其衆，惴惴焉蚤夜以𤾉，仰成聖天子求賢之制，此監臨者之心也，百執事之責也。高岡何言哉？高岡惟賓興之典，自周人三物之制不行，試言遂不可易。後世之士，刼刼焉聲華是究，而飭躬軌道之意疎，飾情而詭物，深衷
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the jiyou year of Jiajing [1549], a year of the empire-wide triennial examinations, I, Gaogang, was invited to evaluate examination essays in Guangxi. When the record was completed, it already had a preface; Wang Shiqiao, the censor serving as Supervising Official, entrusted its closing pages to me. What could I say? To enforce and put in order the examination regulations, thereby guiding the candidates by established standards; to remain apprehensively vigilant morning and night [?], respectfully carrying out the sagely Son of Heaven’s ordinance for seeking worthy men—this is the Supervising Official’s heartfelt purpose and the responsibility of all the officials engaged in the examination. What could I say?

I reflect that, in the ceremony of honoring and recommending worthy men, once the Zhou system of the three categories [virtue, conduct, and accomplishments] ceased to operate, testing men through their written words became a practice that could no longer be changed. Scholars of later ages anxiously pursue literary reputation and brilliance, while giving little thought to disciplining their conduct and following the Way. They disguise their feelings and misrepresent things, concealing their inmost thoughts [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而自澤或失則輕或失則淺
或失則卑夫帝王需材以用
世也而輕也奚以任也淺也
奚以受也卑也易以陵也即
得士若此國將焉賴哉是故
浮華者不可任以治取士而
得浮華焉猶獲乎赤箭青芝
===
也雖美無所用之高岡受聘
之初亦未嘗不惴惴焉蚤夜
以惕天地之生材也洪纖一
氣纖之不可爲洪辟則梀之
不可爲檟也聖王之用材也
小大異任小之不可爲大辟
則榱之不可爲棟也吾受提
punctuated:
而自澤，或失則輕，或失則淺，或失則卑。夫帝王需材以用世也，而輕也奚以任也？淺也奚以受也？卑也易以陵也。即得士若此，國將焉賴哉？是故浮華者不可任以治，取士而得浮華焉，猶獲乎赤箭青芝也，雖美，無所用之。
高岡受聘之初，亦未嘗不惴惴焉，蚤夜以惕。天地之生材也，洪纖一氣，纖之不可爲洪，辟則梀之不可爲檟也。聖王之用材也，小大異任，小之不可爲大，辟則榱之不可爲棟也。吾受提
translation_en:
…and embellish themselves. Some err in being frivolous, some in being shallow, and some in being base. Emperors and kings require men of talent to serve the world. Yet how can the frivolous shoulder responsibility? How can the shallow receive it? The base are easily overborne. If the men selected are like this, upon whom will the state depend? Thus, those who are showy and superficial cannot be entrusted with government. To select such men is like acquiring red-arrow herbs and green numinous fungi: beautiful though they may be, there is no use for them.
When I, Gaogang, first accepted the invitation to serve, I too was apprehensive, remaining vigilant morning and night. When Heaven and Earth produce timber, the massive and the slender arise from the same vital force; yet the slender cannot become massive, just as a su tree [?] cannot become a catalpa. When sage kings employ talent, they assign different responsibilities to those of lesser and greater capacity. The lesser cannot serve as the greater, just as a rafter cannot serve as a ridgepole. I have accepted the charge of wielding…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
斤之任而入粤求材能無惕
乎或曰因材而篤天地生物
之仁隨材器使匠氏不得已
之意嗟乎士乎吾寧使人不
得不用不用不已而使人不
得已而用之乎我
國家養士百八十餘年
===
仁義禮樂亦既浹洽
聖皇御極涵濡益深
聲敎四達夷夏颯颯乃今甌粤
之士人知飭躬崇學爭自澡
雪與日俱新蓄材待用視昔
爲盛頃高岡執策而來也自
衡湘而南觀粤之山盤礴周
punctuated: 斤之任而入粤求材，能無惕乎？或曰：「因材而篤，天地生物之仁；隨材器使，匠氏不得已之意。」嗟乎，士乎！吾寧使人不得不用，不用不已，而使人不得已而用之乎？我國家養士百八十餘年，仁義禮樂亦既浹洽。聖皇御極，涵濡益深，聲敎四達，夷夏颯颯。乃今甌粤之士，人知飭躬崇學，爭自澡雪，與日俱新，蓄材待用，視昔爲盛。頃高岡執策而來也，自衡湘而南，觀粤之山，盤礴周
translation_en:
