…the responsibility of wielding the axe, and enter Yue to seek timber—men of talent—how could I be without apprehension? Someone says: “To nurture each according to its capacities is the benevolence with which Heaven and Earth bring forth living things; to employ each according to its capacities is the craftsman’s intention, constrained by necessity.” Ah, scholars! Would I not rather make others unable to refrain from employing me, unable to rest until they do, than make them employ me only because they have no alternative?

Our dynasty has nurtured scholars for more than one hundred and eighty years. Benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music have already permeated all. Since our sage emperor ascended the throne, his nurturing influence has grown still deeper. His civilizing teachings reach in every direction, and both non-Chinese and Chinese respond with vigor [?]. Now, among the scholars of Ou and Yue, everyone knows to discipline his conduct and esteem learning. They vie to cleanse themselves, renewing themselves daily, storing up their talents and awaiting employment. Compared with former times, they flourish more abundantly.

Recently, when Gaogang came bearing a riding whip, traveling south from Heng and Xiang, he beheld the mountains of Yue, sprawling majestically and encircling…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
析理入微則固躍躍乎渙焉
以釋也夫文之足以知人也
自昔言之其人狷者其文急
以怨狂者其文怪以怒纖者
其文碎夸者其文誕由中發
外人若自貌莫之或失也則
夫今日粤之諸士吾未睹其
===
貌而得其神情文固神情之
所注也沈雄者干城之才精
鍊者宗廟之器峻潔者命世
之英吾知其不爲狷不爲狂
不爲纖夸而重也無弗任也
深也無弗受也辟則大車以
載攸往而利也諸士之謂邪
punctuated: 析理入微，則固躍躍乎渙焉以釋也。夫文之足以知人也，自昔言之。其人狷者，其文急以怨；狂者，其文怪以怒；纖者，其文碎；夸者，其文誕。由中發外，人若自貌，莫之或失也。則夫今日粤之諸士，吾未睹其貌，而得其神情，文固神情之所注也。沈雄者，干城之才；精鍊者，宗廟之器；峻潔者，命世之英。吾知其不爲狷，不爲狂，不爲纖夸，而重也無弗任也，深也無弗受也。辟則大車以載，攸往而利也。諸士之謂邪？
translation_en:
…when their analysis of principles penetrates the subtlest details, it is indeed animated and expansive, dissolving perplexities [?]. That writing suffices to reveal a person has been said since antiquity. Those who are narrowly scrupulous write with urgency and resentment; those who are unrestrained write with strangeness and anger; those who are petty write in fragments; those who boast write extravagantly. What is within emerges outwardly, as though each person were drawing his own portrait, without a single failure of likeness. Thus, although I have not seen the faces of the scholars of Yue assembled today, I have grasped their spirit and disposition: writing is indeed where spirit and disposition find expression.

Those whose writing is profound and vigorous have the talents to serve as the state's shield and rampart; those whose writing is refined and polished are vessels fit for the ancestral temple; those whose writing is lofty and pure are outstanding men destined to distinguish their age. I know that they are neither narrowly scrupulous nor unrestrained, neither petty nor boastful. In their weightiness, there is no responsibility they cannot bear; in their depth, there is nothing they cannot accommodate. They are like a great cart bearing its load, proceeding advantageously wherever it goes. Does this not describe these scholars?

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
官先事士先志爾諸士其益
懋平生所學志以先之勞以
成之用効忠於
國毋負主司今日達才之意云
江西廣信府鉛山縣儒學敎
諭林高岡謹序
punctuated:
官先事，士先志。爾諸士其益懋平生所學，志以先之，勞以成之，用効忠於國，毋負主司今日達才之意云。
江西廣信府鉛山縣儒學敎諭林高岡謹序。
translation_en:
For officials, duties come first; for scholars, resolve comes first. You scholars should strive still harder in the learning you have pursued throughout your lives, leading with resolve and bringing it to fruition through effort, thereby rendering loyal service to the state. Do not disappoint the chief examiner’s intention in advancing worthy talent today.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Lin Gaogang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
洪惟
皇上協
天敷極文明之化浹邇曁遠今玆
己酉復當鄉試之期惟廣西
監臨御史王士翹慶逢
鴻典乃播宣
===
上德用揚作人之懿以興起百執
事復飭章度俾百執事得各
因職舒効用成以人事
君之忠簾內外罔弗共焉先是巡
按御史蕭世延程用擴式授
事責成緘儀諸方禮聘儒臣
右都御史張岳昔柄文鐸舟
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序

洪惟皇上協天敷極，文明之化浹邇曁遠。今玆己酉，復當鄉試之期。惟廣西監臨御史王士翹慶逢鴻典，乃播宣上德，用揚作人之懿，以興起百執事；復飭章度，俾百執事得各因職舒効，用成以人事君之忠，簾內外罔弗共焉。先是，巡按御史蕭世延、程用擴式授事責成，緘儀諸方，禮聘儒臣。右都御史張岳昔柄文鐸，舟
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

We reverently reflect that His Majesty, in accord with Heaven, establishes the supreme standard, and that his civilizing influence permeates places both near and far. Now, in this jiyou year [1549], the time for the Provincial Examination has come again. Wang Shiqiao, the censor serving as Supervising Official in Guangxi, rejoicing at this grand occasion, proclaimed the sovereign’s virtue and extolled his admirable nurturing of talent, thereby inspiring all the officials concerned. He further put the regulations and procedures in order, enabling each official to perform effectively according to his duties and thus fulfill the loyalty of serving the ruler by obtaining worthy men. All those within and outside the examination curtain worked together in this endeavor.

Previously, the Regional Inspectors Xiao Shiyan and Cheng Yongkuo had duly assigned duties and demanded their fulfillment, sending sealed ceremonial gifts in various directions [?] and respectfully inviting Confucian scholars to serve. Zhang Yue, Censor-in-Chief of the Right, had formerly wielded the bell of literary instruction [directed education]; [the final character 舟, “boat,” is doubtful here] …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
振武戈邇復兼制風敎維新
兵部右侍郎兼右副都御史
歐陽必進肅清方隅表宣文
化士無警奪顓攻術業太保
總兵官平江伯陳圭克佐成
焉珊與敎諭林高岡至則謬
主考試同考試則學正吳時
昭敎諭江汝楫馬進階蕭祥
庚林以毅聞實提調則左布
政使鄭漳右參政魏良輔監
試則副使沈宏僉事何中行
旣鎖院進提學僉事謝少南
遴簡士千有百人三試之奉
制額擢五十五人錄其名及文以
punctuated: 振武戈，邇復兼制，風敎維新。兵部右侍郎兼右副都御史歐陽必進肅清方隅，表宣文化，士無警奪，顓攻術業。太保總兵官平江伯陳圭克佐成焉。珊與敎諭林高岡至，則謬主考試。同考試則學正吳時昭、敎諭江汝楫、馬進階、蕭祥庚、林以毅、聞實。提調則左布政使鄭漳、右參政魏良輔。監試則副使沈宏、僉事何中行。旣鎖院，進提學僉事謝少南遴簡士千有百人，三試之。奉制額擢五十五人，錄其名及文以
translation_en:
…wielded the weapons of war; recently he again assumed concurrent command, renewing moral instruction. Ouyang Bijin, Right Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, pacified the region and disseminated civilizing instruction, so that the scholars could devote themselves exclusively to their studies without disruption by alarms. Chen Gui, Earl of Pingjiang, Grand Guardian and Regional Commander, ably assisted in accomplishing this.

When I, Shan, arrived together with Lin Gaogang, Instructor, we were unworthily entrusted with serving as Examiners. The Associate Examiners were Wu Shizhao, School Director, and the Instructors Jiang Ruji, Ma Jinjie, Xiao Xianggeng, Lin Yiyi, and Wen Shi. The Proctors were Zheng Zhang, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Wei Liangfu, Right Administration Vice Commissioner. The examination monitors were Shen Hong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and He Zhongxing, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner.

After the examination compound was sealed, we admitted the eleven hundred scholars selected by Xie Shaonan, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner for Education, and examined them in three sessions. In accordance with the quota prescribed by imperial decree, we selected fifty-five men and recorded their names and essays in order to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
獻珊以例僭序篇首夫廣西嶺
徼之地其極界去
京師萬里冠裳文物由漢而下
漸同中州至唐柳宗元始敎
爲進士業史稱湘南之士執
經其門爲文多中程度然唯
其文而已矣宋張栻爲靜江
===
===
乃闡濂洛關閩之說訓敎學
徒朱熹謂其明義反本遵先
王之遺意文士駸駸有興第
時值偏安王化無本君子有
遺憾焉仰惟我
太祖高皇帝用夏變夷紀綱四方
廣西内附於是
punctuated: 獻。珊以例僭序篇首。夫廣西，嶺徼之地，其極界去京師萬里。冠裳文物，由漢而下，漸同中州。至唐，柳宗元始敎爲進士業。史稱湘南之士執經其門，爲文多中程度，然唯其文而已矣。宋張栻爲靜江，乃闡濂洛關閩之說，訓敎學徒。朱熹謂其明義反本，遵先王之遺意，文士駸駸有興。第時值偏安，王化無本，君子有遺憾焉。仰惟我太祖高皇帝，用夏變夷，紀綱四方，廣西内附，於是
translation_en:
…to present to the throne. Following precedent, I, Shan, presume to write a preface at the beginning of this volume. Guangxi is a frontier land amid the mountain ranges; its farthest border lies ten thousand li from the capital. From the Han onward, its ceremonial dress and cultural institutions gradually came to resemble those of the Central Plains. In the Tang, Liu Zongyuan first taught men to prepare for the jinshi examination. The histories relate that scholars of Xiangnan came to his door bearing the Classics, and that their compositions often met the prescribed standards. Yet this amounted only to literary accomplishment.

In the Song, Zhang Shi administered Jingjiang and expounded the teachings of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min, instructing his students. Zhu Xi said that he clarified righteousness and returned to the foundations, following the intentions bequeathed by the former kings. Men of letters flourished increasingly. But this was a time when the dynasty held sway over only part of the realm, and kingly moral transformation lacked a foundation—a matter of lasting regret to gentlemen.

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao transformed the non-Chinese peoples through the civilization of Xia and established order throughout the four quarters. Guangxi submitted to his rule, and thereupon…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
王封官守無異齊魯蓋自漢入
中國至是始盡用中國之治
成祖文皇帝曁我
列聖相承一道教化熈洽故其人
文由黃虞後亦至我
國家始開百八十餘年其間輔
弼端揆之臣往往迭出今即
窮陬僻邑談道而謀義禮作
而行脩是孰使之然哉
皇上中興
德教光被人文化成雖跂行喙
息之鄉胥陶鑄于禮樂鼓舞
于風聲矧如粵西冠裳文物
齊而中州若是久遠者哉故
punctuated:
王封官守，無異齊魯。蓋自漢入中國，至是始盡用中國之治。成祖文皇帝曁我列聖相承，一道教化熈洽。故其人文，由黃虞後，亦至我國家始開。百八十餘年，其間輔弼端揆之臣，往往迭出。今即窮陬僻邑，談道而謀義，禮作而行脩，是孰使之然哉？
皇上中興，德教光被，人文化成。雖跂行喙息之鄉，胥陶鑄于禮樂，鼓舞于風聲，矧如粵西，冠裳文物齊而中州，若是久遠者哉？故
translation_en:
…princes were enfeoffed and officials appointed, just as in Qi and Lu. Although the region had entered China under the Han, only then did it fully adopt China’s governance. Emperor Wen, Chengzu, and our successive sage emperors carried on this legacy, unifying the Way and bringing their civilizing instruction into harmonious accord. Thus, in all the time since the Yellow Emperor and Shun, its cultural flowering began only under our dynasty. Over more than 180 years, ministers who assisted the sovereign and presided over government emerged one after another. Today, even in remote corners and secluded towns, people discuss the Way and deliberate upon righteousness; ritual flourishes and conduct is cultivated. Who has brought this about?
His Majesty has brought about a restoration: his virtuous instruction shines everywhere, and human culture transforms the people. Even lands inhabited by creatures that creep and breathe through beaks are all molded by rites and music and stirred by the influence of his example. How much more must this apply to western Yue, whose ceremonial dress and cultural institutions have equaled those of the Central Plain for so long? Therefore…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
洲觀諸士文藝其雄深雅健
蓋有得于宗元之緒如劉禹
錫所謂繁星麗天而芒寒色
正望而敬于五行者庶幾再
見且其語性命則窺從出之
源議政事則究躬行之實或
則經以闡微或確質以孚理
===
擴如奧如金響玉韻張栻所
爲拳拳于往日者類亹亹然
發之詞端無疑礙無矯頗珊
竊斂衽豈唯齊魯之所與同
雖都人士炳炳蔚蔚何以異
哉因是而仰歎而俯思益有
感于
punctuated: 洲觀諸士文藝，其雄深雅健，蓋有得于宗元之緒。如劉禹錫所謂「繁星麗天，而芒寒色正，望而敬于五行」者，庶幾再見。且其語性命，則窺從出之源；議政事，則究躬行之實。或則經以闡微，或確質以孚理，擴如奧如，金響玉韻。張栻所爲拳拳于往日者，類亹亹然發之詞端，無疑礙，無矯頗。珊竊斂衽，豈唯齊魯之所與同？雖都人士炳炳蔚蔚，何以異哉？因是而仰歎而俯思，益有感于
translation_en: …Zhou [?], on examining these scholars’ literary compositions, finds them powerful, profound, elegant, and vigorous, evidently inheriting something of Zongyuan’s legacy. What Liu Yuxi described as “myriad stars adorning heaven, their rays cold and their colors true, regarded with reverence among the Five Phases [?]” may perhaps be seen again. Moreover, when they discuss human nature and destiny, they discern the source from which these arise; when they deliberate on government affairs, they investigate the realities of personal practice. Some employ the Classics to elucidate subtleties [?]; others, through solidity and substance, accord with principle. Expansive and profound, their writings resonate like metal and jade. What Zhang Shi cherished so earnestly in former days seems to emerge continually in their words, without uncertainty or impediment, affectation or bias. I, Shan [?], respectfully gather my robes in admiration. How could they merely stand on a par with the scholars of Qi and Lu? Even the splendid literary accomplishments of the men of the capital—how do these differ from theirs? Thus, looking upward in admiration and downward in reflection, I am all the more deeply moved by…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇上德化之應文教之訖於戲盛
矣抑聞之
國家之選士非為士榮已也
天工所需而萬化攸畀乃其貴重
矣顧于始進不免程諸文藝
亦豈徒取諸空言已也孔孟
之學必成己而成物故曰夫
===
人幼而學之壯而欲行之夫
行之云者行其所學焉爾非
能亮
天工而宣萬化安所徵學然切近
精實取諸其身而已珊嘗考
諸張栻其告語粤西之士謂
心為萬事之宗必收其放存
punctuated: 皇上德化之應，文教之訖。於戲，盛矣！抑聞之，國家之選士，非為士榮已也。天工所需，而萬化攸畀，乃其貴重矣。顧于始進，不免程諸文藝，亦豈徒取諸空言已也？孔孟之學，必成己而成物，故曰：「夫人幼而學之，壯而欲行之。」夫行之云者，行其所學焉爾。非能亮天工而宣萬化，安所徵學？然切近精實，取諸其身而已。珊嘗考諸張栻，其告語粤西之士，謂心為萬事之宗，必收其放，存
translation_en: …the response to His Majesty’s transforming virtue and the reach of literary instruction [?]. Ah, how splendid! Yet I have heard that the state selects scholars not merely to confer glory upon them. They are needed for Heaven’s work and entrusted with its myriad transformations: herein lies the weight and dignity of their calling. When they first seek advancement, however, they must be assessed through literary composition. Could this mean that they are chosen merely for empty words? The learning of Confucius and Mencius requires one to perfect oneself and bring other beings to fulfillment. Thus it is said: “A person studies in youth and, on reaching maturity, wishes to put that learning into practice.” Putting it into practice means simply carrying out what one has learned. Unless one can assist in Heaven’s work and give effect to its myriad transformations, how can one’s learning be demonstrated? Yet what is immediately relevant, exact, and substantial is to be sought only within oneself. I, Shan, have examined Zhang Shi’s teachings. In addressing the scholars of Yuexi, he said that the mind is the governing source of all affairs: one must recall it from its wandering and preserve…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其良謂天下之事皆人所當
為必自其視聽言動之間而
求諸君臣父子夫婦昆弟朋
友之實斯則孔孟之微言而
周程之大旨取諸身而至足
推之事而有常粤西之先民
固聞之而今固傳之亦憾其
===
不克究施矣方今
全盛之日諸士對主司旣發之
文詞慨若自任珊竊感焉如
挹諸士于張栻之門而待之
于孔孟周程之途非敢取諸
其空言云爾况由此而升試
春曹奉
punctuated:
其良，謂天下之事皆人所當為，必自其視聽言動之間，而求諸君臣父子夫婦昆弟朋友之實。斯則孔孟之微言，而周程之大旨，取諸身而至足，推之事而有常。粤西之先民固聞之，而今固傳之，亦憾其不克究施矣。
方今全盛之日，諸士對主司旣發之文詞，慨若自任，珊竊感焉。如挹諸士于張栻之門，而待之于孔孟周程之途，非敢取諸其空言云爾。况由此而升試春曹，奉
translation_en:
…its innate goodness. He said that the affairs of the world are all things people ought to undertake: one must begin with one’s seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting, and seek their fulfillment in the actual relationships between ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, and friends. These are the subtle teachings of Confucius and Mencius and the essential purport of Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers. Sought within oneself, they are wholly sufficient; extended to affairs, they provide enduring standards. The forebears of western Guangxi certainly heard these teachings, and they are certainly transmitted today; yet it is regrettable that they have not been fully put into practice.
Now, in this age of flourishing prosperity, the candidates, in the compositions they have presented in response to the presiding examiners, express an ardor suggesting that they take this responsibility upon themselves. I, Shan, am privately moved by this. It is as though I were drawing these candidates into the school of Zhang Shi and awaiting them along the path of Confucius, Mencius, Zhou Dunyi, and the Cheng brothers; I would not presume to judge them merely by empty words. Moreover, from here they will advance to sit the examination at the Ministry of Rites and receive…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廷問所以先資自獻者已即此
在可不慎乎哉不然則瑰奇
絕特之文雖無殊宗元乃其
人得無不可者乎主司過慮
復丁寧而不自已亦誠過望
他日輔弼端揆之臣有自是
科繼出大行張栻之說亮
===
天工而宣萬化以佐于
聖明之廷豈唯主司之幸亦廣西
無窮之光也詎不益盛矣哉
諸士勉旃是舉也右布政使
楊〔本仁〕掌使司〔少南〕署按察
右參將劉〔遠〕署副總兵事署
都指揮僉事李〔霖〕署都司皆
punctuated:
廷問，所以先資自獻者，已即此在，可不慎乎哉？不然，則瑰奇絕特之文，雖無殊宗元，乃其人得無不可者乎？主司過慮，復丁寧而不自已，亦誠過望他日輔弼端揆之臣有自是科繼出，大行張栻之說，亮天工而宣萬化，以佐于聖明之廷。豈唯主司之幸，亦廣西無窮之光也，詎不益盛矣哉？諸士勉旃！
是舉也，右布政使楊〔本仁〕掌使司，〔少南〕署按察，右參將劉〔遠〕署副總兵事，署都指揮僉事李〔霖〕署都司，皆
translation_en:
…the questioning at court: the means by which you first prepare to present yourselves already lie here. Can you fail to exercise care? Otherwise, though your writings may be as magnificent, extraordinary, and exceptional as those of Liu Zongyuan, might you yourselves nevertheless prove unworthy? The examiners are excessively anxious and cannot stop repeating their earnest admonitions. This also reflects their profound hope that ministers who assist the sovereign and occupy the highest offices will in time emerge in succession from this examination cohort, put Zhang Shi’s teachings widely into practice, assist Heaven’s work and further its myriad transformations, thereby serving the court of our sagacious ruler. Would this be good fortune only for the examiners? It would also bring Guangxi everlasting glory. Would this not mark still greater flourishing? Exert yourselves, gentlemen!
For this examination, Yang Benren, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, was in charge of the Provincial Administration Commission. [An official identified only as] Shaonan [?] served as acting Surveillance Commissioner. Liu Yuan, Right Assistant Regional Commander, served as acting Vice Regional Commander. Li Lin, acting Assistant Commander of the Regional Military Commission, was in acting charge of that commission. All …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
防檢于院以外而俾無所擾
于內者也右參政潘倣右參
議康朗副使徐禎僉事趙塤
左參將王寵咸有事于蒼梧
兩江而督傳厲兵供衛百執
事以逮諸士與有勞焉左參
政范欽僉事楊濂署都指揮
===
僉事張武先期入賀
萬壽都督僉事副總兵沈希儀先
期調征海南然樂逢盛舉則
自覩興事胥交慶焉得附書
之
福建興化府儒學教授詹珊
謹序
punctuated:
防檢于院以外，而俾無所擾于內者也。右參政潘倣、右參議康朗、副使徐禎、僉事趙塤、左參將王寵，咸有事于蒼梧、兩江，而督傳厲兵，供衛百執事以逮諸士，與有勞焉。左參政范欽、僉事楊濂、署都指揮僉事張武，先期入賀萬壽；都督僉事副總兵沈希儀，先期調征海南。然樂逢盛舉，則自覩興事，胥交慶焉，得附書之。
福建興化府儒學教授詹珊謹序。
translation_en:
…maintained security outside the examination compound, ensuring that there were no disturbances within. Pan Fang, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right; Kang Lang, Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Right; Xu Zhen, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Zhao Xun, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Wang Chong, Assistant Regional Commander of the Left, all had duties in Cangwu and the Two Rivers region. They supervised relay transport and readied the troops, providing supplies and protection for all the officials engaged in the examination and for the candidates as well. They too contributed their efforts.
Fan Qin, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left; Yang Lian, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Zhang Wu, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, had departed earlier for court to offer congratulations on the emperor’s birthday. Shen Xiyi, Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief and Regional Vice Commander, had earlier been transferred to campaign in Hainan. Yet, delighted to encounter this grand occasion, they all exchanged congratulations upon witnessing the undertaking get under way [?]. Thus I have been able to append this account of them.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Zhan Shan, Professor of the Confucian School of Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:

punctuated:
嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試

巡按廣西監察御史王士翹〔民瞻，江西永新縣籍，安福縣人，戊戌進士〕。

廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使鄭漳〔世績，福建閩縣人，丁丑進士〕。
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政魏良輔〔師召，江西新建縣人，丙戌進士〕。

直隸鳳陽府潁州太和縣儒學教諭江汝楫〔濟之，江西南昌縣人，庚子貢士〕。

translation_en:
Guangxi Provincial Examination, the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing (1549)

Supervising Official
Wang Shiqiao, Investigating Censor on巡按 duty in Guangxi. His courtesy name was Minzhan; he was registered in Yongxin County, Jiangxi, and was a native of Anfu County. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the wuxu year.

Proctors
Zheng Zhang, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Shiji; he was a native of Min County, Fujian, and became a metropolitan graduate in the dingchou year.
Wei Liangfu, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right in the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Shizhao; he was a native of Xinjian County, Jiangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in the bingxu year.

Examination Supervisors
Shen Hong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Guangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Weiyuan; he was a native of Chongde County, Zhejiang, and became a metropolitan graduate in the yiwei year.
He Zhongxing, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Guangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Cuifu; he was a native of Shunde County, Guangdong, and became a metropolitan graduate in the renchen year.

Examiners
Zhan Shan, Professor at the Confucian School of Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. His courtesy name was Tingpei; he was a native of Fuliang County, Jiangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year.
Lin Gaogang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Fengming; he was a native of Huai'an County, Fujian, and became a tribute student (gongshi) in the bingwu year.

Associate Examiners
Wu Shizhao, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xuzhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region. His courtesy name was Yide; he was a native of Huai'an County, Fujian, and became a tribute student in the guimao year.
Jiang Ruji, Instructor at the Confucian School of Taihe County, Yingzhou, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. His courtesy name was Jizhi; he was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and became a tribute student in the gengzi year.
Ma Jinjie, Instructor at the Confucian School of Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Kangfu; he was a native of Neijiang County, Sichuan, and became a tribute student in the gengzi year.
Xiao Xianggeng, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shanghang County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian. His courtesy name was Wenhuan; he was a native of Taihe County, Jiangxi, and became a tribute student in the gengzi year.
Lin Yiyi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Chun'an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Chenghong; he was a native of Houguan County, Fujian, and became a tribute student in the bingwu year.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
顏淵季路侍子曰盍各言爾志子路曰願
車馬衣輕裘與朋友共敝之而無憾顏
淵曰願無伐善無施勞子路曰願聞子
之志子曰老者安之朋友信之少者懷
之
上天之載無聲無臭至矣
至於心獨無所同然乎心之所同然者何
===
也謂理也義也聖人先得我心之所同
然耳
易
彖曰大畜剛健篤實輝光日新其德
受玆介福以中正也
易與天地準故能彌綸天地之道
復德之本也恆德之固也
書
帝曰咨四岳有能典朕三禮僉曰伯夷帝
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

顏淵、季路侍。子曰：「盍各言爾志？」子路曰：「願車馬衣輕裘，與朋友共，敝之而無憾。」顏淵曰：「願無伐善，無施勞。」子路曰：「願聞子之志。」子曰：「老者安之，朋友信之，少者懷之。」

「上天之載，無聲無臭。」至矣！

至於心，獨無所同然乎？心之所同然者何也？謂理也，義也。聖人先得我心之所同然耳。

易

彖曰：「大畜，剛健篤實，輝光日新其德。」

受玆介福，以中正也。

易與天地準，故能彌綸天地之道。

復，德之本也；恆，德之固也。

書

帝曰：「咨，四岳！有能典朕三禮？」僉曰：「伯夷。」帝
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Yan Yuan and Ji Lu were attending upon the Master. The Master said, “Why does each of you not state his aspirations?” Zilu said, “I wish to share my carriages, horses, and light fur robes with my friends, and have no regrets even if they wear them out.” Yan Yuan said, “I wish neither to boast of my merits nor to make a display of my services.” Zilu said, “We would like to hear your aspirations, Master.” The Master said, “To give the aged peace, to be trusted by friends, and to cherish the young.”

“The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” This is the utmost!

As for the heart, is it alone without anything that all hearts alike approve? What is it that all hearts alike approve? It is principle and righteousness. The sages simply apprehended before us what our hearts alike approve.

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Judgment says: “Great Accumulation: firm and vigorous, substantial and true, radiant and bright, daily renewing its virtue.”

“To receive this great blessing” is due to being central and correct.

The Changes accords with Heaven and Earth; thus it can encompass and weave together the Way of Heaven and Earth.

Return is the foundation of virtue; Constancy is the firmness of virtue.

文王惟克厥宅心乃克立兹常事司牧人
以克俊有德
不剛不柔厥德允修
詩
四之日其蚤獻羔祭韭
===
樂具入奏以綏後祿
昭兹來許繩其祖武於萬斯年受天之祜
受天之祜四方來賀於萬斯年不遐有
佐
四海來假來假祈祈景員維河殷受命咸
宜百祿是何
春秋
春齊人陳人曹人伐宋〔莊公十有四年〕
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
punctuated:
曰：「俞！咨！伯，汝作秩宗，夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。」伯拜稽首，讓于夔、龍。帝曰：「俞！往，欽哉！」
「其爾克紹乃辟于先王，永綏民。」說拜稽首，曰：「敢對揚天子之休命。」
文王惟克厥宅心，乃克立兹常事、司牧人，以克俊有德。
不剛不柔，厥德允修。
詩
四之日其蚤，獻羔祭韭。
樂具入奏，以綏後祿。
昭兹來許，繩其祖武。於萬斯年，受天之祜。受天之祜，四方來賀。於萬斯年，不遐有佐。
四海來假，來假祈祈。景員維河，殷受命咸宜，百祿是何。
春秋
春，齊人、陳人、曹人伐宋。〔莊公十有四年〕
秦人伐晉。〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦。〔文公四年〕
translation_en:
…said: “Yes! Ah, Bo, you shall serve as Minister of Ancestral Rites. Be reverent morning and night; be upright and pure.” Bo bowed and knocked his head to the ground, yielding the appointment to Kui and Long. The emperor said: “Yes! Go, and be reverent!”
“May you enable your sovereign to carry on the work of the former kings and bring lasting peace to the people.” Yue bowed and knocked his head to the ground, saying: “I venture to acknowledge and extol the Son of Heaven’s gracious command.”
King Wen was able to set his heart aright; thus he could appoint those responsible for regular affairs and those who shepherded the people, employing men of outstanding virtue.
Neither harsh nor yielding, his virtue was truly cultivated.
Book of Odes
In the fourth month, early in the season, they offer a lamb and sacrifice with chives.
All the musicians enter and perform, securing blessings to come.
Illuminate those who come after, following your ancestors’ footsteps. For ten thousand years, receive Heaven’s blessings. Receive Heaven’s blessings, and let the four quarters come to congratulate you. For ten thousand years, shall you not have helpers?
From all within the four seas they come, arriving in multitudes. Vast and encompassing is the River [?]. Yin received the mandate in full accord with what was fitting, bearing a hundred blessings.
Spring and Autumn Annals
In spring, troops of Qi, Chen, and Cao attacked Song. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
Troops of Qin attacked Jin. 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin. 〔Fourth year of Duke Wen.〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
夏齊人伐我北鄙僖公二十有六年晉欒
書帥師救鄭成公六年冬公會晉侯宋
公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯
小邾子齊世子光伐鄭十有二月已亥
同盟于戲襄公九年
夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷齊人
來歸鄆讙龜陰田俱定公十年叔孫州
仇帥師墮郈季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師
墮費俱定公十有二年
===
禮記
禮也者猶體也體不備君子謂之不成人
設之不當猶不備也禮有大有小有顯
有微大者不可損小者不可益顯者不
可揜微者不可大也故經禮三百曲禮
三千其致一也未有入室而不由戶者
是故情見而義立樂終而德尊
忠臣以事其君孝子以事其親其本一也
氣如白虹天也精神見于山川地也
punctuated:
夏，齊人伐我北鄙。僖公二十有六年。晉欒書帥師救鄭。成公六年。冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月，已亥，同盟于戲。襄公九年。
夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。俱定公十年。叔孫州仇帥師墮郈。季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。俱定公十有二年。
禮記
禮也者，猶體也。體不備，君子謂之不成人；設之不當，猶不備也。禮有大，有小，有顯，有微。大者不可損，小者不可益，顯者不可揜，微者不可大也。故經禮三百，曲禮三千，其致一也。未有入室而不由戶者。
是故情見而義立，樂終而德尊。
忠臣以事其君，孝子以事其親，其本一也。
氣如白虹，天也；精神見于山川，地也。
translation_en:
In summer, the men of Qi attacked our northern borderlands. The twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi. Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. The sixth year of Duke Cheng. In winter, the duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, the Viscount of Xiaozhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the yihai [?] day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Xi. The ninth year of Duke Xiang.
In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. The men of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. All are from the tenth year of Duke Ding. Shusun Zhouchou led an army to demolish the fortifications of Hou. Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army to demolish the fortifications of Bi. Both are from the twelfth year of Duke Ding.
Record of Rites (Liji)
Ritual is like the body. If the body is incomplete, the gentleman calls it an incomplete person; if its parts are improperly arranged, that is likewise incompleteness. Ritual has great and small elements, conspicuous and subtle elements. The great must not be diminished, the small must not be augmented, the conspicuous must not be obscured, and the subtle must not be magnified. Thus there are three hundred principal rules of ritual and three thousand detailed rules, but their ultimate purpose is one. No one enters a room without passing through its doorway.
Thus feelings become manifest and righteousness is established; when the music ends, virtue is honored.
The loyal minister thereby serves his ruler, and the filial son thereby serves his parents: their foundation is one.
Vital force like a white rainbow pertains to Heaven; spiritual essence manifest in the mountains and rivers pertains to Earth.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之隆皆未有如我
太祖高皇帝之盛者也仰惟
功德高厚
身兼創守未易窺測然其
恢鴻略以啓再造之景運
垂燕翼以綿萬世之太平者必有道焉可得
而揚言之與程氏論王道必本之學術
孔子歎堯無能名固曰煥乎其有文章
然則學術文章亦可以窺
===
皇祖之萬一否乎伏聞
皇祖與待制秦裕伯論學術學士詹同論文章
聖謨洋洋固是道也當時或發之事業脩之播
告與夫臣工之所贊述亦可得而聞其
槩與詩書所稱二帝三王之道詳矣其
同符者可指言之與漢唐宋開造之迹
與其學術文章固無足論者恭惟
皇上中興
聖德
punctuated: 之隆，皆未有如我太祖高皇帝之盛者也。仰惟功德高厚，身兼創守，未易窺測。然其恢鴻略以啓再造之景運，垂燕翼以綿萬世之太平者，必有道焉，可得而揚言之與？程氏論王道，必本之學術；孔子歎堯無能名，固曰：「煥乎其有文章！」然則學術文章，亦可以窺皇祖之萬一否乎？伏聞皇祖與待制秦裕伯論學術，學士詹同論文章，聖謨洋洋，固是道也。當時或發之事業，脩之播告，與夫臣工之所贊述，亦可得而聞其槩與？《詩》《書》所稱二帝三王之道詳矣，其同符者，可指言之與？漢唐宋開造之迹，與其學術文章，固無足論者。恭惟皇上中興，聖德
translation_en:
…in the magnificence of their governance, none has ever equaled the greatness of our Emperor Taizu Gao. Reverently considering his lofty achievements and profound virtue, and how he combined in his own person the founding and preservation of the dynasty, we find these things difficult to fathom. Yet there must have been a Way by which he extended his grand strategy to inaugurate the glorious destiny of renewed creation, and bequeathed provision for his descendants to perpetuate peace for myriad generations. Can you expound it openly? Master Cheng, in discussing the kingly Way, invariably grounded it in learning. Confucius, marveling that none could adequately name Yao’s greatness, nevertheless said: “How splendid were his cultural accomplishments!” Might learning and literary accomplishment, then, also afford a glimpse of even one ten-thousandth of our imperial ancestor’s greatness?

We have humbly heard that our imperial ancestor discussed learning with the Auxiliary Qin Yubo and literary composition with the Academician Zhan Tong. His sagely counsels were vast and abundant: surely they embodied this Way. As for what was then expressed in his undertakings, elaborated in his proclamations, and praised and recorded by his ministers, might we also hear an outline of it? The Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings is described in detail in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. Can you identify and explain the points at which his Way accorded with theirs? The founding achievements of the Han, Tang, and Song, together with their learning and literary accomplishments, are certainly unworthy of discussion. Reverently considering His Majesty’s restoration of flourishing rule, his sagely virtue…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天縱學術文章淵源炳蔚光揚
前烈丕纘
祖謨我
皇祖申錫無疆之休至是益巍巍蕩蕩矣
聖祖
神孫授守一道必有所本與諸士子服濡
聖化有年願鋪張于篇以鳴
國家之盛
問經以載道學以窮經誦其文弗知其義
===
淆於衆莫折其衷謂之窮經可乎玆以
經學之疑與二三子訂之周官太卜掌
三易夏商之易取七八周易取九六何
不同也周易上經三十卦下經三十四
卦或謂以反觀之皆十八卦然與否與
孔子刪書斷自唐虞以下迄於周終於
秦誓秦誓費誓果可與帝王之書相繼
而並傳乎傳之後儒何以為古文今文
之辨詩三百始關雎也有謂詩有四始
punctuated:
天縱，學術文章淵源炳蔚，光揚前烈，丕纘祖謨。我皇祖申錫無疆之休，至是益巍巍蕩蕩矣。聖祖神孫，授守一道，必有所本與？諸士子服濡聖化有年，願鋪張于篇，以鳴國家之盛。

問：經以載道，學以窮經，誦其文弗知其義，淆於衆莫折其衷，謂之窮經可乎？玆以經學之疑與二三子訂之。《周官》太卜掌三易，夏商之易取七八，《周易》取九六，何不同也？《周易》上經三十卦，下經三十四卦，或謂以反觀之皆十八卦，然與否與？孔子刪《書》，斷自唐虞以下，迄於周，終於《秦誓》。《秦誓》《費誓》果可與帝王之書相繼而並傳乎？傳之後儒，何以為古文今文之辨？《詩》三百，始《關雎》也，有謂詩有四始
translation_en:
…endowed by Heaven, with learning and literary accomplishments of profound origins and brilliant expression, he glorifies the achievements of his predecessors and grandly carries forward his ancestors’ plans. Our imperial ancestor has bestowed blessings without limit, which have now become still more lofty and vast. The sage ancestor and his divine descendant follow a single Way in transmitting and preserving their inheritance: surely this must have a foundation? You examination candidates have long been steeped in the sage sovereign’s transforming influence. We ask you to expound this fully in your essays, proclaiming the flourishing state of the dynasty.

Question: The classics convey the Way, and learning seeks to fathom the classics. If one recites their words without understanding their meaning, is confused by the multitude of opinions, and cannot determine the proper interpretation, can this be called fathoming the classics? Here, then, are some disputed points in classical learning for you gentlemen to resolve. In the Offices of Zhou, the Grand Diviner has charge of the three Changes. The Changes of the Xia and Shang use seven and eight, whereas the Changes of Zhou uses nine and six. Why do they differ? The upper section of the Changes of Zhou contains thirty hexagrams, and the lower section thirty-four. Some say that, when considered in terms of inversion, each contains eighteen hexagrams. Is this correct or not? When Confucius edited the Documents, he began with Tang and Yu, continued down to the Zhou, and concluded with the “Oath of Qin.” Can the “Oath of Qin” and the “Oath at Fei” truly follow the documents of the emperors and kings and be transmitted alongside them? As the text was transmitted to later Confucian scholars, on what basis was the distinction between the Old Text and the New Text made? The three hundred poems of the Odes begin with “Guanju” (“The Ospreys”). Some say that the Odes has four beginnings…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者其說何居春秋之義微哉婉矣有謂
大義數十炳如日星者其要安在禮記
始於曲禮名曲禮者何義豈著作於曲
臺緇衣依倣論語作緇衣者何人曷拘
泥於援引月令紀時政紀王居紀方位
王制言爵位言官制言巡狩抑皆經世
不易之道否耶後世有孟氏易梁丘易
大小夏侯尚書歐陽尚書言詩者四家
各爲專門言春秋者三傳互相牴牾言
===
禮者后蒼大小戴王鄭異喙而爭鳴其
於聖經孰爲得其宗派也他如太玄擬
易與司馬氏之潛虛孰優湯征擬書與
河內女子之秦誓孰正馬鄭之發明衛
孔之序說孰有功於毛詩范氏之集解
戴氏之解疑孰無媿於公穀皇熊諸氏
南北異派孰於經禮無背馳耶此皆經
學之大疑知道者所宜辨析其究言之
問忠孝生人之大端節義持身之大閑所
punctuated:
者，其說何居？《春秋》之義微哉婉矣，有謂大義數十炳如日星者，其要安在？《禮記》始於《曲禮》，名《曲禮》者何義？豈著作於曲臺？《緇衣》依倣《論語》，作《緇衣》者何人？曷拘泥於援引？《月令》紀時政、紀王居、紀方位，《王制》言爵位、言官制、言巡狩，抑皆經世不易之道否耶？後世有孟氏易、梁丘易、大小夏侯尚書、歐陽尚書，言《詩》者四家，各爲專門；言《春秋》者三傳，互相牴牾；言禮者后蒼、大小戴、王、鄭，異喙而爭鳴，其於聖經孰爲得其宗派也？他如《太玄》擬《易》，與司馬氏之《潛虛》孰優？《湯征》擬《書》，與河內女子之《秦誓》孰正？馬、鄭之發明，衛、孔之序說，孰有功於《毛詩》？范氏之《集解》、戴氏之《解疑》，孰無媿於公、穀？皇、熊諸氏，南北異派，孰於經禮無背馳耶？此皆經學之大疑，知道者所宜辨析，其究言之。

問：忠孝，生人之大端；節義，持身之大閑，所
translation_en:
…what is the basis for this explanation? The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is subtle and indirect. Some say that its several dozen great principles shine as brightly as the sun and stars: where does their essence lie? The Record of Rites begins with “Detailed Rules of Propriety” (Quli). What does this title mean? Could it be that the text was composed at the Qu Terrace? “Black Robes” (Ziyi) follows the example of the Analects. Who composed “Black Robes”? Why did its author adhere so rigidly to citing earlier texts? “Monthly Ordinances” records seasonal government measures, the king’s residences, and the cardinal directions; “Royal Regulations” discusses ranks of nobility, official institutions, and tours of inspection. Are these all immutable principles for ordering the world? In later ages there were the Meng and Liangqiu traditions of the Changes, and the Elder and Younger Xiahou and Ouyang traditions of the Documents. The four schools expounding the Odes each established a specialized tradition; the Three Commentaries expounding the Spring and Autumn Annals contradict one another; and those expounding ritual—Hou Cang, the Elder and Younger Dai, Wang, and Zheng—contend with one another in divergent voices. Which of them inherited the true lineage of the sages’ classics? Further, the Supreme Mystery (Taixuan) takes the Changes as its model: how does it compare in merit with Master Sima’s Hidden Void (Qianxu)? “Tang’s Expedition” (Tang zheng) takes the Documents as its model: which is more orthodox, it or the “Oath of Qin” associated with the woman of Henei? Of Ma’s and Zheng’s elucidations and Wei’s and Kong’s prefatory explanations, which contributed most to the Mao Odes? Of Master Fan’s Collected Explanations and Master Dai’s Resolution of Doubts, which does justice to the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries? Among Huang, Xiong, and the other scholars belonging to the different northern and southern schools, who did not depart from the canonical teachings on ritual? These are all major disputed questions in classical scholarship, which those who understand the Way ought to distinguish and analyze. Discuss them exhaustively.

Question: Loyalty and filial piety are the great foundations of human life; integrity and righteousness are the great restraints governing personal conduct, the means by which…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以扶綱常立人紀世道攸賴試稽往牒
與諸士商之仗節匈奴與志不忘宋者
其忠同乎陳情歸養與棄官尋母者其
孝同乎畏知却金與擲金不顧者孰優
千家待火與千畝給族者孰賢抑其所
遇時勢不同或出一念感激未必其蹈
于中庸否耶夫忠孝一道也盡忠晉室
者何以絕裾于親負名國士者何以辱
身于虜節義並用也抗表不屈者何以
有三上書之議輔政同心者何以有附
許史之譏漢庭師傅當時倚重槐里
令廷辱數言邪佞顯矣柳州惠政千古
流芳觀王叔文陳情一表悖謬甚矣是
數子者得失可言要之勢難曲全時不
我遇有當原情誅心者邪余觀甌駱旣
郡風氣漸開賢材彙征後先表著若正
色立朝募兵衛國刻木祀母甘露降亭
亦可以言忠孝矣忤時謝病罵賊守城
punctuated: 以扶綱常，立人紀，世道攸賴。試稽往牒，與諸士商之。仗節匈奴與志不忘宋者，其忠同乎？陳情歸養與棄官尋母者，其孝同乎？畏知却金與擲金不顧者，孰優？千家待火與千畝給族者，孰賢？抑其所遇時勢不同，或出一念感激，未必其蹈于中庸否耶？夫忠孝一道也，盡忠晉室者何以絕裾于親？負名國士者何以辱身于虜？節義並用也，抗表不屈者何以有三上書之議？輔政同心者何以有附許史之譏？漢庭師傅，當時倚重，槐里令廷辱數言，邪佞顯矣。柳州惠政，千古流芳，觀王叔文陳情一表，悖謬甚矣。是數子者，得失可言。要之，勢難曲全，時不我遇，有當原情誅心者邪？余觀甌駱旣郡，風氣漸開，賢材彙征，後先表著。若正色立朝，募兵衛國，刻木祀母，甘露降亭，亦可以言忠孝矣。忤時謝病，罵賊守城，
translation_en:
… by which the cardinal relationships and constant virtues are upheld and the norms of human relations established: on these the moral order of the world depends. Let us examine the records of the past and discuss them with you candidates. Were the man who held fast to his envoy’s tally among the Xiongnu and the man whose resolve never forsook the Song alike in loyalty? Were the man who submitted a statement of his circumstances and returned home to care for his elder and the man who abandoned office to seek his mother alike in filial devotion? Who was superior: the man who refused gold because he feared that his conduct was known, or the man who cast gold aside without a backward glance? Who was worthier: the man whose thousand households awaited fire [?], or the man who provided a thousand mu of land to support his clan? Or did the circumstances of their times differ, with some acting upon a moment’s intense emotion, so that they did not necessarily tread the path of the Mean?
Loyalty and filial devotion constitute a single Way. Why, then, did the man who devoted himself loyally to the Jin ruling house sever his robe’s skirt to break away from his parent? Why did the man renowned as an outstanding man of the realm suffer personal humiliation among the enemy? Integrity and righteousness must be exercised together. Why, then, did the man who resolutely submitted a memorial and refused to yield incur criticism for submitting letters three times? Why did those who assisted the government with a common purpose incur reproach for attaching themselves to the Xu and Shi families? The tutor at the Han court was greatly relied upon in his day; yet the Magistrate of Huaili publicly denounced him at court in a few words, making his wickedness and flattery plain. The benevolent administration of Liuzhou has left a fragrant reputation through the ages; yet consider the memorial setting forth Wang Shuwen’s circumstances [?]: how gravely perverse and mistaken it was! The merits and faults of these men can be discussed. Ultimately, circumstances make it difficult to satisfy every obligation, and the times may afford a man no opportunity. Are there cases in which we should consider the circumstances sympathetically, and others in which we should condemn the underlying intent?
I observe that, once Ouluo had been organized into commanderies, its customs gradually became more enlightened. Worthy and talented men advanced together, distinguishing themselves one after another. Such deeds as standing upright and grave at court, recruiting troops to defend the state, carving a wooden image through which to offer sacrifices to one’s mother, and causing sweet dew to descend upon a pavilion may indeed be spoken of as loyalty and filial devotion. Defying the temper of the times and pleading illness to retire, reviling rebels and defending a city…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
遠妾不取直金却賜請蠲郡賦亦可以
言節義矣不知亦視古相伯仲否也諸
士幸際
明時應玆掄選居常臧否古人詳矣矧同鄕
先哲尤在景仰顧所自期待當不止是
其詳著之以覘異時所樹立者
問綏衆保邦守令莫先禦侮敵愾將帥獨
重蓋聞古之守令將帥固有京師蒙福
而河內願留虎爲却走而犬不驚吠野
===
麥獻瑞而三異化成其視民不忍欺人
不敢犯民不見吏路不拾遺者何如也
或雄虎視于山東或絕胡騎于塞北或
三十年遠却秦兵或一人不殺而下江
南其視雅歌投壺輕裘緩帶單騎見虜
西賊膽寒者何如也我
朝稽古立法文武並用故當時前後粤西諸
臣有民饑不暇請賑捐俸以活者有課
農興學禱雨隨應者又有衣冠入峒賊
punctuated:
遠妾不取，直金却賜，請蠲郡賦，亦可以言節義矣。不知亦視古相伯仲否也？諸士幸際明時，應玆掄選，居常臧否古人詳矣，矧同鄕先哲，尤在景仰。顧所自期待，當不止是。其詳著之，以覘異時所樹立者。
問：綏衆保邦，守令莫先；禦侮敵愾，將帥獨重。蓋聞古之守令將帥，固有京師蒙福而河內願留，虎爲却走而犬不驚吠，野麥獻瑞而三異化成。其視民不忍欺、人不敢犯、民不見吏、路不拾遺者何如也？或雄虎視于山東，或絕胡騎于塞北，或三十年遠却秦兵，或一人不殺而下江南。其視雅歌投壺、輕裘緩帶、單騎見虜、西賊膽寒者何如也？我朝稽古立法，文武並用，故當時前後粤西諸臣，有民饑不暇請賑、捐俸以活者，有課農興學、禱雨隨應者，又有衣冠入峒，賊
translation_en:
…refusing a concubine sent from afar [?], declining a gift of gold [?], and requesting remission of a commandery’s taxes—these, too, may be called integrity and righteousness. Yet I wonder whether they rank alongside the men of antiquity. You candidates are fortunate to live in an enlightened age and to participate in this selection. In your ordinary studies, you have assessed the merits and faults of the ancients in detail; all the more should you admire the worthy predecessors of your own region. Yet what you expect of yourselves should go beyond this. Set out your views fully, so that we may discern what you will accomplish in the future.
Question: In bringing peace to the people and safeguarding the state, none take precedence over prefects and magistrates; in resisting aggression and confronting the enemy, generals bear particular responsibility. We have heard that among the prefects, magistrates, and generals of antiquity were men whose blessings reached the capital and whom the people of Henei wished to retain; men before whom tigers retreated and under whom dogs did not bark in alarm; and men under whom wild wheat appeared as an auspicious sign and three extraordinary portents marked the success of their transforming influence. How do they compare with those whom the people could not bear to deceive, whom no one dared offend, under whom the people never saw an official, or under whom no one picked up lost property on the roads? Some stood in Shandong with the commanding gaze of a tiger; some cut off the cavalry of the Hu beyond the northern frontier; some kept Qin’s armies far away for thirty years; and some subdued Jiangnan without killing a single person. How do they compare with those who sang refined songs and played pitch-pot, wore light fur robes with loosely fastened sashes, rode alone to meet the enemy, or struck terror into the western rebels?
Our dynasty has examined antiquity in establishing its institutions and employed civil and military talent together. Thus, among the successive officials who served in western Yue, there were those who, when the people starved, gave up their salaries to keep them alive, without waiting to request famine relief; those who encouraged agriculture and promoted learning, and whose prayers for rain were promptly answered; and those who entered the mountain settlements in official cap and robes, and the bandits …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
隨以化者是皆守令之賢果有龔黃卓
魯之循良否耶有克靜江而禁止剽掠
者有掛印出鎭而秋毫無犯者又有平
兩江五谿而峒寨悉降者是皆將帥之
良果有伏波韓岳之風聲否耶邇矣南
服二者之選視內爲重而民流戶泯甚
于昔時飛矢鳴鏑殆無虛日其故安在
玆欲使布列郡縣介胄封疆者咸得其
人果何道以致之諸士目睹衷惕有懷
===
久矣願明著于篇
問我
皇祖式昭丕訓有曰治兵始可以休兵講武始
可以偃武穆如遠哉固萬世
保大之鴻憲也乃若廣西則自昔用武之地
所不可一日而去兵者今試撮舉要害
莫如三江紛紛之議胡累日積歲卒無
畫一豈治兵講武未得其道邪夫斷藤
之寇最號劇猾乃今曠然空土旅人宵
punctuated:
隨以化者，是皆守令之賢，果有龔黃卓魯之循良否耶？有克靜江而禁止剽掠者，有掛印出鎭而秋毫無犯者，又有平兩江五谿而峒寨悉降者，是皆將帥之良，果有伏波韓岳之風聲否耶？邇矣，南服二者之選視內爲重，而民流戶泯甚于昔時，飛矢鳴鏑殆無虛日，其故安在？玆欲使布列郡縣、介胄封疆者咸得其人，果何道以致之？諸士目睹衷惕，有懷久矣，願明著于篇。
問：我皇祖式昭丕訓，有曰：「治兵始可以休兵，講武始可以偃武。」穆如遠哉！固萬世保大之鴻憲也。乃若廣西，則自昔用武之地，所不可一日而去兵者。今試撮舉要害，莫如三江。紛紛之議，胡累日積歲卒無畫一？豈治兵講武未得其道邪？夫斷藤之寇最號劇猾，乃今曠然空土，旅人宵
translation_en:
…whereupon they were reformed. These were all worthy prefects and magistrates; did they indeed possess the conscientious goodness of Gong, Huang, Zhuo, and Lu? There were those who captured Jingjiang and prohibited plundering, those who received their seals of command and went out to guard the region without allowing the slightest encroachment upon the people, and those who pacified the Two Rivers and Five Streams, so that all the dong settlements and stockades surrendered. These were all fine generals; did they indeed possess the influence and renown of the General Who Calms the Waves, Han, and Yue? Recently, appointments to these two kinds of office in the southern territories have been regarded as more important than those in the interior. Yet the displacement of the people and disappearance of households have become worse than before, and scarcely a day passes without flying arrows and whistling arrowheads. Where does the cause lie? If we now wish to ensure that the right men fill all the posts throughout the prefectures and counties and serve in armor on the frontiers, by what means can we accomplish this? You gentlemen have witnessed these things, felt alarm in your hearts, and long harbored thoughts about them. Please set these out clearly in your essays.
Question: Our imperial ancestor clearly proclaimed a great instruction, saying: “Only by putting the troops in order can one bring military operations to rest; only by practicing the martial arts can one lay arms aside.” How august and far-reaching! This is indeed a grand rule for preserving the greatness of the realm through all ages. Guangxi, however, has been a place of warfare since ancient times, where troops cannot be dispensed with for even a single day. If we now briefly identify the strategically crucial places, none surpasses the Three Rivers. Why, amid the welter of proposals, have days and years accumulated without a unified plan ever being reached? Could it be that the proper way to organize troops and practice military skills has not been found? The bandits of Duanteng were reputed to be the most violent and cunning, yet now the land lies open and empty, and travelers at night…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
征矣古田近邑往稱繁庶數十年來顧
爾頑梗此其故何哉時與勢殊邪抑所
謂治兵講武昔勤而今或弛邪說者謂
左右兩江經略已定所未備者節目之
詳若府江一帶與古田獷獠非別有區
畫未可但已然與否與夫平居而負天
下之責士之自待宜不多讓且鄉井之
間耳目時及必有抱百年無事之策者
况休兵偃武有司願聞固不得而默如
===
也
punctuated: 征矣。古田近邑，往稱繁庶，數十年來顧爾頑梗，此其故何哉？時與勢殊邪？抑所謂治兵講武，昔勤而今或弛邪？說者謂左右兩江經略已定，所未備者節目之詳；若府江一帶與古田獷獠，非別有區畫，未可但已。然與否與？夫平居而負天下之責，士之自待宜不多讓。且鄉井之間，耳目時及，必有抱百年無事之策者。况休兵偃武，有司願聞，固不得而默如也。
translation_en:
…journey by night. Gutian, a nearby county, was formerly known for its prosperity and populousness; yet for several decades it has been obstinately defiant. What accounts for this? Have the times and circumstances changed? Or were people formerly diligent in what is called organizing troops and practicing military skills, while now they have perhaps grown lax? Some say that the overall strategy for the Zuo and You Rivers has already been settled, and that what remains incomplete is the detail of its implementation; but that the Fu River region and the fierce Lao people of Gutian require separate planning, without which matters cannot simply be left as they are. Is this so or not?

Even in private life, scholars bear responsibility for all under Heaven; in what they expect of themselves, they should not readily yield that responsibility to others. Moreover, these are matters within your own home region, which you hear and see from time to time. Surely some among you hold a plan that could secure a hundred years free from trouble. Furthermore, the responsible officials wish to hear how troops may be rested and warfare brought to an end. You certainly must not remain silent.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
顏淵季路侍子曰盍各言爾志子路曰願
車馬衣輕裘與朋友共敝之而無憾顏淵
曰願無伐善無施勞子路曰願聞子之志
子曰老者安之朋友信之少者懷之
張元舉
同考試官教諭林批詞暢理順善學聖賢而有得者
同考試官教諭蕭批聖賢氣象讀此宛然可見
===
考試官教諭林批言志處親切有味佳士也
考試官教授詹批能發聖賢之蘊允魁多士錄之
聖賢問答各言其志而小大可見也夫志於人
大矣觀於聖賢之志而其小大之異有不可見
哉昔顏淵季路侍於聖門夫子啓之曰士固有
志人每異趨二子之志何不各言之蓋示以辨
志之教也子路乃言曰人惟病于自私是故不
能以所有者公於人由則願己之有是車馬輕
裘焉通於朋友初無所吝也至於敝壞亦不爲
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
顏淵、季路侍。子曰：「盍各言爾志？」子路曰：「願車馬衣輕裘，與朋友共，敝之而無憾。」顏淵曰：「願無伐善，無施勞。」子路曰：「願聞子之志。」子曰：「老者安之，朋友信之，少者懷之。」
張元舉
同考試官教諭林批：「詞暢理順，善學聖賢而有得者。」
同考試官教諭蕭批：「聖賢氣象，讀此宛然可見。」
考試官教諭林批：「言志處親切有味，佳士也。」
考試官教授詹批：「能發聖賢之蘊，允魁多士，錄之。」
聖賢問答，各言其志，而小大可見也。夫志於人大矣，觀於聖賢之志，而其小大之異有不可見哉？昔顏淵、季路侍於聖門，夫子啓之曰：「士固有志，人每異趨，二子之志何不各言之？」蓋示以辨志之教也。子路乃言曰：「人惟病于自私，是故不能以所有者公於人。由則願己之有是車馬輕裘焉，通於朋友，初無所吝也；至於敝壞，亦不爲
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

Yan Yuan and Ji Lu were attending upon the Master. The Master said, “Why does each of you not state his aspiration?” Zilu said, “I wish to share my carriages, horses, and light fur garments with my friends, without regret even if they wear them out.” Yan Yuan said, “I wish neither to boast of my goodness nor to make a display of my meritorious efforts.” Zilu said, “We would like to hear your aspiration.” The Master said, “To give the aged ease, to be trustworthy toward friends, and to cherish the young.”

Zhang Yuanju

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The language flows freely and the reasoning proceeds smoothly. He has learned well from the sages and worthies and gained insight.”

Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: “Reading this, one can vividly perceive the bearing of the sages and worthies.”

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The passages stating the aspirations are direct and rich in meaning. An excellent scholar.”

Examiner Zhan, Professor, comments: “He can bring out the profound meanings of the sages and worthies. Truly deserving to head the many scholars; include this answer in the record.”

As the sage and worthies questioned and answered one another, each stated his aspiration, and their lesser and greater scope became apparent. Aspiration is indeed of great consequence to a person. When we consider the aspirations of the sage and worthies, how could the difference in their scope fail to be apparent? In former times, Yan Yuan and Ji Lu attended upon the Master in his school. The Master prompted them, saying, “Scholars certainly have aspirations, yet people often pursue different courses. Why do you two not each state your aspiration?” Thus he offered instruction in discerning aspirations. Zilu then said, “People suffer from selfishness, and therefore cannot share what they possess with others. As for me, You, I wish to make whatever carriages, horses, and light fur garments I possess available to my friends, without the slightest reluctance from the outset. Even when these become worn out, I would not consider it…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
憾也此其由之志乎顏淵乃言曰人惟狃于自
滿是故恒以所長者矜於人回則願已之有是
善與勞焉善世不伐有而若無也有功不德實
而若虛也此其回之志乎子路喜於有聞從而
請曰夫子之志固所願聞蓋欲審所尚以為的
也夫子乃告之曰不齊者在物之情順施者吾
心之理天下之人有老者有朋友有少者至不
一也其欲安其欲信其欲懷情則同也吾欲使
斯人老者養之以安朋友與之以信少者懷之
===
以恩即其所有之理盡其所處之道於彼無加
也於我無與也廓然其大公物來而順應吾之
志如斯而已矣吁子路之不私者物也顏淵之
不有者善也勞也若夫子則無物無我無善無
勞如太和元氣之渾然流行而萬物各得其所
此固聖賢之別也謂為天地氣象詎不信哉大
抵聖人之心天地之心也天地普萬物而無心
聖人順萬事而無情道一而已回由二子則固
囿於天地中者由之升堂回之卓爾時雨化之
punctuated: 憾也。此其由之志乎？顏淵乃言曰：「人惟狃于自滿，是故恒以所長者矜於人。回則願已之有是善與勞焉，善世不伐，有而若無也；有功不德，實而若虛也。此其回之志乎？」子路喜於有聞，從而請曰：「夫子之志，固所願聞。」蓋欲審所尚以為的也。夫子乃告之曰：「不齊者，在物之情；順施者，吾心之理。天下之人，有老者，有朋友，有少者，至不一也。其欲安，其欲信，其欲懷，情則同也。吾欲使斯人，老者養之以安，朋友與之以信，少者懷之以恩。即其所有之理，盡其所處之道，於彼無加也，於我無與也。廓然其大公，物來而順應。吾之志如斯而已矣。」吁！子路之不私者，物也；顏淵之不有者，善也，勞也。若夫子，則無物無我，無善無勞，如太和元氣之渾然流行，而萬物各得其所。此固聖賢之別也。謂為天地氣象，詎不信哉？大抵聖人之心，天地之心也。天地普萬物而無心，聖人順萬事而無情，道一而已。回、由二子，則固囿於天地中者。由之升堂，回之卓爾，時雨化之
translation_en:
…nor would I regret it. Would this not be my aspiration, as You?” Yan Yuan then said: “People become habituated to self-satisfaction, and so constantly boast to others of their strengths. My wish, as Hui, is that, whatever goodness and meritorious service I possess, I might benefit the world without boasting, possessing yet seeming to possess nothing; that I might achieve merit without claiming credit, being full yet seeming empty. Would this not be my aspiration, as Hui?” Zilu, delighted by what he had heard, then asked: “We earnestly wish to hear the Master’s aspiration.” He wished to ascertain what the Master esteemed and take it as his own target. The Master then told them: “Diversity lies in the circumstances of things; responding appropriately lies in the principle of my heart. Among the people of the world there are the old, friends, and the young: they differ greatly. Yet in wishing for security, trustworthiness, and affection, their feelings are alike. I wish to nourish the old so that they enjoy security, to associate with friends in trustworthiness, and to cherish the young with kindness. Following the principles inherent in them, I would fulfill the Way appropriate to each situation, adding nothing to them and contributing nothing of my own. Vast in impartiality, I would respond appropriately as things came to me. Such, and only such, is my aspiration.”

Ah! What Zilu would not reserve for himself were material possessions; what Yan Yuan would not claim as his own were goodness and meritorious service. As for the Master, there was neither object nor self, neither goodness nor meritorious service: he was like the primordial vital force of supreme harmony, flowing as an undivided whole, with each of the myriad things finding its proper place. This is indeed the distinction between sage and worthy. Is it not true to describe this as the bearing of Heaven and Earth? In general, the sage’s heart is the heart of Heaven and Earth. Heaven and Earth extend to all things without deliberate intent; the sage responds appropriately to all affairs without partial feeling. Their Way is one and the same. Hui and You, however, remained within the bounds of Heaven and Earth. You’s ascending into the hall and Hui’s vision of what stood loftily before him—the timely rain of instruction transformed them…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
矣然他日四子言志獨與曾點而此不與回由
豈弗如點哉或與或告無非至教告之者乃所
以深與之故聖人之教猶天地之化不可以淺
近窺也
上天之載無聲無臭至矣
鍾徠秀
考試官教諭林批不顯篤恭之妙惟天道足以擬之
義理精深作者往往難於措辭此篇善形容善發明非有心得者不
能宜錄之
===
考試官教授詹批無聲無臭不過見天道之微妙必
循字求義則失之粗矣此作獨爲得之至矣處講尤透徹蓋其力學
深造故言之親切而有味也魁選允宜
中庸引言天道之至妙足以狀君子之至德也
夫德而不顯德之至者也非卽天道其何以擬
之子思子由下學立心之始而推以及此若曰
言道君子盡之矣言德不顯盡之矣然所謂不
顯之德者可以易言哉彼皇矣烝民之詩猶有
迹也是未足以盡其妙也不若文王之詩有曰
punctuated:
矣。然他日四子言志，獨與曾點，而此不與回由，豈弗如點哉？或與或告，無非至教；告之者，乃所以深與之。故聖人之教，猶天地之化，不可以淺近窺也。

上天之載，無聲無臭，至矣。
鍾徠秀

考試官教諭林批：不顯篤恭之妙，惟天道足以擬之。義理精深，作者往往難於措辭。此篇善形容，善發明，非有心得者不能，宜錄之。

考試官教授詹批：無聲無臭，不過見天道之微妙，必循字求義，則失之粗矣。此作獨爲得之，「至矣」處講尤透徹。蓋其力學深造，故言之親切而有味也，魁選允宜。

《中庸》引言，天道之至妙，足以狀君子之至德也。夫德而不顯，德之至者也。非卽天道，其何以擬之？子思子由下學立心之始，而推以及此，若曰：言道，君子盡之矣；言德，不顯盡之矣。然所謂不顯之德者，可以易言哉？彼《皇矣》《烝民》之詩，猶有迹也，是未足以盡其妙也。不若《文王》之詩有曰：
translation_en:
…Yet on another occasion, when four disciples spoke of their aspirations, he approved Zeng Dian alone. Does his not approving Hui and You here mean that they were inferior to Dian? Whether expressing approval or offering instruction, he was always imparting the highest teaching. His instructing them was precisely how he expressed his profound approval of them. Thus the sage’s teaching resembles the transforming activity of Heaven and Earth: it cannot be fathomed through a shallow understanding.

“The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell. This is perfection.”
Zhong Laixiu

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The subtlety of unmanifest virtue and earnest reverence can be likened only to the Way of Heaven. The principles involved are profound, and writers often find it difficult to put them into words. This essay excels in description and elucidation—something impossible without personal insight. It merits inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: “Neither sound nor smell” simply reveals the subtlety of the Way of Heaven. To insist on seeking its meaning word by word is to err through a crude understanding. This essay alone captures it; its explanation of “This is perfection” is particularly penetrating. Evidently the author has studied diligently and attained a deep understanding; hence his words are precise and full of significance. His selection for first place is entirely fitting.

The Doctrine of the Mean quotes these words because the supreme subtlety of the Way of Heaven can describe the consummate virtue of the gentleman. Virtue that does not manifest itself is virtue at its highest. Unless one turns to the Way of Heaven, what can serve as its likeness? Master Zisi proceeds from the initial establishment of one’s resolve through elementary learning and extends his argument to this point. It is as though he were saying: when speaking of the Way, the gentleman embodies it fully; when speaking of virtue, its fullness lies in remaining unmanifest. Yet can this so-called unmanifest virtue be spoken of lightly? The poems “Great Is God Above” (Huang yi) and “The Multitude of the People” (Zheng min) still contain perceptible traces; they therefore do not fully express its subtlety. They are unlike the poem “King Wen” (Wen wang), which says: …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
上天之載無聲無臭夫聲臭有氣無形固極天
下之微妙者矣然猶曰無聲猶曰無臭則是動
靜不可求其端也陰陽不可求其始也以是而
擬不顯之德吾知微乎至微同一見聞所不及
妙乎至妙均非方體所能窺於穆之命即君子
之退藏於密理固徹上而徹下者也可謂上下
異致乎無極之真即君子之神明其德善言人
而徵諸天者也可以天人殊觀乎乾知始而妙
萬物者精矣性性以存神者亦非粗也於稽其
===
類足以極形容之妙蓋得意而不可得名焉天
不言而成變化者深矣物物以過化者亦非淺
也即彼喻此足以盡擬議之微蓋至極而無復
餘蘊焉吁不顯之德擬諸天道君子之所以不
可及也德至于此謂之天德學至于此謂之聖
學過此以往其未之或知者乎抑觀子思子之
作中庸始以天命之性終以上天之載者其義
何居始之以天言自天賦人也終之以天言以
人合天也天人合一終篇之義淵乎深矣而其
punctuated: 「上天之載，無聲無臭。」夫聲臭，有氣無形，固極天下之微妙者矣。然猶曰無聲，猶曰無臭，則是動靜不可求其端也，陰陽不可求其始也。以是而擬不顯之德，吾知微乎至微，同一見聞所不及；妙乎至妙，均非方體所能窺。於穆之命，即君子之退藏於密，理固徹上而徹下者也，可謂上下異致乎？無極之真，即君子之神明其德，善言人而徵諸天者也，可以天人殊觀乎？乾知始而妙萬物者，精矣；性性以存神者，亦非粗也。於稽其類，足以極形容之妙，蓋得意而不可得名焉。天不言而成變化者，深矣；物物以過化者，亦非淺也。即彼喻此，足以盡擬議之微，蓋至極而無復餘蘊焉。吁！不顯之德擬諸天道，君子之所以不可及也。德至于此，謂之天德；學至于此，謂之聖學。過此以往，其未之或知者乎？抑觀子思子之作《中庸》，始以天命之性，終以上天之載者，其義何居？始之以天，言自天賦人也；終之以天，言以人合天也。天人合一，終篇之義淵乎深矣，而其
translation_en:
…“The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” Sound and smell possess qi but no form, and surely rank among the subtlest things in the world. Yet it still says “without sound” and “without smell”: thus no first point can be sought in its movement and stillness, nor any beginning in its yin and yang. When this is used to describe virtue that does not manifest itself, I understand that, subtle to the utmost subtlety, both lie beyond what seeing and hearing can reach; wondrous to the utmost wonder, neither can be discerned through spatial location or bodily form. Heaven’s profound and majestic mandate is precisely the noble man’s withdrawal into hidden secrecy. Principle indeed penetrates both above and below: can their ultimate purport be said to differ? The reality of the Ultimate of Nonbeing is precisely the noble man’s making his virtue spiritually luminous. This is to speak well of humanity and verify it by reference to Heaven: can Heaven and humanity be viewed separately?

Qian, the Creative, governs beginnings and wondrously brings forth the myriad things: this is refined. To realize one’s nature as nature and thereby preserve its spiritual efficacy is likewise no crude matter. In examining their correspondence, one can attain the utmost subtlety of description: their meaning can be grasped, but no name can be found for it. Heaven accomplishes change and transformation without speaking: this is profound. To deal with each thing as it is and transform wherever one passes is likewise no shallow matter. Using the former to illuminate the latter exhausts the subtleties of comparison and deliberation: one reaches the utmost limit, with no further hidden meaning remaining.

Ah! That unmanifest virtue can be compared to the Way of Heaven is what makes the noble man beyond others’ reach. Virtue that reaches this point is called heavenly virtue; learning that reaches this point is called sage learning. Beyond this, might there be nothing anyone can know? Now consider Master Zisi’s composition of the Doctrine of the Mean: it begins with the nature conferred by Heaven’s mandate and ends with the workings of Heaven above. Wherein lies the meaning of this? Beginning with Heaven expresses how Heaven endows humanity; ending with Heaven expresses how humanity unites with Heaven. Heaven and humanity become one: how profound is the meaning with which the work concludes! And its…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
爲己謹獨之功下學上達之幾尤有不可誣者
是故君子知天知人然後可與論學可與入德
矣
至於心獨無所同然乎心之所同然者何
也謂理也義也聖人先得我心之所同然
耳
陶曾
同考試官教諭馬批論心性聖人渾融明到體認理義
尤真讀之有餘味
===
考試官教諭林批人心同然處說理最妙
考試官教授詹批發明性善意詳切足有心學之士
大賢指人心同然之妙而徵諸聖人焉蓋理義
人心所同然者也惟聖人爲能全之亦何以異
於人哉孟子之意若曰人受天地之中以生繼
之者善成之者性其統之者心也彼口之同耆
耳之同聽目之同美夫物則亦有然者也而况
于吾心乎小體且然而况于大體乎是其心之
所同然者果何在邪方其未感之先中涵而理
punctuated:
爲己謹獨之功、下學上達之幾，尤有不可誣者。是故君子知天知人，然後可與論學，可與入德矣。

至於心，獨無所同然乎？心之所同然者何也？謂理也，義也。聖人先得我心之所同然耳。

陶曾

同考試官教諭馬批：論心性聖人，渾融明到；體認理義尤真，讀之有餘味。

考試官教諭林批：人心同然處，說理最妙。

考試官教授詹批：發明性善意，詳切，足有心學之士。

大賢指人心同然之妙，而徵諸聖人焉。蓋理義，人心所同然者也，惟聖人爲能全之，亦何以異於人哉？孟子之意若曰：人受天地之中以生，繼之者善，成之者性，其統之者心也。彼口之同耆、耳之同聽、目之同美，夫物則亦有然者也，而况于吾心乎？小體且然，而况于大體乎？是其心之所同然者，果何在邪？方其未感之先，中涵而理
translation_en:
…the effort to cultivate oneself and exercise vigilance in solitude, and the subtle workings by which learning below leads to understanding above, are especially undeniable. Thus only after the gentleman understands Heaven and humanity can one discuss learning with him and advance with him into virtue.

“When it comes to the heart, does it alone have nothing that all hearts alike approve? What is it that all hearts alike approve? It is principle and righteousness. The sage has simply apprehended before us what our hearts alike approve.”

Tao Zeng.

Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: “The discussion of the heart, human nature, and the sage is thoroughly integrated, lucid, and penetrating. Its apprehension of principle and righteousness is especially true. Reading it leaves a lingering savor.”

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of principle is most subtle where it treats what human hearts alike approve.”

Examiner Zhan, Professor, comments: “The exposition of the meaning of the goodness of human nature is detailed and precise: a scholar accomplished in the learning of the heart [?].”

The great worthy points out the subtle significance of what human hearts alike approve and verifies it by reference to the sage. Principle and righteousness are what human hearts alike approve; only the sage can realize them fully. How, then, is he different from other people? Mencius’s meaning is as if to say: People receive the balanced endowment of Heaven and Earth and thereby come into being. What continues it is goodness; what completes it is human nature; what governs it is the heart. Mouths share the same tastes, ears delight in the same sounds, and eyes admire the same beauty. Even in relation to things, there is this common approval; how much more so with our hearts! If this is true even of the lesser parts of our constitution, how much more so of the greater part! Where, then, does what hearts alike approve actually reside? Before the heart is stirred, it holds within itself, and principle…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
具是理也心所同得者也懿德之好非秉彜之
性乎及其旣感之後用顯而義行是義也心所
同有者也時出之宜非可欲之善乎至虛者必
至靈良心眞切之地以已而度人一也有物者
必有則良知良能之天以一心而觀萬心同也
夫理義爲心所同然如此不觀諸聖人乎語聰
明之盡若弗可及矣然不過清明在躬先知乎
此理之在我者察之由之無蔽而無不通焉耳
語道德之極若出乎類矣然不過陽明常勝先
===
覺乎此義之在我者性焉安焉不勉而無不中
焉耳理所同也而盡性踐形以至於順理之裕
者聖人亦率是性豈能於性分之外而有所增
益者乎義所同也而觀物察則以極於精義之
妙者聖人亦與人同豈能外人性之常而更有
所事者乎吁此可見理義不假外求聖人可學
而至也人性之善豈不信哉抑是理也卽吾心
之全體喜怒哀樂未發之中仁義禮智之性也
是義也卽吾心之大用發而皆中節之和□□
punctuated:
具，是理也，心所同得者也。懿德之好，非秉彜之性乎？及其旣感之後，用顯而義行，是義也，心所同有者也。時出之宜，非可欲之善乎？至虛者必至靈，良心眞切之地，以已而度人，一也；有物者必有則，良知良能之天，以一心而觀萬心，同也。夫理義爲心所同然如此，不觀諸聖人乎？語聰明之盡，若弗可及矣，然不過清明在躬，先知乎此理之在我者，察之由之，無蔽而無不通焉耳。語道德之極，若出乎類矣，然不過陽明常勝，先覺乎此義之在我者，性焉安焉，不勉而無不中焉耳。理所同也，而盡性踐形，以至於順理之裕者，聖人亦率是性，豈能於性分之外而有所增益者乎？義所同也，而觀物察則，以極於精義之妙者，聖人亦與人同，豈能外人性之常而更有所事者乎？吁！此可見理義不假外求，聖人可學而至也。人性之善，豈不信哉？

抑是理也，卽吾心之全體，喜怒哀樂未發之中，仁義禮智之性也。是義也，卽吾心之大用，發而皆中節之和，□□
translation_en:
…is fully present: this principle is what all hearts alike possess. Is the love of admirable virtue not an expression of the constant nature with which we are endowed? Once the heart has been stirred, its functioning becomes manifest and righteousness is enacted: this righteousness is what all hearts alike possess. Is the fitting response that emerges as circumstances require not the goodness that is worthy of desire? What is utterly empty must be utterly responsive. At the point where the good heart is genuine and earnest, judging others by oneself reveals that we are one. Wherever there is a thing, there must be a norm. In the Heaven-endowed capacity to know and act rightly without learning, viewing the myriad hearts through a single heart reveals their sameness.

Since principle and righteousness are thus what all hearts alike affirm, should we not examine the sages? Speaking of their consummate perceptiveness, it seems beyond our reach. Yet this is merely clarity and illumination embodied in them: they know before others this principle present within themselves, discern it and follow it, without obscuration and with nothing they fail to comprehend. Speaking of their supreme virtue, they seem to rise above their kind. Yet this is merely the constant ascendancy of brightness: they awaken before others to this righteousness present within themselves, act upon it naturally and rest in it at ease, hitting the mark in everything without exertion.

Principle is shared by all. In fully realizing their nature and giving fulfillment to their bodily form, thereby attaining an ample ease in following principle, sages merely follow this same nature. How could they add anything beyond their allotted nature? Righteousness is shared by all. In observing things and discerning their norms, thereby reaching the subtle consummation of refined righteousness, sages are likewise the same as other people. How could they have some further undertaking outside the constant endowment of human nature? Ah! From this we can see that principle and righteousness need not be sought outside ourselves, and that sagehood can be attained through learning. Is the goodness of human nature not indeed certain?

Furthermore, this principle is the complete substance of our heart: the equilibrium before joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure arise, and the nature constituted by benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom. This righteousness is the great functioning of our heart: the harmony in which those feelings, once aroused, all attain their proper measure, [two illegible characters]…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
羞惡辭讓是非之情也孺子入井而怵惕形焉
爾汝之受而慚忿生焉此則悅理義之眞也學
而至於能悅火然泉達理義不可勝用矣然則
悅之時義大矣哉
易
彖曰大畜剛健篤實輝光日新其德
張元舉
同考試官教諭林批交養立意甚是切當詞亦純雅可取
同考試官教諭蕭批畜德全功盡於此矣錄以爲式
===
考試官教諭林批畜義詳明易道精矣
考試官教授詹批以内外言畜是知易者
彖傳發大畜之義必本其德之所由畜焉夫德
必內外交修而後日新之盛可幾也卦德具有
是善名卦之義有在矣彖傳之意若謂君子之
學不有所畜固无以要其成畜之不大亦无以
致其極伏羲所以名卦爲大畜者蓋言學裕諸
中而涵養足以資无窮之用道充于已而蘊畜
有以妙不匱之源固有大畜之義矣而果何所
punctuated:
羞惡、辭讓、是非之情也。孺子入井而怵惕形焉，爾汝之受而慚忿生焉，此則悅理義之眞也。學而至於能悅，火然泉達，理義不可勝用矣。然則悅之時義大矣哉！
易
彖曰：「大畜，剛健篤實輝光，日新其德。」
張元舉
同考試官教諭林批：「交養立意甚是切當，詞亦純雅可取。」
同考試官教諭蕭批：「畜德全功盡於此矣，錄以爲式。」
考試官教諭林批：「畜義詳明，易道精矣。」
考試官教授詹批：「以内外言畜，是知易者。」
彖傳發大畜之義，必本其德之所由畜焉。夫德必內外交修，而後日新之盛可幾也。卦德具有是善，名卦之義有在矣。彖傳之意若謂君子之學，不有所畜，固无以要其成；畜之不大，亦无以致其極。伏羲所以名卦爲大畜者，蓋言學裕諸中，而涵養足以資无窮之用；道充于已，而蘊畜有以妙不匱之源。固有大畜之義矣，而果何所
translation_en:
…the feelings of shame and aversion, deference and yielding, and approval and disapproval. When a little child falls into a well, alarm and apprehension appear; when one is addressed with the disrespectful “er” and “ru,” shame and indignation arise. These are genuine manifestations of delight in moral principle and righteousness. When learning reaches the point of being able to take such delight, it is like fire beginning to burn or a spring breaking forth: moral principle and righteousness become inexhaustible in their application. Great indeed is the significance of such delight in its proper time!

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Judgments says: “Great Accumulation: firm and vigorous, substantial and solid, radiant and bright; daily renewing its virtue.”

Zhang Yuanju

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The conception of mutual cultivation is very apt. The language, too, is pure and elegant, and merits acceptance.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “The complete work of accumulating virtue is fully expressed here. Recorded as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The meaning of accumulation is explained fully and clearly; the Way of the Changes is treated with precision.”

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: “To discuss accumulation in terms of the inner and outer is to understand the Changes.”

In expounding the meaning of Great Accumulation, the Commentary on the Judgments necessarily grounds its explanation in the means by which virtue is accumulated. Only through cultivating virtue both inwardly and outwardly can one hope to attain the fullness of daily renewal. The virtues of this hexagram possess all these excellences; herein lies the meaning of its name. The Commentary on the Judgments seems to say that, in the noble man’s learning, without accumulation there can assuredly be no completion; and unless that accumulation is great, he cannot reach its utmost extent. Fuxi named the hexagram Great Accumulation to express how learning enriches what is within, so that nurture and cultivation suffice to sustain inexhaustible application; and how the Way fills oneself, so that what is stored and accumulated brings into wondrous operation an unfailing source. This assuredly conveys the meaning of Great Accumulation. But from what, precisely, is it derived…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
取乎蓋大畜之爲卦也内體乾也其德爲剛健
外體艮也其德爲篤實輝光惟其内之剛健則
天德之良不奪於攻取之私而毅然者不失吾
常強立之德常伸於萬物之上而浩然者適得
吾體天理爲主人欲退聽矣惟其外之篤實輝
光則庸行之謹允迪乎道義之正而敦復足以
自考君子之光日著於踐履之餘而昭明足以
有融闇然而章誠不可揜矣夫然則敬以直内
而義方於外者有本利用安身而致養於内者
===
有資學不病于一偏而德自修于罔覺有長裕
不設之機矣功已極於交致而道自積於厥躬
有時乃日新之益矣蓋至是則由美而大而窮
神知化之地可馴至焉謂之大畜信其然乎大
抵天下之德必畜之大而後可以會其全畜德
之功必循其序而後可以造其極否則凌節不
遜者失之驟矣惡足以言畜德哉故夫子之行
不踰矩必自志學始而孟子之自得亦于深造
以道得之也後之君子欲從事于畜德之功者
punctuated: 取乎？蓋大畜之爲卦也，内體乾也，其德爲剛健；外體艮也，其德爲篤實輝光。惟其内之剛健，則天德之良不奪於攻取之私，而毅然者不失吾常；強立之德常伸於萬物之上，而浩然者適得吾體。天理爲主，人欲退聽矣。惟其外之篤實輝光，則庸行之謹允迪乎道義之正，而敦復足以自考；君子之光日著於踐履之餘，而昭明足以有融。闇然而章，誠不可揜矣。夫然則敬以直内而義方於外者有本，利用安身而致養於内者有資。學不病于一偏，而德自修于罔覺，有長裕不設之機矣；功已極於交致，而道自積於厥躬，有時乃日新之益矣。蓋至是，則由美而大，而窮神知化之地可馴至焉。謂之大畜，信其然乎！大抵天下之德，必畜之大而後可以會其全；畜德之功，必循其序而後可以造其極。否則凌節不遜者失之驟矣，惡足以言畜德哉？故夫子之行不踰矩，必自志學始；而孟子之自得，亦于深造以道得之也。後之君子欲從事于畜德之功者……
translation_en:
…upon what, then, is this based? In the hexagram Great Accumulation (Dachu), the inner trigram is Qian, whose virtue is firmness and vigor; the outer trigram is Gen, whose virtue is substantial sincerity and radiant brilliance. Through its inner firmness and vigor, the goodness of heavenly virtue is not displaced by selfish striving for gain, and steadfast resolve preserves my enduring nature. The virtue of standing firm always rises above the myriad things, and its vast strength fully realizes my essential being. Heavenly principle rules, and human desires withdraw in obedience. Through its outward substantial sincerity and radiant brilliance, care in everyday conduct truly follows the correctness of the Way and righteousness, and a wholehearted return to the good suffices for self-examination. The gentleman’s radiance grows daily through putting his principles into practice, and its brightness suffices to shine far and wide. Unassuming yet manifest, sincerity cannot be concealed.

Thus, reverence that straightens the inner self and righteousness that squares outward conduct have a foundation; beneficial action that brings security to one’s person and nourishes the inner self has resources. Learning does not suffer from one-sidedness, and virtue develops without one’s being conscious of it: herein lies the capacity to grow in abundance without contrivance. Effort reaches its fullest through the mutual advancement of inner and outer cultivation, and the Way accumulates within one’s person: herein lies the benefit of daily renewal in due season. At this point, one advances from beauty to greatness and can gradually reach the realm of fathoming the spiritual and understanding transformation. How truly, then, is it called Great Accumulation!

In general, only when virtue is accumulated greatly can its wholeness be attained; only when the work of accumulating virtue follows its proper sequence can its ultimate fulfillment be reached. Otherwise, those who skip stages and disregard the proper order err through haste. How could this qualify as accumulating virtue? Thus, the Master’s conduct that never overstepped the bounds necessarily began with setting his heart on learning; and Mengzi’s personal attainment likewise came through advancing deeply by following the Way. As for gentlemen of later ages who wish to undertake the work of accumulating virtue…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
可不致審于內外交修之學哉
易與天地準故能彌綸天地之道
李際時
同考試官教諭林批易道之大子能真知而善言者可錄
同考試官教諭蕭批易書盡天地之道是作能發其蘊
考試官教諭林批理順語新彌綸處尤見善講
考試官教授詹批論易與天地之道皆自胷中流出
大傳言易書之大而有以妙乎造化之道也夫
道莫大于天地而皆具于易書此易道之大所
===
以侔乎天地而聖人用之也與嘗謂易書未作
道在天地易書既作道具易書是易者聖人載
道之器也吾嘗仰而觀之天以道而運于上故
言大者必歸焉而易之于天初无彼此之別也
吾嘗俯而察之地以道而奠于下故言大者必
歸焉而易之于地實有合一之妙也超乎形器
之外與上下而同其神運于陰陽之表兼俯仰
而一其類信乎惟天地爲大惟易書準之矣故
凡道之散見于兩間者若是乎不一也易則渾
punctuated:
可不致審于內外交修之學哉？

易與天地準，故能彌綸天地之道。
李際時
同考試官教諭林批：易道之大，子能真知而善言者，可錄。
同考試官教諭蕭批：易書盡天地之道，是作能發其蘊。
考試官教諭林批：理順語新，彌綸處尤見善講。
考試官教授詹批：論易與天地之道，皆自胷中流出。

大傳言易書之大，而有以妙乎造化之道也。夫道莫大于天地，而皆具于易書，此易道之大所以侔乎天地，而聖人用之也與！嘗謂易書未作，道在天地；易書既作，道具易書。是易者，聖人載道之器也。吾嘗仰而觀之，天以道而運于上，故言大者必歸焉，而易之于天，初无彼此之別也。吾嘗俯而察之，地以道而奠于下，故言大者必歸焉，而易之于地，實有合一之妙也。超乎形器之外，與上下而同其神；運于陰陽之表，兼俯仰而一其類。信乎，惟天地爲大，惟易書準之矣！故凡道之散見于兩間者，若是乎不一也，易則渾
translation_en:
…can one fail to examine carefully the learning through which inward and outward cultivation advance together?

“The Changes accords with Heaven and Earth, and therefore can encompass and order the Way of Heaven and Earth.”
Li Jishi
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “You truly understand the greatness of the Way of the Changes and express it well. This merits selection.”
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: “The Book of Changes fully comprehends the Way of Heaven and Earth. This composition brings out its hidden meaning.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is coherent and the language fresh. The discussion of ‘encompassing and ordering’ shows particular skill in exposition.”
Examiner Zhan, Professor, comments: “The discussion of the Changes and the Way of Heaven and Earth flows entirely from his own heart.”

The Great Commentary speaks of the greatness of the Book of Changes and its capacity to fathom the wonders of the Way of creative transformation. Now, nowhere is the Way greater than in Heaven and Earth, yet it is wholly contained in the Book of Changes. Is this not why the greatness of the Way of the Changes matches Heaven and Earth, and why the sages employ it? It has been said: before the Book of Changes was composed, the Way resided in Heaven and Earth; once the Book of Changes was composed, the Way was embodied in that book. Thus the Changes is the vessel in which the sages convey the Way. I have looked upward and observed: Heaven moves above by virtue of the Way, and therefore those who speak of greatness invariably turn to it. Yet between the Changes and Heaven there has never been any distinction of this and that. I have looked downward and examined: Earth is established below by virtue of the Way, and therefore those who speak of greatness invariably turn to it. Yet the Changes and Earth truly possess the marvel of unity. Transcending physical forms and vessels, it shares the spiritual efficacy of what is above and below; operating beyond yin and yang, it embraces what is seen looking downward and upward and unites them in one category. Truly, Heaven and Earth alone are great, and the Book of Changes alone accords with them! Thus, although the manifestations of the Way scattered throughout the space between Heaven and Earth are so manifold, the Changes is an integrated…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
然全具合萬爲一而不見其有遺道之根柢乎
太極者若是乎至精也易則燦然條析一實萬
分而不淪于无别卦畫立而有以極天下之賾
凡陽皆竒凡陰皆偶幷包並蓄而天地无餘蘊
矣諸爻設而有以效天下之動剛柔立本變通
趨時脉絡分明而造化其不息矣故曰彌綸天
地之道信乎旣非空疎又无殽雜而彼此兼盡
焉不然則天地亦大矣是易胡能準之也哉雖
然易非聖人不能作亦非聖人不能用故用以
===
窮理而幽明死生之道昭焉用以盡性而安土
樂天之道形焉用以至命而範圍曲成神化之
道著焉是无往而非道則无往而非易无往而
非易則无往而非聖人之用所以然者聖人有
心易焉學者苟不求之心則雖日對聖人且无
如之何而况易書所載皆陳迹乎故曰神而明
之存乎其人
書
帝曰咨四岳有能典朕三禮僉曰伯夷帝
punctuated:
然全具，合萬爲一，而不見其有遺。道之根柢乎太極者，若是乎至精也，易則燦然條析，一實萬分，而不淪于无别。卦畫立，而有以極天下之賾；凡陽皆竒，凡陰皆偶，幷包並蓄，而天地无餘蘊矣。諸爻設，而有以效天下之動；剛柔立本，變通趨時，脉絡分明，而造化其不息矣。故曰：「彌綸天地之道。」信乎旣非空疎，又无殽雜，而彼此兼盡焉。不然，則天地亦大矣，是易胡能準之也哉？雖然，易非聖人不能作，亦非聖人不能用。故用以窮理，而幽明死生之道昭焉；用以盡性，而安土樂天之道形焉；用以至命，而範圍曲成神化之道著焉。是无往而非道，則无往而非易；无往而非易，則无往而非聖人之用。所以然者，聖人有心易焉。學者苟不求之心，則雖日對聖人，且无如之何，而况易書所載皆陳迹乎？故曰：「神而明之，存乎其人。」
書
帝曰：「咨，四岳！有能典朕三禮？」僉曰：「伯夷。」帝
translation_en:
…comprehensively contains it all, uniting the myriad into one without leaving anything out. The Way, rooted in the Supreme Ultimate, is supremely subtle; yet the Changes clearly distinguishes its ramifications, dividing a single reality into myriad particulars without allowing their distinctions to disappear. The hexagram lines are established, enabling it to fathom the deepest mysteries of all under Heaven. All yang lines are odd, and all yin lines are even; it embraces and contains them together, leaving none of the hidden riches of Heaven and Earth unexpressed. The individual lines are set out, enabling it to represent all movements under Heaven. The firm and yielding establish the foundation; change and adaptation accord with the times. Their interconnections are clear, and the work of creation never ceases. Thus it is said: “It encompasses and orders the Way of Heaven and Earth.” Indeed, it is neither empty and unsubstantiated nor confused and indiscriminate, but exhaustively embraces both aspects. Otherwise, vast as Heaven and Earth are, how could the Changes serve as their standard?
Nevertheless, only a sage could compose the Changes, and only a sage can put it to use. Thus, when it is used to investigate principle fully, the Way of the hidden and manifest, of death and life, becomes clear. When it is used to realize one's nature fully, the Way of being content with one's place and rejoicing in Heaven becomes apparent. When it is used to reach an understanding of destiny, the Way of encompassing all things and bringing each to fulfillment through spiritual transformation becomes evident. There is nowhere that is not the Way, and thus nowhere that is not the Changes; there is nowhere that is not the Changes, and thus nowhere beyond the sage's application of it. This is so because the sage possesses the Changes within his heart. If students do not seek it in their hearts, then even if they faced a sage every day, they could do nothing with it. How much more is this so when everything recorded in the book of Changes consists of traces left by the past? Thus it is said: “Making it spiritually efficacious and illuminating it rests with the person.”
Book of Documents
