title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曰俞咨伯汝作秩宗夙夜惟寅直哉惟清
伯拜稽首讓于夔龍帝曰俞往欽哉
陶曾
同考試官教諭馬批虞廷慎重典禮之意發明殆盡信
為程式之文錄之
考試官教諭林批寅直意講得透徹取之
考試官教授詹批此作詞既清雅氣亦充暢深得帝
舜命官典禮之意宜為多士式
聖君求禮官得人而命之因讓而申飭之也夫
===
典禮貴得人也觀聖君所以命夷者不亦慎且
專耶昔舜重禮官之選而咨于四岳謂夫治人
之道莫急於禮而禮莫重於祭是故三禮也者
所以備郊社之義而修孝享之誠也惟賢者達
其情亦惟賢者能其事汝諸臣有能典朕三禮
者乎于是僉協廷論之公而以伯夷對蓋諒其
足以膺帝之命也此固素履之孚者故帝然其
舉而咨伯曰汝作秩宗而以禮神為職其知交
神之道乎夫交神之道格之以心而已汝其致
punctuated:
曰：「俞！咨，伯！汝作秩宗，夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。」伯拜稽首，讓于夔、龍。帝曰：「俞！往，欽哉！」
陶曾
同考試官教諭馬批：虞廷慎重典禮之意，發明殆盡，信為程式之文，錄之。
考試官教諭林批：寅直意講得透徹，取之。
考試官教授詹批：此作詞既清雅，氣亦充暢，深得帝舜命官典禮之意，宜為多士式。
聖君求禮官，得人而命之，因讓而申飭之也。夫典禮貴得人也，觀聖君所以命夷者，不亦慎且專耶？昔舜重禮官之選，而咨于四岳，謂夫治人之道，莫急於禮，而禮莫重於祭。是故三禮也者，所以備郊社之義，而修孝享之誠也。惟賢者達其情，亦惟賢者能其事。汝諸臣有能典朕三禮者乎？于是僉協廷論之公，而以伯夷對，蓋諒其足以膺帝之命也。此固素履之孚者，故帝然其舉而咨伯曰：「汝作秩宗，而以禮神為職，其知交神之道乎？夫交神之道，格之以心而已。汝其致
translation_en:
…said: “Yes! Ah, Bo! You shall serve as Minister of Ancestral Sacrifices. Day and night be reverent; be upright and pure.” Bo bowed and knocked his head to the ground, yielding the appointment to Kui or Long. The emperor said: “Yes! Go, and be respectful!”
Tao Zeng
Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor: This brings out almost completely the care with which the court of Shun entrusted responsibility for the rites. It is indeed an essay worthy to serve as a model. Record it.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The meaning of reverence and uprightness is explained thoroughly. Accept it.
Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: The diction of this composition is refined and elegant, and its vital force ample and fluent. It deeply grasps Emperor Shun’s intention in appointing an official to oversee the rites. It should serve as a model for the many candidates.
The sage ruler sought an official for the rites; finding the right man, he appointed him, and when that man yielded the appointment, he renewed his admonition. In entrusting the rites, obtaining the right person is paramount. Observing how the sage ruler appointed Yi, do we not see both his care and his singleness of purpose?
Formerly, Shun regarded the selection of an official for the rites as a weighty matter and consulted the Four Mountains, saying: “In the way of governing people, nothing is more urgent than ritual; and in ritual, nothing is weightier than sacrifice. Thus, the three rites serve to fulfill the significance of the sacrifices to Heaven and to the soil, and to cultivate the sincerity of filial offerings. Only a worthy man comprehends their inner meaning, and only a worthy man can carry out their duties. Is there anyone among you ministers who can oversee my three rites?”
Thereupon, all concurred in the impartial judgment of the court and named Bo Yi in reply, trusting that he was fully capable of receiving the emperor’s charge. This confidence rested upon his established conduct. The emperor therefore approved their nomination and addressed Bo: “You shall serve as Minister of Ancestral Sacrifices, taking the ritual service of the spirits as your duty. Do you understand the way of communing with the spirits? The way of communing with the spirits consists simply in reaching them through the heart. You should exert …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
嚴於夙夜而亹亹乎善事吾心務祇肅之匪懈
操存於念慮而惺惺乎敬以直內使私曲之弗
萌則其心無物欲之汚自有得乎靜虛之體而
精明之德已豫孚於對越之先矣寧不可以事
神乎哉既而夷致拜稽之敬而讓於夔龍蓋慮
己不足以堪帝之命也然夔龍匪優於夷者故
帝雖然之而復飭之曰秩宗之命朕方嚴於汝
而汝可遜諸人乎況廷論有歸勿之廢焉爾矣
汝其往涖厥職而寅直之語奉之以周旋慎乃
===
攸司而主敬之心勿忘於夙夜庶百神爲之受
職三禮不爲虛文而民心以同治道於是乎出
矣其無替朕命也哉噫帝之委重乎夷亦至矣
抑于是見任選之嚴焉見荐揚之公焉見推讓
之和焉見簡畀之專焉夫咨四岳嚴也舉伯夷
公也讓夔龍和也不聽其讓專也一事而眾美
咸備此禮官所以得其人也厥后伯夷降典並
禹稷而成殷民之功有以哉
文王惟克厥宅心乃克立兹常事司牧人
punctuated:
嚴於夙夜，而亹亹乎善事吾心，務祇肅之匪懈；操存於念慮，而惺惺乎敬以直內，使私曲之弗萌。則其心無物欲之汚，自有得乎靜虛之體，而精明之德已豫孚於對越之先矣，寧不可以事神乎哉？」既而夷致拜稽之敬，而讓於夔龍，蓋慮己不足以堪帝之命也。然夔龍匪優於夷者，故帝雖然之，而復飭之曰：「秩宗之命，朕方嚴於汝，而汝可遜諸人乎？況廷論有歸，勿之廢焉爾矣。汝其往涖厥職，而寅直之語奉之以周旋，慎乃攸司，而主敬之心勿忘於夙夜。庶百神爲之受職，三禮不爲虛文，而民心以同，治道於是乎出矣。其無替朕命也哉！」噫！帝之委重乎夷亦至矣！抑于是見任選之嚴焉，見荐揚之公焉，見推讓之和焉，見簡畀之專焉。夫咨四岳，嚴也；舉伯夷，公也；讓夔龍，和也；不聽其讓，專也。一事而眾美咸備，此禮官所以得其人也。厥后伯夷降典，並禹稷而成殷民之功，有以哉！

文王惟克厥宅心，乃克立兹常事司牧人。
translation_en:
…be vigilant morning and night, diligently tending your own heart, striving never to slacken in reverence and solemnity. Preserve your heart amid your thoughts, remaining alert and using reverence to make your inner self upright, so that selfishness and perversity do not arise. Then your heart will be unstained by material desires, naturally attaining a state of stillness and emptiness; your pure and luminous virtue will already have established communion with the spirits before you stand in their presence. How could you then be unable to serve them?” Thereupon Bo Yi respectfully bowed and touched his forehead to the ground, yielding the appointment to Kui and Long, presumably because he feared that he himself was unequal to the emperor’s charge. Yet Kui and Long were not superior to Bo Yi. Thus, although the emperor acknowledged his words, he admonished him again: “I am solemnly charging you with the office of Minister of Ancestral Rites. Can you yield it to others? Moreover, the court’s deliberations have reached agreement; simply do not set that decision aside. Go and take up your office. Uphold the injunction to be reverent and upright in all your conduct, attend carefully to your responsibilities, and never forget, morning or night, to make reverence the guiding principle of your heart. Then may the hundred spirits each fulfill their allotted functions, the three rites cease to be empty formalities, and the people’s hearts be united. From this will emerge the way of good government. Do not neglect my command!” Ah! The emperor went to the utmost in entrusting this weighty responsibility to Bo Yi. Here, moreover, we see rigor in selection for office, impartiality in recommendation, harmony in yielding to others, and firmness in choosing and appointing. Consulting the Four Mountains exemplified rigor; recommending Bo Yi, impartiality; yielding to Kui and Long, harmony; and refusing his request to yield, firmness. All these virtues were fully present in a single affair: this is why the right man was secured for the ritual office. There was good reason why Bo Yi subsequently handed down the canons and, alongside Yu and Ji, accomplished the work of bringing prosperity to the people!

King Wen was able to settle his heart, and thus was able to establish these regular offices and shepherd the people…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以克俊有德
周希正
同考試官教諭馬批善發文王知人得人之旨結復歸
重純心尤爲有見
考試官教諭林批周公告成王法祖用人之意子能發之
考試官教授詹批知至信篤意發明無遺且文理瑩
粹子亦宅俊之賢者允宜高薦
聖君於三宅惟其知而信之故能用得其人也
蓋知之至信之篤則用無弗當者矣此聖君所
===
以爲知恤歟周公告成王若曰建官爲治之要
也三宅百官之表也苟得其人則用使皆吉人
矣文王於三宅何如哉蓋嘗即其行事觀其用
心而於精神心術之微真有以洞察而無眩相
知以心相得以道而於聚精會神之日直與之
孚契而弗疑不徒謀諸面也而究極其底蘊之
精是能獨觀其深而明哲之用有真知也不徒
信以迹也而起信於中孚之吉是能深諒其德
而忱恂之及皆至誠也所謂惟克厥宅心如此
punctuated:
以克俊有德。
周希正
同考試官教諭馬批：善發文王知人得人之旨，結復歸重純心，尤爲有見。
考試官教諭林批：周公告成王法祖用人之意，子能發之。
考試官教授詹批：知至信篤意，發明無遺，且文理瑩粹，子亦宅俊之賢者，允宜高薦。
聖君於三宅，惟其知而信之，故能用得其人也。蓋知之至，信之篤，則用無弗當者矣。此聖君所以爲知恤歟！周公告成王若曰：建官爲治之要也，三宅百官之表也。苟得其人，則用使皆吉人矣。文王於三宅何如哉？蓋嘗即其行事，觀其用心，而於精神心術之微，真有以洞察而無眩；相知以心，相得以道，而於聚精會神之日，直與之孚契而弗疑。不徒謀諸面也，而究極其底蘊之精，是能獨觀其深，而明哲之用有真知也；不徒信以迹也，而起信於中孚之吉，是能深諒其德，而忱恂之及皆至誠也。所謂惟克厥宅心如此。
translation_en:
…thereby being able to employ outstanding men possessed of virtue.

Zhou Xizheng

Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: You skillfully bring out the meaning of King Wen’s discerning men and securing suitable men for office. The conclusion returns the emphasis to purity of heart, showing particular insight.

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: You have brought out the Duke of Zhou’s intention in exhorting King Cheng to follow his ancestor’s example in employing men.

Examiner Zhan, Director of Studies, comments: You elucidate exhaustively the meaning of complete understanding and steadfast trust. Moreover, the reasoning of your composition is lucid and refined. You too are a worthy man fit to be placed among the outstanding [?], and certainly deserve a high recommendation.

In filling the three principal appointments, the sage ruler understands and trusts the men concerned; thus he is able to employ the right men. For when understanding is complete and trust steadfast, no appointment will be inappropriate. Is this not how the sage ruler knows where to direct his concern?

The Duke of Zhou’s admonition to King Cheng was as if to say: Establishing offices is essential to government, and those holding the three principal appointments are exemplars for all officials. If the right men are obtained, all those employed in service will be good men. How did King Wen approach these three appointments? He examined their conduct to observe their intentions, truly penetrating the subtleties of their spirit and inner dispositions without being misled. They understood one another through their hearts and found accord through the Way. When their minds and spirits were brought into full communion, he entered directly into mutual confidence and accord with them, without doubt.

He did not merely assess what appeared on the surface, but thoroughly explored the finest depths of their inner character. Thus he alone could perceive their profundity, and his exercise of enlightened discernment rested on true knowledge. Nor did he trust merely on the evidence of outward deeds: his trust arose from the auspiciousness of inner sincerity. Thus he could deeply appreciate their virtue, and the confidence he extended to them was wholly sincere. Such was the meaning of the words, “He was able to settle their hearts.” …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而用之有不得其人乎蓋惟其知之至也既足
爲選用之地而信之篤也又極其簡在之專故
能度德定位而立爲常事者用得乎一時之俊
彥而卓乎爲有德之人以德詔爵而用爲常伯
者克致乎俊乂之在官而藹乎爲常德之士天
事之理天民之托凡所以相修和之治者非三
德之宣則六德之嚴也夫孰非德稱其位者乎
以之任事以之牧民凡所以弼咸和之化者非
純德之望則秉德之良也又焉有位浮其德者
===
乎是皆用得其人而準人可類見矣我文王知
恤而興夫豈偶哉抑文之知恤亦以純心爲之
地耳詩人頌文王曰緝熈敬止又曰文王之德
之純言純心也夫純則一一則公公則明明且
公而知人善任固其所矣易通之言曰純心要
矣用賢急焉文王蓋兼有之
詩
昭兹來許繩其祖武於萬斯年受天之祜
受天之祜四方來賀於萬斯年不遐有佐
punctuated:
而用之有不得其人乎？蓋惟其知之至也，既足爲選用之地；而信之篤也，又極其簡在之專。故能度德定位，而立爲常事者，用得乎一時之俊彥，而卓乎爲有德之人；以德詔爵，而用爲常伯者，克致乎俊乂之在官，而藹乎爲常德之士。天事之理，天民之托，凡所以相修和之治者，非三德之宣，則六德之嚴也。夫孰非德稱其位者乎？以之任事，以之牧民，凡所以弼咸和之化者，非純德之望，則秉德之良也。又焉有位浮其德者乎？是皆用得其人，而準人可類見矣。我文王知恤而興，夫豈偶哉？抑文之知恤，亦以純心爲之地耳。詩人頌文王曰：「緝熈敬止。」又曰：「文王之德之純。」言純心也。夫純則一，一則公，公則明。明且公，而知人善任，固其所矣。《易通》之言曰：「純心要矣，用賢急焉。」文王蓋兼有之。

詩
昭兹來許，繩其祖武。於萬斯年，受天之祜。受天之祜，四方來賀。於萬斯年，不遐有佐。
translation_en:
…and could he then fail to employ the right men? His thorough knowledge of them provided a foundation for selection and appointment, while his profound trust made his choice of them utterly steadfast. Thus he could assess virtue and determine rank: those established as regular administrative officers were outstanding talents of their age, distinguished as men of virtue. In conferring rank according to virtue, those he employed as regular chiefs brought outstanding ability into office and were abundantly endowed with constant virtue. In managing Heaven’s affairs and accepting responsibility for Heaven’s people, all who assisted in cultivating harmonious government either manifested the three virtues or rigorously upheld the six virtues. Whose virtue did not match his position? Those entrusted with affairs and charged with governing the people, all who assisted the transforming influence of universal harmony, were either eminent men of pure virtue or worthy men who held fast to virtue. How could any hold positions exceeding their virtue? In all these appointments the right men were employed, and the same may be inferred concerning judicial officials. Our King Wen understood the need for anxious care and rose to greatness: could this have been accidental?

Yet King Wen’s understanding of this need likewise rested upon purity of heart. The poet praised King Wen, saying, “Continuously bright, he abided in reverence,” and again, “The purity of King Wen’s virtue.” These words speak of purity of heart. Purity brings singleness of purpose; singleness brings impartiality; impartiality brings discernment. Discerning and impartial, he naturally understood men and employed them well. The Comprehensive Interpretation of the Changes (Yitong) says, “Purity of heart is essential; employing the worthy is urgent.” King Wen possessed both.

Book of Odes

Illuminate those who come after;
Follow your ancestors’ footsteps.
For ten thousand years,
Receive Heaven’s blessings.
Receive Heaven’s blessings,
As all quarters come to offer congratulations.
For ten thousand years,
Will you not have helpers?

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
趙恂
同考試官教諭聞批脩詞純正說理詳明蓋有志於光
裕之孝者
同考試官教諭江批此作能得詩人本意說天人處尤
明暢善學詩者矣
考試官教諭林批此篇簡而備純而正誦之而有餘
味錄之可傳
考試官教授詹批措辭清簡不失經旨是善言創守
者可取
===
詩人賛聖孝之著而因推其垂裕之遠焉甚矣
聖人之孝通于天下也繼其道而天人交與不
亦垂裕之遠哉是詩美武王作也至此若曰德
之未至者固不足以成可大之業則亦不足以
垂可久之休惟我武王孝思之至孚于萬邦順
德之應光于四海其道之昭明也有如此吾知
創守一道前之所詒後之所承也誠使爲之來
世者率乃攸行而繼序之不忘監于成憲而率
履之不越世德之所在夫固天命之所歸而祿
punctuated:
趙恂

同考試官教諭聞批：脩詞純正，說理詳明，蓋有志於光裕之孝者。

同考試官教諭江批：此作能得詩人本意，說天人處尤明暢，善學詩者矣。

考試官教諭林批：此篇簡而備，純而正，誦之而有餘味，錄之可傳。

考試官教授詹批：措辭清簡，不失經旨，是善言創守者，可取。

詩人賛聖孝之著，而因推其垂裕之遠焉。甚矣，聖人之孝通于天下也！繼其道而天人交與，不亦垂裕之遠哉？是詩美武王作也。至此若曰：德之未至者，固不足以成可大之業，則亦不足以垂可久之休。惟我武王，孝思之至，孚于萬邦；順德之應，光于四海。其道之昭明也有如此。吾知創守一道，前之所詒，後之所承也。誠使爲之來世者，率乃攸行而繼序之不忘，監于成憲而率履之不越，世德之所在，夫固天命之所歸，而祿
translation_en:
Zhao Xun 趙恂

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: His phrasing is pure and correct, and his explanation of principle detailed and clear. He evidently aspires to the filial devotion that brings glory to one's forebears and leaves abundant blessings to posterity.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: This composition captures the poet's original intent. Its discussion of Heaven and humanity is especially clear and fluent. Here is someone who studies the Odes well.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: This essay is concise yet comprehensive, pure and correct. Reciting it leaves a lingering savor; recorded here, it merits transmission to posterity.

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: The phrasing is clear and concise and remains faithful to the classic's meaning. This is an able discussion of founding an undertaking and preserving it, and merits selection.

The poet praises the manifest filial devotion of the sage and proceeds to infer how far into the future his generous legacy will extend. How profound it is that a sage's filial devotion reaches throughout the world! When his way is continued and Heaven and humanity alike lend their support, does this not show how far that legacy extends? This ode was composed to praise King Wu. At this point it is as though the poet says: Those whose virtue falls short cannot accomplish an undertaking capable of greatness, nor can they bequeath blessings capable of enduring. Our King Wu alone, through his consummate filial devotion, commands the trust of the myriad states; the response to his obedient virtue shines throughout the Four Seas. Such is the radiance of his way. I know that founding and preserving follow a single way: what predecessors bequeath, successors inherit. If those of later generations truly follow his conduct, never forgetting to carry on the succession, and take established statutes as their guide, never transgressing them in their conduct, then where hereditary virtue resides is assuredly where Heaven's mandate comes to rest; and emoluments…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
位名壽集之於大來之慶也豐亨豫泰引之於
優游之休也君德之無窮則天命亦無窮於萬
斯年殆不改夫于京之舊受天之祜寧有窮乎
夫旣受天之祜則天人一機天之所與人之所
歸也將見爲之諸侯者切朝宗之心冠裳於是
乎咸萃虔入覲之禮玉帛於此乎攸同人心之
所趨夫固多助之所至而疏附先後罔不輸沃
心之益也奔走禦侮咸願盡篤棐之忠也君德
之無窮則人心亦無窮於萬斯年殆不異夫媚
===
玆之日得人之助又可旣乎是何也武王之道
天命人心之本也不惟可法於天下而且可傳
於後世盛德大業亦至矣周之子孫惡得而不
繹思之抑觀中庸論武王周公之達孝曰善繼
人之志善述人之事至此詩所稱則又言武王
之孝光裕先後而道爲可傳焉是蓋能繼人之
志者故其志爲可繼能述人之事者故其事爲
可述也厥後明文昭定武烈成鳧鷖旣醉之太
平者論者以爲有所本信矣是故頌武王而稱
punctuated: 位名壽集之於大來之慶也，豐亨豫泰引之於優游之休也。君德之無窮，則天命亦無窮，於萬斯年，殆不改夫于京之舊，受天之祜寧有窮乎？夫旣受天之祜，則天人一機，天之所與，人之所歸也。將見爲之諸侯者，切朝宗之心，冠裳於是乎咸萃；虔入覲之禮，玉帛於此乎攸同。人心之所趨，夫固多助之所至，而疏附先後，罔不輸沃心之益也；奔走禦侮，咸願盡篤棐之忠也。君德之無窮，則人心亦無窮，於萬斯年，殆不異夫媚玆之日，得人之助又可旣乎？是何也？武王之道，天命人心之本也，不惟可法於天下，而且可傳於後世，盛德大業亦至矣。周之子孫惡得而不繹思之？抑觀《中庸》論武王、周公之達孝，曰：「善繼人之志，善述人之事。」至此詩所稱，則又言武王之孝光裕先後，而道爲可傳焉。是蓋能繼人之志者，故其志爲可繼；能述人之事者，故其事爲可述也。厥後明文昭、定武烈、成《鳧鷖》《旣醉》之太平者，論者以爲有所本，信矣。是故頌武王而稱
translation_en:
…rank, renown, and longevity gather upon him in the blessing of great good fortune; abundance, success, contentment, and peace lead him into the felicity of ease and repose. If the ruler’s virtue is inexhaustible, Heaven’s mandate is likewise inexhaustible. For ten thousand years, things will surely remain as they were of old in the capital: how could the blessings received from Heaven ever end? Once Heaven’s blessings have been received, Heaven and humanity work through a single impulse: the one whom Heaven supports is the one to whom the people turn. We shall see the feudal lords earnestly desiring to attend court, gathering together in their ceremonial caps and robes; reverently observing the rites of audience, they will assemble with their offerings of jade and silk. Where people’s hearts incline, abundant assistance naturally arrives. Those who bring the distant near, attach others to the ruler, guide him, and support him all contribute counsel that enriches his heart; those who hasten about in service and ward off aggression all wish to devote their loyalty to steadfastly assisting him. If the ruler’s virtue is inexhaustible, the people’s allegiance is likewise inexhaustible. For ten thousand years, things will surely remain as on the day when he was beloved here: how could the assistance he receives from others ever cease?

Why is this so? King Wu’s Way is the foundation of Heaven’s mandate and the people’s allegiance. It can serve as a model throughout the realm and can also be handed down to later generations. His flourishing virtue and great achievements reached their utmost perfection. How could the descendants of Zhou fail to ponder them repeatedly?

Consider, moreover, how the Doctrine of the Mean discusses the universally acknowledged filial piety of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou: “They excelled at carrying on others’ intentions and continuing others’ undertakings.” What this ode celebrates goes further: King Wu’s filial piety brought glory and abundance to those before and after him, making his Way fit to be transmitted. Precisely because he could carry on others’ intentions, his own intentions could be carried on; because he could continue others’ undertakings, his own undertakings could be continued. As for those who afterward magnified King Wen’s brilliance, secured King Wu’s achievements, and brought about the great peace celebrated in Wild Ducks and Gulls (Fu yi) and Already Drunk (Ji zui), commentators hold that these accomplishments had a foundation. How true this is! Thus, in praising King Wu, they extol…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
成康之德不衰有以哉
四海來假來假祈祈景員維河殷受命咸
宜百祿是何
張翀
同考試官教諭聞批此題固見成湯世澤之遠亦重後
王能以武德繼湯故受命咸宜此為得之
同考試官教諭江批商家以世德相承故得人心土地
之盛而命祿因之此作發揮明備用錄以式
考試官教諭林批講以德字立意詞亦整明商家一
===
統之盛讀此可見矣
考試官教授詹批此篇說成湯遺後之德處最詳盡
真佳士也
商人祀先必言時王一統之盛而表其得天之
隆也夫人心萃而國勢尊王者大一統之盛也
則其受命之宜獲福之多不亦從可見乎此商
人所以播之於宗廟登歌也其意蓋謂一代王
業有開必先有承必後而世德世業夫固有相
因者矣我商今日之天下何如哉是故王者饗
punctuated:
成康之德不衰，有以哉！

四海來假，來假祈祈。景員維河，殷受命咸宜，百祿是何。

張翀

同考試官教諭聞批：此題固見成湯世澤之遠，亦重後王能以武德繼湯，故受命咸宜，此為得之。

同考試官教諭江批：商家以世德相承，故得人心土地之盛，而命祿因之。此作發揮明備，用錄以式。

考試官教諭林批：講以德字立意，詞亦整明。商家一統之盛，讀此可見矣。

考試官教授詹批：此篇說成湯遺後之德處最詳盡，真佳士也。

商人祀先，必言時王一統之盛，而表其得天之隆也。夫人心萃而國勢尊，王者大一統之盛也，則其受命之宜、獲福之多，不亦從可見乎？此商人所以播之於宗廟登歌也。其意蓋謂一代王業，有開必先，有承必後，而世德世業，夫固有相因者矣。我商今日之天下何如哉？是故王者饗
translation_en:
…There is good reason, then, that the virtue of Kings Cheng and Kang is praised as undiminished!

“From the Four Seas they come; they come in multitudes. Mount Jing is encompassed by the River [?]. Yin received the Mandate in full propriety and bears a hundred blessings.”

Zhang Chong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: This topic certainly reveals the enduring benefits that Cheng Tang bequeathed to later generations. It also emphasizes how subsequent kings could succeed Tang through martial virtue, and thus received the Mandate in full propriety. This essay captures that meaning.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: The Shang house transmitted its virtue from generation to generation, thereby winning abundant popular allegiance and extensive territory; the Mandate and blessings followed accordingly. This composition expounds these points clearly and fully. It is included as a model.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The exposition takes virtue as its central idea, and its language is orderly and clear. Reading it reveals the flourishing unity of the Shang realm.

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: This essay is most thorough in explaining the virtue that Cheng Tang bequeathed to his descendants. Its author is truly an excellent scholar.

When the people of Shang sacrificed to their ancestors, they invariably spoke of the flourishing unity achieved by the reigning king, thereby displaying the greatness of the favor he had received from Heaven. When the people's hearts converge and the state's standing is exalted, this is the flourishing grand unity of a king's realm. Does this not also reveal how fittingly he received the Mandate and how abundantly he obtained blessings? This is why the people of Shang proclaimed these things in the songs sung in the ancestral temple hall. Their meaning was presumably this: the royal enterprise of a dynasty must have founders who come first and successors who follow afterward; the virtue and achievements of successive generations assuredly build upon one another. What, then, is the condition of the realm of our Shang today? Thus, when the king presents offerings…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
親而祀所以明有孝也而人心之萃渙恒於是
今焉龍旂之載有以奔走乎群工大禧之承有
以會同乎四海凡夫肅雝秉德以爲有廟之假
者固已祈祈然其衆多矣王者宅中而治所以
明有尊也而國勢之盛衰恒於是今焉景山峙
於中有以會陰陽之交大河環於外有以據天
設之險則夫居重馭輕以爲四方之極者固已
翼翼然其整飭矣夫以人心向往之同山河表
裏之固如此則受命不殆在殷之先后有以逢
===
其適世德重光在武丁孫子有以承其休曆數
膺而帝心簡在夫固偪之不疚而質之不愧矣
其受命也不亦咸宜乎由是命之所集者畀之
福澤以厚其生天之所眷者錫之富有以大其
業百順聚而天休滋至夫固受之不匱而積之
不苑矣其荷百祿也不其信然乎是則卽其統
治之盛見其得天之隆天人上下之間其機固
如此揆厥所由何莫非先后貽福之所及哉大
抵王者中天下而立有可傳之業必有可繼之
punctuated:
親而祀，所以明有孝也，而人心之萃渙恒於是。今焉龍旂之載，有以奔走乎群工；大禧之承，有以會同乎四海。凡夫肅雝秉德，以爲有廟之假者，固已祈祈然其衆多矣。王者宅中而治，所以明有尊也，而國勢之盛衰恒於是。今焉景山峙於中，有以會陰陽之交；大河環於外，有以據天設之險。則夫居重馭輕，以爲四方之極者，固已翼翼然其整飭矣。夫以人心向往之同、山河表裏之固如此，則受命不殆，在殷之先后有以逢其適；世德重光，在武丁孫子有以承其休。曆數膺而帝心簡在，夫固偪之不疚而質之不愧矣。其受命也，不亦咸宜乎？由是命之所集者，畀之福澤以厚其生；天之所眷者，錫之富有以大其業。百順聚而天休滋至，夫固受之不匱而積之不苑矣。其荷百祿也，不其信然乎？是則卽其統治之盛，見其得天之隆。天人上下之間，其機固如此。揆厥所由，何莫非先后貽福之所及哉！

大抵王者中天下而立，有可傳之業，必有可繼之
translation_en:
…his parents with offerings and sacrifices, thereby manifesting his filial devotion; and the gathering or dispersal of the people’s allegiance always depends upon this. Now the dragon banners are raised, bringing the assembled officers hurrying to their duties; great blessings are received, bringing together all within the Four Seas. Those who come to the ancestral temple, reverent and harmonious and holding fast to virtue, already form a vast and stately throng. The king dwells at the center and governs, thereby manifesting his exalted standing; and the strength or decline of the state always depends upon this. Now Mount Jing rises in the center, where yin and yang meet; the great river encircles the outside, providing Heaven’s own natural defenses. Thus the royal seat, occupying the commanding center and controlling the outlying regions as the pivot of the four quarters, is already solemn and well ordered.

With the people united in their allegiance and mountains and rivers securing the realm within and without in this way, Yin’s former sovereigns received the Mandate without peril, encountering the fitting occasion; and the descendants of Wu Ding inherited their blessings, making the virtue of successive generations shine anew. They received the allotted succession of rule and were chosen in the heart of the Lord on High. Indeed, even when pressed they were without fault [?], and when put to the test they had no cause for shame. Was not their reception of the Mandate entirely fitting? Consequently, those upon whom the Mandate converges are granted blessings to enrich their lives; those whom Heaven cherishes are bestowed wealth and abundance to enlarge their undertaking. Every favorable circumstance gathers, and Heaven’s blessings arrive in increasing measure: received, they are inexhaustible; accumulated, they do not wither. Is it not indeed true that they bear a hundred blessings? Thus the flourishing of their unified rule reveals the fullness of Heaven’s favor. Such is the working of the relationship between Heaven above and humanity below. If we trace its source, what part of this does not arise from the blessings bequeathed by the former sovereigns?

In general, when a king takes his place at the center of the world, if he possesses an undertaking that can be handed down, he must possess something that can be carried on…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
德德盛而可繼業之傳也不亦遠哉商之天下
歷數世而人心土宇如故固湯之武德遺之也
遺之而不忘所遺則又存乎爲後者所繼承何
如耳讀詩者固當知先德之所遺又當知所以
不忘所遺者然後可
春秋
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
鍾徠秀
考試官教諭林批此題作者類多以王事常情分說
===
子獨歸善秦穆深得傳意可以爲式
考試官教授詹批讀此終篇不惟知秦穆之賢亦可
見聖人責備賢者與人改過之意宜錄之
春秋以王事望賢君因其貳過而責之備因其
改過而善之深蓋遷善補過王者之事觀秦晉
交伐而春秋之予奪秦穆者義可見矣秦抱取
汪彭衙之耻于是有伐晉之役胡以責秦君子
曰穆自殺函以來歸作誓言一念悔悟之明匪
日自責如流者乎使其勇於改過不遠之復誰
punctuated:
德。德盛而可繼，業之傳也不亦遠哉？商之天下，歷數世而人心土宇如故，固湯之武德遺之也。遺之而不忘所遺，則又存乎爲後者所繼承何如耳。讀詩者固當知先德之所遺，又當知所以不忘所遺者，然後可。

春秋
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕，晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕。
鍾徠秀

考試官教諭林批：此題作者類多以王事、常情分說，子獨歸善秦穆，深得傳意，可以爲式。

考試官教授詹批：讀此終篇，不惟知秦穆之賢，亦可見聖人責備賢者、與人改過之意，宜錄之。

春秋以王事望賢君，因其貳過而責之備，因其改過而善之深。蓋遷善補過，王者之事。觀秦晉交伐，而春秋之予奪秦穆者，義可見矣。秦抱取汪彭衙之耻，于是有伐晉之役。胡以責秦？君子曰：「穆自殺函以來，歸作誓言，一念悔悟之明，匪日自責如流者乎？使其勇於改過，不遠之復，誰
translation_en:
…virtue. When virtue flourishes and can be carried on, will not the enterprise endure far into the future? The Shang realm passed through several generations, yet the people's allegiance and its territory remained as before: this was indeed the legacy of Tang's martial virtue. Whether that legacy, once bestowed, would be remembered depended in turn on how his successors carried it on. Readers of the Book of Odes must understand what their predecessors' virtue bequeathed, and must also understand how that legacy was kept from being forgotten; only then will their understanding suffice.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“The men of Qin attacked Jin”〔Third year of Duke Wen〕; “The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin”〔Fourth year of Duke Wen〕.
Zhong Laixiu

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Most who write on this topic discuss separately the work of a true king and ordinary human feelings. You alone accord praise to Duke Mu of Qin, profoundly grasping the commentary's meaning. This may serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: Reading this essay through, one understands not only Duke Mu of Qin's worthiness, but also the Sage's intention to demand perfection of the worthy and to approve people's correction of their faults. It deserves inclusion.

The Spring and Autumn Annals expects worthy rulers to undertake the work of a true king. When they repeat a fault, it demands perfection of them; when they correct a fault, it praises them profoundly. For turning toward goodness and making amends for faults are the work of a true king. By examining the reciprocal attacks of Qin and Jin, one can discern the principle underlying the Annals' praise and blame of Duke Mu of Qin. Qin harbored shame over [the defeat at?] Pengya—the preceding wording is garbled [?]—and thus undertook the campaign against Jin. Why blame Qin? The gentleman says: “After Mu returned from [the campaign at?] Xiaohan [?], he composed an oath. In that moment of clear repentance and awakening, was he not reproaching himself as freely as a flowing stream [?]? Had he been courageous in correcting his fault and returned before straying far, who …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
能議之乃以為三戰三北吾辱矣濟河焚舟封
尸取邑必願比一洒然後快於心與忿不懲慾
不窒有如是者是其内訟之念不勝夫耻敗之
心前日之誓蓋靜言而庸則違矣曾是可以為
賢乎經於秦穆以人稱豈固微秦哉若曰文過
者庸人之事穆以賢者而亦為此其去庸人一
間耳於王事不已遠乎是故貶而稱人所以備
責之云晉懷取官及郊之憤于是在伐秦之師
胡以善秦君子曰穆自彭衙以來罔恤誓詞一
===
念逞忿之私匪曰責人無難者乎使其終於憚
改迷復之凶誰其與之乃以為構怨構兵吾過
矣攻我邘邑圍我新城固甘於直受不復尤而
效之也爭以息怨以遠有如是者是其令圖之
美足以蓋旣往之愆前日之言始躬行而允蹈
之矣非賢而能若是乎經於晉襄以爵稱豈徒
恕晉哉若曰報怨者常人之情穆處無道而弗
報焉其視常人有間矣於王事不已近乎是故
不譏晉侯所以深善秦伯云明乎此則知聖人
punctuated:
能議之？乃以為：「三戰三北，吾辱矣。」濟河焚舟，封尸取邑，必願比一洒，然後快於心與？忿不懲，慾不窒，有如是者！是其内訟之念不勝夫耻敗之心，前日之誓，蓋靜言而庸則違矣。曾是可以為賢乎？經於秦穆以人稱，豈固微秦哉？若曰：「文過者，庸人之事。穆以賢者而亦為此，其去庸人一間耳，於王事不已遠乎？」是故貶而稱人，所以備責之云。
晉懷取官及郊之憤，于是在伐秦之師。胡以善秦？君子曰：「穆自彭衙以來，罔恤誓詞，一念逞忿之私，匪曰責人無難者乎？使其終於憚改，迷復之凶，誰其與之？乃以為：『構怨構兵，吾過矣。』攻我邘邑，圍我新城，固甘於直受，不復尤而效之也。爭以息，怨以遠，有如是者！是其令圖之美足以蓋旣往之愆，前日之言，始躬行而允蹈之矣。非賢而能若是乎？經於晉襄以爵稱，豈徒恕晉哉？若曰：『報怨者，常人之情。穆處無道而弗報焉，其視常人有間矣，於王事不已近乎？』是故不譏晉侯，所以深善秦伯云。」明乎此，則知聖人
translation_en:
…who could have censured him? Instead, he thought: “Three battles and three defeats: this is my humiliation.” He crossed the river, burned his boats, raised burial mounds over the dead, and captured towns, determined to wipe away this humiliation [?] before his heart could be satisfied. Such was his failure to restrain anger and check desire! His impulse to reproach himself inwardly could not overcome his shame at defeat. His earlier oath was thus something he spoke in repose but contradicted in practice. Could this qualify as worthiness? When the Classic refers to Duke Mu of Qin merely as a “man,” does it simply mean to belittle Qin? It is as though it says: “Glossing over faults is the business of ordinary men. If Mu, a worthy man, also acts thus, he is scarcely distinguishable from an ordinary man. Is he not already far removed from the work of a true king?” Thus, demoting him by calling him a “man” serves to hold him fully accountable.
Jin harbored resentment over the taking of Guan and Jiao [?], and so again sent an army against Qin. Why, then, does this commend Qin? The gentleman says: “Since Pengya, Mu had disregarded the words of his oath, privately intent only on venting his anger. Was this not what is meant by finding it easy to reproach others? Had he persisted in shrinking from reform, incurring the misfortune of ‘going astray in returning,’ who would have approved of him? Instead, he thought: ‘Fomenting enmity and warfare was my fault.’ When they attacked his town of Yu and besieged his Xincheng, he willingly accepted it outright, no longer blaming them and following their example. Thus contention ceased and enmity receded! The excellence of this good resolve was sufficient to cover his past faults. Only then did he personally carry out and faithfully fulfill his earlier words. Could anyone but a worthy man act in this way? When the Classic refers to Duke Xiang of Jin by his noble rank, does it merely mean to excuse Jin? It is as though it says: ‘Repaying resentment is the usual human impulse. Mu was subjected to unprincipled treatment yet did not retaliate. He thus stood apart from ordinary men. Was he not already close to the work of a true king?’ Hence, refraining from censuring the Marquis of Jin serves to commend the Earl of Qin profoundly.” Understanding this, one knows that the Sage…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
所以待秦晉者大改過嘉釋怨樂與人爲善之
意深矣抑仲虺之誥唯曰改過吉甫之詩唯曰
補闕商湯周宣固由此其選乎秦誓之詞蓋庶
幾焉所以列于百篇之末也惜乎賤勇夫貴良
士惡娼疾思彥聖徒托空言而孟明子桑無能
將順此秦穆所以僅霸西戎君子不能無遺憾
焉
夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷齊人
來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔俱定公十年〕叔孫州仇
===
帥師墮郈季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費
〔俱定公十有二年〕
胡希旦
考試官教諭林批曲盡孔子神化之妙非邃於經學
者不能及此
考試官教授詹批聖人以禮行于齊魯俄頃之化未
易形容此能發明之而歸重於禮是善作者可以薦矣
春秋紀望國外服內順之事見聖化之大行也
夫聖人者存神而過化者也齊服而侵地歸三
punctuated:
所以待秦晉者，大改過，嘉釋怨，樂與人爲善之意深矣。抑仲虺之誥唯曰改過，吉甫之詩唯曰補闕，商湯周宣固由此其選乎？秦誓之詞蓋庶幾焉，所以列于百篇之末也。惜乎賤勇夫，貴良士，惡娼疾，思彥聖，徒托空言，而孟明子桑無能將順，此秦穆所以僅霸西戎，君子不能無遺憾焉。
夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田。〔俱定公十年〕叔孫州仇帥師墮郈，季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費。〔俱定公十有二年〕
胡希旦
考試官教諭林批：曲盡孔子神化之妙，非邃於經學者不能及此。

…The intention underlying his treatment of Qin and Jin is profound: to esteem the correction of faults, commend the relinquishing of resentment, and gladly help others do good. Moreover, the Announcement of Zhonghui speaks simply of correcting faults, and Jifu’s ode simply of remedying deficiencies. Was it not through this that Tang of Shang and King Xuan of Zhou distinguished themselves? The words of the Oath of Qin come close to this ideal; hence its placement at the end of the hundred chapters of the Book of Documents. Regrettably, disdaining men of mere courage, esteeming worthy men, detesting jealousy [?], and yearning for accomplished and sagely men remained empty words. Mengming and Zisang could do nothing to support and advance these intentions. This is why Duke Mu of Qin achieved hegemony only over the western Rong; the gentleman cannot but feel lingering regret.
“In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. Men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.〔All in the tenth year of Duke Ding.〕 Shusun Zhouqiu led an army to demolish the fortifications of Hou; Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army to demolish the fortifications of Fei.〔Both in the twelfth year of Duke Ding.〕”
Hu Xidan
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “This fully brings out the subtlety of Confucius’s wondrous transforming influence. Only someone deeply versed in Classical learning could attain this.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
家順而私邑毀其感化之機一何妙哉且魯本
周公之後世稱秉禮之邦定公嗣守日益弗競
以言乎敵國外患則有齊焉自揚州門廩丘攻
齊固甘心於魯者兩國之平未幾夾谷之會途
講時則犂彌以謀獻萊夷以兵逞乃齊人復以
享行震于其躬魯幾不測矣幸有孔子相君於
會歷階而升談笑而卻曰干盟偪好曰不祥愆
義其詞嚴而義則正者于是齊君愧於古道齊
臣引以謝過鄆讙龜陰之田章章然咸來歸焉
===
由以禮責齊而齊化也不然彼以霸國餘業革
車使從夫固脅持之術胡遽心服若此哉非所
謂一言而威重於三軍者乎故書會書來歸雖
疑於自序其績不以為嫌也以言乎越禮內叛
則有三家焉自世卿專郈費城三家固厲階於
魯者侯犯之叛未幾狃鄹之謀益險時則費人
逞其奸家隸擬其後雖三卿亦不能制末大必
折魯幾不免矣幸而孔子為政於國明以禮制
諭以忠貞曰家藏甲兵曰邑固城池其名正而
punctuated:
家順而私邑毀，其感化之機一何妙哉！且魯本周公之後，世稱秉禮之邦。定公嗣守，日益弗競。以言乎敵國外患，則有齊焉。自揚州門廩丘攻，齊固甘心於魯者。兩國之平未幾，夾谷之會途講。時則犂彌以謀獻，萊夷以兵逞，乃齊人復以享行震于其躬，魯幾不測矣。幸有孔子相君於會，歷階而升，談笑而卻，曰干盟偪好，曰不祥愆義。其詞嚴而義則正者，于是齊君愧於古道，齊臣引以謝過。鄆、讙、龜陰之田，章章然咸來歸焉。由以禮責齊而齊化也。不然，彼以霸國餘業，革車使從，夫固脅持之術，胡遽心服若此哉？非所謂一言而威重於三軍者乎？故書會、書來歸，雖疑於自序其績，不以為嫌也。

以言乎越禮內叛，則有三家焉。自世卿專郈費城，三家固厲階於魯者。侯犯之叛未幾，狃鄹之謀益險。時則費人逞其奸，家隸擬其後，雖三卿亦不能制。末大必折，魯幾不免矣。幸而孔子為政於國，明以禮制，諭以忠貞，曰家藏甲兵，曰邑固城池。其名正而
translation_en:
…the houses submitted and their private strongholds were demolished. How marvelous was the working of his transforming influence! Lu was originally the domain of the descendants of the Duke of Zhou, renowned through the generations as a state that upheld ritual propriety. After Duke Ding succeeded to its rule, it grew daily weaker. As for rival states and external threats, there was Qi. From the attacks involving Yangzhou Gate and Linqiu [?], Qi had been intent on having its way with Lu. Not long after peace was established between the two states, the meeting at Jiagu was convened [?]. Li Mi then offered his scheme, and the Lai tribesmen flaunted their weapons. The men of Qi further used a banquet to intimidate the ruler in person, and Lu nearly suffered an unforeseen calamity.

Fortunately, Confucius assisted his ruler at the meeting. He ascended the steps and, amid conversation and laughter, repelled them, declaring that they were violating the covenant and coercing a friendly state, and that their conduct was inauspicious and contrary to righteousness. His words were stern and his principles correct. Thus the ruler of Qi felt shame before the ancient Way, and Qi’s ministers acknowledged their fault and apologized. The lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin were all duly returned. This happened because Confucius called Qi to account through ritual propriety, and Qi was transformed. Otherwise, relying on the remaining power of its former hegemony and using war chariots to compel obedience—plainly methods of coercion—why would Qi so suddenly have submitted with such sincerity? Is this not what is meant by a single utterance carrying greater authority than the three armies? Thus, in recording the meeting and recording the return of the lands, Confucius did not regard it as objectionable, even though he might seem to be recounting his own achievements.

As for violations of ritual propriety and internal rebellion, there were the Three Houses. Since hereditary ministers monopolized power and fortified Hou and Fei [?], the Three Houses had indeed been a source of calamity for Lu. Not long after Hou Fan’s rebellion, the plotting of Niu and Zou [?] became still more dangerous. The men of Fei then pursued their treachery, and household retainers prepared to follow their example. Even the three chief ministers could not control them. When the branches grow too large, they inevitably break: Lu nearly failed to escape this fate.

Fortunately, Confucius administered the state. He enlightened them through ritual institutions and instructed them in loyalty and steadfastness, speaking of households storing armor and weapons and of towns strengthening their walls and moats [?]. His terms were correct, and …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
言則順者于是叔孫悟而革心季孫悅而改圖
郈費之邑凜凜然相繼墮焉由以禮正三家而
三家化也不然彼皆植根已深弱榦強枝夫固
僭逼之態胡遽效順若此哉非所謂以禮爲國
而可以爲之兆者乎故書墮郈墮費見其推而
行諸魯國而準而王政可行也吁齊之服三家
之順此孔子所以見諸行事之深切著明者也
變齊變魯之幾亦略可覘矣嗟乎孔子在魯兆
足以行信也三田歸而魯之削弱滋甚二邑毀
===
而成之負固自如豈亦有所不能哉蓋其所能
者人所不能者天天乎人也何尤而東周之志
聖人固未嘗一日忘魯也
禮記
是故情見而義立樂終而德尊
蔣焞
同考試官學正吳 批 體認義立德尊處最爲親切是深
達樂禮之妙者錄之可也
考試官教諭林 批 發明作樂始終之義詳盡可式
punctuated:
言則順者，於是叔孫悟而革心，季孫悅而改圖。郈費之邑，凜凜然相繼墮焉，由以禮正三家而三家化也。不然，彼皆植根已深，弱榦強枝，夫固僭逼之態，胡遽效順若此哉？非所謂以禮爲國而可以爲之兆者乎？故書墮郈、墮費，見其推而行諸魯國，而準而王政可行也。吁！齊之服，三家之順，此孔子所以見諸行事之深切著明者也。變齊變魯之幾，亦略可覘矣。嗟乎！孔子在魯，兆足以行信也。三田歸而魯之削弱滋甚，二邑毀而成之負固自如，豈亦有所不能哉？蓋其所能者人，所不能者天。天乎！人也何尤？而東周之志，聖人固未嘗一日忘魯也。

禮記
是故情見而義立，樂終而德尊。
蔣焞

同考試官學正吳批：體認義立德尊處，最爲親切，是深達樂禮之妙者，錄之可也。

考試官教諭林批：發明作樂始終之義，詳盡可式。
translation_en:
…and speech consequently accords with what is right. Thus Shusun came to understand and changed his heart; Jisun was pleased and revised his plans. The fortifications of Hou and Fei were successively demolished in awed compliance. This came about because Confucius used ritual propriety to rectify the Three Families, and they were transformed. Otherwise, their roots were already deep, their branches strong while the trunk was weak: this was plainly a situation of usurpation and encroachment. Why would they suddenly have shown such obedience? Was this not what is meant by governing a state through ritual propriety and thereby establishing a beginning? Thus the record says “demolished Hou” and “demolished Fei,” showing that, by extending this practice throughout Lu and taking it as a standard [?], kingly government could be implemented. Ah! Qi’s submission and the Three Families’ obedience were the profound and unmistakable manifestations of Confucius’s work in practice. Here one can glimpse the beginnings of the transformation of Qi and Lu.

Alas! While Confucius was in Lu, the signs were sufficient for putting trust into practice [?]. Yet although the three tracts of land were returned, Lu’s decline grew still worse; although the two fortified towns were demolished, Cheng continued as before to rely defiantly on its defenses. Were there, then, things even he could not accomplish? What lay within his power belonged to human affairs; what lay beyond it belonged to Heaven. It was Heaven! What blame could be placed on a man? Yet the sage’s ambition to establish an Eastern Zhou meant that he never forgot Lu for a single day.

Record of Rites
“Thus the feelings become manifest and righteousness is established; when the music concludes, virtue is honored.”
Jiang Tun

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, an Instructor: His understanding of the establishment of righteousness and the honoring of virtue is especially direct and intimate. This is someone who profoundly comprehends the subtleties of music and ritual. The essay merits inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Lin, an Instructor: His elucidation of the significance of making music, from beginning to end, is detailed and exhaustive, and may serve as a model.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授詹批〔禮義樂德四字講說甚切文亦純〕
正是知樂之情者
記者論樂備始終之善焉夫樂之教合人己而
一之也而德義由之備焉所觀不亦深乎記樂
記者通論樂舞之理如此意謂先王之作樂備
始終之善而極功化之隆非無因而強作者矣
彼樂之始作也存乎情性其情動於中而後樂
形于外是故詩以言其志也歌以咏其聲也舞
以動其容也律呂之布被要皆心術之流行文
===
物之昭宣本之志意之湮鬱是情見於樂之初
矣而君子之義立於是可見焉蓋其反情和志
攻取之私不能搖其湛一之體比類成行邪僻
之氣無以干其天德之良感必以正所以養其
心知者罔不宜也義之與比所以行其眾體者
無不順也夫義立於樂之先則所以著之樂者
皆正否則本之既荒何以成其始耶樂之終行
也存乎化惟其教被於至廣而後化行於無外
是故或聽之和以敬也或聽之和以順也或聽
punctuated:
考試官教授詹批〔禮義樂德四字講說甚切，文亦純〕正，是知樂之情者。

記者論樂，備始終之善焉。夫樂之教，合人己而一之也，而德義由之備焉，所觀不亦深乎？記《樂記》者通論樂舞之理如此，意謂先王之作樂，備始終之善，而極功化之隆，非無因而強作者矣。彼樂之始作也，存乎情性。其情動於中，而後樂形于外。是故詩以言其志也，歌以咏其聲也，舞以動其容也。律呂之布被，要皆心術之流行；文物之昭宣，本之志意之湮鬱。是情見於樂之初矣，而君子之義立，於是可見焉。蓋其反情和志，攻取之私不能搖其湛一之體；比類成行，邪僻之氣無以干其天德之良。感必以正，所以養其心知者罔不宜也；義之與比，所以行其眾體者無不順也。夫義立於樂之先，則所以著之樂者皆正；否則本之既荒，何以成其始耶？樂之終行也，存乎化。惟其教被於至廣，而後化行於無外。是故或聽之和以敬也，或聽之和以順也，或聽

Examiner Zhan, Professor, comments: 〔The exposition of the four words “ritual,” “rightness,” “music,” and “virtue” is most apt; the writing is also pure〕 and upright. This is someone who understands the essential nature of music.

The recorder discusses music as encompassing goodness from beginning to end. The teaching of music unites oneself and others as one, and through it virtue and rightness become complete. Is this not a profound insight? Such is the comprehensive account of the principles of music and dance given by the compiler of the Record of Music (Yueji). His meaning is that the former kings’ making of music encompassed goodness from beginning to end and brought its transformative achievements to their highest flourishing. It was not something arbitrarily contrived without a basis.

When music first arises, its basis lies in feelings and human nature. Feelings stir within, and only then does music take form without. Thus poetry expresses aspirations, singing gives voice to their sounds, and dance sets bodily expression in motion. The diffusion of the pitch standards is, in essence, entirely the flowing forth of the workings of the heart; the splendid manifestation of ceremonial forms and objects has its source in aspirations and intentions pent up within. Thus feelings become manifest at music’s inception, and here we can see the gentleman’s rightness established. For he returns to his true feelings and harmonizes his aspirations, so that selfish impulses to attack and seize cannot shake his clear and undivided inner substance. He orders things by their kinds into proper ranks, so that deviant influences cannot intrude upon the goodness of his Heaven-endowed virtue. His responses are invariably guided by correctness, and everything by which he nourishes his mind and understanding is fitting. He aligns himself with rightness, and everything by which he moves the parts of his body accords with proper order. If rightness is established before music, everything expressed in music will be correct. Otherwise, if its root has already fallen into neglect, how could its beginning be perfected?

The ultimate operation of music lies in transformation. Only when its teaching has spread most broadly does its transforming influence reach everywhere without exception. Thus some hear it and become harmonious and reverent; some hear it and become harmonious and compliant; some hear …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之和以親也風移俗易而天下皆寧心安氣和
而斯世大順是化行於樂之終矣而君子之德
尊自是可知焉蓋其志既和矣壙而充之以至
於備道全美之極行既成矣廓而大之而造于
篤恭不顯之神一人和德於上故百姓感而太
和焉順之達者信之體也惟聖建其有極故斯
民歸於皇極焉化之宣者德之盛也夫德尊於
樂之行則所以驗其樂者益善否則用之既窒
何以成其終耶是則樂之本立是為己者和而
===
平此所以獨樂其志不厭其道也樂之用行是
為人者愛而公此所以備舉其道不私其欲也
然則生民之道樂孰大焉抑樂之為道猶天地
之化也樂之本於德猶化之由於氣也氣之不
盛無以神其化而及於物德有未深又何以著
之樂而感乎人哉君子之為樂也本之身心性
情以為之體達諸聖神功化而為之用以宣八
風之氣以平天下之情終之于道配天地淵乎
微矣然必禮之用行而後樂之效達故周子曰
punctuated: 之和以親也。風移俗易，而天下皆寧；心安氣和，而斯世大順。是化行於樂之終矣，而君子之德尊，自是可知焉。蓋其志既和矣，壙而充之，以至於備道全美之極；行既成矣，廓而大之，而造于篤恭不顯之神。一人和德於上，故百姓感而太和焉。順之達者，信之體也。惟聖建其有極，故斯民歸於皇極焉。化之宣者，德之盛也。夫德尊於樂之行，則所以驗其樂者益善；否則用之既窒，何以成其終耶？是則樂之本立，是為己者和而平，此所以獨樂其志、不厭其道也。樂之用行，是為人者愛而公，此所以備舉其道、不私其欲也。然則生民之道，樂孰大焉？抑樂之為道，猶天地之化也。樂之本於德，猶化之由於氣也。氣之不盛，無以神其化而及於物；德有未深，又何以著之樂而感乎人哉？君子之為樂也，本之身心性情，以為之體；達諸聖神功化，而為之用，以宣八風之氣，以平天下之情，終之于道配天地，淵乎微矣！然必禮之用行，而後樂之效達。故周子曰：
translation_en:
…and, on hearing it, become harmonious and affectionate. Customs and manners are transformed, and all under Heaven are at peace; hearts are tranquil and vital energies harmonious, and the world attains great concord. This is transformation taking effect at the culmination of music; from this one can see how the gentleman’s virtue is exalted. Once his purpose is harmonious, he broadens and fully develops it, reaching the utmost completeness of the Way and perfection of beauty. Once his conduct is formed, he expands and magnifies it, attaining the spiritual efficacy of profound reverence that makes no outward display. The one ruler above harmonizes his virtue, and thus the common people respond and attain supreme harmony. Concord fully realized is the embodiment of trustworthiness. Only the sage establishes the supreme standard, and thus the people turn to the august standard. Transformation widely diffused is virtue in its fullness. When virtue is exalted through the practice of music, the effects by which music is assessed become ever better. Otherwise, if its operation is obstructed, how can it reach its culmination?

Thus, when the foundation of music is established, one’s cultivation of oneself is harmonious and balanced: this is why one delights in one’s own purpose and never tires of the Way. When music’s function is put into practice, one’s dealings with others are loving and impartial: this is why one fully carries out the Way and does not indulge private desires. Among the ways of nurturing the people, then, what is greater than music? Moreover, music as a Way resembles the transforming activity of Heaven and Earth. Music’s grounding in virtue resembles transformation’s arising from vital energy. Unless vital energy is abundant, it cannot give transformation its spiritual efficacy and extend it to all things. If virtue is not yet profound, how can it be manifested in music and move others?

In making music, the gentleman grounds it in his person and mind, his nature and feelings, to constitute its substance. He extends it to the achievements and transforming influence of sagely and spiritual efficacy to constitute its function, thereby diffusing the vital energies of the eight winds and bringing balance to the feelings of all under Heaven. Ultimately his Way matches Heaven and Earth: how profound and subtle it is! Yet only after ritual is put into practice can music’s effects fully unfold. Thus Master Zhou said: …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬物得其理而後和又曰禮先樂後然則禮樂
之用爲急而推行之序又有所自始云
忠臣以事其君孝子以事其親其本一也
唐文迪
同考試官學正吳批忠孝一夲一意甚難發揮此作獨明
白順暢是學禮有得者也
考試官教諭林批善道忠孝自盡之意
考試官教授詹批即忠孝説出備義甚悉觀子之
文他日所樹立者可知矣勉之
===
觀賢者之敬於所事同於內盡其心也夫忠以
事君孝以事親臣子之道殊矣而內盡之心要
之無不同焉備之爲義端可識矣記祭統者意
謂賢者之能祭本於能備即其內盡外順而所
謂備者見矣是故賢者在國自事君言之有臣
道焉而忠其所先也今觀其事君也靖共爾位
利害休戚舉切于其心篤棐厥辟腹心手足若
爲之一體責難而弼唐虞之治恭之大也居安
而陳盛滿之戒慮之遠也是其所以忠于君者
punctuated:
萬物得其理而後和，又曰：「禮先樂後。」然則禮樂之用爲急，而推行之序又有所自始云。

忠臣以事其君，孝子以事其親，其本一也。
唐文迪

同考試官學正吳批：「忠孝一夲一意，甚難發揮。此作獨明白順暢，是學禮有得者也。」
考試官教諭林批：「善道忠孝自盡之意。」
考試官教授詹批：「即忠孝説出備義甚悉。觀子之文，他日所樹立者可知矣。勉之！」

觀賢者之敬於所事，同於內盡其心也。夫忠以事君，孝以事親，臣子之道殊矣，而內盡之心，要之無不同焉。備之爲義，端可識矣。記《祭統》者，意謂賢者之能祭，本於能備，即其內盡外順，而所謂備者見矣。是故賢者在國，自事君言之，有臣道焉，而忠其所先也。今觀其事君也，靖共爾位，利害休戚，舉切于其心；篤棐厥辟，腹心手足，若爲之一體。責難而弼唐虞之治，恭之大也；居安而陳盛滿之戒，慮之遠也。是其所以忠于君者
translation_en:
…“Only after all things attain their proper principles do they become harmonious.” He also said, “Ritual comes first, music afterward.” Thus, putting ritual and music into practice is an urgent matter, yet the order of their implementation has its own necessary starting point.

“The loyal minister thereby serves his ruler, and the filial son thereby serves his parents: their foundation is one.”
Tang Wendi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, School Director: “The idea that loyalty and filial devotion share one foundation is exceedingly difficult to expound. This composition is exceptionally clear and fluent. Its author has gained insight through studying ritual.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “It aptly expresses the idea of giving oneself fully in loyalty and filial devotion.”
Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: “Through loyalty and filial devotion, it explains the meaning of completeness in great detail. Reading your composition, one can discern what you will establish and accomplish in the future. Persevere!”

When we observe the worthy person's reverence toward those he serves, we find the same inward devotion of his whole heart. Loyalty serves the ruler, and filial devotion serves one's parents. The duties of minister and son differ, yet the heart devoted fully within is, in essence, the same in both. From this, the meaning of completeness can indeed be understood. The author of “The System of Sacrifices” meant that the worthy person's ability to offer sacrifice rests upon his ability to achieve completeness. In his inward devotion and outward compliance, what is called completeness becomes manifest.

Thus, when the worthy person is in the state, considered in terms of his service to the ruler, he has the duties of a minister, and loyalty takes precedence. Now observe how he serves his ruler: “Attend quietly and reverently to your office”—advantage and harm, happiness and sorrow all lie close to his heart. He earnestly assists his sovereign, serving as heart and belly, hands and feet, as though they formed a single body. By demanding that his ruler undertake difficult duties, he assists him in achieving the governance of Tang and Yu: this is reverence at its greatest. While dwelling in security, he presents admonitions against the dangers of prosperity and fullness: this is foresight reaching far. Thus, the way he is loyal to his ruler…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
一德而不貳矣賢者於家自事親言之有子道
焉孝其所先也今觀其事親也分之所在則用
勞用力而各伸其情時之所在則致養致思而
各成其愛舉足出言之不傷不忘全而歸之也
喜之怒之而勿忘勿怨順以受之也是其所以
孝于親者聚順而無愧矣夫忠以事君賢者之
心非有假於外也蓋臣之所止在于是焉夫苟
一行之有疑於君臣道虧矣彼不貳之誠要皆
中心之盡無所逃于天地者也孝以事親賢者
===
之心非有倚於物也蓋子之所止在于是焉夫
苟一念之有戾於親子道虧矣彼罔極之報要
皆秉彝之致無以易其天性者也故遠之事君
明有尊也倫之不可踰也比之為子則國之順
者家之理也名位雖殊心膂共之夫何迹之拘
哉邇之事父明有親也情之不可已也比之為
臣則忠之輸者孝之移也遠近雖異懿德同之
夫何理之間哉是則賢者之事君親內盡於已
斯外順於道矣此其所謂備而能盡祭之義與
punctuated:
一德而不貳矣。賢者於家，自事親言之，有子道焉，孝其所先也。今觀其事親也，分之所在，則用勞用力而各伸其情；時之所在，則致養致思而各成其愛。舉足出言之不傷不忘，全而歸之也；喜之怒之而勿忘勿怨，順以受之也。是其所以孝于親者，聚順而無愧矣。
夫忠以事君，賢者之心非有假於外也，蓋臣之所止在于是焉。夫苟一行之有疑於君，臣道虧矣。彼不貳之誠，要皆中心之盡，無所逃于天地者也。孝以事親，賢者之心非有倚於物也，蓋子之所止在于是焉。夫苟一念之有戾於親，子道虧矣。彼罔極之報，要皆秉彝之致，無以易其天性者也。
故遠之事君，明有尊也，倫之不可踰也。比之為子，則國之順者，家之理也。名位雖殊，心膂共之，夫何迹之拘哉？邇之事父，明有親也，情之不可已也。比之為臣，則忠之輸者，孝之移也。遠近雖異，懿德同之，夫何理之間哉？是則賢者之事君親，內盡於已，斯外順於道矣。此其所謂備而能盡祭之義與？
translation_en:
…with undivided devotion and no wavering. Within the household, considered in terms of serving his parents, the worthy man has the duties of a son, foremost among which is filial piety. Observe how he serves his parents: as his allotted duties require, he undertakes toil and exerts his strength, giving full expression to his feelings in each instance; as the occasion requires, he provides sustenance and thoughtful care, fully realizing his love in each instance. In every step and utterance, he neither causes injury nor forgets his parents, thus returning intact the person they gave him. Whether they are pleased with him or angry, he neither forgets them nor resents them, but receives their treatment obediently. Thus, in his filial service to his parents, he brings together every form of obedience and has nothing of which to be ashamed.
In serving his ruler loyally, the worthy man’s heart borrows nothing from outside itself, for this is where a minister must take his stand. If even a single action gives his ruler cause for doubt, his duties as a minister are impaired. His unwavering sincerity is, in essence, the complete fulfillment of his innermost heart, which has nowhere to hide between Heaven and Earth. In serving his parents filially, the worthy man’s heart depends on no external thing, for this is where a son must take his stand. If even a single thought runs contrary to his parents, his duties as a son are impaired. His repayment of their boundless kindness is, in essence, the fullest realization of the constant moral nature with which he is endowed; nothing can alter this Heaven-given nature.
Thus, in serving his ruler in the more distant sphere, he makes manifest the reverence due to a superior: the bounds of this relationship cannot be overstepped. Compared with his conduct as a son, the obedience he shows in the state follows the same principle that governs the household. Though his designation and position differ, he brings the same heart and strength to both. How could he be constrained by outward forms? In serving his father in the nearer sphere, he makes manifest the affection due to a parent: such feeling cannot be suppressed. Compared with his conduct as a minister, the loyalty he offers is the extension of his filial piety. Though the spheres differ in their distance, the fine virtue is the same. What division could there be in their underlying principle? Thus, when the worthy man serves his ruler and his parents, he fulfills himself completely within and thereby accords outwardly with the Way. Is this not what is meant by being fully prepared and thus able to fulfill the meaning of sacrifice?

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
抑古人祭祀以感格爲重而幽明之交以忠信
爲先然必吾之備得于素定而後神之歆見于
陟降仁人享帝孝子享親端不外此書曰黍稷
非馨明德惟馨又曰鬼神無常享享于克誠夫
曰明德曰誠備之謂也至於能享則百神受職
百貨可極景福之介純嘏之錫無往不利矣然
則祭也者又休咎感召之機也可無愼乎
第貳塲
論
===
君子脩之吉
張元舉
同考試官教諭林 批 通篇俱在圖內發明不事泛言是
有理學之士也應首選
同考試官教諭蕭 批 敬與吉意義說有分曉蓋優於論者
考試官教諭林 批 以太極立意甚得周子之旨
考試官教授詹 批 此篇說太極之理渾融明白可錄
人心一太極也君子作聖之功主敬以全夫太
極而已矣太極之理隨物而賦隨在各足自聖
punctuated:
抑古人祭祀，以感格爲重，而幽明之交，以忠信爲先。然必吾之備得于素定，而後神之歆見于陟降。仁人享帝，孝子享親，端不外此。書曰：「黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。」又曰：「鬼神無常享，享于克誠。」夫曰明德，曰誠，備之謂也。至於能享，則百神受職，百貨可極，景福之介，純嘏之錫，無往不利矣。然則祭也者，又休咎感召之機也，可無愼乎？
第貳塲
論
君子脩之吉
張元舉
同考試官教諭林批：通篇俱在圖內發明，不事泛言，是有理學之士也，應首選。
同考試官教諭蕭批：敬與吉意義說有分曉，蓋優於論者。
考試官教諭林批：以太極立意，甚得周子之旨。
考試官教授詹批：此篇說太極之理，渾融明白，可錄。
人心一太極也。君子作聖之功，主敬以全夫太極而已矣。太極之理，隨物而賦，隨在各足，自聖
translation_en:
Moreover, the ancients placed greatest weight in sacrifice on moving the spirits to respond, and in intercourse between the unseen and visible realms they gave priority to loyalty and trustworthiness. Yet our own full preparedness must first be firmly established in ordinary life; only then will the spirits manifest their acceptance as they ascend and descend. The benevolent person's offering to the Lord on High and the filial son's offering to his parents depend on precisely this. The Book of Documents says: “Millet is not the fragrant offering; luminous virtue alone is fragrant.” It also says: “Spirits do not invariably accept offerings; they accept those of one who can be sincere.” Luminous virtue and sincerity refer to this full preparedness. When one succeeds in presenting acceptable offerings, the hundred spirits discharge their offices, and all manner of goods may be obtained in abundance. With the aid of great blessings and the bestowal of ample felicity, nothing one undertakes will fail to prosper. Sacrifice, then, is also the pivotal means by which good or ill fortune is elicited. Can one afford to be incautious?
Second Session
Discourse
“The Gentleman Cultivates It and Has Good Fortune”
Zhang Yuanju
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Throughout, the essay elucidates what is contained in the diagram, without resorting to vague generalities. This is a scholar versed in the Learning of Principle, who should be selected first.
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: The meanings of reverent attentiveness and good fortune are explained distinctly. This is indeed an accomplished writer of discourses.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: By making the Supreme Ultimate the central idea, the essay captures Master Zhou's intent very well.
Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: This essay explains the principle of the Supreme Ultimate coherently and clearly. It merits selection.
The human mind is itself a Supreme Ultimate. The gentleman's work of becoming a sage consists simply in making reverent attentiveness his guiding principle, thereby preserving the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety. The principle of the Supreme Ultimate is endowed in each thing, and wherever it resides it is complete in itself, from sages…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
人以達於衆人一也聖人全之而衆人昧焉人
化物而滅其天其去聖人始遠矣非聖人之有
異於人也君子知吾之心即聖人之心吾心之
太極即聖人之心之太極一念幾微之際聖狂
天淵之判而可以不敬乎敬則欲寡理明靜虛
動直太極在我而聖人可學焉故曰君子脩之
吉敬也者脩之之功吉也者脩之之驗此周子
作圖之意可得而測識矣蓋嘗論之太極動靜
陰陽分而兩儀立真精妙合萬物生而變化形
===
自其統體者言之萬物一太極無不包括也自
其散殊者言之一物一太極不相假借也是人
物莫不有此太極之理動靜其機也仁義中正
其具也所謂天地之心而人之極也孰塗之人
而可爲堯舜者此也而何假於君子之脩之耶
必脩之而後吉太極之理豈由外鑠我哉誠以
人之生也負陰而抱陽形生神發之後繼善成
性之餘渾然理也粹然精也初無聖人君子之
別也唯夫五常之性感物而動善惡以分萬事
punctuated: 人以達於衆人，一也。聖人全之，而衆人昧焉。人化物而滅其天，其去聖人始遠矣，非聖人之有異於人也。君子知吾之心即聖人之心，吾心之太極即聖人之心之太極，一念幾微之際，聖狂天淵之判，而可以不敬乎？敬則欲寡理明，靜虛動直，太極在我，而聖人可學焉。故曰：「君子脩之吉。」敬也者，脩之之功；吉也者，脩之之驗。此周子作圖之意，可得而測識矣。蓋嘗論之，太極動靜，陰陽分而兩儀立，真精妙合，萬物生而變化形。自其統體者言之，萬物一太極，無不包括也；自其散殊者言之，一物一太極，不相假借也。是人物莫不有此太極之理，動靜其機也，仁義中正其具也，所謂天地之心而人之極也。孰塗之人而可爲堯舜者，此也，而何假於君子之脩之耶？必脩之而後吉，太極之理豈由外鑠我哉？誠以人之生也，負陰而抱陽，形生神發之後，繼善成性之餘，渾然理也，粹然精也，初無聖人君子之別也。唯夫五常之性感物而動，善惡以分，萬事
translation_en:
…from sages down to ordinary people, it is the same. Sages preserve it whole, whereas ordinary people are unaware of it. When people are transformed by external things and extinguish their Heaven-endowed nature, they begin to diverge far from the sages. It is not that sages are inherently different from other people. The gentleman knows that his own mind is the very same as the sage’s mind, and that the Supreme Ultimate in his mind is the very same as the Supreme Ultimate in the sage’s mind. At the subtle inception of a single thought, the distinction between sagehood and folly becomes as great as that between Heaven and the abyss. How, then, can one fail to maintain reverence? With reverence, desires diminish and principle becomes clear; in stillness one is empty, and in activity upright. The Supreme Ultimate is present within oneself, and sagehood can be learned. Thus it is said: “The gentleman cultivates it and has good fortune.” Reverence is the work of cultivating it; good fortune is the evidence of that cultivation. Through this we can discern Master Zhou’s intention in making his diagram.

I have considered this: through the Supreme Ultimate’s activity and stillness, yin and yang divide and the Two Modes are established. The true essence and the vital essences unite wondrously; the myriad things are born, and transformations take form. Viewed in its comprehensive unity, the myriad things are one Supreme Ultimate, which embraces everything. Viewed in their separate differentiation, each thing has its own Supreme Ultimate, without borrowing from another. Thus people and things all possess this principle of the Supreme Ultimate. Activity and stillness are its moving springs; benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and correctness are its constituent virtues. This is what is called the mind of Heaven and Earth and the ultimate standard for humanity. This is why any person on the road [?] can become a Yao or a Shun. Yet why should it depend upon the gentleman’s cultivation? If cultivation must precede good fortune, could the principle of the Supreme Ultimate be infused into me from outside?

Indeed, at birth people bear yin on their backs and embrace yang. Once bodily form has arisen and spirit has become active, following the continuation of goodness and the completion of human nature, there is integral principle and pure essence. Initially there is no distinction separating them from sages and gentlemen. It is only when the nature endowed with the Five Constant Virtues is stirred by contact with things that good and evil become differentiated, and the myriad affairs…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以出欲動情勝利害相攻陰濁汨而失之於靜
太極之體所以昏也悔吝生而失之於動太極
之用所以窒也動靜交戰人極不立而所以定
之者不能不賴於聖人也彼聖人者性與天合
一動一靜莫非仁義中正之德而又本之於靜
以立人極以一天下之動以贊化育以叅天地
是以天地日月四時鬼神咸有所不能違矣君
子有見於聖人之與我同也以為吾心之極與
聖人之極非有異者也聖人有以全動靜之德
===
而立人極而吾未能焉則誠自棄自暴而自遠
於聖人吾不可以不脩之也然聖人之主靜也
無欲者也貞夫一者也寂然不動感而遂通天
下之故者也吾未能聖人而靜焉求之不幾於
強制吾心坐忘而坐馳者耶於是乎有主敬之
功焉敬也者所以學為靜者也所以貫動靜而
用其力者也念慮未發之際則即其體而不失
乎存之之妙敬之涵養於靜者如是也念慮旣
發之時則因其端而致夫察之之功敬之涵養
punctuated:
以出，欲動情勝，利害相攻，陰濁汨而失之於靜，太極之體所以昏也；悔吝生而失之於動，太極之用所以窒也。動靜交戰，人極不立，而所以定之者，不能不賴於聖人也。彼聖人者，性與天合，一動一靜，莫非仁義中正之德，而又本之於靜，以立人極，以一天下之動，以贊化育，以叅天地。是以天地日月四時鬼神，咸有所不能違矣。君子有見於聖人之與我同也，以為吾心之極與聖人之極，非有異者也。聖人有以全動靜之德而立人極，而吾未能焉，則誠自棄自暴而自遠於聖人，吾不可以不脩之也。
然聖人之主靜也，無欲者也，貞夫一者也，寂然不動，感而遂通天下之故者也。吾未能聖人而靜焉求之，不幾於強制吾心，坐忘而坐馳者耶？於是乎有主敬之功焉。敬也者，所以學為靜者也，所以貫動靜而用其力者也。念慮未發之際，則即其體而不失乎存之之妙，敬之涵養於靜者如是也；念慮旣發之時，則因其端而致夫察之之功，敬之涵養
translation_en:
…thereby arise. Desires stir and emotions prevail; benefit and harm contend with one another. When turbid yin confounds the mind and it goes astray in stillness, the substance of the Supreme Ultimate is thereby obscured. When regret and shame arise and it goes astray in activity, the functioning of the Supreme Ultimate is thereby obstructed. Activity and stillness clash, and the ultimate standard for humanity is not established. To bring these into settled order, one cannot but rely upon the sage. The sage’s nature accords with Heaven. His every movement and every stillness embody the virtues of benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and correctness. Moreover, he roots these in stillness, thereby establishing the ultimate standard for humanity, unifying all activity under Heaven, assisting transformation and nurture, and forming a triad with Heaven and Earth. Thus Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon, the four seasons, and spirits all have that which they cannot contravene. The gentleman perceives that the sage is of the same kind as himself and considers that the ultimate standard within his own mind differs in no way from that of the sage. The sage can fully realize the virtues of activity and stillness and establish the ultimate standard for humanity. If I cannot yet do so, then indeed I abandon and injure myself and distance myself from the sage. I cannot fail to cultivate myself.
Yet the sage’s making stillness primary consists in being without desire and steadfast in unity: quiescent and unmoving, yet, when stimulated, penetrating all the affairs of the world. If I have not yet become a sage but seek this through stillness, would I not come close to forcibly restraining my mind—sitting in forgetfulness while my thoughts race? Hence there is the practice of making reverent attentiveness primary. Reverent attentiveness is the means by which one learns to attain stillness; it is also the means by which one applies one’s effort throughout both activity and stillness. Before thoughts and deliberations have arisen, one attends to the mind’s substance without losing the subtle art of preserving it. Such is the nurturing effected by reverent attentiveness in stillness. Once thoughts and deliberations have arisen, one follows their first beginnings and fully applies the work of scrutiny. The nurturing effected by reverent attentiveness…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
於動者如是也其行之也必求其中其處之也
必求其正其發之也必求其仁其裁之也必求
其義合動靜而一於敬者也一於敬則吾心常
惺惺矣常整齊嚴肅矣常虛常靈而夜氣清矣
陽明勝而德性用人欲淨而天理流行矣由是
而居之安資之深取之左右逢其原以靜則有
常以動則不括以之爲己則順而祥以之爲人
則愛而公以之爲天下國家則無所處而不當
所謂聰明睿智皆由是出者有也所謂守之貴
===
行之利廓之配天地者有也吾知天地之德也
日月之明也四時之序也鬼神之吉凶也一無
極而太極之理爲之也太極之理存乎我者旣
無闕欠則是踐形惟肖吾之德亦聖人之德矣
不愧屋漏吾之明亦聖人之明矣知化以善述
其事窮神以善繼其志吾心之照臨通乎晝夜
吾心之往來同乎屈伸一聖人之出入造化者
矣其合德合明合序合吉凶聖人之所能者吾
亦能之聖人固無欲而靜不假脩爲以立極吾
punctuated: 於動者如是也。其行之也，必求其中；其處之也，必求其正；其發之也，必求其仁；其裁之也，必求其義。合動靜而一於敬者也。一於敬，則吾心常惺惺矣，常整齊嚴肅矣，常虛常靈而夜氣清矣，陽明勝而德性用，人欲淨而天理流行矣。由是而居之安，資之深，取之左右逢其原。以靜則有常，以動則不括；以之爲己則順而祥，以之爲人則愛而公，以之爲天下國家則無所處而不當。所謂「聰明睿智皆由是出」者有也，所謂「守之貴，行之利，廓之配天地」者有也。吾知天地之德也，日月之明也，四時之序也，鬼神之吉凶也，一無極而太極之理爲之也。太極之理存乎我者旣無闕欠，則是踐形惟肖，吾之德亦聖人之德矣；不愧屋漏，吾之明亦聖人之明矣。知化以善述其事，窮神以善繼其志。吾心之照臨通乎晝夜，吾心之往來同乎屈伸，一聖人之出入造化者矣。其合德、合明、合序、合吉凶，聖人之所能者，吾亦能之。聖人固無欲而靜，不假脩爲以立極，吾
translation_en:
…in activity is like this. In acting, one must seek the mean; in taking one’s position, one must seek correctness; in expressing oneself, one must seek humaneness; in making judgments, one must seek righteousness. This unites activity and stillness in reverent attentiveness. Through this unity in reverent attentiveness, my mind is always alert, always orderly and solemn, always empty and responsive, and the vital energy of the night is clear. Luminous yang prevails and moral nature functions; human desires are cleansed away and heavenly principle flows freely. Thus I dwell securely in it, draw deeply upon it, and find its source wherever I turn. In stillness there is constancy; in activity there is no constraint. Applied to oneself, it brings accord and auspiciousness; applied to others, it brings love and impartiality; applied to the realm and the state, it makes every response appropriate. Here is what is meant by “perceptiveness, understanding, insight, and wisdom all issue from this,” and by “to preserve it is noble; to practice it is beneficial; to expand it is to match Heaven and Earth.”

I know that the virtue of Heaven and Earth, the brightness of the sun and moon, the sequence of the four seasons, and the auspicious and inauspicious workings of ghosts and spirits are all brought about by the single principle of the Ultimateless and yet the Supreme Ultimate. Once the principle of the Supreme Ultimate within me lacks nothing, I fulfill my bodily form and truly resemble the sage: my virtue, too, is the sage’s virtue. Having nothing to be ashamed of even in the most secluded corner of my room, my illumination, too, is the sage’s illumination. By understanding transformation, I ably carry forward his undertakings; by fathoming the numinous, I ably continue his intent. My mind’s illumination extends through day and night; its coming and going accord with contraction and expansion. I am wholly like a sage moving within the workings of creation and transformation. In matching the virtue of Heaven and Earth, the brightness of the sun and moon, the sequence of the four seasons, and the auspicious and inauspicious workings of ghosts and spirits, what the sage can do, I too can do. title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
亦敬以作所而人極於我乎立矣君子之吉孰
大於是然君子豈有心於獲吉而計其功哉亦
曰脩之自我者當如是其吉與否有不在我者
雖聖人不能必君子固將居易以俟之而已而
天之所助者順也人之所助者信也履信思乎
順是以自天祐之吉無不利也在易震之象曰
君子以恐懼脩省夫君子固動必以天者矣然
感洊雷之義則其恐懼脩省之心自有所不能
已也蹇之象曰君子以反身脩德夫君子之德
===
固無所闕矣然當處蹇之時則其反身脩德之
念自有所不容已也曰脩省曰脩德非所以全
夫太極之理哉非君子之脩之而求至於聖人
之立極者哉抑觀太極一圖周子嘗手授二程
矣二程有所得而廣之一則曰動亦定靜亦定
無將迎無内外固聖人主靜之說也一則曰涵
養須用敬固君子脩之之功也然於此圖則未
嘗輕以語人非以其微妙而難言者乎故曰先
生之精因圖以示先生之蘊因圖以發又曰百
punctuated: 亦敬以作所，而人極於我乎立矣。君子之吉，孰大於是？然君子豈有心於獲吉而計其功哉？亦曰脩之自我者，當如是。其吉與否，有不在我者，雖聖人不能必。君子固將居易以俟之而已。而天之所助者順也，人之所助者信也。履信思乎順，是以自天祐之，吉無不利也。在《易》，震之象曰：「君子以恐懼脩省。」夫君子固動必以天者矣，然感洊雷之義，則其恐懼脩省之心自有所不能已也。蹇之象曰：「君子以反身脩德。」夫君子之德固無所闕矣，然當處蹇之時，則其反身脩德之念自有所不容已也。曰脩省，曰脩德，非所以全夫太極之理哉？非君子之脩之而求至於聖人之立極者哉？抑觀太極一圖，周子嘗手授二程矣。二程有所得而廣之，一則曰：「動亦定，靜亦定，無將迎，無内外。」固聖人主靜之說也。一則曰：「涵養須用敬。」固君子脩之之功也。然於此圖，則未嘗輕以語人，非以其微妙而難言者乎？故曰：「先生之精，因圖以示；先生之蘊，因圖以發。」又曰：「百
translation_en:
…I too make reverence my foundation, and thus the ultimate standard for humanity is established within me. What good fortune for the gentleman could be greater than this? Yet would the gentleman deliberately seek good fortune and calculate the rewards of his efforts? He merely says that cultivation, insofar as it proceeds from himself, ought to be like this. Whether good fortune follows depends in part on things beyond his control; even a sage cannot guarantee it. The gentleman therefore simply abides in ease and awaits what comes. What Heaven assists is compliance; what people assist is trustworthiness. By practicing trustworthiness and keeping compliance in mind, he receives help from Heaven: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.

In the Book of Changes, the Image of Zhen, Thunder, says: “The gentleman, through fear and apprehension, cultivates and examines himself.” The gentleman certainly accords with Heaven whenever he acts. Yet, moved by the meaning of repeated thunder, he cannot restrain his impulse to cultivate and examine himself in fear and apprehension. The Image of Jian, Obstruction, says: “The gentleman turns back upon himself and cultivates virtue.” The gentleman’s virtue certainly lacks nothing. Yet when he finds himself amid obstruction, he cannot suppress the thought of turning back upon himself and cultivating virtue. Are the injunctions to cultivate and examine oneself, and to cultivate virtue, not means of preserving in full the principle of the Supreme Ultimate? Are they not the gentleman’s cultivation through which he seeks to attain the sage’s establishment of the ultimate standard?

Consider, moreover, the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate: Master Zhou once personally transmitted it to the two Cheng brothers. The two Chengs grasped its meaning and elaborated upon it. One said: “In activity there is stability; in stillness there is also stability. There is neither anticipating nor going out to meet things, neither inner nor outer.” This is indeed the teaching that the sage takes stillness as primary. The other said: “In nurturing oneself, one must employ reverence.” This is indeed the work of the gentleman’s self-cultivation. Yet they never spoke lightly to others about this diagram. Was that not because its subtleties were difficult to put into words? title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
世道術淵源詎不信夫
同前
蔣惇
同考試官學正吳批詞氣清健定善作者取之
考試官教諭林批比用易通誠字立意語新可録
考試官教授詹批周子倡道學以覺天下意發明詳盡
儒者倡明斯道而示天下以求道之要然後知
天之不遠于人而入聖者有階矣夫道之在天
下本無不明而人之爲學多昧焉而不知求昧
===
者未覺而忽倡其說以鳴於天下是故言天言
聖既不可少貶于高論則天下之驟聞而駭畏
難而阻者吾懼其且千百爲羣而起矣然天者
未始不爲人而聖人者可學而至者也第學絶
而罔傳倡寡而和稀夫人未之知耳故于是必
示以脩之之說知所脩則及門者可望見于堂
室而至之不難矣知所至則知聖人之道在我
而所謂天者亦不異于我矣今夫天之運也陰
靜陽動而已矣孰綱維是太極而已矣詩曰維
punctuated:
世道術淵源，詎不信夫？

同前。
蔣惇。
同考試官學正吳批：詞氣清健，定善作者，取之。
考試官教諭林批：比用易通誠字立意，語新可録。
考試官教授詹批：周子倡道學以覺天下意，發明詳盡。

Only when a Confucian scholar proclaims and clarifies this Way, showing all under Heaven the essentials of seeking it, do people understand that Heaven is not far from humanity and that there are steps by which to attain sagehood. The Way in the world is fundamentally clear in every respect, yet those who pursue learning are often ignorant of it and do not know to seek it. If, before the ignorant have awakened, someone suddenly proclaims this teaching throughout the world, then, since discourse on Heaven and the sages cannot be lowered even slightly from its lofty level, I fear that those startled by hearing it so abruptly, and deterred by their fear of its difficulty, will arise in groups numbering hundreds and thousands. Yet Heaven has never been separate from humanity, and sagehood can be attained through learning. It is only that this learning has been interrupted and has gone untransmitted; few proclaim it and few respond, so people do not yet understand it. Thus one must explain to them the teaching of self-cultivation. Once they know what to cultivate, those who have reached the gate can glimpse the hall and inner chambers, and reaching them will not be difficult. Once they know what they are to attain, they will understand that the Way of the sages lies within themselves, and that what is called Heaven is likewise no different from themselves. title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天之命於穆不已誠也誠卽太極也聖人之□
天全乎動靜之德而已矣所以全動靜之德者
主靜而已矣卽誠也卽太極之所以立也天維
誠故陰陽錯焉五氣布焉四時行而萬物生焉
天之爲道盡于是矣聖人維誠故人極立焉中
正仁義出焉由是而與天地合其德日月合其
明四時合其序鬼神合其吉凶而聖人之爲聖
人盡于是矣夫天道若是乎其淵以妙也聖人
之道若是乎其高且美也語塗之人而曰天之
===
道備于而躬聖人者而可至也有不聞而駭畏
而阻者哉然不知天無心渾乎其誠也聖人有
心誠而已矣天之道唯聖人能全之而君子之
求道脩其爲聖人者而已矣蓋人之生也繼之
者善成之者性天之道在人也方其湛然虛明
萬理畢備何者非天聖人此心塗人亦此心也
然聖人所以異于人者不殽于欲而已君子之
脩之求所以無欲而已無欲則誠誠未可以遽
至持之以敬斯幾矣何以言之夫人之昏昧放
punctuated: 天之命，於穆不已」，誠也。誠卽太極也。聖人之□天，全乎動靜之德而已矣。所以全動靜之德者，主靜而已矣，卽誠也，卽太極之所以立也。天維誠，故陰陽錯焉，五氣布焉，四時行而萬物生焉，天之爲道盡于是矣。聖人維誠，故人極立焉，中正仁義出焉。由是而與天地合其德，日月合其明，四時合其序，鬼神合其吉凶，而聖人之爲聖人盡于是矣。夫天道若是乎其淵以妙也，聖人之道若是乎其高且美也。語塗之人而曰：「天之道備于而躬，聖人者，而可至也。」有不聞而駭、畏而阻者哉？然不知天無心，渾乎其誠也；聖人有心，誠而已矣。天之道唯聖人能全之，而君子之求道，脩其爲聖人者而已矣。蓋人之生也，繼之者善，成之者性，天之道在人也。方其湛然虛明，萬理畢備，何者非天？聖人此心，塗人亦此心也。然聖人所以異于人者，不殽于欲而已。君子之脩之，求所以無欲而已。無欲則誠，誠未可以遽至，持之以敬，斯幾矣。何以言之？夫人之昏昧放
translation_en: …“Heaven’s mandate—how profound, unceasing!” This is sincerity. Sincerity is the Supreme Ultimate. The sage’s [illegible] Heaven [?] consists simply in fully realizing the virtue of activity and stillness. What fully realizes this virtue is simply taking stillness as the governing principle. This is sincerity; this is how the Supreme Ultimate is established. Because Heaven is sincere, yin and yang interweave, the five vital energies spread, the four seasons proceed, and the myriad things come into being. The Way of Heaven is entirely encompassed in this. Because the sage is sincere, the supreme standard for humanity is established, and centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness emerge. Through this, the sage accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth, in brightness with the sun and moon, in sequence with the four seasons, and in good and ill fortune with ghosts and spirits. Everything that makes the sage a sage is encompassed in this. The Way of Heaven is so profound and wondrous; the Way of the sage is so lofty and beautiful. If one tells a person on the road, “The Way of Heaven is fully present in your own person, and you can attain sagehood,” would anyone fail to be startled on hearing this, or to shrink back in fear? Yet such people do not understand that Heaven has no deliberate mind and is wholly sincere; the sage has a mind, but it is simply sincere. Only the sage can fully realize the Way of Heaven, while the gentleman’s pursuit of the Way consists simply in cultivating what makes him a sage. For when human beings come into existence, what carries on the Way is goodness, and what completes it is their nature: this is the Way of Heaven within human beings. When the mind is serene, empty, and luminous, with all principles fully present, what in it is not Heaven? The sage has this mind, and the person on the road likewise has this mind. What distinguishes the sage from others is simply that he is not muddled by desires. The gentleman’s cultivation consists simply in seeking how to be without desires. Without desires, one is sincere. Sincerity cannot be attained all at once; by maintaining reverent attentiveness, one comes close to it. Why do I say this? When people become benighted and abandon themselves to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
逸遂至於欲動情勝利害相攻者豈其性哉不
知檢其心耳心無所檢則肆肆則認欲為理而
無以全其天矣惟狂罔念而侮聖人之言矣卒
蹈于艱難險阻而百逆萃之夫固有以自取之
爾是以君子持敬之功不可以已也然貫動靜
而無不在者聖人之誠君子之持敬亦自其動
靜求之可矣子思子曰戒慎乎其所不睹恐懼
乎其所不聞夫不睹不聞此何時也戒慎恐懼
此何心也斯靜無不存矣不但已也又曰莫見
===
乎隱莫顯乎微君子必慎其獨隱也微也此何
時也君子慎獨此何心也斯動無不察矣其行
之也中其發之也仁聖人定之于動者何如也
吾脩之而求于動不敢以弗敬焉則中與仁可
幾而太極之用庶乎行矣其處之也正其裁之
也義聖人定之于靜者何如也吾脩之而求于
靜不敢以弗敬焉則正與義可幾而太極之體
庶乎立矣聖人與天地合其德吾而未能然易
知簡能可求也從而脩之而天地之德幾矣聖
punctuated: 逸，遂至於欲動情勝、利害相攻者，豈其性哉？不知檢其心耳。心無所檢則肆，肆則認欲為理，而無以全其天矣。惟狂罔念，而侮聖人之言矣，卒蹈于艱難險阻，而百逆萃之，夫固有以自取之爾。是以君子持敬之功不可以已也。然貫動靜而無不在者，聖人之誠；君子之持敬，亦自其動靜求之可矣。子思子曰：「戒慎乎其所不睹，恐懼乎其所不聞。」夫不睹不聞，此何時也？戒慎恐懼，此何心也？斯靜無不存矣。不但已也，又曰：「莫見乎隱，莫顯乎微，君子必慎其獨。」隱也微也，此何時也？君子慎獨，此何心也？斯動無不察矣。其行之也中，其發之也仁，聖人定之于動者何如也？吾脩之而求于動，不敢以弗敬焉，則中與仁可幾，而太極之用庶乎行矣。其處之也正，其裁之也義，聖人定之于靜者何如也？吾脩之而求于靜，不敢以弗敬焉，則正與義可幾，而太極之體庶乎立矣。聖人與天地合其德，吾而未能，然易知簡能可求也，從而脩之，而天地之德幾矣。聖
translation_en:
…unrestrained, until desires are stirred, feelings prevail, and considerations of advantage and harm contend—is this really their inherent nature? It is merely that they do not know to restrain their minds. Without restraint, the mind becomes wanton; becoming wanton, it mistakes desire for principle and thus cannot preserve intact its Heaven-endowed nature. Reckless and unreflective, they slight the words of the sages. In the end they fall into hardships and perils, and a hundred adversities converge upon them. They have indeed brought this upon themselves. Thus the gentleman must never cease his efforts to maintain reverent attentiveness. What pervades both activity and stillness, being absent nowhere, is the sage’s sincerity. The gentleman, in maintaining reverent attentiveness, may likewise seek it within his own activity and stillness.

Master Zisi said: “Be watchful and cautious concerning what you do not see, fearful and apprehensive concerning what you do not hear.” What moment is this, when one neither sees nor hears? What state of mind is this watchfulness, caution, fear, and apprehension? In this way, in stillness there is nothing that is not preserved. Nor does it stop there. He also said: “Nothing is more visible than what is hidden; nothing is more manifest than what is minute. The gentleman must be watchful over himself when alone.” What moment is this hiddenness and minuteness? What state of mind is this watchfulness over oneself when alone? In this way, in activity there is nothing that is not examined.

In conduct there is centrality; in outward expression there is benevolence. How does the sage establish these in activity? If I cultivate myself and seek them in activity, never daring to lack reverent attentiveness, then centrality and benevolence may be approached, and the functioning of the Supreme Ultimate may come into operation. In repose there is correctness; in judgment there is righteousness. How does the sage establish these in stillness? If I cultivate myself and seek them in stillness, never daring to lack reverent attentiveness, then correctness and righteousness may be approached, and the substance of the Supreme Ultimate may become established.

The sage accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth. Though I have not yet achieved this, their ease in knowing and simplicity in accomplishing may be sought. By cultivating myself accordingly, I may approach the virtue of Heaven and Earth. The sage…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
人與日月合其明吾而未能然當知當行可求
也從而脩之而日月之明幾矣聖人與四時合
其序鬼神合其吉凶吾而未能焉時止時行福
善禍淫可求也從而脩之而四時之序鬼神之
吉凶幾矣由是靜虛而明通動直而公溥以之
為己則順而祥以之為人則愛而公以之為天
下國家則無所處而不當故曰吉是君子之所
履也非假于外也又由是將無所用于脩而聖
人之域忽不自知其優入而所謂天道者亦不
===
□□我而得之矣於戲聖人以誠而合天君子
以敬而入聖道果遠乎哉學聖者不曰有階巳
□然周子之望于人者深矣顧聞是圖手授程
子之外鮮有傳者程子得之不復聞有所授豈
默識言意之表固難其人邪朱子作解亦曰辯
詰紛然苦于應酬之不給則知而信之而果于
脩為者亦希見矣抑周子豈徒望于當時巳也
百世而下神會心解有如周子承墜緒于孔孟
則倡鳴絕學者固不可病其寡和雖然以誠敬
punctuated: 人與日月合其明，吾而未能然，當知當行可求也。從而脩之，而日月之明幾矣。聖人與四時合其序，鬼神合其吉凶，吾而未能焉，時止時行、福善禍淫可求也。從而脩之，而四時之序、鬼神之吉凶幾矣。由是靜虛而明通，動直而公溥，以之為己則順而祥，以之為人則愛而公，以之為天下國家則無所處而不當，故曰吉。是君子之所履也，非假于外也。又由是將無所用于脩，而聖人之域忽不自知其優入，而所謂天道者亦不□□我而得之矣。於戲！聖人以誠而合天，君子以敬而入聖，道果遠乎哉？學聖者不曰有階巳□然？周子之望于人者深矣。顧聞是圖手授程子之外，鮮有傳者，程子得之，不復聞有所授，豈默識言意之表，固難其人邪？朱子作解，亦曰辯詰紛然，苦于應酬之不給，則知而信之而果于脩為者亦希見矣。抑周子豈徒望于當時巳也？百世而下，神會心解，有如周子承墜緒于孔孟，則倡鳴絕學者固不可病其寡和。雖然，以誠敬
translation_en:
…the sage accords in his illumination with the sun and moon. Though I cannot yet do so, I can seek what ought to be known and what ought to be done. By cultivating myself accordingly, I may approach the illumination of the sun and moon. The sage accords in his order with the four seasons, and in his good and ill fortune with the spirits. Though I cannot yet achieve this, I can seek to understand stopping and acting at the proper times, and the blessing of goodness and punishment of wickedness. By cultivating myself accordingly, I may approach the order of the four seasons and the good and ill fortune of the spirits. Thus, in stillness, one becomes empty, lucid, and penetrating; in activity, upright, impartial, and all-embracing. Applied to oneself, this brings harmony and auspiciousness; applied to others, love and impartiality; applied to the world, the state, and the family, it leaves no circumstance improperly handled. Hence it is called auspicious. This is what the gentleman puts into practice; it is not borrowed from outside himself. Proceeding further, he will have no more need to exert himself in cultivation, and will suddenly find that he has entered the realm of the sage with ease, without knowing it. And what is called the Way of Heaven will also be attained by me [?; two characters illegible]. Alas! Through sincerity the sage accords with Heaven; through reverence the gentleman enters sagehood. Is the Way really so distant? Would those who study to become sages not say that there are steps by which to ascend [?]? Master Zhou’s expectations of others were indeed profound.

Yet I have heard that, apart from his personally handing this diagram to Master Cheng, it was transmitted to few others. After Master Cheng received it, we hear no further report of his passing it on. Could it be that someone able silently to apprehend what lies beyond words and their meanings is inherently difficult to find? When Master Zhu wrote his explanation, he too said that disputes and challenges arose in such profusion that he struggled to keep up with responding. Thus, those who understand and believe it, and resolutely put it into practice through self-cultivation, are seldom seen. But did Master Zhou place his hopes only in the people of his own time? A hundred generations later, there may be someone who grasps it in spirit and understands it in his heart, just as Master Zhou took up the broken thread of transmission from Confucius and Mencius. Those who proclaim a learning whose transmission has been severed surely cannot be faulted for having few who respond. Nevertheless, taking sincerity and reverence as…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
爲入門程子蓋已言之矣
表
擬宋以孔宜爲曲阜主簿奉孔子祀謝表
乾德四年
趙恂
同考試官教諭聞批純雅典則得宋表體
同考試官教諭江批敷揚敘述俱有次第可錄
考試官教諭林批表貴駢儷尤尚精雅此作可取
考試官教授詹批述先聖而不失之誇言五代而不
===
失之怨宛然孔氏家法亦得恭謝之體表之佳者
乾德四年正月某日具官臣孔宜伏蒙
聖恩以臣宜爲曲阜主簿奉臣祖孔丘祀謹奉
表稱
謝者伏以
運隆
天造
恩徽穆被于宮墻
澤逮雲仍
punctuated:
爲入門，程子蓋已言之矣。

表
擬宋以孔宜爲曲阜主簿奉孔子祀謝表
乾德四年
趙恂

同考試官教諭聞批：純雅典則，得宋表體。
同考試官教諭江批：敷揚敘述，俱有次第，可錄。
考試官教諭林批：表貴駢儷，尤尚精雅，此作可取。
考試官教授詹批：述先聖而不失之誇，言五代而不失之怨，宛然孔氏家法，亦得恭謝之體，表之佳者。

乾德四年正月某日，具官臣孔宜伏蒙聖恩，以臣宜爲曲阜主簿，奉臣祖孔丘祀，謹奉表稱謝者。伏以運隆天造，恩徽穆被于宮墻；澤逮雲仍，
translation_en:
…as the gateway to learning, Master Cheng has surely already spoken of this.

Memorial
A simulated memorial of thanks for the Song appointment of Kong Yi as Registrar of Qufu to maintain the sacrifices to Confucius.
Fourth year of Qiande [966].
By Zhao Xun.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: “Pure, elegant, and classically ordered; it captures the form of Song memorials.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The exposition and narration are both well ordered. Worth including.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Memorials prize parallel phrasing and particularly esteem refinement and elegance. This composition is worthy of selection.”
