Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: “It recounts the Former Sage without lapsing into exaggeration and speaks of the Five Dynasties without lapsing into resentment. It perfectly reflects the Kong family's tradition and also achieves the proper form of respectful thanks: an excellent memorial.”

On a certain day of the first month of the fourth year of Qiande, your servant Kong Yi, holding the stated office, has humbly received your sagely favor appointing your servant Yi as Registrar of Qufu to maintain the sacrifices to my ancestor Kong Qiu. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks.

I humbly consider that, as the fortunes of the age flourish through Heaven's creative work, your gracious favor serenely extends to the walls of the Sage's sanctuary; your beneficence reaches his distant descendants…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
寵秩重光于俎豆綏分里邑喜切門庭於昭
曠代之榮茂衍承家之系臣宜誠惶誠恐
稽首頓首緬惟逖祖生值成周降宿紱麟
鍾兩儀之間氣金聲玉振集羣聖之大成
聞而知之期應五百餘歲識其大者教傳
七十二賢嘅道大而世莫能容故時違而
主不終遇曰王曰帝斯文在茲先聖先師
美報於後漢肇祀于過魯唐集議而從房
並錄孫枝丕延祖委褒成紹聖名以代殊
===
王襲賓崇禮緣時異駸尋五季之世罔念
三恪之傳眇此尼宗幾同編戶無曰末裔
敢期屈蠖之伸利見
大人幸覩
飛龍之會玆蓋伏遇
○○○○
體元則大
凝命奉宸
清和克紹於帝猷
punctuated: 寵秩重光于俎豆，綏分里邑，喜切門庭。於昭曠代之榮，茂衍承家之系。臣宜誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。緬惟逖祖，生值成周，降宿紱麟，鍾兩儀之間氣；金聲玉振，集羣聖之大成。聞而知之，期應五百餘歲；識其大者，教傳七十二賢。嘅道大而世莫能容，故時違而主不終遇。曰王曰帝，斯文在茲；先聖先師，美報於後。漢肇祀于過魯，唐集議而從房。並錄孫枝，丕延祖委。褒成紹聖，名以代殊；王襲賓崇，禮緣時異。駸尋五季之世，罔念三恪之傳。眇此尼宗，幾同編戶。無曰末裔，敢期屈蠖之伸；利見大人，幸覩飛龍之會。玆蓋伏遇○○○○，體元則大，凝命奉宸，清和克紹於帝猷。
translation_en:
…The honored rank lends renewed glory to the sacrificial vessels; a secure appointment in a local district brings heartfelt joy to our household. How splendid is this honor, unparalleled through the ages, abundantly extending the lineage that inherits our ancestral legacy! Your servant Yi, in deepest fear and trembling, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly prostrates himself.

I reflect upon my distant ancestor, born in the flourishing age of Zhou. A star descended, and a qilin bore a ceremonial sash [?]; he embodied the rare, harmonious vital force of Heaven and Earth. Like the sounding of bronze bells and the concluding resonance of jade chimes, he brought together the consummate achievements of all the sages. Knowing the Way through what he had heard, he appeared at the appointed interval of more than five hundred years; his teaching was transmitted to seventy-two worthy disciples who understood its greater principles. Alas, his Way was so great that the world could not accommodate it; the times opposed him, and he never ultimately encountered a ruler who would employ him. Whether under kings or emperors, this cultural tradition resided in him; as the Former Sage and Former Teacher, he received fitting recompense in later ages. The Han inaugurated sacrifices when the emperor passed through Lu; the Tang convened deliberations and followed Fang’s proposal. They also enrolled his descendants for honors, thereby grandly perpetuating his ancestral legacy. Titles such as Baocheng, “Completing in Praise,” and Shaosheng, “Continuing the Sage,” differed from dynasty to dynasty; royal rank, hereditary succession, and honored treatment as a guest [?] varied in their ceremonial forms with the times.

As the age of the Five Dynasties unfolded, no heed was paid to the tradition of the Three Honored Lineages. This humble lineage of Confucius became almost indistinguishable from ordinary registered households. Though only a remote descendant, how could I have dared hope to stretch forth like the inchworm after its bending? Finding it favorable to behold the great man, I have fortunately witnessed the moment of the flying dragon’s ascent.

This is because I have humbly encountered ○○○○, who embodies the primal principle and takes greatness as his model, firmly upholds the Mandate and occupies the imperial seat, and through purity and harmony ably carries forward the imperial designs …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
顯懿肆聯於王表願
聖人早生之祝
昌期適應當時慶
赤光滿室之祥
文明預覘今日軍中不釋卷何淮甸數車以
爲多天下自此寧信華山一言而可証蜀
宮辨鏡讀書知宰相之賢汴雪解貂
頒賜來元戎之感乃當
天與人歸之際式昭
===
崇儒重道之風惟
制作定世符允資垂憲在
君師立人極雅屬弘文慨自唐移遹存殷鑒經
殘教弛詎云絃誦之微世降道污遑恤典
章之議非
大聖之有作何絶學之能興初
御乾龍配位亟成于藻繪甫
開日馭祀儀聿正于春秋
賛秩
punctuated:
顯懿肆聯於王表。願聖人早生之祝，昌期適應當時；慶赤光滿室之祥，文明預覘今日。軍中不釋卷，何淮甸數車以爲多？天下自此寧，信華山一言而可証。蜀宮辨鏡，讀書知宰相之賢；汴雪解貂，頒賜來元戎之感。乃當天與人歸之際，式昭崇儒重道之風。
惟制作定世符，允資垂憲；在君師立人極，雅屬弘文。慨自唐移，遹存殷鑒。經殘教弛，詎云絃誦之微？世降道污，遑恤典章之議？非大聖之有作，何絶學之能興？初御乾龍，配位亟成于藻繪；甫開日馭，祀儀聿正于春秋。賛秩
translation_en:
…Manifest virtue and noble excellence were thus joined in the royal exemplar [?]. The prayer that the sage might soon be born found its timely fulfillment in that flourishing age; the auspicious sign of red light filling the chamber foretold the cultural brilliance of today. Even amid the army, you never put down your books: why consider the several cartloads from the Huai region an abundance? “All under Heaven will henceforth be at peace”: the single utterance at Mount Hua can indeed serve as proof. In the palace of Shu, discerning the nature of a mirror showed that reading enabled one to recognize a chief councillor’s worth; amid the snow at Bian, removing and bestowing a sable robe elicited a commander’s gratitude. At the moment when Heaven granted its favor and the people pledged allegiance, you thus manifested the spirit of honoring Confucian learning and esteeming the Way.
Establishing institutions fixes the tokens of an age [?] and truly provides models for posterity; serving as ruler and teacher establishes the highest standard for humanity and especially calls for advancing learning. Alas, since the passing of the Tang, the warning furnished by the Yin dynasty has remained. With the classics damaged and instruction neglected, could this be merely a matter of declining musical instruction and recitation? As the age deteriorated and the Way was debased, who had leisure to consider ritual institutions? Without the emergence of a great sage, how could interrupted traditions of learning be revived? As soon as you mounted the heavenly dragon to rule, painted images were promptly completed for those accorded places as accompanying recipients of sacrifice; scarcely had you begun your solar chariot’s course when the rites of spring and autumn sacrifice were duly set right. Praise and rank [?] …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
宸章燦奎文之煥赫
詔增畫戟儼法衛之森羅
褒嘉遠邁于前王
廕敘復覃于後嗣猥蒙
殊錫濫及匪材伏念臣謬忝科名未閑詩禮
昔遭喪亂抱祭器以徒傷今遘
聖明覩朝衣而思振俛奉揚于
王化僅守六經冀表正乎儒風愧膺
一命荷
===
天休之洊至思祖德以如存泰嶽維巖倏增高
于闕里洙源有混並演浚于長河臣敢不
奠獻陳詞慶千年之獲偶蒸嘗合族諭萬
指以知
恩矢畏門高祗欽
國厚式懷貽穀勗成訓于過庭益勉傾葵攄
孤忠于對
闕伏願
純綏
punctuated: 宸章燦奎文之煥赫，詔增畫戟，儼法衛之森羅。褒嘉遠邁于前王，廕敘復覃于後嗣。猥蒙殊錫，濫及匪材。伏念臣謬忝科名，未閑詩禮。昔遭喪亂，抱祭器以徒傷；今遘聖明，覩朝衣而思振。俛奉揚于王化，僅守六經；冀表正乎儒風，愧膺一命。荷天休之洊至，思祖德以如存。泰嶽維巖，倏增高于闕里；洙源有混，並演浚于長河。臣敢不奠獻陳詞，慶千年之獲偶；蒸嘗合族，諭萬指以知恩。矢畏門高，祗欽國厚。式懷貽穀，勗成訓于過庭；益勉傾葵，攄孤忠于對闕。伏願純綏
translation_en:
… Your Majesty’s compositions shine with the radiant brilliance of Kui, the constellation of literary culture. Your decree adds painted halberds, imposing in their ordered ranks as a ceremonial guard. Your commendations far surpass those of former kings, and the privilege of appointment through ancestral merit extends also to later descendants. These exceptional gifts have graciously reached even an unworthy man like myself.

I humbly reflect that I, your servant, have undeservedly attained examination distinction, yet remain unversed in the Odes and the Rites. Formerly, amid mourning and disorder, I could only grieve as I clasped the sacrificial vessels; now, encountering Your sagely and enlightened Majesty, I behold the court robes and aspire to renewed endeavor. Humbly striving to spread Your Majesty’s transforming influence, I have merely kept to the Six Classics. Hoping to set a proper example for Confucian scholars, I am ashamed to receive even this initial official appointment.

As Heaven’s blessings come repeatedly, I think upon my ancestor’s virtue as though he were still present. Lofty Mount Tai seems suddenly to rise still higher at Queli; the abundant springs of the Zhu River flow forth, deepening its long course. How could I, your servant, fail to present offerings and words of gratitude, rejoicing in this encounter granted once in a thousand years? At the winter and autumn sacrifices I shall assemble the clan and instruct its numerous members to acknowledge Your grace. I pledge to hold my lineage’s eminence in awe and reverently honor the state’s generosity. Mindful of bequeathing goodness to posterity, I shall earnestly impart the established teachings, as when a son passes through his father’s courtyard. Still more diligently, like the sunflower turning toward the sun, I shall express my solitary loyalty as I face the palace gates. I humbly pray that complete peace may be bestowed upon …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
帝社愉饗
天心
道統承千載之正傳
德業參兩間而成位
雅樂攸定恊音律以宣八風
文德聿脩舞干羽以來五國
福昭景貺早傳沙塞之肅清
穰錫溥將永奠
瑶圖于鞏固臣無任瞻
===
===
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策五道
第一問
張元舉
punctuated:
帝社，愉饗天心。道統承千載之正傳，德業參兩間而成位。雅樂攸定，恊音律以宣八風；文德聿脩，舞干羽以來五國。福昭景貺，早傳沙塞之肅清；穰錫溥將，永奠瑶圖于鞏固。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄場
策五道
第一問
張元舉
translation_en:
…the imperial altars of soil, and gladden Heaven’s heart with offerings. May the succession of the Way carry forward the orthodox transmission of a thousand years; may your virtue and achievements stand alongside Heaven and Earth, completing their triad. May the elegant music be established, its pitches harmonized to circulate the winds of the eight directions; may civil virtue be cultivated, and dances with shields and plumes bring the five states into allegiance. May blessings manifest Heaven’s great bounty, and news soon arrive that the sandy frontier has been pacified; may abundant gifts be widely bestowed, securing the imperial realm forever.
Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, cannot contain his utmost fervor and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks and bring them to Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Zhang Yuanju

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭林批我
聖祖暨我
皇上學術文章敻卓千古無能名狀此作頌揚有法錄之爲百世臣民佩服之助
同考試官敎諭蕭批鋪張不遺揄揚有則是必佳士
考試官敎諭林批我
聖祖
神孫授守一道此策備之猗歟盛哉
考試官敎授詹批敷對詳整必蘊藉之士錄之
知道統之承傳者可以論帝王之學術矣
===
知天地之易簡者可以論帝王之文章矣
大道統之承傳非必其丁寧告語而後學
術之眞傳可得也卽其默契潛孚而妙若
合一者斯學術之至者也天地之易簡非
必其摹擬形似而後文章之眞訣可得也
卽其生成化育而妙出無心者斯文章之
至者也然根本盛大而後英華敷茂兼內
外而該本末其實一以貫之而已王天下
者負有君師之責故學術文章均之不可
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭林批：「我聖祖暨我皇上，學術文章敻卓千古，無能名狀。此作頌揚有法，錄之爲百世臣民佩服之助。」
同考試官敎諭蕭批：「鋪張不遺，揄揚有則，是必佳士。」
考試官敎諭林批：「我聖祖神孫，授守一道，此策備之。猗歟盛哉！」
考試官敎授詹批：「敷對詳整，必蘊藉之士，錄之。」
知道統之承傳者，可以論帝王之學術矣；知天地之易簡者，可以論帝王之文章矣。大道統之承傳，非必其丁寧告語而後學術之眞傳可得也；卽其默契潛孚而妙若合一者，斯學術之至者也。天地之易簡，非必其摹擬形似而後文章之眞訣可得也；卽其生成化育而妙出無心者，斯文章之至者也。然根本盛大而後英華敷茂，兼內外而該本末，其實一以貫之而已。王天下者負有君師之責，故學術文章均之不可
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The learning and literary accomplishments of our sagely ancestor and our reigning emperor stand far above all ages, beyond the power of words to describe. This composition offers praise with proper method. It is selected to help subjects through a hundred generations reverently embrace their example.”
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: “Its expansive exposition leaves nothing out, and its praise follows proper standards. This must be a fine scholar.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Our sagely ancestor and his divine descendant transmit and preserve one and the same Way. This policy essay fully sets it forth. Ah, how magnificent!”
Examiner Zhan, Professor, comments: “The response is detailed and well ordered. Its author must be a scholar of cultivated depth. Select it.”
Those who understand the transmission of the succession to the Way can discuss the learning of emperors and kings; those who understand the ease and simplicity of Heaven and Earth can discuss the literary accomplishments of emperors and kings. As for the transmission of the succession to the Way [?], the true transmission of learning need not be attained only through earnest verbal instruction. Rather, where there is tacit accord and unspoken correspondence, so wondrously close as to seem one, there lies the highest attainment of learning. As for the ease and simplicity of Heaven and Earth, the true secret of literary accomplishment need not be attained only through imitation of outward forms. Rather, where generation, transformation, and nurture arise wondrously without conscious intention, there lies the highest attainment of literary accomplishment. Yet only when the roots are strong and abundant can the blossoms flourish luxuriantly. Embracing both the inward and the outward, encompassing both root and branch, these are in truth threaded together by a single principle. Those who rule All under Heaven bear the responsibilities of both ruler and teacher; thus learning and literary accomplishment alike must not be…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
闕焉然遡觀前古固未有如我
太祖高皇帝暨我
皇上之獨盛者矣愚也何足以知之姑敬述所
聞質之執事慨自胡元汚我華夏九十餘
年之間天地之精陰陽之奥萃于中國文
明之域以成斯民禮義之衷者淆奪于薰
染剥蝕于汚穢殆亦甚矣
天厭元德篤生我
高皇帝□□□□□不唯復自古帝王之土宇
而又有以□□下生人之靈性天地以位
日月以明山河以奠草木鳥獸以若以寧
洪荒而降章蔀紀元凡幾更革至是又一
大開闢也故旣以
身創萬古未有之業而又
□垂萬世丕延之統
得國之正
致治之隆振古鮮儷豈偶然哉夫衰極而盛
否極而泰周
punctuated:
闕焉。然遡觀前古，固未有如我太祖高皇帝暨我皇上之獨盛者矣。愚也何足以知之？姑敬述所聞，質之執事。慨自胡元汚我華夏，九十餘年之間，天地之精、陰陽之奥，萃于中國文明之域，以成斯民禮義之衷者，淆奪于薰染，剥蝕于汚穢，殆亦甚矣。
天厭元德，篤生我高皇帝□□□□□，不唯復自古帝王之土宇，而又有以□□下生人之靈性。天地以位，日月以明，山河以奠，草木鳥獸以若以寧。洪荒而降，章蔀紀元凡幾更革，至是又一大開闢也。故旣以身創萬古未有之業，而又□垂萬世丕延之統。得國之正，致治之隆，振古鮮儷，豈偶然哉？夫衰極而盛，否極而泰，周
translation_en:
…be lacking. Yet, looking back over antiquity, none has attained such singular eminence as our Emperor Taizu Gao and our present Emperor. How could someone as unlearned as I adequately comprehend this? Let me respectfully recount what I have heard and submit it to your judgment. Alas, during the more than ninety years in which the barbarian Yuan defiled our land of Huaxia, the essence of Heaven and Earth and the mysteries of yin and yang—which gathered in the civilized realm of the Central States to form this people’s inner disposition toward ritual propriety and righteousness—were confused and displaced by corrupting influences, eroded by pollution. This had indeed reached an extreme.
Heaven, displeased with the virtue of the Yuan, brought forth our Emperor Gao [five illegible characters]. He not only restored the territory of the emperors and kings of antiquity, but also had the means to [two illegible characters] the spiritual nature of the people under Heaven [?]. Thus Heaven and Earth assumed their proper places, the sun and moon shone brightly, the mountains and rivers were secured, and plants, birds, and beasts flourished in harmony and peace. Since primordial times, how many calendrical cycles—zhang, bu, ji, and yuan—had succeeded one another! At this point there was once again a great opening of Heaven and Earth. Thus, having personally founded an achievement unprecedented throughout all antiquity, he also [one illegible character] bequeathed a dynastic succession extending grandly through ten thousand generations. The legitimacy with which he gained the realm and the greatness of the order he established have seldom been matched since antiquity. Could this have been accidental? When decline reaches its utmost, prosperity follows; when obstruction reaches its utmost, ease follows; zhou [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天眷之有在然我
皇祖弘道以迓
景命
履貞而凝休祥者固自有以致之也蓋帝王
有帝王之學術非儒者佔畢之云而已昔
者堯舜禹湯文武所以見知聞知者乃其
要旨危微精一敬怠義欲焉爾數聖人後
得其傳者或寡矣我
皇祖則曠百世而承之觀其
===
與待制秦裕伯論學術曰爲學之道志不可
滿量不可隘意不可矜志滿則盈量隘則驕
意矜則小故聖人之學以天爲準賢人之學
以聖爲則苟局于狹小而拘于凡近豈能充
廣其學哉斯言也非得于帝王之真傳者而
有是乎人見
皇祖之奄有六合規模氣象恢恢乎上下與天
地同流而不知其根本盛大固有自矣是
故以内夏外夷之大分檄中原以伐暴救
punctuated: 天眷之有在，然我皇祖弘道以迓景命，履貞而凝休祥者，固自有以致之也。蓋帝王有帝王之學術，非儒者佔畢之云而已。昔者堯舜禹湯文武所以見知聞知者，乃其要旨：危微精一、敬怠義欲焉爾。數聖人後，得其傳者或寡矣。我皇祖則曠百世而承之。觀其與待制秦裕伯論學術曰：「爲學之道，志不可滿，量不可隘，意不可矜。志滿則盈，量隘則驕，意矜則小。故聖人之學以天爲準，賢人之學以聖爲則。苟局于狹小而拘于凡近，豈能充廣其學哉？」斯言也，非得于帝王之真傳者而有是乎？人見皇祖之奄有六合，規模氣象恢恢乎上下與天地同流，而不知其根本盛大固有自矣。是故，以内夏外夷之大分檄中原，以伐暴救
translation_en:
…Heaven’s favor had its chosen recipient. Yet our Imperial Ancestor’s magnifying the Way to welcome Heaven’s great mandate, and his treading the path of rectitude to gather blessings and auspicious signs, certainly had their own causes. Emperors and kings have a learning of their own; it is not merely the textual study of Confucian scholars. What Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu understood through seeing their predecessors or hearing of them lay in these essential teachings: the precariousness of the human mind and the subtlety of the mind of the Way, refinement and singleness of purpose, reverence and negligence, righteousness and desire. After these sages, few perhaps received their transmission. Our Imperial Ancestor, however, inherited it across a hundred generations.

Consider his discussion of learning with the Academician-in-Waiting Qin Yubo: “In pursuing learning, one’s aspirations must not become complacent, one’s capacity must not be narrow, and one’s mind must not be conceited. Complacent aspirations lead to self-satisfaction; narrow capacity leads to arrogance; a conceited mind leads to pettiness. Thus the sage’s learning takes Heaven as its standard, and the worthy person’s learning takes the sage as its model. If one confines oneself within narrow limits and remains bound by the commonplace and immediate, how can one enlarge one’s learning?” Could anyone who had not received the true transmission of emperors and kings have spoken these words? People see that our Imperial Ancestor possessed all within the six directions, and that the scope and grandeur of his rule were so vast as to move in unison with Heaven and Earth above and below. Yet they do not understand that the greatness of his foundations assuredly had its source. Thus he issued proclamations to the Central Plain invoking the fundamental distinction that places the Chinese within and the non-Chinese without, and, invoking the assault upon the violent and the rescue of…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
民之至仁諭將帥建學校而先北方罷詞
賦而顓經術削正山川之封號條定祭祀
之章程禁兄弟之婚均父母之服謹宮府
之政嚴内外之防大政大事未易縷數然
無一而非人倫之切近物理之精實皆所
以援拯生民之昏溺而覺之以斯道者也
是故學術之盛難乎其形容矣帝王有帝
王之文章非書生藻麗之云而已典謨其
至也□□□也乃其正詮平易敷暢發
===
揮事□□□漢而下操其藝者惑鑿矣
我
皇祖則駕千載而獨得之觀其
與學士詹同論文章曰古人爲文章明白易
知無深恠險僻之語近世文士不究道德之
本不達當世之務立詞雖艱深而意實淺近
即使過於相如何裨實用斯言也非得于文
章之眞傳者而有是哉人見
皇祖之酬應萬幾諄切懇至洋洋乎如造化之
punctuated:
民之至仁，諭將帥；建學校而先北方，罷詞賦而顓經術，削正山川之封號，條定祭祀之章程，禁兄弟之婚，均父母之服，謹宮府之政，嚴内外之防。大政大事，未易縷數，然無一而非人倫之切近、物理之精實，皆所以援拯生民之昏溺，而覺之以斯道者也。是故學術之盛，難乎其形容矣！
帝王有帝王之文章，非書生藻麗之云而已。典謨其至也，□□□也，乃其正詮，平易敷暢，發揮事□□□。漢而下，操其藝者惑鑿矣。我皇祖則駕千載而獨得之。觀其與學士詹同論文章曰：「古人爲文章，明白易知，無深恠險僻之語。近世文士不究道德之本，不達當世之務，立詞雖艱深，而意實淺近。即使過於相如，何裨實用？」斯言也，非得于文章之眞傳者而有是哉？人見皇祖之酬應萬幾，諄切懇至，洋洋乎如造化之
translation_en:
…with the utmost benevolence toward the people, he instructed his generals and commanders. He established schools, giving priority to the north; abolished verse and rhapsody as examination subjects and concentrated on classical learning; removed or corrected the honorific titles conferred on mountains and rivers; set out regulations for sacrificial rites; prohibited marriages between brothers and sisters; equalized the mourning obligations for fathers and mothers; carefully regulated the administration of palace and government; and strictly maintained the separation between the inner and outer spheres. His great policies and undertakings cannot readily be enumerated. Yet every one concerned the immediate realities of human relationships and the essential truths of things. All served to rescue the people from the ignorance in which they were submerged and awaken them through this Way. Thus the flourishing of his learning is difficult indeed to describe!
Emperors and kings have their own kind of writing: it is more than the ornate elegance of scholars. The Canons and Counsels represent its highest attainment. [Illegible passage: □□□.] Its proper exposition is plain and accessible, expansive and lucid, elucidating affairs [?; damaged text: 事□□□]. From the Han onward, practitioners of the literary art became misguided and contrived [?]. Our imperial progenitor alone rose above a thousand years and grasped its essence. Consider his discussion of writing with Academician Zhan Tong: “The ancients wrote clearly and intelligibly, without language that was obscure, strange, tortuous, or eccentric. Recent writers do not investigate the foundations of the Way and virtue or understand the affairs of their own age. Although their wording is difficult and abstruse, their meaning is actually shallow. Even if they surpassed Xiangru, what benefit would this bring to practical affairs?” Could such words have come from anyone who had not received the true transmission of the art of writing? People see how our imperial progenitor attended to the myriad affairs of government, earnest and deeply sincere, with an abundance like that of the workings of creation …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
簡易易知而不知其英華敷茂特餘事耳
是故
作
祖訓以示
聖子
神孫製樂章以祭
天享地思
□發天性之眞
□之異註洪範則傳箕子之
□蔡沉之失他如農桑學校
===
詔赦宥存恤之文萌賢之篇省頑之諭弘詞隱
義未可類求然無一而非性情之正大聖
賢之精微皆所以洗滌近代之纖媚而訓
之以敷言者也是故文章之盛難乎其名
狀矣然愚又嘗聞之
皇祖誥諭臣下有曰以仁義定天下雖遲而長
久又
punctuated:
簡易易知，而不知其英華敷茂，特餘事耳。是故作祖訓以示聖子神孫，製樂章以祭天享地，思□發天性之眞，□之異；註洪範，則傳箕子之□、蔡沉之失。他如農桑學校詔、赦宥存恤之文、萌賢之篇、省頑之諭，弘詞隱義，未可類求。然無一而非性情之正大、聖賢之精微，皆所以洗滌近代之纖媚，而訓之以敷言者也。是故文章之盛，難乎其名狀矣。
然愚又嘗聞之，皇祖誥諭臣下有曰：「以仁義定天下，雖遲而長久。」又
translation_en:
…simple and readily understood, yet they do not realize that the luxuriant flowering of his literary brilliance was merely incidental. Thus he composed the Ancestral Instructions to instruct his sagely sons and divine grandsons, and composed ritual songs for sacrifices to Heaven and offerings to Earth. His thoughts □ expressed the authenticity of his innate nature [?]; □ its differences [?]. In annotating the Great Plan, he transmitted Jizi’s □ and addressed Cai Chen’s errors [?]. Other examples include edicts on agriculture, sericulture, and schools; writings on pardons, relief, and assistance; pieces concerning the worthy [?]; and admonitions to awaken the obstinate. Their expansive language and profound meanings cannot readily be comprehended by classification. Yet every one embodies the rectitude and greatness of human nature and feeling, and the subtle insights of sages and worthies. All serve to cleanse the affected delicacy of recent writing and instruct people in the proper exposition of their words. Thus the magnificence of his writings is difficult indeed to describe.
Yet I, in my ignorance, have also heard that the Imperial Ancestor, in admonishing his ministers, said: “To bring order to All under Heaven through benevolence and righteousness may be slow, but the result endures.” Again…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曰周之仁厚可以爲法又
曰聖人統馭四海而宰制萬物仁以居之義
以行之故賢者樂有仁義而不肖者有所視
效於戲我
皇祖平時之言一則曰仁義二則曰仁義可以
仰窺
聖德精微□□入理醇固此則所謂根本盛大與
□□□合一者然也當時臣下之
===
□□□□□□作爲文章擧筆立就莫不言近而
指遠至于
詔諭遐方明燭萬里若見肺肝又曰
帝爲文或不喜書命侍臣坐榻下操觚受詞終
食之頃滚滚千餘言
天光昭回赫著簡袠眞所謂天之文也於戲我
皇祖爲文之妙一則曰明燭二則曰昭回又可
以仰窺
punctuated:
曰：「周之仁厚，可以爲法。」又曰：「聖人統馭四海而宰制萬物，仁以居之，義以行之，故賢者樂有仁義，而不肖者有所視效。」於戲！我皇祖平時之言，一則曰仁義，二則曰仁義，可以仰窺聖德精微，□□入理醇固。此則所謂根本盛大，與□□□合一者然也。
當時臣下之□□□□□□，作爲文章，擧筆立就，莫不言近而指遠。至于詔諭遐方，明燭萬里，若見肺肝。又曰：「帝爲文，或不喜書，命侍臣坐榻下，操觚受詞，終食之頃，滚滚千餘言。」天光昭回，赫著簡袠，眞所謂天之文也。於戲！我皇祖爲文之妙，一則曰明燭，二則曰昭回，又可以仰窺
translation_en:
…he said: “The benevolence and generosity of the Zhou may serve as a model.” He also said: “The sage rules all within the Four Seas and governs the myriad things, abiding in benevolence and acting through righteousness. Thus the worthy delight in possessing benevolence and righteousness, while the unworthy have something to look to and emulate.” Ah! In the ordinary words of our Imperial Ancestor, first he spoke of benevolence and righteousness, and again he spoke of benevolence and righteousness. Through these we may reverently glimpse the subtle profundity of his sagely virtue, [two illegible characters] his penetration of principle, his purity and firmness [?]. This indeed is what is meant by a root that is flourishing and great, united as one with [three illegible characters].
At that time, his ministers’ [six illegible characters; the connection is unclear]. In composing literary works, he would raise his brush and complete them at once; invariably, his language was accessible but its meaning far-reaching. As for his edicts instructing distant regions, their illumination reached ten thousand li, as though laying bare the innermost thoughts of those addressed. It is further said: “When the Emperor composed, he sometimes did not wish to write himself. He ordered an attendant official to sit below his couch, holding a writing tablet to take down his words; in the time it took to finish a meal, more than a thousand words poured forth.” Heavenly radiance shone all around, brilliantly manifest upon the written volumes: truly, this was what is called the writing of Heaven. Ah! The wonder of our Imperial Ancestor’s literary composition is described first as ‘illuminating brightly’ and again as ‘shining all around.’ Through this, too, we may reverently glimpse…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖學啓口容聲莫非至德此則所謂英華敷茂
與天地化育同一妙出無心者然也若夫
漢高之不事詩書唐宗之閨門慚德宋藝
祖之質朴自然其得國致治與其學術文
章豈可以同日而語哉仰惟
皇上嗣承大統
聖神
□□
===
□□□□有
□□□不言
神授于默成者故學術無一而不孚契文章無
一而不脗合伏覩
明倫大典一書推明統嗣之不同詳論義情之
兼盡
尊尊
親親並行攸當名正言順禮備樂成
立人極而光
punctuated:
聖學，啓口容聲，莫非至德。此則所謂英華敷茂，與天地化育同一妙，出無心者然也。若夫漢高之不事詩書，唐宗之閨門慚德，宋藝祖之質朴自然，其得國致治與其學術文章，豈可以同日而語哉？
仰惟皇上嗣承大統，聖神□□，□□□□有□□□不言，神授于默成者，故學術無一而不孚契，文章無一而不脗合。伏覩《明倫大典》一書，推明統嗣之不同，詳論義情之兼盡，尊尊親親，並行攸當，名正言順，禮備樂成，立人極而光
translation_en:
…his sagely learning: whenever he opened his mouth and gave voice to words, all expressed consummate virtue. This is what is meant by splendid flowering and luxuriant growth, sharing the same subtle workings as the transforming and nurturing powers of Heaven and Earth, arising without deliberate intent. As for Gaozu of Han, who did not devote himself to the Odes and Documents; Taizong of Tang, whose conduct within his household brought shame upon his virtue; and the founding emperor of Song, with his natural simplicity and plainness—how could their acquisition of the realm and achievement of orderly government, or their learning and literary compositions, be spoken of in the same breath as his?
We reverently consider how Your Majesty succeeded to the great imperial line. Sagely and divinely perceptive [illegible passage], without words [?], divinely imparted and silently accomplished. Thus, in learning there is nothing that does not accord, and in literary composition nothing that does not conform. We humbly observe that the Great Canon for Clarifying Human Relationships (Minglun dadian) elucidates the distinction between succession to the imperial line and succession as an heir, and discusses fully how both moral duty and familial feeling may be fulfilled. Honoring the honorable and cherishing one’s kin each find their proper expression together; names are correct and words accord with them; rites are complete and music perfected. It establishes the supreme standard for human conduct and brings glory to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖孝所謂考三王而不謬建天地而不悖者也
是書也質諸
皇祖祖訓之篇
正本以睦親
齊家以及天下之義眞同條而共貫矣至于
冊
天之文恭上
□□□□帝泰號義取人情道通神理蓋
===
重建極者也是文也質諸
皇祖初定郊
天之禮欽崇
昊天並隆
四祖三陽開泰敬率臣僚恭祀之文眞異世而
同符矣嘗
御製敬一箴有曰匪一弗純匪敬弗聚卽
皇祖之言曰兢兢業業不敢自逸曰誠一弗二
punctuated:
聖孝，所謂考三王而不謬，建天地而不悖者也。是書也，質諸皇祖祖訓之篇，正本以睦親，齊家以及天下之義，眞同條而共貫矣。至于冊天之文，恭上□□□□帝泰號，義取人情，道通神理，蓋重建極者也。是文也，質諸皇祖初定郊天之禮，欽崇昊天，並隆四祖，三陽開泰，敬率臣僚恭祀之文，眞異世而同符矣。
嘗御製《敬一箴》，有曰：「匪一弗純，匪敬弗聚。」卽皇祖之言曰：「兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」曰：「誠一弗二。」
translation_en:
…sagely filial piety—what is meant by being tested against the Three Kings without error and established before Heaven and Earth without contradiction. When this book is compared with the Imperial Ancestor’s Ancestral Injunctions, its principles of rectifying the foundation to bring harmony among kin, and ordering the family so as to extend that order throughout the realm, truly belong to the same branch and run along a common thread. As for the text conferring a title upon Heaven [?], reverently presenting the exalted title “□□□□ Sovereign” [?], its meaning accords with human feelings and its Way accords with divine principles; it thus gives weight to establishing the supreme standard. Compared with the Imperial Ancestor’s text from when he first established the suburban sacrificial rites to Heaven—reverently exalting Vast Heaven, jointly honoring the Four Ancestors, and respectfully leading his officials in solemn sacrifice as the three yang forces ushered in prosperity—this text truly accords with it, though composed in a different age.
His Majesty once composed the Admonition on Reverence and Oneness, which says: “Without oneness, there is no purity; without reverence, there is no concentration.” This is precisely what the Imperial Ancestor expressed when he said, “Vigilant and apprehensive, I dare not indulge in ease,” and, “Sincere and single-minded, without wavering”…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
對越在天之義也心箴有註則揭要於克
正之一言四箴有註則歸重於辨賢否審
聽納善號令合道理之數語而皆究極於
此心卽
皇祖之言曰人心虛靈乘氣機出入操而存之
爲難之指也又如欽
天記頌之製答
□徵于於穆所以明祗受之誠也
□飛□□
===
□□□□水
□之求也其他
制禮作樂
宏綱大要浩博如天地流行如江河要皆學
術文章之昭著與
皇祖之學術文章同一煥乎炳蔚而爲太平有
道之長其在
今日則尤巍巍蕩蕩不可名言矣雖然文章
之美本於學術之正而學術文章又必本
punctuated: 對越在天之義也。《心箴》有註，則揭要於克正之一言；《四箴》有註，則歸重於辨賢否、審聽納、善號令、合道理之數語，而皆究極於此心。卽皇祖之言曰：「人心虛靈，乘氣機出入，操而存之爲難。」之指也。又如《欽天記頌》之製，答□徵于於穆，所以明祗受之誠也。□飛□□□□□□水□之求也。其他制禮作樂，宏綱大要，浩博如天地，流行如江河，要皆學術文章之昭著，與皇祖之學術文章同一煥乎炳蔚，而爲太平有道之長。其在今日，則尤巍巍蕩蕩，不可名言矣。雖然，文章之美本於學術之正，而學術文章又必本
translation_en:
…the meaning of reverently facing Heaven above. In the commentary on the Admonition on the Mind (Xin zhen), the essential point is brought out in the single expression “being able to rectify”; in the commentary on the Four Admonitions (Si zhen), emphasis falls on the phrases “distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy,” “exercising discernment in hearing and accepting counsel,” “making commands good,” and “conforming to moral principle.” All ultimately trace back to this mind. This is precisely the purport of the Imperial Ancestor’s words: “The human mind is empty and numinous; it comes and goes with the workings of vital energy. To hold fast to it and preserve it is difficult.” Further, in the imperial composition Record and Eulogy of Revering Heaven (Qintian ji song) [?], the passage concerning a response … and evidence in the profound mystery [?] makes manifest the sincerity with which Heaven’s gifts are reverently received. …flying … water … seeking [?].

As for the other works concerning the establishment of rites and the making of music, their broad outlines and essential principles are as vast as Heaven and Earth and flow like rivers. In essence, all are manifest expressions of learning and literary accomplishment. Together with the learning and literary accomplishment of the Imperial Ancestor, they shine with the same splendid brilliance and stand foremost in an age of Great Peace governed according to the Way. In the present day, they are especially lofty and expansive, beyond what words can describe. Nevertheless, the beauty of literary composition is rooted in the correctness of learning, and learning and literary accomplishment must in turn be rooted in…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
於道德我
皇祖曁我
皇上道德之隆與
天地並是以蘊之爲學術則道統相傳之緒
帝王之聖學也發之爲文章則日星山河之麗
天地之至文也敷之爲治道則兼五帝軼
三王雍熙泰和之至治也
皇明億萬載無疆之休端在是矣愚生莫罄揄
揚何
===
第二問
周希正
同考試官教諭馬批百家專門之學諸儒合一之見此
策備之可與論經矣
考試官教諭林批士以明經致用經疑一策所決□
盡觀子之蘊足以知所用
考試官教授詹批經學疑義辯析無遺誠淹貫明經
之士可到是宜録出
punctuated:
於道德。我皇祖曁我皇上道德之隆，與天地並。是以蘊之爲學術，則道統相傳之緒，帝王之聖學也；發之爲文章，則日星山河之麗，天地之至文也；敷之爲治道，則兼五帝、軼三王，雍熙泰和之至治也。皇明億萬載無疆之休，端在是矣。愚生莫罄揄揚，何

第二問

周希正

同考試官教諭馬批：「百家專門之學，諸儒合一之見，此策備之，可與論經矣。」

考試官教諭林批：「士以明經致用，經疑一策，所決□盡。觀子之蘊，足以知所用。」

考試官教授詹批：「經學疑義，辯析無遺，誠淹貫明經之士可到是，宜録出。」
translation_en:
…upon moral virtue. The greatness of the moral virtue of our imperial ancestor and our reigning Emperor equals Heaven and Earth. Thus, embodied in learning, it is the thread transmitting the succession of the Way—the sagely learning of emperors and kings. Expressed in literary composition, it is the splendor of sun and stars, mountains and rivers—the supreme patterned expression of Heaven and Earth. Extended into governance, it combines the achievements of the Five Emperors and surpasses the Three Kings: consummate government marked by concord, prosperity, and supreme harmony. Here indeed lies the foundation of the august Ming’s boundless blessings for countless millions of years. This humble student cannot exhaust its praises; how…

Second Question

Zhou Xizheng

Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: “The specialized learning of the hundred schools and the unified understanding of the Confucian scholars are both fully present in this policy essay. Its author is someone with whom one may discuss the Classics.”

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “A scholar brings his understanding of the Classics to practical use. This policy essay on disputed points in the Classics resolves them [completely?]. Observing the learning you possess is sufficient to discern how you will put it to use.”

Examiner Zhan, Professor, comments: “Doubtful meanings in the study of the Classics are analyzed and distinguished without omission. Truly, a scholar of extensive and comprehensive learning who understands the Classics can attain this level [?]. This essay should be selected for inclusion in the record.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖人之作經以明道也學者之窮經以會
道也道載於經經不作道幾乎息矣道不
會經不可傳矣訓詁者失之鑿擬經者失
之僭支離附會將以明之適以晦之將以
擬之適以叛之可乎知此則可以究經學
之微而辩諸儒之得失矣且夫六經之作
聖人所以洩天地之秘而敎萬世無窮也
是經雖不同而其爲明道則一而已蓋嘗
求之□□□數以存理也數無定體故
===
夏商□□□不變爲占周取九六以變
爲占取數於變者以其有變易之義也乃
若卦之别於上下經者則以卦可反觀而
無反者八上經反卦二十四止爲十二而
不反者六固十八卦也下經反卦三十二
止爲十六而不反者二亦十八卦也故曰
以反觀之皆十八卦聖人之旨深哉書之
道紀帝王爲治之迹也秦誓費誓並傳者
何費之誓師得甘誓牧誓之遺意秦之悔
punctuated:
聖人之作經，以明道也；學者之窮經，以會道也。道載於經，經不作，道幾乎息矣；道不會，經不可傳矣。訓詁者失之鑿，擬經者失之僭。支離附會，將以明之，適以晦之；將以擬之，適以叛之，可乎？知此，則可以究經學之微，而辩諸儒之得失矣。且夫六經之作，聖人所以洩天地之秘，而敎萬世無窮也。是經雖不同，而其爲明道則一而已。蓋嘗求之，□□□數以存理也。數無定體，故夏商□□□不變爲占，周取九六以變爲占。取數於變者，以其有變易之義也。乃若卦之别於上下經者，則以卦可反觀，而無反者八。上經反卦二十四，止爲十二，而不反者六，固十八卦也；下經反卦三十二，止爲十六，而不反者二，亦十八卦也。故曰：「以反觀之，皆十八卦。」聖人之旨深哉！

書之道，紀帝王爲治之迹也。《秦誓》《費誓》並傳者，何？費之誓師，得《甘誓》《牧誓》之遺意；秦之悔
translation_en:
The sages composed the classics to illuminate the Way; scholars exhaustively study the classics to comprehend the Way. The Way is embodied in the classics: had the classics not been composed, the Way would almost have perished; unless the Way is comprehended, the classics cannot be transmitted. Those who explain words and phrases err through forced interpretations; those who imitate the classics err through presumption. With fragmented interpretations and strained connections, they intend to illuminate them but instead obscure them; they intend to emulate them but instead depart from them. Can this be acceptable? Understanding this, one can investigate the subtleties of classical learning and distinguish the successes and failures of the various scholars. The sages composed the Six Classics to disclose the mysteries of Heaven and Earth and teach all generations without end. Although these classics differ, they are one in their purpose of illuminating the Way. I have sought to investigate this: [three illegible characters] numbers preserve principle [?]. Numbers have no fixed form. Thus, under the Xia and Shang, [three illegible characters] the unchanging was used for divination [?], while the Zhou employed nines and sixes, using change for divination. They took their numbers from change because these embody the meaning of transformation.

As for the division of the hexagrams between the upper and lower sections of the Classic of Changes, hexagrams can be viewed inverted, but eight do not change when inverted. In the upper section, the twenty-four invertible hexagrams amount to only twelve pairs; together with the six that do not change upon inversion, they indeed make eighteen. In the lower section, the thirty-two invertible hexagrams amount to only sixteen pairs; together with the two that do not change upon inversion, they likewise make eighteen. Thus it is said: “Viewed in terms of inversion, each section has eighteen hexagrams.” How profound was the sages’ intent!

The purport of the Book of Documents is to record the deeds of emperors and kings in governing. Why have both the “Oath of Qin” and the “Oath at Bi” been transmitted? The address to the troops at Bi preserves the intent of the “Oath at Gan” and the “Oath at Mu”; as for Qin’s remorse …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
過有改過不吝之餘風亦可訓矣乃若古
今文之辨則自秦火既烈孔壁所藏安國
所傳者二十五篇謂之古文即蝌蚪書也
伏生所授鼂錯所傳者二十九篇謂之今
文即漢隸書也然今文多艱澁古文反平
易學者可無辨與詩以志民風昭國政三
百篇而始關雎王化之本也漢儒四始之
說則以關雎之治家爲國風始鹿鳴之治
□□□文王之述先德爲大雅始清
廟之爲三頌始義各有攸當也若
春秋之作定褒貶示勸懲夫子假魯史以
寓王法也程子謂其大義數十炳如日星
非以尊君而卑臣貴王而賤覇内中國而
外夷狄之類乎至於微詞奥義各適乎時
措之宜者未易窺測故曰史外傳心要典
也禮記一書定於孔聖成於七十子之徒
示天下以恭儉莊敬之道也曲禮名義言
禮之委曲纖悉耳彼謂作於曲臺者其妄
punctuated: 過，有改過不吝之餘風，亦可訓矣。乃若古今文之辨，則自秦火既烈，孔壁所藏、安國所傳者二十五篇，謂之古文，即蝌蚪書也；伏生所授、鼂錯所傳者二十九篇，謂之今文，即漢隸書也。然今文多艱澁，古文反平易，學者可無辨與？詩以志民風，昭國政，三百篇而始關雎，王化之本也。漢儒四始之說，則以關雎之治家爲國風始，鹿鳴之治□□□，文王之述先德爲大雅始，清廟之爲三頌始，義各有攸當也。若春秋之作，定褒貶，示勸懲，夫子假魯史以寓王法也。程子謂其大義數十，炳如日星，非以尊君而卑臣、貴王而賤覇、内中國而外夷狄之類乎？至於微詞奥義，各適乎時措之宜者，未易窺測，故曰史外傳心要典也。禮記一書，定於孔聖，成於七十子之徒，示天下以恭儉莊敬之道也。曲禮名義，言禮之委曲纖悉耳。彼謂作於曲臺者，其妄
translation_en:
…faults preserves something of the spirit of correcting errors without reluctance; it too can serve as instruction. As for the distinction between the Old Text and New Text versions, after the destructive fires of Qin, the twenty-five chapters concealed in the wall of Confucius’s residence and transmitted by Kong Anguo were called the Old Text, written in tadpole script. The twenty-nine chapters taught by Fu Sheng and transmitted by Chao Cuo were called the New Text, written in Han clerical script. Yet the New Text is often difficult and obscure, while the Old Text is, on the contrary, plain and accessible. Can scholars dispense with examining this distinction?

The Book of Poetry records the customs of the people and makes manifest the governance of the states. Its three hundred poems begin with “The Ospreys” (Guanju), the foundation of kingly moral transformation. According to the Han scholars’ account of the “four beginnings,” “The Ospreys,” concerning the ordering of the family, begins the Airs of the States; “The Deer Cry” (Luming), concerning governance [three illegible characters; ?]; “King Wen” (Wenwang), recounting ancestral virtue, begins the Greater Odes; and “The Pure Temple” (Qingmiao) begins the three groups of Hymns. Each has its appropriate significance.

As for the composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals, it establishes praise and blame and sets forth encouragement and admonition: the Master used the historical records of Lu to embody the laws of true kingship. Master Cheng said that its several dozen major principles shine as brightly as the sun and stars. Are these not such principles as honoring rulers and subordinating ministers, esteeming true kings and disparaging hegemons, and treating the central states as insiders and the Yi and Di peoples as outsiders? As for its subtle wording and profound meanings, each suited to what was appropriate to enact at the particular time, these are not readily fathomed. Hence it is called an essential canon that transmits the sage’s mind beyond the historical record.

The Book of Rites was settled by the sage Confucius and completed by the followers of his seventy disciples, showing all under Heaven the way of humility, frugality, solemnity, and reverence. The meaning of the title “Detailed Rites” (Quli) refers simply to the intricate particulars of ritual. As for those who say that it was composed at the Qu Terrace, their absurdity…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
誕不經之甚與緇衣之語意倣魯論而作
也然不免援引拘泥其漢儒附會之失與
吕不韋脩月令似也然紀時政而雜災異
嫌於巫史之流而王者四時異居服色悉
依方位則陰陽拘忌之說耳漢博士錄王
制似也然敘爵位而竊軻書不過因襲之
見而官制倣左氏之舊巡狩雜公穀之文
亦影響糟粕之粗耳惡足以知禮經者哉
□□□□紛紛究心經學而六經之
□益□□孟氏雜陰陽災異之說梁丘
本京房數學之流淺之乎言易矣若楊子
雲之太玄司馬光之潛虛則求之愈深而
失之愈遠優劣奚足較耶夏侯講明洪範
徒為希世取寵之資歐陽八世傳書未明
貨寶無總之義其言書可知矣若白居易
之湯征河內女子之泰誓則僭竊之甚而
繆妄之尤正否奚足言耶漢平帝立四家
詩固以申公轅固韓嬰毛公為宗也然申
punctuated:
誕不經之甚與！《緇衣》之語，意倣《魯論》而作也，然不免援引拘泥，其漢儒附會之失與！吕不韋脩《月令》，似也，然紀時政而雜災異，嫌於巫史之流；而王者四時異居，服色悉依方位，則陰陽拘忌之說耳。漢博士錄《王制》，似也，然敘爵位而竊軻書，不過因襲之見；而官制倣左氏之舊，巡狩雜公穀之文，亦影響糟粕之粗耳，惡足以知禮經者哉！
□□□□紛紛究心經學，而六經之□益□□。孟氏雜陰陽災異之說，梁丘本京房數學之流，淺之乎言《易》矣！若楊子雲之《太玄》、司馬光之《潛虛》，則求之愈深而失之愈遠，優劣奚足較耶？夏侯講明《洪範》，徒為希世取寵之資；歐陽八世傳《書》，未明「貨寶無總」之義，其言《書》可知矣。若白居易之「湯征河內」、女子之《泰誓》，則僭竊之甚而繆妄之尤，正否奚足言耶？漢平帝立四家《詩》，固以申公、轅固、韓嬰、毛公為宗也，然申
translation_en:
…absurd and utterly contrary to the canons! The language of “Black Robes” was apparently composed in imitation of the Lu version of the Analects. Yet its citations inevitably become forced and inflexible: is this not the error of strained interpretation committed by Han Confucians? The claim that Lü Buwei compiled the “Monthly Ordinances” seems plausible. Yet it records seasonal government measures interspersed with disasters and anomalies, suggesting the work of shamans and scribes. Its prescriptions that the king occupy different residences in the four seasons and that the colors of his clothing conform entirely to the cardinal directions are merely doctrines of restrictive yin–yang taboos. The claim that Han Erudites recorded the “Royal Regulations” likewise seems plausible. Yet its account of noble ranks borrows surreptitiously from the book of Meng Ke and offers no more than inherited views. Its official organization imitates old arrangements in the Zuo Commentary, while its accounts of royal inspection tours mingle passages from the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries. These, too, are merely crude echoes and dregs. How could such writings suffice for understanding the classic of ritual?
[Four illegible characters] busily devoted themselves to classical learning, yet the Six Classics’ [illegible] increasingly [two illegible characters; sense uncertain]. Master Meng mixed in doctrines of yin and yang, disasters, and anomalies; Liangqiu drew on the current of numerological learning associated with Jing Fang [?]. How shallow their discussions of the Changes were! As for Yang Ziyun’s Supreme Mystery and Sima Guang’s Fathoming the Hidden, the deeper their inquiries, the further they strayed. What point is there in comparing their relative merits? Xiahou’s exposition of the “Great Plan” served merely as a means of courting contemporary approval and obtaining favor. The Ouyang lineage transmitted the Documents for eight generations without understanding the meaning of “Do not accumulate wealth and treasures.” The quality of their discussions of the Documents can thus be judged. As for Bai Juyi’s “Tang campaigned in Henei” and the woman’s “Great Declaration” [?], these are the most egregious instances of presumptuous appropriation and the worst of erroneous fabrications. What point is there in discussing whether they are correct? Emperor Ping of the Han established the four schools of the Odes, taking Shen Gong, Yuan Gu, Han Ying, and Mao Gong as their founding authorities. Yet Shen …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
轅韓皆章句陋儒而毛特優於三子云爾
故曰齊魯毛韓詩之末也彼馬融鄭康成
衛宏孔穎達輩雖有功毛詩寧無媿於先
聖與春秋三傳固左丘明公羊穀梁互相
牴牾也然左氏浮誇公穀誣謬蓋胥失之
故曰三傳作而春秋散也彼范甯作集解
戴宏作解疑雖無媿公穀抑何補於聖經
乎后蒼得高堂生十七篇之傳乃倡明禮
□□戴□□同師后蒼其氏分門王通
===
鄭康成俱□□戴同經異說南北派凡數
十家熊安其表表者且不免背本經而援
外義他何足言哉是皆摹擬其近似補綴
其緒餘詳於訓詁而略於大義工於考索
而昧於會通以言乎知道則未也昔人有
言秦人焚書而書存漢儒窮經而經絕其
深有感矣故曰明之者晦之擬之者叛之
也然則經終不可明乎待其人焉爾有宋
奎聚大儒迭興得群聖心學之傳發六經
punctuated:
轅、韓皆章句陋儒，而毛特優於三子云爾。故曰：「齊、魯、毛、韓，詩之末也。」彼馬融、鄭康成、衛宏、孔穎達輩，雖有功毛詩，寧無媿於先聖與？春秋三傳，固左丘明、公羊、穀梁互相牴牾也。然左氏浮誇，公、穀誣謬，蓋胥失之。故曰：「三傳作而春秋散也。」彼范甯作集解，戴宏作解疑，雖無媿公、穀，抑何補於聖經乎？后蒼得高堂生十七篇之傳，乃倡明禮。□□戴□□同師后蒼，其氏分門。王通、鄭康成俱□□戴，同經異說，南北派凡數十家。熊安其表表者，且不免背本經而援外義，他何足言哉？是皆摹擬其近似，補綴其緒餘，詳於訓詁而略於大義，工於考索而昧於會通。以言乎知道，則未也。昔人有言：「秦人焚書而書存，漢儒窮經而經絕。」其深有感矣。故曰：「明之者晦之，擬之者叛之也。」

然則經終不可明乎？待其人焉爾。有宋奎聚，大儒迭興，得群聖心學之傳，發六經
translation_en:
…Yuan and Han were all narrow-minded scholars of textual divisions and phrases; Mao was merely superior to the other three. Hence the saying: “The Qi, Lu, Mao, and Han traditions represent the decline of the Poetry.” Although Ma Rong, Zheng Kangcheng, Wei Hong, Kong Yingda, and their like contributed to the Mao tradition of the Poetry, could they have faced the former sages without shame? The Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals—those of Zuo Qiuming, Gongyang, and Guliang—certainly contradict one another. Yet Zuo is extravagant, while Gongyang and Guliang are misleading and erroneous: all miss the mark. Hence the saying: “When the Three Commentaries arose, the Spring and Autumn Annals became fragmented.” Fan Ning compiled the Collected Explanations, and Dai Hong wrote the Resolution of Doubts. Though they need feel no shame before Gongyang and Guliang, what did they contribute to the Sage’s Classic? Hou Cang received the transmission of Gaotang Sheng’s seventeen chapters and then promoted the elucidation of ritual. [Illegible text] Dai [illegible text] studied under Hou Cang together, and their lineages divided into separate schools [?]. Wang Tong and Zheng Kangcheng both [illegible text] Dai [?]; interpretations of the same classic diverged, and the northern and southern branches numbered several dozen schools in all. Even Xiong An [?], an outstanding figure among them, could not avoid departing from the original classic and drawing on meanings from outside it. What need is there to speak of the others? All these men imitated superficial resemblances and patched together remnants. They were meticulous about glosses but cursory about the larger meaning, skilled in textual investigation but ignorant of comprehensive understanding. As for knowing the Way, they had not attained it. Someone of old said: “The men of Qin burned the books, yet the books survived; the scholars of Han exhaustively studied the classics, yet the classics’ transmission was severed.” These words express a deeply felt concern. Hence the saying: “Those who elucidate it obscure it; those who imitate it betray it.”

Does this mean, then, that the classics can never be elucidated? They need only await the right men. Under the Song, the stars of Kui gathered, heralding literary flourishing, and great scholars arose in succession. They received the transmission of the learning of the mind from the many sages and brought to light the Six Classics’…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
未發之蘊程朱之於易蔡仲默之於書朱
元晦之於詩禮胡安國之於春秋咸有以
詣其極而朱子則集其大成者也故易書
詩春秋諸傳爲聖經羽翼而儀禮經傳通
解實於禮經大有發明所謂昭如日星學
者由是以求聖人之道六經在吾心矣其
於經學復奚疑
第三問
張翀
===
同考試□訓聞批書生談大節歷歷可數必有志之士錄之
同考試官教諭江批尚論古人忠孝節義皆能識其大
而言有折衷非習於口耳者可以觀志矣
考試官教諭林批議論正而品題當非徒取其文也
考試官教授詹批論先哲歸諸聖賢是以全德自期者
士之生于天地間固貴乎有以自立尤貴
乎有以適道何者天下之勢常變無形事
幾之來緩急亦異毁則蔑義者謂之失已
太過不及者謂之失中二者雖有間矣以
punctuated:
未發之蘊。程朱之於《易》，蔡仲默之於《書》，朱元晦之於《詩》《禮》，胡安國之於《春秋》，咸有以詣其極，而朱子則集其大成者也。故《易》《書》《詩》《春秋》諸傳爲聖經羽翼，而《儀禮經傳通解》實於禮經大有發明，所謂昭如日星。學者由是以求聖人之道，六經在吾心矣，其於經學復奚疑？

第三問
張翀

同考試□訓聞批：書生談大節，歷歷可數，必有志之士，錄之。
同考試官教諭江批：尚論古人忠孝節義，皆能識其大，而言有折衷，非習於口耳者，可以觀志矣。
考試官教諭林批：議論正而品題當，非徒取其文也。
考試官教授詹批：論先哲，歸諸聖賢，是以全德自期者。

士之生于天地間，固貴乎有以自立，尤貴乎有以適道。何者？天下之勢，常變無形；事幾之來，緩急亦異。毁則蔑義者，謂之失已；太過不及者，謂之失中。二者雖有間矣，以
translation_en:
…the profundities that had not previously been revealed. Cheng and Zhu, in their treatment of the Book of Changes; Cai Zhongmo, of the Book of Documents; Zhu Yuanhui, of the Book of Odes and the rites; and Hu Anguo, of the Spring and Autumn Annals—all attained the utmost depths of their subjects. Master Zhu, however, brought their achievements together in a great synthesis. Thus the commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Odes, and Spring and Autumn Annals serve as wings to the sages’ classics, while the Comprehensive Interpretation of the Classic and Commentaries of the Ceremonies and Rites truly casts much light upon the ritual classic. This is what is meant by being as clear as the sun and stars. If students follow these works in seeking the Way of the sages, the Six Classics will reside within their own minds. What further doubts could they have about classical learning?

Third Question
Zhang Chong

Comment by the Associate Examiner [title and name unclear: □訓聞]: This scholar discusses great matters of moral integrity, setting them out distinctly, one by one. He must be a man of resolve. Accept his essay.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: In assessing the loyalty, filial piety, integrity, and righteousness of the ancients, he consistently recognizes what is essential, and his judgments are balanced. His learning is not merely passed from ear to mouth; his aspirations can be discerned here.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: His arguments are sound and his assessments apt. It is not merely for its literary qualities that we select this essay.

Comment by Examiner Zhan, Professor: In discussing earlier worthies, he takes the sages and worthies as his ultimate standard. He is someone who aspires to complete virtue.

For a scholar born between Heaven and Earth, it is certainly important to have the means to establish his moral independence; still more important is the means to accord with the Way. Why is this? Circumstances in the world constantly change and have no fixed form; the critical junctures that arise in affairs likewise differ in urgency. Those who destroy standards and scorn righteousness are said to lose themselves [?]; those who go too far or fall short are said to lose the proper mean. Although there is a distinction between these two, in terms of …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
言乎適道則未也君子知此而求諸巳方
其無事之際涵養於內者必有不可易之
見以定其守及其事變之遇振作於外者
必有不可奪之氣以鼓其趨夫然後心與
道會道與天會行成而名立心安而德全
矣且夫蘇武之使匈奴猶洪皓之使金也
北海嚙雪之苦無異於陰山瘴海之憂雖
其厚功薄賞與夫坐貶殊方均難以病其
忠要之□□□九年之久者其氣猶烈也
===
李密之陳□歸養猶朱壽昌之棄官尋母
也形影之相弔無異於年久之不知一則
困終餘年之是慮一則不省所恃之爲憂
要皆不失其爲孝獨於少事偽朝之云不
無遺憾也金一也楊震畏四知而不受管
寧見攫金而不顧有所畏於心者終不若
不動於心者之爲優然關西孔子之語子
孫清白之遺而名動一時震亦未可厚非
焉惠一也晏嬰之待火千家范仲淹之給
punctuated:
言乎適道，則未也。君子知此而求諸巳，方其無事之際，涵養於內者，必有不可易之見以定其守；及其事變之遇，振作於外者，必有不可奪之氣以鼓其趨。夫然後心與道會，道與天會，行成而名立，心安而德全矣。且夫蘇武之使匈奴，猶洪皓之使金也。北海嚙雪之苦，無異於陰山瘴海之憂。雖其厚功薄賞，與夫坐貶殊方，均難以病其忠。要之，□□□九年之久者，其氣猶烈也。
李密之陳□歸養，猶朱壽昌之棄官尋母也。形影之相弔，無異於年久之不知。一則困終餘年之是慮，一則不省所恃之爲憂，要皆不失其爲孝。獨於少事偽朝之云，不無遺憾也。金一也，楊震畏四知而不受，管寧見攫金而不顧。有所畏於心者，終不若不動於心者之爲優。然關西孔子之語，子孫清白之遺，而名動一時，震亦未可厚非焉。惠一也，晏嬰之待火千家，范仲淹之給
translation_en:
…as for according with the Way, however, they have yet to do so. The gentleman understands this and seeks within himself. In times free from affairs, his inward cultivation must establish an unalterable conviction that steadies what he upholds; when he encounters changing circumstances, his outward exertions must display an indomitable spirit that spurs his advance. Only then does his heart accord with the Way, and the Way with Heaven; his conduct is perfected and his reputation established, his heart is at peace and his virtue complete. Su Wu’s mission to the Xiongnu was like Hong Hao’s mission to the Jin. The hardship of chewing snow at the Northern Sea was no different from the distress of the Yin Mountains and the pestilential seas. Whether great service received scant reward, or a man was condemned to demotion in a distant region, neither circumstance gives grounds to impugn his loyalty. In sum, even after □□□ nine years [?], his spirit remained ardent.
Li Mi’s presentation of a □ requesting to return home to care for his elder was like Zhu Shouchang’s abandonment of office to seek his mother. Having only one’s body and shadow to console each other was no different from not knowing a parent’s whereabouts for many years. One worried about hardship through the remaining years of life [?]; the other grieved at not knowing where his mother was. Both, in essence, remained filial. Yet the statement that Li Mi had served an illegitimate dynasty in his youth leaves some cause for regret. Gold was the same in both cases: Yang Zhen feared the “four who knew” and would not accept it, while Guan Ning saw someone snatch up gold and paid no heed. A heart restrained by fear is ultimately inferior to a heart that remains unmoved. Yet Yang Zhen was called the “Confucius west of the passes,” and left his descendants a legacy of unstained integrity; his fame stirred his age. Nor, therefore, should he be severely censured. Benevolence likewise was the same in both cases: Yan Ying’s assistance to a thousand households afflicted by fire [?], and Fan Zhongyan’s provision of …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
族千畝假仁假義者終不若先憂後樂者
之爲愈然狐裘三十年豚肩不掩豆而以
其君顯嬰亦未可過議焉忠而不能孝者
温嶠之絶裾非也其灑泣登舟以急君而
討峻之功遂成王事多難不遑將毋賢於
王導遠矣此忠義慷慨風節表著所以稱
爲晉室之名臣焉孝而不能忠者李陵之
辱身罪也雖矢窮力竭以就降而國士之
風安在哉□心志敗名失節愧於子卿多
===
矣即别詩□戀情未忘漢亦何以贖前日
之咎哉韓愈羨二鳥之榮三上書以干進
用夫固戚戚之窮者而佛骨一表名高千
古君子取其節焉况文起八代之衰道濟
天下之溺如愈可多得哉此蘇軾所以謂
其浩然而獨存者也魏相痛霍氏之横因
許廣漢以行其說夫固比匪之傷者而輔
政同心名垂史冊君子取其義焉况諫伐
匈奴一疏條漢便宜數事如相可深讓哉
punctuated:
族千畝，假仁假義者終不若先憂後樂者之爲愈。然狐裘三十年，豚肩不掩豆，而以其君顯，嬰亦未可過議焉。
忠而不能孝者，温嶠之絶裾非也。其灑泣登舟，以急君而討峻之功遂成。王事多難，不遑將毋，賢於王導遠矣。此忠義慷慨，風節表著，所以稱爲晉室之名臣焉。
孝而不能忠者，李陵之辱身罪也。雖矢窮力竭以就降，而國士之風安在哉？□心志，敗名失節，愧於子卿多矣。即别詩□戀，情未忘漢，亦何以贖前日之咎哉？
韓愈羨二鳥之榮，三上書以干進用，夫固戚戚之窮者，而佛骨一表，名高千古，君子取其節焉。况文起八代之衰，道濟天下之溺，如愈可多得哉？此蘇軾所以謂其浩然而獨存者也。
魏相痛霍氏之横，因許廣漢以行其說，夫固比匪之傷者，而輔政同心，名垂史冊，君子取其義焉。况諫伐匈奴一疏，條漢便宜數事，如相可深讓哉？
translation_en:
…a thousand mu of land for his clan. Those whose benevolence and righteousness are merely assumed are ultimately inferior to one who worries before others and takes his pleasure after them. Yet Yan Ying wore the same fox-fur robe for thirty years, and the pork shoulder served at his table did not cover the offering dish; through him his ruler attained distinction. Ying, too, should not be criticized excessively.
As for being loyal but unable to fulfill filial duty, Wen Jiao was wrong to cut off the hem of his robe to leave his mother. Yet he boarded the boat weeping, hastened to his ruler’s aid, and ultimately succeeded in the campaign against Su Jun. With royal affairs beset by difficulties, he had no leisure to tend his mother [?]. He was far worthier than Wang Dao. His ardent loyalty and righteousness, and his conspicuous integrity, explain why he is acclaimed as an eminent minister of the Jin ruling house.
As for being filial but unable to remain loyal, Li Ling was culpable for disgracing himself. Though he surrendered only after his arrows were exhausted and his strength spent, where was the bearing of an outstanding servant of the state? His resolve [?], his ruined reputation, and his lost integrity left him much to be ashamed of beside Ziqing. Even if his farewell poems expressed attachment [?] and his feelings for the Han remained, how could this redeem his earlier fault?
Han Yu envied the honors enjoyed by the two birds and submitted three letters seeking advancement and employment. He was indeed one who fretted in adversity. Yet a single memorial on the Buddha’s bone made his name illustrious for all ages; the gentleman esteems his integrity. Moreover, his writing revived literature after eight dynasties of decline, and his Way rescued the world from drowning. Could many men like Yu be found? This is why Su Shi said that his vast, unyielding spirit alone endured.
Wei Xiang deplored the Huo family’s arrogance and used Xu Guanghan to put his proposals into effect. He was indeed tainted by association with unworthy men. Yet he worked in harmony with his colleagues in assisting the government, and his name has been handed down in the histories; the gentleman esteems his righteousness. Moreover, in a single memorial remonstrating against an attack on the Xiongnu, he set out several measures beneficial to the Han. Could a man like Xiang be severely reproached?

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
此張栻所以惜其進之不能以正也張禹
之在漢庭望重師傅而災異之對陰黨王
氏槐里令朱雲所以欲請尚方之劔也禹
之邪佞可知或譏其不識剛正字者此爾
柳宗元之在柳州惠政流芳而王叔文母
死代表陳情豈固甘心於王伾輩之外黨
耶宗元之悖謬可見或譏其不識節義字
者此爾之數子者人品不同行事亦異千
載而下□□昭如是非得失固有不能遁
===
其情者夫粵西僻在嶺徼自有郡縣
以來風氣日開人文漸著如覃光佃之忠
言日進彈劾無避其爲臣忠矣而糓蠟召
兵卽募死士以入衞孤軍倍道敢抗金虜
而不辭李珙之忠又難於佃也丁蘭之刻
木祀母每事必稟其爲子孝矣而母喪廬
墓有甘露芝草之祥扁易亭名來蘇軾表
章之美梁詔之孝無愧於蘭也論劉季述
輩而謝病以歸官終侍讀若唐之趙觀文
punctuated:
此張栻所以惜其進之不能以正也。張禹之在漢庭，望重師傅，而災異之對，陰黨王氏，槐里令朱雲所以欲請尚方之劔也。禹之邪佞可知，或譏其不識剛正字者，此爾。柳宗元之在柳州，惠政流芳，而王叔文母死，代表陳情，豈固甘心於王伾輩之外黨耶？宗元之悖謬可見，或譏其不識節義字者，此爾。之數子者，人品不同，行事亦異。千載而下，□□昭如，是非得失，固有不能遁其情者。
夫粵西僻在嶺徼，自有郡縣以來，風氣日開，人文漸著。如覃光佃之忠言日進，彈劾無避，其爲臣忠矣。而糓蠟召兵，卽募死士以入衞，孤軍倍道，敢抗金虜而不辭，李珙之忠又難於佃也。丁蘭之刻木祀母，每事必稟，其爲子孝矣。而母喪廬墓，有甘露芝草之祥，扁易亭名，來蘇軾表章之美，梁詔之孝無愧於蘭也。論劉季述輩而謝病以歸，官終侍讀，若唐之趙觀文
translation_en:
This is why Zhang Shi regretted that his advancement had not been achieved by upright means. At the Han court, Zhang Yu enjoyed great prestige as the emperor’s tutor; yet in his response concerning calamities and anomalies, he secretly sided with the Wang clan. This was why Zhu Yun, Magistrate of Huaili, sought to request the sword of the Imperial Manufactories. Zhang Yu’s wickedness and sycophancy are evident. This explains why some mocked him as not knowing the meaning of “firmness and uprightness.” Liu Zongyuan left a lasting reputation for benevolent government in Liuzhou; yet when Wang Shuwen’s mother died, he composed a memorial on Wang’s behalf setting forth his feelings. Could he really have been content to belong to the outer faction of Wang Pi and his associates? Liu Zongyuan’s perversity and error are apparent. This explains why some mocked him as not knowing the meaning of “integrity and righteousness.” These men differed in character, and their actions also differed. A thousand years later, □□ remain clear [?]; in matters of right and wrong, success and failure, there are truths about them that cannot be concealed.
Now western Yue—that is, Guangxi—lies remotely on the frontier beyond the mountain ranges. Since commanderies and counties were first established there, its customs have daily become more enlightened, and its cultural accomplishments have gradually become conspicuous. Qin Guangdian, for instance, continually offered loyal counsel and spared no one in his impeachments: as a minister, he was loyal indeed. Yet when troops were summoned at Gula [?], Li Gong immediately recruited men prepared to die and brought them to defend the court. With an isolated force, he marched at twice the usual speed, daring to resist the Jin invaders without demur. Li Gong’s loyalty was thus displayed under circumstances still more difficult than Guangdian’s. Ding Lan carved a wooden image of his mother and made offerings to it, reporting every matter to her: as a son, he was filial indeed. Yet Liang Zhao, upon his mother’s death, dwelt in a hut beside her grave, and auspicious sweet dew and numinous mushrooms appeared. A pavilion’s name was changed on its inscribed plaque [?], eliciting Su Shi’s praise in celebration of his virtue. Liang Zhao’s filial devotion was worthy of comparison with Ding Lan’s. As for one who denounced Liu Jishu and his associates, then pleaded illness and returned home, ending his official career as Reader-in-waiting, there was Zhao Guanwen of the Tang …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也因李接攻城而奮兵與戰罵賊以斃者
宋之毛士毅也行不同而節同均之有可
取焉乞歸奉母不受錫賚而請蠲一郡丁
賦者後漢之梁嵩是已郡人立祠以報德
非其人情之感乎買妾憫父惻然遣還而
不索原受直金者有宋之馮商是已竟得
馮京以為嗣非其天道之報乎事不同而
義同均之為可嘉焉之數子者山川靈異
咸鍾其美□□行高潔均適乎道忠孝節義
===
信其無愧□古人矣是皆廣右前哲而其
他光明俊偉作於前者殆未易悉舉唯論
世尚友者能自師法云爾極而論之則前
數子者皆一行一事之美適于道者或寡
矣必如周公之忠然後可以為忠之至所
謂赤舄几几德音不瑕者是已必如大舜
之孝然後可以為孝之至所謂為法於天
下可傳於後世者是已必如泰伯之節與
夫夷齊之義然後可以為節義之至所謂
punctuated:
也。因李接攻城而奮兵與戰，罵賊以斃者，宋之毛士毅也。行不同而節同，均之有可取焉。乞歸奉母，不受錫賚，而請蠲一郡丁賦者，後漢之梁嵩是已。郡人立祠以報德，非其人情之感乎？買妾憫父，惻然遣還，而不索原受直金者，有宋之馮商是已。竟得馮京以為嗣，非其天道之報乎？事不同而義同，均之為可嘉焉。之數子者，山川靈異，咸鍾其美，□□行高潔，均適乎道。忠孝節義，信其無愧□古人矣。是皆廣右前哲，而其他光明俊偉作於前者，殆未易悉舉。唯論世尚友者，能自師法云爾。

極而論之，則前數子者，皆一行一事之美，適于道者或寡矣。必如周公之忠，然後可以為忠之至，所謂「赤舄几几，德音不瑕」者是已。必如大舜之孝，然後可以為孝之至，所謂「為法於天下，可傳於後世」者是已。必如泰伯之節，與夫夷齊之義，然後可以為節義之至，所謂
translation_en:
…was such a man. When Li Jie attacked the city, the man who roused his troops to fight him and died cursing the rebels was Mao Shiyi of the Song. Their conduct differed, but their integrity was the same; both had qualities worth emulating. The man who requested leave to return home to serve his mother, declined imperial gifts, and instead asked for remission of the poll tax throughout a commandery was Liang Song of the Later Han. The people of the commandery erected a shrine to repay his kindness: was this not an expression of their heartfelt gratitude? The man who bought a concubine, took pity on her father [?], and compassionately sent her back without demanding repayment of the original purchase price was Feng Shang of the Song. He eventually had Feng Jing as his heir: was this not Heaven’s recompense? Their deeds differed, but their righteousness was the same; both were worthy of praise. In these men, the numinous powers of the mountains and rivers concentrated all their excellence. [Two characters illegible] Their conduct was lofty and pure, and all accorded with the Way. In loyalty, filial piety, integrity, and righteousness, they were surely worthy of comparison with the ancients [one character illegible]. These were all earlier worthies of Guangyou. The other illustrious and outstanding men who arose in earlier times could scarcely all be enumerated. Only those who examine their age and befriend the ancients can take them as their own teachers and models.

Yet, considered in the fullest sense, each of the men just mentioned excelled in a single form of conduct or a single deed; the respects in which they accorded with the Way may have been few. Only loyalty like that of the Duke of Zhou can be called loyalty at its utmost. This is what is meant by: “Dignified in his red shoes; his virtuous reputation is without flaw.” Only filial piety like that of the great Shun can be called filial piety at its utmost. This is what is meant by: “Serving as a model for all under Heaven, worthy of transmission to later generations.” Only integrity like that of Taibo and righteousness like that of Boyi and Shuqi can be called integrity and righteousness at their utmost. This is what is meant by…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
無得而稱求仁而得仁者是已是數聖賢
者道全而德備體立而用行遇君則爲忠
遇親則爲孝遇事變之來則爲節爲義不
思不勉從容中道蓋易地而皆然者也顧
士之所自擇者當何如亦曰取法乎上而
已矣雖然人秉天地之正氣與元氣相爲
流通三代以前道德隆盛泰和之氣渾厚
未鑿是故後先相望無非忠孝節義之士
粹乎其□□也三代以後道衰德薄人漸
===
澆漓故□□忠孝節義者寥寥僅見可取
者少而可議者多亦其時勢然也於乎三
代以前之士吾不得而見得見如蘇武韓
愈范仲淹其人亦可矣蘇韓范三子吾不
得而見得見如丁蘭管寧楊震以下諸君
子亦可矣論人至此不能不重有所感云
第四問
鍾徠秀
考試官教諭林 批 條陳先正之賢補救今是意誠
punctuated:
「無得而稱」、「求仁而得仁」者是已。是數聖賢者，道全而德備，體立而用行，遇君則爲忠，遇親則爲孝，遇事變之來則爲節爲義，不思不勉，從容中道，蓋易地而皆然者也。顧士之所自擇者當何如？亦曰取法乎上而已矣。雖然，人秉天地之正氣，與元氣相爲流通。三代以前，道德隆盛，泰和之氣渾厚未鑿，是故後先相望，無非忠孝節義之士，粹乎其□□也。三代以後，道衰德薄，人漸澆漓，故□□忠孝節義者寥寥僅見，可取者少，而可議者多，亦其時勢然也。於乎！三代以前之士，吾不得而見，得見如蘇武、韓愈、范仲淹其人亦可矣。蘇、韓、范三子，吾不得而見，得見如丁蘭、管寧、楊震以下諸君子亦可矣。論人至此，不能不重有所感云。

第四問
鍾徠秀

考試官教諭林批：條陳先正之賢，補救今是，意誠
translation_en:
…These are precisely those of whom it was said, “No adequate praise could be found,” and “They sought benevolence and attained it.” In these sages and worthies, the Way was whole and virtue complete; its substance was established and its functions put into practice. In serving their rulers, they displayed loyalty; in serving their parents, filial devotion; in confronting changing circumstances, integrity and righteousness. Without deliberation or effort, they naturally accorded with the Way. Had they exchanged places, each would have acted likewise. What, then, should a scholar choose for himself? Simply to take the highest as his model.

Nevertheless, human beings receive the upright vital energy of Heaven and Earth, which circulates in mutual communion with primordial vital energy. In the Three Dynasties and earlier, the Way and virtue flourished, and the vital energy of supreme harmony was full, pure, and unspoiled. Thus, generation after generation, men were without exception devoted to loyalty, filial devotion, integrity, and righteousness—pure in their □□ [?]. After the Three Dynasties, the Way declined and virtue grew thin, while people gradually became shallow and insincere. Hence those who □□ [?] loyalty, filial devotion, integrity, and righteousness were scarcely to be found. Few deserved approval, and many invited criticism: this, too, resulted from the circumstances of their times.

Alas! I cannot meet the men of the Three Dynasties and earlier; it would suffice to meet men like Su Wu, Han Yu, and Fan Zhongyan. I cannot meet those three, Su, Han, and Fan; it would suffice to meet gentlemen such as Ding Lan, Guan Ning, Yang Zhen, and the others mentioned below them. Having carried this discussion of men so far, I cannot help feeling deeply moved once again.

Fourth Question
Zhong Laixiu

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: You set out in detail the worthiness of earlier exemplary men, seeking to remedy present conditions [?]; your intent is sincere…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
如予言地方仰頼録之
考試官教授詹批〔守令將帥在粤西尤急而貴於得人子能較量不爽區畫周悉其識時務者乎〕
善為治者能立天下之法而後天下之治
成善用法者能操天下之機而後天下之
法裕夫法立則可循機操則可久而古先
哲王所以長治久安凡有法以為聯屬人
心之具而通變不窮與時偕行則又視法
之所趨向而亟反而善調之非法則無所
依據將紛然而莫吾一非機以運之于中
吾見法敝而治亦隨之矣是可與語治哉
蓋嘗聞之書曰德惟善政政在養民言牧
民之良也詩曰文武吉甫萬邦為憲言將
兵之善也是故三代而上治出于一州牧
侯伯皆惟其人無事則為卿有事則為將
此所以愛植甘棠績歌采芑召公之德方
叔之休至今猶為美談自郡縣置而守令
設兵農分而將相不兼矣然亦未嘗借才
punctuated:
如予言，地方仰頼，録之。
考試官教授詹批〔守令將帥在粤西尤急，而貴於得人。子能較量不爽，區畫周悉，其識時務者乎！〕
善為治者能立天下之法，而後天下之治成；善用法者能操天下之機，而後天下之法裕。夫法立則可循，機操則可久。而古先哲王所以長治久安，凡有法以為聯屬人心之具，而通變不窮，與時偕行，則又視法之所趨向，而亟反而善調之。非法則無所依據，將紛然而莫吾一；非機以運之于中，吾見法敝而治亦隨之矣。是可與語治哉？
蓋嘗聞之，書曰：「德惟善政，政在養民。」言牧民之良也。詩曰：「文武吉甫，萬邦為憲。」言將兵之善也。是故三代而上，治出于一，州牧侯伯皆惟其人，無事則為卿，有事則為將。此所以愛植甘棠，績歌采芑，召公之德、方叔之休，至今猶為美談。自郡縣置而守令設，兵農分而將相不兼矣。然亦未嘗借才
translation_en:
…accords with what I have said. The locality may look to him for support. Include this answer.
Examiner Zhan, a Prefectural School Instructor, comments: 〔In western Guangxi, the need for prefects, magistrates, and military commanders is especially urgent; what matters is finding the right men. You weigh the issues accurately and plan thoroughly. Surely you understand the pressing affairs of the time!〕
Those skilled in governing can establish laws for all under Heaven; only then can orderly government be achieved throughout the realm. Those skilled in applying laws can grasp the pivotal circumstances of all under Heaven; only then can the realm’s laws operate with flexibility. Once laws are established, they can be followed; once the pivotal circumstances are grasped, government can endure. The sage kings of antiquity achieved lasting order and enduring peace by using laws as instruments to bind people’s hearts together. Yet to respond inexhaustibly to change and advance with the times, they also observed the direction in which the laws were tending, promptly reconsidering and skillfully adjusting them. Without laws, there would be nothing to rely upon: confusion would prevail, with nothing to bring us into unity. Without an understanding of circumstances to guide their operation from within, I foresee the decay of the laws, with government following them into decline. Could this be called an understanding of government?
I have heard it said in the Book of Documents: “Virtue consists in good government; government lies in nourishing the people.” This speaks of excellence in tending the people. The Book of Odes says: “Jifu, accomplished in civil and military affairs, is a model for the myriad states.” This speaks of excellence in commanding troops. Thus, in the Three Dynasties and earlier, government proceeded from a single source. Regional governors and territorial lords were all men suited to their positions: in peaceful times they served as ministers, and in times of trouble as generals. Hence affection found expression in preserving the sweet pear tree, and achievements were celebrated in “Gathering Millet.” The virtue of the Duke of Shao and the glory of Fang Shu remain subjects of praise to this day. Once commanderies and counties were established, prefects and magistrates were appointed; once soldiers and farmers became separate, the offices of general and chief minister were no longer held together. Yet there was never any need to borrow talent …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
於異代也以守令言之京師蒙福世祖所
以獎郭伋也願借一年河内所以留寇恂
也麥穗兩岐張堪所以守漁陽也化致三
異魯恭所以令中牟也宋均守九江虎爲
却走岑熈守魏郡犬不驚吠非有善政能
如是乎其視卓茂之力行敎化而民不忍
欺董宣之鋤擊豪強而人不敢犯賈敦實
之政尚清凈而民不見吏張允濟之治從
寬簡而路不拾遺治效淺深固較然矣以
===
將帥言之白起據函谷雄虎視於山東李
牧在鴈門絕胡騎於塞北三十餘年秦兵
不加廉頗之重趙也一人不戮江南自下
曹彬之取唐也非有勇略能如是乎其視
祭遵之取用儒術雅歌投壺羊祜之恩信
服人輕裘緩帶郭汾陽之威德素著單騎
見虜范文正之甲兵數萬西賊破膽事爲
優劣自可觀矣故嘗謂郭寇張堪宋岑能
吏也魯恭能而良者也卓董賈張其循良
punctuated:
於異代也。以守令言之，京師蒙福，世祖所以獎郭伋也；願借一年，河内所以留寇恂也；麥穗兩岐，張堪所以守漁陽也；化致三異，魯恭所以令中牟也。宋均守九江，虎爲却走；岑熈守魏郡，犬不驚吠。非有善政，能如是乎？其視卓茂之力行敎化而民不忍欺，董宣之鋤擊豪強而人不敢犯，賈敦實之政尚清凈而民不見吏，張允濟之治從寬簡而路不拾遺，治效淺深，固較然矣。
以將帥言之，白起據函谷，雄虎視於山東；李牧在鴈門，絕胡騎於塞北；三十餘年秦兵不加，廉頗之重趙也；一人不戮江南自下，曹彬之取唐也。非有勇略，能如是乎？其視祭遵之取用儒術，雅歌投壺；羊祜之恩信服人，輕裘緩帶；郭汾陽之威德素著，單騎見虜；范文正之甲兵數萬，西賊破膽，事爲優劣，自可觀矣。故嘗謂郭、寇、張堪、宋、岑，能吏也；魯恭，能而良者也；卓、董、賈、張，其循良
translation_en:
…from other ages. To speak of prefects and magistrates: “The capital enjoys blessings”—this was how Emperor Shizu commended Guo Ji. “We wish to borrow him for another year”—this was how the people of Henei sought to retain Kou Xun. Wheat ears grew with two branches under Zhang Kan’s administration of Yuyang; moral transformation brought about three extraordinary phenomena under Lu Gong’s administration of Zhongmou. When Song Jun governed Jiujiang, tigers withdrew; when Cen Xi governed Wei Commandery, dogs did not bark in alarm. Could such things have happened without good government? Yet compare these men with Zhuo Mao, who vigorously promoted moral instruction so that the people could not bear to deceive him; Dong Xuan, who rooted out and struck down powerful bullies so that people dared not transgress; Jia Dunshi, whose government prized tranquility and freedom from interference, so that the people scarcely saw officials; and Zhang Yunji, whose administration favored leniency and simplicity, so that no one took articles others had lost on the roads. The relative depth of their achievements in government is surely evident.
As for generals: Bai Qi held Hangu Pass and gazed like a mighty tiger upon the lands east of the mountains; Li Mu was stationed at Yanmen and kept Hu cavalry out of the northern frontier. For more than thirty years Qin’s troops did not attack: such was the strength Lian Po lent Zhao. Without a single person being put to death, Jiangnan submitted of its own accord: such was Cao Bin’s conquest of Tang. Could such things have happened without courage and strategic ability? Yet compare these men with Ji Zun, who employed Confucian methods, sang refined songs, and played pitch-pot; Yang Hu, whose kindness and trustworthiness won people’s allegiance, and who wore a light fur robe with his sash loosely tied; Guo, Prince of Fenyang, whose prestige and virtue were long established, and who rode alone to meet the enemy; and Fan Wenzheng, whose tens of thousands of armored troops struck terror into the western foes. The relative merits of their deeds can readily be discerned. Thus I have often said: Guo Ji, Kou Xun, Zhang Kan, Song Jun, and Cen Xi were capable officials; Lu Gong was both capable and virtuous; as for Zhuo Mao, Dong Xuan, Jia Dunshi, and Zhang Yunji, they were among the conscientious and virtuous…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之儔匹與王李廉頗勇將也曹彬勇而仁
者也祭羊郭范其儒將之翹楚與我
國家以
神武定天下以
文德致太平憲
天立法酌古垂制布列郡縣者既藹藹之吉人
守禦封疆者又赳赳之武士故百八十餘
年内安外謐文煕武恬真匹休隆古三代
之盛而□□唐宋于下風者由此其選也
===
試舉其績□□西者如章復之守桂林課
農興學百廢具舉暇日則行飲射讀法之
禮大旱則有每禱輒雨之應何源之守梧
州時值饑饉議欲請賑源恐待報之無及
乃亟捐俸以活民若張霖之宰馬平則有
愛民如子之心有感神捕虎之驗恩信孚
於峒賊衣冠化其強暴此三子者皆守令
之賢而章復則尤能以禮讓為政教有古
循良之風其與龔遂黃霸之治渤賴卓茂
punctuated:
之儔匹與？王、李、廉頗，勇將也；曹彬，勇而仁者也；祭、羊、郭、范，其儒將之翹楚與？我國家以神武定天下，以文德致太平，憲天立法，酌古垂制。布列郡縣者，既藹藹之吉人；守禦封疆者，又赳赳之武士。故百八十餘年，内安外謐，文煕武恬，真匹休隆古三代之盛，而□□唐宋于下風者，由此其選也。

試舉其績□□西者，如章復之守桂林，課農興學，百廢具舉。暇日則行飲射讀法之禮，大旱則有每禱輒雨之應。何源之守梧州，時值饑饉，議欲請賑，源恐待報之無及，乃亟捐俸以活民。若張霖之宰馬平，則有愛民如子之心，有感神捕虎之驗，恩信孚於峒賊，衣冠化其強暴。此三子者，皆守令之賢，而章復則尤能以禮讓為政教，有古循良之風。其與龔遂、黃霸之治渤賴，卓茂
translation_en:
…their peers? Wang, Li, and Lian Po were valiant generals; Cao Bin was valiant and humane. Were not Ji, Yang, Guo, and Fan outstanding among scholarly generals? Our dynasty pacified the realm through divine martial prowess and brought about peace through civil virtue. It modeled its laws on Heaven and weighed ancient precedents in establishing institutions for posterity. Those stationed throughout the prefectures and counties were gracious men of worth; those defending the frontiers were stalwart warriors. Thus, for more than 180 years, there has been security within and tranquility without, with civil affairs flourishing and military affairs at peace. That our dynasty truly matches the glory of the Three Dynasties of high antiquity and [two illegible characters] leaves the Tang and Song in an inferior position is due to its selection of such men.

Let us cite examples of their achievements in [two illegible characters]xi [?]. When Zhang Fu served as prefect of Guilin, he encouraged agriculture and promoted learning, reviving every neglected undertaking. In his leisure he conducted the rites of communal drinking, archery, and reading the laws aloud. During severe droughts, his prayers invariably elicited rain. When He Yuan served as prefect of Wuzhou, famine struck. There was discussion of requesting relief, but Yuan feared that waiting for a reply would make it too late. He therefore promptly contributed his own salary to keep the people alive. As for Zhang Lin, magistrate of Maping, he loved the people as his own children. His efficacy was demonstrated in moving the spirits and capturing tigers. His kindness and trustworthiness won the confidence of the grotto bandits, and his civil bearing transformed their violent ways. All three were worthy prefects or magistrates, but Zhang Fu was especially able to make ritual propriety and deference the basis of government and instruction, embodying the spirit of the conscientious and benevolent officials of antiquity. Compared with Gong Sui and Huang Ba in their administration of Bo and Lai [?], and Zhuo Mao …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
魯恭之治密牟蓋相伯仲矣又如楊璟以
征南將軍攻克靜江戒張彬之屠戮下剽
掠之禁令卒致土官遣使齎印來降山雲
以總兵掛印出鎮廣西臨戰陳則身先士
卒持廉介則秋毫無犯卒致蠻夷懾服居
民安堵若江陰侯吳良之討兩江五谿懷
之以恩德招之以納款洞寨二百餘所悉
為編戶興師不踰四月遂定古州此三子
者皆將帥之良而山雲則尤能以威信馭
===
土官有古良將之風其與馬援之在漢韓
世忠岳飛之在宋蓋相頡頏矣嗟乎宜於
古者或不宜於今遠有所慕者則近或有
所遺郭伋王剪之輩歷世遠矣姑舍是也
章復諸子非守令之法則乎山雲諸子非
將帥之軌範乎誠使今之為守令者貪墨
是懲每先公而後私怠荒必戒不見利而
忘義勸相以時而賦稅以平優恤其財而
愛養其力常體乎節用愛人之意則居者
punctuated:
魯恭之治密牟，蓋相伯仲矣。又如楊璟以征南將軍攻克靜江，戒張彬之屠戮，下剽掠之禁令，卒致土官遣使齎印來降。山雲以總兵掛印出鎮廣西，臨戰陳則身先士卒，持廉介則秋毫無犯，卒致蠻夷懾服，居民安堵。若江陰侯吳良之討兩江五谿，懷之以恩德，招之以納款，洞寨二百餘所悉為編戶，興師不踰四月，遂定古州。此三子者，皆將帥之良，而山雲則尤能以威信馭土官，有古良將之風，其與馬援之在漢、韓世忠岳飛之在宋，蓋相頡頏矣。
嗟乎！宜於古者，或不宜於今；遠有所慕者，則近或有所遺。郭伋王剪之輩，歷世遠矣，姑舍是也。章復諸子，非守令之法則乎？山雲諸子，非將帥之軌範乎？誠使今之為守令者，貪墨是懲，每先公而後私，怠荒必戒，不見利而忘義，勸相以時而賦稅以平，優恤其財而愛養其力，常體乎節用愛人之意，則居者
translation_en:
…and Lu Gong in their administration of Mi and Mou, he was broadly their equal. Likewise, Yang Jing, as General Who Subdues the South, captured Jingjiang, warned Zhang Bin against slaughter, and issued orders prohibiting plunder. Ultimately, the native officials sent envoys bearing their seals to surrender. Shan Yun, invested with the seal of Regional Commander, went out to command the garrison in Guangxi. In battle he led his officers and soldiers from the front; in maintaining his integrity, he did not encroach upon even a hair’s breadth of others’ property. In the end, the non-Han peoples submitted in awe, and the inhabitants lived securely. When Wu Liang, Marquis of Jiangyin, campaigned against the Two Rivers and Five Streams, he won their allegiance through kindness and beneficence and invited them to submit. More than two hundred cave settlements and stockaded villages were all incorporated into the household registers. Within four months of mobilizing his forces, he had pacified Guzhou. These three men were all excellent commanders, but Shan Yun was particularly able to control the native officials through authority and trustworthiness, displaying the qualities of the fine generals of antiquity. He was broadly the equal of Ma Yuan under the Han and Han Shizhong and Yue Fei under the Song.
Alas! What suited antiquity may not suit the present; those who admire distant examples may overlook those close at hand. Men such as Guo Ji and Wang Jian belong to ages long past; let us set them aside for now. Are not Zhang Fu and the others models for prefects and magistrates? Are not Shan Yun and the others exemplars for military commanders? If only today’s prefects and magistrates would curb their greed and corruption, always place public duties before private interests, guard against negligence, and never forget righteousness at the sight of profit; if they would encourage and assist farming at the proper seasons, levy taxes equitably, show generous concern for the people’s resources, and cherish and sustain their strength, always putting into practice the principle of frugality in expenditure and care for the people, then those who remain in their homes…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有樂土之願逃者有復業之望又何户口
流亡之足患哉為將帥者公以奉法而衛
士不為私門之役廉以蒞官而軍貲不為
房闥之需督其屯種而斂納以時嚴其簡
教而賞罰惟信常念乎士卒甘苦之同則
居常而結其歡心遇變而得其死力又何
盜賊充斥之足慮哉然此特論其槩耳若
夫粤西邊鄙民之生于其地者其害尤倍
于中州□□而墾田寡也賊繁而角奪甚
===
也法廢而□横興也食衆而生産微也所
賴官于其地者為之啓利而損害耳不然
中谷之歎興六月之師動邊民其終魚鼈
乎必于守令也超遷不拘于資格考覈靡
狥于愛憎如卓茂令密邑而以為太傅張
平長全椒而以為議郎可也不惑于即墨
之毀言日至致察于膠東之户口偽增可
也而又遴選近地沙汰老弱使風氣相宜
精神不倦庶得以安其位而行其志民患
punctuated:
有樂土之願，逃者有復業之望，又何户口流亡之足患哉？為將帥者，公以奉法，而衛士不為私門之役；廉以蒞官，而軍貲不為房闥之需；督其屯種，而斂納以時；嚴其簡教，而賞罰惟信；常念乎士卒甘苦之同，則居常而結其歡心，遇變而得其死力，又何盜賊充斥之足慮哉？
然此特論其槩耳。若夫粤西邊鄙，民之生于其地者，其害尤倍于中州：□□而墾田寡也，賊繁而角奪甚也，法廢而□横興也，食衆而生産微也。所賴官于其地者，為之啓利而損害耳。不然，《中谷》之歎興，《六月》之師動，邊民其終魚鼈乎？
必于守令也，超遷不拘于資格，考覈靡狥于愛憎，如卓茂令密邑而以為太傅，張平長全椒而以為議郎，可也；不惑于即墨之毀言日至，致察于膠東之户口偽增，可也。而又遴選近地，沙汰老弱，使風氣相宜，精神不倦，庶得以安其位而行其志，民患
translation_en:
…may aspire to a happy land, and those who have fled may hope to return to their livelihoods. What cause would there then be to worry about households fleeing and becoming displaced? Those serving as military commanders should uphold the law impartially, so that guard soldiers are not made to labor for private households; administer their offices incorruptibly, so that military funds are not used to meet the expenses of their inner chambers; oversee military farming and collect its dues at the proper times; rigorously conduct selection and training, and make rewards and punishments trustworthy; and always remember to share their soldiers’ hardships and comforts. Then, in ordinary times, they will win the soldiers’ affection, and in emergencies obtain their service to the death. What cause would there then be to fear bandits overrunning the land?
Yet this discusses only the broad outlines. As for the borderlands of Yuexi, the people born there suffer harms far greater than those of the central regions: [two illegible characters], and little land is cultivated; bandits are numerous, and struggles over plunder are severe; laws fall into disuse, and [?] lawlessness flourishes; mouths to feed are many, and production is scant. Their sole reliance is on those holding office there to open up sources of benefit and diminish their hardships. Otherwise, the lament of “In the Valley” will arise, and the armies of “The Sixth Month” will be mobilized. Will the border people ultimately become fish and turtles?
In the case of prefects and magistrates, exceptional promotion must not be constrained by formal qualifications, and evaluations must not yield to personal likes and dislikes. It would be fitting to follow the examples of Zhuo Mao, who served as magistrate of Mi and was appointed Grand Mentor, and Zhang Ping, who served as magistrate of Quanjiao and was appointed Court Gentleman for Consultation. It would also be fitting not to be misled by the daily stream of slander against Jimo’s administrator, and to scrutinize the fictitious increases in Jiaodong’s household and population figures. Furthermore, select men from nearby places and weed out the old and infirm, so that the local climate suits them and their energies do not flag. They may then be able to settle securely into their posts and carry out their aims. The people’s afflictions…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其有瘳乎于將帥也爵必視其功績任必
擇其智勇如范仲淹所謂搜羅班中試以
武藝歐陽脩所謂校其軍中拔爲大將可
也申武學之教不視爲虚文嚴臨陣之法
以驗其實用可也而又勿奪其權少繩以
法使鼓舞有方展布如意庶得以畢其技
而効其長民生其有頼乎是謂通其法于
不窮識其重而亟反之者也有復受直怠
事而不思所以宣力布武者非夫也昔漢
===
文帝患匈奴難制而拊髀以思頗牧宣帝
稱良二千石欲與共圖治理故漢世良吏
爲盛而良將亦多享國長久夷狄無患有
以也我
皇上明見萬里屢頒
綸音軫念遐陬凡所以
立天下之法
操天下之機以生以衞此粤西之民者無所
不至矣則夫厝斯民於衽席襁褓之安而
punctuated:
其有瘳乎？于將帥也，爵必視其功績，任必擇其智勇。如范仲淹所謂搜羅班中，試以武藝，歐陽脩所謂校其軍中，拔爲大將，可也。申武學之教，不視爲虚文；嚴臨陣之法，以驗其實用，可也。而又勿奪其權，少繩以法，使鼓舞有方，展布如意，庶得以畢其技而効其長，民生其有頼乎？是謂通其法于不窮，識其重而亟反之者也。有復受直怠事，而不思所以宣力布武者，非夫也。
昔漢文帝患匈奴難制，而拊髀以思頗牧；宣帝稱良二千石，欲與共圖治理。故漢世良吏爲盛，而良將亦多，享國長久，夷狄無患，有以也。我皇上明見萬里，屢頒綸音，軫念遐陬，凡所以立天下之法、操天下之機，以生以衞此粤西之民者，無所不至矣。則夫厝斯民於衽席襁褓之安，而
translation_en:
…might their suffering then be relieved? As for military commanders, their noble rank must reflect their achievements, and their appointment must depend on their wisdom and courage. It would be fitting to follow Fan Zhongyan’s proposal to seek out men within the ranks and test their martial skills, or Ouyang Xiu’s proposal to assess men within the army and promote them to high command. It would also be fitting to reinforce instruction in military learning, without treating it as an empty formality, and to enforce strictly the rules governing conduct in battle, thereby testing its practical effectiveness. Moreover, commanders should not be deprived of their authority and should be less constrained by regulations, so that they can inspire their troops effectively and carry out their plans as intended. They might thus fully exercise their skills and put their strengths to use. Might the people’s livelihood then have something to depend upon? This is what is meant by adapting these methods so that their efficacy is inexhaustible, recognizing what matters most, and promptly returning to it. Anyone who still draws his pay while neglecting his duties, without considering how to exert himself and display military prowess, is no worthy man.
In former times, Emperor Wen of Han, troubled by the difficulty of bringing the Xiongnu under control, slapped his thigh and longed for men like Lian Po and Li Mu. Emperor Xuan praised capable officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank, wishing to work with them to bring about good government. Thus, under the Han, capable civil officials flourished, and capable generals were also numerous.
